explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.Filter.comap_comap: A theorem demonstrating that the composition of two filter transformations is equivalent to applying the composition of the corresponding functions within a single transformation on the filter.
explanatories.Eq.ge: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if two elements are equal, then one is less than or equal to the other.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.Filter.comap_mono: A theorem stating that the operation of mapping a filter through a function preserves the property of monotonicity.

nhds.comment:
A set is called a neighborhood of `x` if it contains an open set around `x`. The set of all
neighborhoods of `x` forms a filter, the neighborhood filter at `x`, is here defined as the
infimum over the principal filters of all open sets containing `x`.

ContinuousAt.code:

  Prop
ContinuousAt.comment:
A function between topological spaces is continuous at a point `x₀`
if `f x` tends to `f x₀` when `x` tends to `x₀`.

explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.

ContinuousAt.description: This defines the condition for a function between topological spaces to be continuous at a specific point by ensuring that the function values approach the value at that point as the input approaches it.

explanatories.Filter.nonempty_of_neBot: A theorem asserting that if a filter is non-empty, then the underlying set of that filter must also be non-empty.

ultrafilter.Lim.fullDefinition: noncomputable nonrec def Ultrafilter.lim (F : Ultrafilter X) : X :=   @lim X _ (nonempty_of_neBot F) F
ultrafilter.Lim.description: The limit of an ultrafilter in a topological space, if it exists, yields a point in that space.

limUnder.comment:

limUnder.description: The limit of a function at a given filter is defined as the point in the topological space that the function approaches under the conditions specified by that filter, provided such a limit exists.

ClusterPt.code: ClusterPt.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] (x : X) (F : Filter X) : Prop
ClusterPt.comment:
A point `x` is a cluster point of a filter `F` if `𝓝 x ⊓ F ≠ ⊥`.
Also known as an accumulation point or a limit point, but beware that terminology varies.
This is *not* the same as asking `𝓝[≠] x ⊓ F ≠ ⊥`, which is called `AccPt` in Mathlib.
See `mem_closure_iff_clusterPt` in particular.
ClusterPt.fullDefinition: def ClusterPt (x : X) (F : Filter X) : Prop :=   NeBot (𝓝 x ⊓ F)
ClusterPt.description: This defines a condition for a point to be a cluster point of a given filter in topology, indicating that the intersection of the filter with the neighborhood of the point is non-empty.

cluster_pt.description: This defines a condition for a point to be a cluster point of a given filter in topology, indicating that the intersection of the filter with the neighborhood of the point is non-empty.

MapClusterPt.comment:

explanatories.Filter.map: A definition describing a transformation of a filter through a function that maps elements from one type to another.

MapClusterPt.fullDefinition: def MapClusterPt {ι : Type*} (x : X) (F : Filter ι) (u : ι → X) : Prop :=   ClusterPt x (map u F)
MapClusterPt.description: This defines a condition for a point to be a cluster point of a sequence when considered with respect to a specific filter by examining its relationship to the image of that sequence under the filter.

IsCompact.code: IsCompact.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] (s : Set X) : Prop
IsCompact.comment:
A set `s` is compact if for every nontrivial filter `f` that contains `s`,
there exists `a ∈ s` such that every set of `f` meets every neighborhood of `a`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

IsCompact.description: This defines the property of a set within a topological space being compact, which requires that for any nontrivial filter containing the set, there is an element within the set such that every set in the filter intersects with every neighborhood of that element.

LocallyCompactPair.exists_mem_nhds_isCom.code:
LocallyCompactPair.exists_mem_nhds_isCompact_mapsTo.{u_3, u_4} {X : Type u_3} {Y : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [TopologicalSpace Y] [self : LocallyCompactPair X Y] {f : X → Y} {x : X} {s : Set Y} :

seqClosure.code: seqClosure.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] (s : Set X) : Set X
seqClosure.comment:
The sequential closure of a set `s : Set X` in a topological space `X` is the set of all `a : X`
which arise as limit of sequences in `s`. Note that the sequential closure of a set is not
guaranteed to be sequentially closed.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.Filter.atTop: This definition introduces a filter that captures the behavior of elements approaching infinity in an ordered set, generated by all sets containing elements greater than or equal to any given element.

seqClosure.fullDefinition: def seqClosure (s : Set X) : Set X :=   { a | ∃ x : ℕ → X, (∀ n : ℕ, x n ∈ s) ∧ Tendsto x atTop (𝓝 a) }
seqClosure.description: This defines the sequential closure of a set in a topological space, consisting of all points that can be reached as limits of sequences from that set.

TopologicalSpace.induced.comment:

that are preimages of some open set in `Y`.
This is the coarsest topology that makes `f` continuous.

explanatories.Set.preimage_univ: The preimage of the universal set under any function is the universal set itself.
explanatories.Inter.inter: The intersection of two sets is a binary operation that produces a new set containing only the elements common to both.
explanatories.Set.preimage_inter: The preimage of the intersection of two sets under a function is equal to the intersection of the preimages of those sets under the same function.
explanatories.Set.forall_mem_image: The condition that a property holds for all images of elements from a set under a function is equivalent to saying that the property holds for the function's output applied to every element of that set.
explanatories.Set.preimage_sUnion: The preimage of the union of a collection of sets under a function is equal to the union of the preimages of each individual set in that collection.
explanatories.Set.biUnion_image: The union of a set of images under a function is equal to the union obtained by first applying the function to the set and then taking the union of the image of each element.
explanatories.Set.sUnion_eq_biUnion: The union of all sets contained in a collection of sets is equal to the union of the individual sets within that collection.
explanatories.Set.iUnion₂_congr: The union of unions of two families of sets is equal if every corresponding set in the two families is equal.

TopologicalSpace.induced.fullDefinition: def induced (f : X → Y) (t : TopologicalSpace Y) : TopologicalSpace X where   IsOpen s := ∃ t, IsOpen t ∧ f ⁻¹' t = s   isOpen_univ := ⟨univ, isOpen_univ, preimage_univ⟩   isOpen_inter := by     rintro s₁ s₂ ⟨s'₁, hs₁, rfl⟩ ⟨s'₂, hs₂, rfl⟩     exact ⟨s'₁ ∩ s'₂, hs₁.inter hs₂, preimage_inter⟩   isOpen_sUnion S h := by     choose! g hgo hfg using h     refine ⟨⋃₀ (g '' S), isOpen_sUnion <| forall_mem_image.2 hgo, ?_⟩     rw [preimage_sUnion, biUnion_image, sUnion_eq_biUnion]     exact iUnion₂_congr hfg

orderBornology.code: orderBornology.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Lattice α] [Nonempty α] : Bornology α
orderBornology.comment:
Order-bornology on a nonempty lattice. The bounded sets are the sets that are bounded both above
and below.

explanatories.Bornology.ofBounded: This constructs a bornology by defining a collection of bounded sets that satisfies properties such as containing the empty set, being closed under subsets and unions, and including all singletons.
explanatories.BddBelow: This definition states that a set is considered bounded below if there exists at least one element that serves as a lower bound for all elements in the set within a preorder structure.
explanatories.BddAbove: This definition states that a set is considered bounded above if there exists at least one element that serves as an upper bound for all elements in the set within a preorder structure.
explanatories.BddBelow.mono: This theorem establishes that if one set is a subset of another and the larger set is bounded below, then the smaller set must also be bounded below within a preorder structure.
explanatories.BddAbove.mono: This theorem states that if one set is a subset of another and the larger set is bounded above, then the smaller set must also be bounded above.
explanatories.BddBelow.union: In a directed order, if two sets are bounded below, then their union is also bounded below.
explanatories.BddAbove.union: This theorem states that in a directed order, if two sets are both bounded above, then their union is also bounded above.

orderBornology.fullDefinition: def orderBornology : Bornology α := .ofBounded   {s | BddBelow s ∧ BddAbove s}   (by simp)   (fun s hs t hst ↦ ⟨hs.1.mono hst, hs.2.mono hst⟩)   (fun s hs t ht ↦ ⟨hs.1.union ht.1, hs.2.union ht.2⟩)   (by simp)
orderBornology.description: This defines the order-bornology for a nonempty lattice, where the bounded sets are those that have both upper and lower bounds.

Preorder.topology.code: Preorder.topology.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) [Preorder α] : TopologicalSpace α
Preorder.topology.comment:
(Order) topology on a partial order `α` generated by the subbase of open intervals
`(a, ∞) = { x ∣ a < x }, (-∞ , b) = {x ∣ x < b}` for all `a, b` in `α`. We do not register it as an
instance as many ordered sets are already endowed with the same topology, most often in a non-defeq
way though. Register as a local instance when necessary.

explanatories.TopologicalSpace.generateFrom: This definition describes the smallest topological space that includes a given collection of basic open sets.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Preorder.topology.fullDefinition: def Preorder.topology (α : Type*) [Preorder α] : TopologicalSpace α :=   generateFrom { s : Set α | ∃ a : α, s = { b : α | a < b } ∨ s = { b : α | b < a } }
Preorder.topology.description: This definition introduces a topology for a partially ordered set by using open intervals generated from the order structure.

explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.

explanatories.nhds_eq_order: This theorem expresses that the neighborhood of a specific element in an order topology is the infimum of the filters generated by the lower and upper open intervals surrounding that element.
explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.
explanatories.iInf_subtype': This theorem establishes an equality between the infimum of a family of values indexed by a property and the infimum of the corresponding function values over all instances satisfying that property within a complete lattice.
explanatories.Filter.hasBasis_iInf_principal_finite: A theorem stating that the family of finite intersections of indexed sets forms a basis for the infimum of the filters generated by those sets.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.inf: A theorem stating that the infimum of two filters, each with a basis, possesses a basis formed by the conjunction of their respective indexed properties and the intersection of their corresponding sets.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.tendstoIxxClass: A theorem asserting that if a filter has a basis and the binary relation defined by a specified class maintains certain inclusion properties within the basis sets, then the class of filters defined by that relation converges to the same filter.
explanatories.Set.ordConnected_biInter: This theorem demonstrates that the intersection of a family of order-connected sets, indexed by a property, is itself order-connected if each individual set in the family is order-connected.
explanatories.Set.OrdConnected.inter: This theorem asserts that the intersection of two order-connected sets is also order-connected.
explanatories.Set.OrdConnected.out: This theorem states that if a set is order-connected, then for any point in the set, the closed interval to any other point in the set is also contained within that set.

explanatories.OrderTopology: This theorem demonstrates that the topology of an order topology is precisely the topology generated by the lower and upper open intervals associated with the preorder structure.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.Filter.tendsto_iInf: A theorem stating that a function converges to the infimum of a family of filters if and only if it converges to each filter in the family individually.
explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.Icc: A theorem stating that if two functions converge to a specified filter along a certain filter, then the image generated by their interval function also converges to the small sets of another filter.
explanatories.Filter.smallSets: The largest filter consisting of all the powersets of the elements in a given filter is defined as the small sets filter of that original filter.
explanatories.nhds_pi: This theorem establishes that the neighborhood of a point in a product space is equal to the product of the neighborhoods of its components.
explanatories.Filter.pi: A definition of the product filter constructed from an indexed family of filters.
explanatories.Filter.smallSets_iInf: The small sets filter of the infimum of a family of filters is equal to the infimum of the small sets filters of each individual filter in that family.
explanatories.Filter.tendsto_comap_iff: A theorem stating that a function converges to a limit under a filter if and only if the composition of that function with another function also converges to a limit under a different filter derived from the second function.
explanatories.continuous_apply: This theorem states that if each type in a family of types has a topology, then the function that selects the component of a dependent pair based on its index is continuous.
explanatories.Continuous.tendsto: A continuous function at a point preserves the convergence of sequences by ensuring that the limit of the function's output at that point is the image of the limit of the input.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.comp: A theorem stating that the composition of two functions that tend to maps between respective filters also results in a function that tends to map from the original filter to the final one.
explanatories.Filter.tendsto_fst: The first component of a product of two filters converges to the first filter.
explanatories.Filter.tendsto_snd: The second component of the product of two filters converges with respect to the second filter.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.smallSets_mono: If a function tends to a filter consisting of small sets and for almost every element in the first filter, the set produced by another function is contained within the first, then this new function also tends to the same small sets filter.
explanatories.Set.image_subset_iff: The image of a set under a function is a subset of another set if and only if the original set is a subset of the preimage of that other set, illustrating a Galois connection between image and preimage.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.

Then the family is countable.

empty (but in fact this can happen only for countably many of them).

explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.LE.le.trans_lt: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is strictly less than the third.

explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.

explanatories.Set.Countable.image: The image of a countable set under a function is also countable.
explanatories.Set.Countable: A set is considered countable if there exists an injective function from that set to the natural numbers.
explanatories.Classical.not_forall: The equivalence between the negation of a universal statement and the existence of a counterexample is demonstrated by showing that not all elements satisfy the property if at least one element does not.
explanatories.not_le: This theorem establishes that, in a linear order, the negation of the relation indicating that the first element is less than or equal to the second is equivalent to asserting that the second element is strictly less than the first.
explanatories.lt_irrefl: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, no element can be less than itself.
explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.Disjoint.symm: If two elements in a lattice are disjoint, then the second element is also disjoint from the first, establishing the symmetry of disjointness.
explanatories.IsTop: An element in a partially ordered set is considered a top element if it is greater than or equal to every other element in that set.
explanatories.Filter.atTop_eq_pure_of_isTop: The filter that describes the topology at infinity in a linear order is equal to the filter that contains only the single point at the top if that point is indeed an upper bound.

explanatories.not_exists: The negation of the existence of an element satisfying a property is equivalent to the property being false for all elements.

instIsCountablyGenerated_atTop.fullDefinition: instance instIsCountablyGenerated_atTop [SecondCountableTopology α] :     IsCountablyGenerated (atTop : Filter α) := by   by_cases h : ∃ (x : α), IsTop x   · rcases h with ⟨x, hx⟩     rw [atTop_eq_pure_of_isTop hx]     exact isCountablyGenerated_pure x   · rcases exists_countable_basis α with ⟨b, b_count, b_ne, hb⟩     have : Countable b := by exact Iff.mpr countable_coe_iff b_count     have A : ∀ (s : b), ∃ (x : α), x ∈ (s : Set α) := by       intro s       have : (s : Set α) ≠ ∅ := by         intro H         apply b_ne         convert s.2         exact H.symm       exact Iff.mp nmem_singleton_empty this     choose a ha using A     have : (atTop : Filter α) = (generate (Ici '' (range a))) := by       apply atTop_eq_generate_of_not_bddAbove       intro ⟨x, hx⟩       simp only [IsTop, not_exists, not_forall, not_le] at h       rcases h x with ⟨y, hy⟩       obtain ⟨s, sb, -, hs⟩ : ∃ s, s ∈ b ∧ y ∈ s ∧ s ⊆ Ioi x :=         hb.exists_subset_of_mem_open hy isOpen_Ioi       have I : a ⟨s, sb⟩ ≤ x := hx (mem_range_self _)       have J : x < a ⟨s, sb⟩ := hs (ha ⟨s, sb⟩)       exact lt_irrefl _ (I.trans_lt J)     rw [this]     exact ⟨_, (countable_range _).image _, rfl⟩

explanatories.Filter.eventually_ge_atTop: This theorem asserts that in an ordered set, eventually all elements will be greater than or equal to a specified element when approaching positive infinity.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.mono: A theorem that states if a property holds for a filter and implies another property, then the latter property also holds for that filter.
explanatories.LT.lt.trans_le: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than a second and that second element is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also strictly less than the third.
explanatories.Filter.eventually_of_forall: A theorem stating that if a property holds for all elements in a type, then it holds for almost all elements with respect to a given filter.
explanatories.LE.le.trans_lt: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is strictly less than the third.

LinearOrder.supConvergenceClass.supConve.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) LinearOrder.supConvergenceClass [TopologicalSpace α] [LinearOrder α]     [OrderTopology α] : SupConvergenceClass α := by   refine ⟨fun a s ha => tendsto_order.2 ⟨fun b hb => ?_, fun b hb => ?_⟩⟩   · rcases ha.exists_between hb with ⟨c, hcs, bc, bca⟩     lift c to s using hcs     exact (eventually_ge_atTop c).mono fun x hx => bc.trans_le hx   · exact eventually_of_forall fun x => (ha.1 x.2).trans_lt hb

Topology.IsUpper.continuous_iff_Iic.comment:
A function `f : β → α` with upper topology in the codomain is continuous
if and only if the preimage of every interval `Set.Iic a` is a closed set.

explanatories.Set.Iic: This definition identifies the set of elements that are less than or equal to a given element in a preorder structure, resulting in a left-infinite and right-closed interval.

Topology.IsUpper.continuous_iff_Iic.description: This theorem states that a function defined from one topological space to another with an upper topology is continuous if and only if the preimage of every lower closed interval is a closed set in the domain.

explanatories.t0Space_iff_inseparable: This theorem states that a topological space is a T0 space if and only if for any pair of inseparable points, those points must be equal.
explanatories.Set.Ici_injective: This theorem asserts that the mapping which takes an element to the set of elements greater than or equal to it in a partially ordered set is injective, meaning distinct elements map to distinct sets.
explanatories.inseparable_iff_closure_eq: The theorem states that two points are inseparable in a topological space if and only if the closure of one point is equal to the closure of the other point.

explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Topology.lower: This definition introduces a topology on a partially ordered type generated by the open sets formed from the complements of left-closed right-infinite intervals.
explanatories.Topology.IsLower.topology_eq_lowerTopolo: This theorem asserts that the topology of a space that is equipped with a lower structure is identical to the lower set topology defined on that space.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.GenerateOpen.basic: This theorem states that if a set is a member of a collection of sets that generate a topology, then that set is open in the topology generated by that collection.
explanatories.isClosed_Ici: This theorem establishes that in a topological space with a closed upper interval topology, the set of all elements greater than or equal to a given element is closed.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.GenerateOpen.inter: This theorem proves that the intersection of two open sets in a topology generated by a family of open sets is also an open set.
explanatories.IsLowerSet.inter: The intersection of two lower sets in an ordered structure is also a lower set.
explanatories.coe_upperClosure: The upper closure of a set in a preordered structure consists of the union of all upper sets defined by each element in that original set.
explanatories.Set.compl_iUnion: The complement of the union of a family of sets is equal to the intersection of the complements of each set in that family.
explanatories.Topology.IsLower.isTopologicalBasis: This theorem confirms that the collection of lower sets forms a topological basis for the topology defined on a preorder equipped with the lower set structure.
explanatories.le_antisymm: This theorem establishes that in a partial order, if one element is less than or equal to another and vice versa, then the two elements must be equal.
explanatories.le_generateFrom: This theorem demonstrates that if a collection of sets is open in a topological space, then the space is contained within the topology generated by that collection of sets.
explanatories.IsClosed.prod: This theorem states that the Cartesian product of two closed sets in topological spaces is also a closed set.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis.prod: The Cartesian product of two topological bases results in a new collection that also forms a topological basis for the product space.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis.eq_g: The topology on a space is uniquely determined by a collection of sets that forms a topological basis for that space.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.le_generateFrom_iff_sub: This theorem characterizes the relationship between a topological space being less than or equal to the space generated from a set of subsets and the condition that those subsets must be open.
explanatories.Set.image2_subset_iff: The image of a binary function applied to two sets is a subset of another set if and only if every value obtained by applying the function to pairs from the two sets is also contained in that other set.
explanatories.Set.prod_eq: The Cartesian product of two sets is equal to the set of pairs where the first component is taken from the first set and the second component from the second set.
explanatories.Set.preimage_iInter: The preimage of the intersection of sets under a function is equal to the intersection of the preimages of those sets.
explanatories.Set.preimage_compl: The preimage of the complement of a set under any function is equal to the complement of the preimage of that set.
explanatories.Set.Finite.isOpen_biInter: The intersection of a finite collection of open sets is also an open set in a topological space.
explanatories.Set.Ici_prod_eq: This theorem asserts that the set of elements that are greater than or equal to a specified pair is equivalent to the Cartesian product of the sets of elements that are greater than or equal to each component of that pair in their respective preorder structures.
explanatories.Set.prod_univ: The theorem states that the Cartesian product of any set with a universal set is equal to the preimage of that set under the projection onto the first component.
explanatories.Set.univ_prod: The theorem asserts that the Cartesian product of a universal set with any set is equal to the preimage of that set under the projection onto the second component.

Topology.instIsLowerProd.fullDefinition: instance instIsLowerProd [Preorder α] [TopologicalSpace α] [IsLower α]     [OrderBot α] [Preorder β] [TopologicalSpace β] [IsLower β] [OrderBot β] :     IsLower (α × β) where   topology_eq_lowerTopology := by     refine le_antisymm (le_generateFrom ?_) ?_     · rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩       exact (isClosed_Ici.prod isClosed_Ici).isOpen_compl     rw [(IsLower.isTopologicalBasis.prod       IsLower.isTopologicalBasis).eq_generateFrom, le_generateFrom_iff_subset_isOpen,       image2_subset_iff]     rintro _ ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩ _ ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩     dsimp     simp_rw [coe_upperClosure, compl_iUnion, prod_eq, preimage_iInter, preimage_compl]     -- without `let`, `refine` tries to use the product topology and fails     let _ : TopologicalSpace (α × β) := lower (α × β)     refine (hs.isOpen_biInter fun a _ => ?_).inter (ht.isOpen_biInter fun b _ => ?_)     · exact GenerateOpen.basic _ ⟨(a, ⊥), by simp [Ici_prod_eq, prod_univ]⟩     · exact GenerateOpen.basic _ ⟨(⊥, b), by simp [Ici_prod_eq, univ_prod]⟩
Topology.instIsLowerProd.description: This definition establishes that the product of two types, each equipped with a lower topology, also possesses a lower topology.

StrictMonoOn.continuousWithinAt_right_of.code:
StrictMonoOn.continuousWithinAt_right_of_exists_between.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [LinearOrder α]
  [TopologicalSpace α] [OrderTopology α] [LinearOrder β] [TopologicalSpace β] [OrderTopology β] {f : α → β} {s : Set α}
  {a : α} (h_mono : StrictMonoOn f s) (hs : s ∈ 𝓝[≥] a) (hfs : ∀ b > f a, ∃ c ∈ s, f c ∈ Ioc (f a) b) :
  ContinuousWithinAt f (Ici a) a
StrictMonoOn.continuousWithinAt_right_of.comment:
If `f` is a function strictly monotone on a right neighborhood of `a` and the
image of this neighborhood under `f` meets every interval `(f a, b]`, `b > f a`, then `f` is
continuous at `a` from the right.

The assumption `hfs : ∀ b > f a, ∃ c ∈ s, f c ∈ Ioc (f a) b` is required because otherwise the
function `f : ℝ → ℝ` given by `f x = if x ≤ 0 then x else x + 1` would be a counter-example at
`a = 0`.

StrictMonoOn.continuousWithinAt_right_of.description: This theorem states that if a function is strictly monotone in a right neighborhood of a point and its image intersects every interval above the function's value at that point, then the function is continuous at that point from the right.

explanatories.Topology.IsUpperSet.topology_eq: This theorem asserts that a topological space with open sets defined by upper sets in a preorder is equal to the standard upper set topology on that space.

Topology.WithUpperSet.map.comment:
A monotone map between preorders spaces induces a continuous map between themselves considered
with the upper set topology.

explanatories.Topology.WithUpperSet.toUpperSet: This definition describes a function that acts as the identity mapping from a type to its associated upper set topology.
explanatories.Topology.WithUpperSet.ofUpperSet: This definition introduces a function that serves as the identity mapping from the upper set topology of a type back to the original type.
explanatories.continuous_def: A function between topological spaces is continuous if and only if the preimage of every open set in the codomain is open in the domain.
explanatories.IsUpperSet.preimage: The preimage of an upper set under a monotone function in a preorder is also an upper set.
explanatories.OrderHom.monotone: This theorem asserts that any order homomorphism between two preordered types is a monotone function.
explanatories.Set.preimage: The preimage of a set under a function consists of all elements that map into the set when the function is applied.
explanatories.IsLowerSet.preimage: The preimage of a lower set under a monotone function is also a lower set.

Topology.WithUpperSet.map.description: This definition states that a monotone function between two ordered spaces induces a continuous map when those spaces are equipped with the upper set topology.

Topology.IsLowerSet.closure_singleton.comment:

interval (-∞,a].

explanatories.Topology.IsUpperSet.closure_singleton: This theorem asserts that in the upper set topology, the closure of a singleton set is equivalent to the interval extending negatively to infinity and including the element itself.

Topology.IsLowerSet.closure_singleton.description: This theorem states that the closure of a singleton set in a lower set topology is equal to the right-closed interval extending to negative infinity and ending at that singleton element.

element.

closure_Ioi'.description: This theorem asserts that the closure of the open interval from a point to infinity is the closed interval starting at that point and going to infinity, unless that point is the maximum element in the order.

DirSupInacc.comment:
A set `s` is said to be inaccessible by directed joins if, when the least upper bound of a
directed set `d` lies in `s` then `d` has non-empty intersection with `s`.

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

explanatories.IsLUB: This definition characterizes an element as the least upper bound of a set if it is an upper bound for the set and no other upper bound is smaller than it within a preorder structure.

DirSupInacc.fullDefinition: def DirSupInacc (s : Set α) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃d⦄, d.Nonempty → DirectedOn (· ≤ ·) d → ∀ ⦃a⦄, IsLUB d a → a ∈ s → (d ∩ s).Nonempty
DirSupInacc.description: This definition characterizes a set as being inaccessible by directed joins if any directed set whose least upper bound is in the set must have a non-empty intersection with it.

DirSupClosed.comment:
A set `s` is said to be closed under directed joins if, whenever a directed set `d` has a least
upper bound `a` and is a subset of `s` then `a` also lies in `s`.

A set `u` is open in the Scott-Hausdorff topology iff when the least upper bound of a directed set

IsPreconnected.mem_intervals.description: This theorem states that a preconnected set in a conditionally complete linear order must belong to a specific collection of intervals or be empty.

is_preconnected.mem_intervals.code:
IsPreconnected.mem_intervals.{u} {α : Type u} [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder α] [TopologicalSpace α]
  [OrderTopology α] {s : Set α} (hs : IsPreconnected s) :
  s ∈
    {Icc (sInf s) (sSup s), Ico (sInf s) (sSup s), Ioc (sInf s) (sSup s), Ioo (sInf s) (sSup s), Ici (sInf s),
      Ioi (sInf s), Iic (sSup s), Iio (sSup s), univ, ∅}
is_preconnected.mem_intervals.comment:
A preconnected set in a conditionally complete linear order is either one of the intervals
`[Inf s, Sup s]`, `[Inf s, Sup s)`, `(Inf s, Sup s]`, `(Inf s, Sup s)`, `[Inf s, +∞)`,
`(Inf s, +∞)`, `(-∞, Sup s]`, `(-∞, Sup s)`, `(-∞, +∞)`, or `∅`. The converse statement requires
`α` to be densely ordered.

      (range Ici ∪ range Ioi ∪ range Iic ∪ range Iio ∪ {univ, ∅})
setOf_isPreconnected_subset_of_ordered.comment:

one can represent `∅` as `(Inf ∅, Inf ∅)`, we include it into the list of possible cases to improve
readability.

  (hgt : ∀ x ∈ s ∩ Ico a b, (s ∩ Ioc x b).Nonempty) : b ∈ s
IsClosed.mem_of_ge_of_forall_exists_gt.comment:
A "continuous induction principle" for a closed interval: if a set `s` meets `[a, b]`
on a closed subset, contains `a`, and the set `s ∩ [a, b)` has no maximal point, then `b ∈ s`.

setOf_isPreconnected_eq_of_ordered.code:
setOf_isPreconnected_eq_of_ordered.{u} {α : Type u} [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder α] [TopologicalSpace α]
  [OrderTopology α] [DenselyOrdered α] :

    range (uncurry Icc) ∪ range (uncurry Ico) ∪ range (uncurry Ioc) ∪ range (uncurry Ioo) ∪
      (range Ici ∪ range Ioi ∪ range Iic ∪ range Iio ∪ {univ, ∅})
setOf_isPreconnected_eq_of_ordered.comment:
In a dense conditionally complete linear order, the set of preconnected sets is exactly
the set of the intervals `Icc`, `Ico`, `Ioc`, `Ioo`, `Ici`, `Ioi`, `Iic`, `Iio`, `(-∞, +∞)`,
or `∅`. Though one can represent `∅` as `(sInf s, sInf s)`, we include it into the list of
possible cases to improve readability.

Function.leftLim.comment:

let `a : α`. The limit strictly to the left of `f` at `a`, denoted with `leftLim f a`, is defined

limit, we use `f a` instead to guarantee a good behavior in most cases.

Topology.lawson.comment: The Lawson topology is defined as the meet of `Topology.lower` and the `Topology.scott`.

The complements of the upper closures of finite sets intersected with Scott open sets form

explanatories.Topology.scott: The Scott topology on a partially ordered set is constructed as the join of the topology of upper sets and the Scott-Hausdorff topology.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

explanatories.upperClosure: The upper closure of a set is the smallest upper set that contains it.

Topology.IsLawson.lawsonBasis.fullDefinition: def lawsonBasis := { s : Set α | ∃ t : Set α, t.Finite ∧ ∃ u : Set α, IsOpen[scott α] u ∧       u \ upperClosure t = s }

TopCat.limitCone.fullDefinition: def limitCone (F : J ⥤ TopCat.{max v u}) : Cone F where   pt := TopCat.of { u : ∀ j : J, F.obj j | ∀ {i j : J} (f : i ⟶ j), F.map f (u i) = u j }   π :=     { app := fun j =>         { toFun := fun u => u.val j           -- Porting note: `continuity` from the original mathlib3 proof failed here.           continuous_toFun := Continuous.comp (continuous_apply _) (continuous_subtype_val) }       naturality := fun X Y f => by         -- Automation fails in various ways in this proof. Why?!         dsimp         rw [Category.id_comp]         apply ContinuousMap.ext         intro a         exact (a.2 f).symm }

explanatories.CategoryTheory.forget: This definition describes a forgetful functor that maps objects from a concrete category to their underlying types in a specific universe.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.ofFaithful: This definition asserts that if a faithful functor maps a cone to a limit cone, then it is sufficient to verify that the induced morphisms for the images of the cones can be lifted to morphisms in the original category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapCone: This definition describes how to obtain a new cone in one category from an existing cone in another category by applying a functor that maps between the two categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.sections: This definition characterizes the sections of a functor as selections of points from the functor's objects that are consistent with the functor's mapping on morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.forget_map_eq_coe: The theorem states that the action of a forgetful functor on a morphism in a concrete category is equivalent to the coercion of that morphism to its underlying type.
explanatories.continuous_iff_coinduced_le: This theorem states that a function between two topological spaces is continuous if and only if the topology induced on the codomain by the function is less than or equal to the original topology on the codomain.
explanatories.le_iInf: This theorem demonstrates that if an element is less than or equal to all elements produced by a function mapping from an index set, then it is also less than or equal to the infimum of those function values in a complete lattice.
explanatories.coinduced_le_iff_le_induced: This theorem establishes a relationship between the coinduced topology and the induced topology, indicating that the coinduced topology is less than or equal to a given topology if and only if the original topology is less than or equal to the induced topology.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.continuous: This theorem states that a continuous map between two topological spaces induces a continuous function when viewed as a function.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.ofFaithf: This definition states that if a faithful functor transforms a specific cocone into a colimit cocone, then it is sufficient to demonstrate that the corresponding induced mappings from the cocone can be extended to morphisms within the original category.

TopCat.limitConeInfiIsLimit.fullDefinition: def limitConeInfiIsLimit (F : J ⥤ TopCat.{max v u}) : IsLimit (limitConeInfi.{v,u} F) := by   refine IsLimit.ofFaithful forget (Types.limitConeIsLimit.{v,u} (F ⋙ forget))     -- Porting note: previously could infer all ?_ except continuity     (fun s => ⟨fun v => ⟨fun j => (Functor.mapCone forget s).π.app j v, ?_⟩, ?_⟩) fun s => ?_   · dsimp [Functor.sections]     intro _ _ _     rw [← comp_apply', forget_map_eq_coe, ← s.π.naturality, forget_map_eq_coe]     dsimp     rw [Category.id_comp]   · exact     continuous_iff_coinduced_le.mpr       (le_iInf fun j =>         coinduced_le_iff_le_induced.mp <|           (continuous_iff_coinduced_le.mp (s.π.app j).continuous : _))   · rfl

TopCat.pullbackConeIsLimit.fullDefinition: def pullbackConeIsLimit (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : IsLimit (pullbackCone f g) :=   PullbackCone.isLimitAux' _     (by       intro S       constructor; swap       · exact           { toFun := fun x =>               ⟨⟨S.fst x, S.snd x⟩, by simpa using ConcreteCategory.congr_hom S.condition x⟩             continuous_toFun := by               apply Continuous.subtype_mk <| Continuous.prod_mk ?_ ?_               · exact (PullbackCone.fst S)|>.continuous_toFun               · exact (PullbackCone.snd S)|>.continuous_toFun           }       refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩       · delta pullbackCone         ext a         -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644         erw [comp_apply, ContinuousMap.coe_mk]       · delta pullbackCone         ext a         -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644         erw [comp_apply, ContinuousMap.coe_mk]       · intro m h₁ h₂         -- Porting note (#11041): used to be `ext x`.         apply ContinuousMap.ext; intro x         apply Subtype.ext         apply Prod.ext         · simpa using ConcreteCategory.congr_hom h₁ x         · simpa using ConcreteCategory.congr_hom h₂ x)

Top.pullback_cone_is_limit.description: This definition states that the pullback cone formed from two morphisms in a category is a limit cone, indicating it satisfies the universal property of limits.

  (i₂ : X ⟶ Z) (i₃ : S ⟶ T) [H₃ : Mono i₃] (eq₁ : f₁ ≫ i₃ = i₁ ≫ g₁) (eq₂ : f₂ ≫ i₃ = i₂ ≫ g₂) :
  Set.range ⇑(pullback.map f₁ f₂ g₁ g₂ i₁ i₂ i₃ eq₁ eq₂) =
    ⇑(pullback.fst g₁ g₂) ⁻¹' Set.range ⇑i₁ ∩ ⇑(pullback.snd g₁ g₂) ⁻¹' Set.range ⇑i₂

  (g₂ : Z ⟶ T) {i₁ : W ⟶ Y} {i₂ : X ⟶ Z} (H₁ : Embedding ⇑i₁) (H₂ : Embedding ⇑i₂) (i₃ : S ⟶ T)
  (eq₁ : f₁ ≫ i₃ = i₁ ≫ g₁) (eq₂ : f₂ ≫ i₃ = i₂ ≫ g₂) : Embedding ⇑(pullback.map f₁ f₂ g₁ g₂ i₁ i₂ i₃ eq₁ eq₂)
TopCat.pullback_map_embedding_of_embeddi.comment:
If there is a diagram where the morphisms `W ⟶ Y` and `X ⟶ Z` are embeddings,
then the induced morphism `W ×ₛ X ⟶ Y ×ₜ Z` is also an embedding.

```
W ⟶ Y
 ↘   ↘
  S ⟶ T
 ↗   ↗
X ⟶ Z
```

TopCat.pullback_map_openEmbedding_of_ope.description: The theorem asserts that if two morphisms are open embeddings and a third morphism is monomorphic, then the induced morphism from the pullback of the first two to the product of the latter two is also an open embedding.

Top.pullback_map_open_embedding_of_open_.code:
TopCat.pullback_map_openEmbedding_of_open_embeddings.{u} {W X Y Z S T : TopCat} (f₁ : W ⟶ S) (f₂ : X ⟶ S) (g₁ : Y ⟶ T)
  (g₂ : Z ⟶ T) {i₁ : W ⟶ Y} {i₂ : X ⟶ Z} (H₁ : OpenEmbedding ⇑i₁) (H₂ : OpenEmbedding ⇑i₂) (i₃ : S ⟶ T) [H₃ : Mono i₃]
  (eq₁ : f₁ ≫ i₃ = i₁ ≫ g₁) (eq₂ : f₂ ≫ i₃ = i₂ ≫ g₂) : OpenEmbedding ⇑(pullback.map f₁ f₂ g₁ g₂ i₁ i₂ i₃ eq₁ eq₂)
Top.pullback_map_open_embedding_of_open_.comment:
If there is a diagram where the morphisms `W ⟶ Y` and `X ⟶ Z` are open embeddings, and `S ⟶ T`
is mono, then the induced morphism `W ×ₛ X ⟶ Y ×ₜ Z` is also an open embedding.

```
W ⟶ Y
 ↘   ↘
  S ⟶ T
 ↗   ↗
X ⟶ Z
```

TopCat.effectiveEpiStructOfQuotientMap.fullDefinition: def effectiveEpiStructOfQuotientMap {B X : TopCat.{u}} (π : X ⟶ B) (hπ : QuotientMap π) :     EffectiveEpiStruct π where   /- `QuotientMap.lift` gives the required morphism -/   desc e h := hπ.lift e fun a b hab ↦     DFunLike.congr_fun (h ⟨fun _ ↦ a, continuous_const⟩ ⟨fun _ ↦ b, continuous_const⟩     (by ext; exact hab)) a   /- `QuotientMap.lift_comp` gives the factorisation -/   fac e h := (hπ.lift_comp e     fun a b hab ↦ DFunLike.congr_fun (h ⟨fun _ ↦ a, continuous_const⟩ ⟨fun _ ↦ b, continuous_const⟩     (by ext; exact hab)) a)   /- Uniqueness follows from the fact that `QuotientMap.lift` is an equivalence (given by   `QuotientMap.liftEquiv`). -/   uniq e h g hm := by     suffices g = hπ.liftEquiv ⟨e,       fun a b hab ↦ DFunLike.congr_fun         (h ⟨fun _ ↦ a, continuous_const⟩ ⟨fun _ ↦ b, continuous_const⟩ (by ext; exact hab))         a⟩ by assumption     rw [← Equiv.symm_apply_eq hπ.liftEquiv]     ext     simp only [QuotientMap.liftEquiv_symm_apply_coe, ContinuousMap.comp_apply, ← hm]     rfl
TopCat.effectiveEpiStructOfQuotientMap.description: This definition establishes that a morphism in the category of topological spaces that is a quotient map is an effective epimorphism.

CompHaus.limitCone.fullDefinition: def limitCone {J : Type v} [SmallCategory J] (F : J ⥤ CompHaus.{max v u}) : Limits.Cone F :=   letI FF : J ⥤ TopCat := F ⋙ compHausToTop   { pt := {       toTop := (TopCat.limitCone FF).pt       is_compact := by         show CompactSpace { u : ∀ j, F.obj j | ∀ {i j : J} (f : i ⟶ j), (F.map f) (u i) = u j }         rw [← isCompact_iff_compactSpace]         apply IsClosed.isCompact         have :           { u : ∀ j, F.obj j | ∀ {i j : J} (f : i ⟶ j), F.map f (u i) = u j } =             ⋂ (i : J) (j : J) (f : i ⟶ j), { u | F.map f (u i) = u j } := by           ext1           simp only [Set.mem_iInter, Set.mem_setOf_eq]         rw [this]         apply isClosed_iInter         intro i         apply isClosed_iInter         intro j         apply isClosed_iInter         intro f         apply isClosed_eq         · exact (ContinuousMap.continuous (F.map f)).comp (continuous_apply i)         · exact continuous_apply j       is_hausdorff :=         show T2Space { u : ∀ j, F.obj j | ∀ {i j : J} (f : i ⟶ j), (F.map f) (u i) = u j } from           inferInstance }     π := {       app := fun j => (TopCat.limitCone FF).π.app j       naturality := by         intro _ _ f         ext ⟨x, hx⟩         simp only [comp_apply, Functor.const_obj_map, id_apply]         exact (hx f).symm } } set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

CompHaus.projective_ultrafilter.fullDefinition: instance projective_ultrafilter (X : Type*) : Projective (of <| Ultrafilter X) where   factors {Y Z} f g hg := by     rw [epi_iff_surjective] at hg     obtain ⟨g', hg'⟩ := hg.hasRightInverse     let t : X → Y := g' ∘ f ∘ (pure : X → Ultrafilter X)     let h : Ultrafilter X → Y := Ultrafilter.extend t     have hh : Continuous h := continuous_ultrafilter_extend _     use ⟨h, hh⟩     apply (forget CompHaus).map_injective     simp only [Functor.map_comp, ContinuousMap.coe_mk, coe_comp]     convert denseRange_pure.equalizer (g.continuous.comp hh) f.continuous _     -- Porting note: We need to get the coercions to functions under control.     -- The next two lines should not be needed.     let g'' : ContinuousMap Y Z := g     have : g'' ∘ g' = id := hg'.comp_eq_id     -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644     erw [comp.assoc, ultrafilter_extend_extends, ← comp.assoc, this, id_comp] set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

Profinite.projective_ultrafilter.fullDefinition: instance projective_ultrafilter (X : Type u) : Projective (of <| Ultrafilter X) where   factors {Y Z} f g hg := by     rw [epi_iff_surjective] at hg     obtain ⟨g', hg'⟩ := hg.hasRightInverse     let t : X → Y := g' ∘ f ∘ (pure : X → Ultrafilter X)     let h : Ultrafilter X → Y := Ultrafilter.extend t     have hh : Continuous h := continuous_ultrafilter_extend _     use ⟨h, hh⟩     apply (forget Profinite).map_injective     simp only [h, ContinuousMap.coe_mk, coe_comp]     convert denseRange_pure.equalizer (g.continuous.comp hh) f.continuous _      -- Porting note: same fix as in `Topology.Category.CompHaus.Projective`     let g'' : ContinuousMap Y Z := g     have : g'' ∘ g' = id := hg'.comp_eq_id     -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644     erw [comp.assoc, ultrafilter_extend_extends, ← comp.assoc, this, id_comp]

Profinite.NobelingProof.Products.code: Profinite.NobelingProof.Products.{u_1} (I : Type u_1) [LinearOrder I] : Type u_1
Profinite.NobelingProof.Products.comment:
`Products I` is the type of lists of decreasing elements of `I`, so a typical element is
`[i₁, i₂, ...]` with `i₁ > i₂ > ...`. We order `Products I` lexicographically, so `[] < [i₁, ...]`,
and `[i₁, i₂, ...] < [j₁, j₂, ...]` if either `i₁ < j₁`, or `i₁ = j₁` and `[i₂, ...] < [j₂, ...]`.

Terms `m = [i₁, i₂, ..., iᵣ]` of this type will be used to represent products of the form
`e C i₁ ··· e C iᵣ : LocallyConstant C ℤ` . The function associated to `m` is `m.eval`.
Profinite.NobelingProof.Products.fullDefinition: def Products (I : Type*) [LinearOrder I] := {l : List I // l.Chain' (·>·)}
Profinite.NobelingProof.Products.description: This definition denotes a type for lists of elements arranged in decreasing order, equipped with a lexicographical ordering.

Profinite.NobelingProof.Products.lt_iff_.description: This theorem relates the ordering of two lists of decreasing elements to a lexicographical comparison of their entries.

Profinite.NobelingProof.GoodProducts.Sum.comment:
Let

`N := LocallyConstant (π C (ord I · < o)) ℤ`

`M := LocallyConstant C ℤ`

`P := LocallyConstant (C' C ho) ℤ`

`ι := GoodProducts (π C (ord I · < o))`

`ι' := GoodProducts (C' C ho')`

`v : ι → N := GoodProducts.eval (π C (ord I · < o))`

Then `SumEval C ho` is the map `u` in the diagram below. It is linearly independent if and only if
`GoodProducts.eval C` is, see `linearIndependent_iff_sum`. The top row is the exact sequence given
by `succ_exact` and `succ_mono`. The left square commutes by `GoodProducts.square_commutes`.
```
0 --→ N --→ M --→  P
      ↑     ↑      ↑
     v|    u|      |
      ι → ι ⊕ ι' ← ι'
```

CompHaus.presentation.fullDefinition: def presentation (X : CompHaus) : Stonean where   compHaus := (projectivePresentation X).p   extrDisc := by     refine CompactT2.Projective.extremallyDisconnected       (@fun Y Z _ _ _ _ _ _ f g hfcont hgcont hgsurj => ?_)     let g₁ : (CompHaus.of Y) ⟶ (CompHaus.of Z) := ⟨g, hgcont⟩     let f₁ : (projectivePresentation X).p ⟶ (CompHaus.of Z) := ⟨f, hfcont⟩     have hg₁ : Epi g₁ := (epi_iff_surjective _).2 hgsurj     refine ⟨Projective.factorThru f₁ g₁, (Projective.factorThru f₁ g₁).2, funext (fun _ => ?_)⟩     change (Projective.factorThru f₁ g₁ ≫ g₁) _ = f _     rw [Projective.factorThru_comp]     rfl

CompHaus.lift.code: CompHaus.lift.{u_1} {X Y : CompHaus} {Z : Stonean} (e : Z.compHaus ⟶ Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) [Epi f] : Z.compHaus ⟶ X
CompHaus.lift.comment:
```
               X
               |
              (f)
               |
               \/
  Z ---(e)---> Y
```
If `Z` is a Stonean space, `f : X ⟶ Y` an epi in `CompHaus` and `e : Z ⟶ Y` is arbitrary, then
`lift e f` is a fixed (but arbitrary) lift of `e` to a morphism `Z ⟶ X`. It exists because
`Z` is a projective object in `CompHaus`.

Stonean.instProjectiveCompHausCompHaus.fullDefinition: instance instProjectiveCompHausCompHaus (X : Stonean) : Projective X.compHaus where   factors := by     intro B C φ f _     haveI : ExtremallyDisconnected X.compHaus.toTop := X.extrDisc     have hf : Function.Surjective f := by rwa [← CompHaus.epi_iff_surjective]     obtain ⟨f', h⟩ := CompactT2.ExtremallyDisconnected.projective φ.continuous f.continuous hf     use ⟨f', h.left⟩     ext     exact congr_fun h.right _

Stonean.pullback.fullDefinition: def pullback : Stonean where   compHaus := {     toTop := TopCat.of (f ⁻¹' (Set.range i))     is_compact := by       dsimp [TopCat.of]       rw [← isCompact_iff_compactSpace]       refine IsClosed.isCompact (IsClosed.preimage f.continuous (IsCompact.isClosed ?_))       simp only [← Set.image_univ]       exact IsCompact.image isCompact_univ i.continuous     is_hausdorff := by       dsimp [TopCat.of]       exact inferInstance }   extrDisc := by     constructor     intro U hU     dsimp at U     have h : IsClopen (f ⁻¹' (Set.range i)) := by       constructor       · refine IsClosed.preimage f.continuous ?_         apply IsCompact.isClosed         simp only [← Set.image_univ]         exact IsCompact.image isCompact_univ i.continuous       · exact IsOpen.preimage f.continuous hi.isOpen_range     have hU' : IsOpen (Subtype.val '' U) := h.2.openEmbedding_subtype_val.isOpenMap U hU     have := ExtremallyDisconnected.open_closure _ hU'     rw [h.1.closedEmbedding_subtype_val.closure_image_eq U] at this     suffices hhU : closure U = Subtype.val ⁻¹' (Subtype.val '' (closure U)) by       rw [hhU]       exact isOpen_induced this     exact ((closure U).preimage_image_eq Subtype.coe_injective).symm

Stonean.struct.fullDefinition: def struct {B X : Stonean.{u}} (π : X ⟶ B) (hπ : Function.Surjective π) : EffectiveEpiStruct π where   desc e h := (QuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous hπ π.continuous).lift e fun a b hab ↦     DFunLike.congr_fun (h ⟨fun _ ↦ a, continuous_const⟩ ⟨fun _ ↦ b, continuous_const⟩     (by ext; exact hab)) a   fac e h := ((QuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous hπ π.continuous).lift_comp e     fun a b hab ↦ DFunLike.congr_fun (h ⟨fun _ ↦ a, continuous_const⟩ ⟨fun _ ↦ b, continuous_const⟩     (by ext; exact hab)) a)   uniq e h g hm := by     suffices g = (QuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous hπ π.continuous).liftEquiv ⟨e,       fun a b hab ↦ DFunLike.congr_fun         (h ⟨fun _ ↦ a, continuous_const⟩ ⟨fun _ ↦ b, continuous_const⟩ (by ext; exact hab))         a⟩ by assumption     rw [← Equiv.symm_apply_eq (QuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous hπ π.continuous).liftEquiv]     ext     simp only [QuotientMap.liftEquiv_symm_apply_coe, ContinuousMap.comp_apply, ← hm]     rfl

LightProfinite.EffectiveEpi.struct.comment:
Implementation: if `π` is a surjective morphism in `LightProfinite`, then it is an effective epi.
The theorem `LightProfinite.effectiveEpi_iff_surjective` should be used instead.

explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.
explanatories.QuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous: This theorem states that a continuous surjective map from a compact space to a Hausdorff space qualifies as a quotient map.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.continuous: This theorem states that a continuous map between two topological spaces induces a continuous function when viewed as a function.
explanatories.QuotientMap.lift: This definition describes a method to create a continuous map from one topological space to another by descending along a quotient map, ensuring the map is constant on the fibers of the quotient.
explanatories.DFunLike.congr_fun: There is no theorem stated in this input.
explanatories.continuous_const: The constant function from one topological space to another is continuous.
explanatories.Equiv.symm_apply_eq: This theorem states that the inverse of an equivalence maps an element back to the original if and only if applying the equivalence to that element results in the same element.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.comp_apply: This theorem establishes that the application of the composition of two continuous maps at a given point equals the application of the first continuous map to the result of the second continuous map at that point.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.

LightProfinite.EffectiveEpi.struct.fullDefinition: def EffectiveEpi.struct {B X : LightProfinite.{u}} (π : X ⟶ B) (hπ : Function.Surjective π) :     EffectiveEpiStruct π where   desc e h := (QuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous hπ π.continuous).lift e fun a b hab ↦     DFunLike.congr_fun (h ⟨fun _ ↦ a, continuous_const⟩ ⟨fun _ ↦ b, continuous_const⟩     (by ext; exact hab)) a   fac e h := ((QuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous hπ π.continuous).lift_comp e     fun a b hab ↦ DFunLike.congr_fun (h ⟨fun _ ↦ a, continuous_const⟩ ⟨fun _ ↦ b, continuous_const⟩     (by ext; exact hab)) a)   uniq e h g hm := by     suffices g = (QuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous hπ π.continuous).liftEquiv ⟨e,       fun a b hab ↦         DFunLike.congr_fun (h ⟨fun _ ↦ a, continuous_const⟩ ⟨fun _ ↦ b, continuous_const⟩         (by ext; exact hab)) a⟩ by assumption     rw [← Equiv.symm_apply_eq (QuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous hπ π.continuous).liftEquiv]     ext     simp only [QuotientMap.liftEquiv_symm_apply_coe, ContinuousMap.comp_apply, ← hm]     rfl

TopologicalSpace.ofClosed.fullDefinition: def TopologicalSpace.ofClosed {X : Type u} (T : Set (Set X)) (empty_mem : ∅ ∈ T)     (sInter_mem : ∀ A, A ⊆ T → ⋂₀ A ∈ T)     (union_mem : ∀ A, A ∈ T → ∀ B, B ∈ T → A ∪ B ∈ T) : TopologicalSpace X where   IsOpen X := Xᶜ ∈ T   isOpen_univ := by simp [empty_mem]   isOpen_inter s t hs ht := by simpa only [compl_inter] using union_mem sᶜ hs tᶜ ht   isOpen_sUnion s hs := by     simp only [Set.compl_sUnion]     exact sInter_mem (compl '' s) fun z ⟨y, hy, hz⟩ => hz ▸ hs y hy

If a filter `f` is majorated by some `𝓝 x`, then it is majorated by `𝓝 (Filter.lim f)`. We
formulate this lemma with a `[Nonempty X]` argument of `lim` derived from `h` to make it useful for

this instance with any other instance.

explanatories.interior.eq_1: The interior of a set is the union of all open sets contained within that set.
explanatories.closure.eq_1: The closure of a set in a topological space is equal to the intersection of all closed sets that contain that set.
explanatories.Dense.eq_1: A set is dense in a topological space if and only if every point in the space belongs to the closure of that set.
explanatories.frontier.eq_1: The frontier of a set in a topological space is defined as the difference between its closure and its interior.
explanatories.ClusterPt.eq_1: A point is a cluster point of a filter in a topological space if and only if the intersection of the neighborhood of that point and the filter is nonempty.
explanatories.AccPt.eq_1: A point is an accumulation point of a filter in a topological space if and only if the intersection of the filter with the neighborhood around that point, excluding the point itself, is non-empty.
explanatories.nhdsWithin.eq_1: The neighborhood of a point within a set is equal to the intersection of the neighborhood of that point with the principal filter generated by the set.
explanatories.Filter.Frequently.eq_1: A property is frequently true with respect to a filter if and only if there is not a point in the filter where it fails to hold for all elements.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.eq_1: A filter eventually satisfies a property if and only if the set of points satisfying that property is included in the filter.
explanatories.Filter.EventuallyEq.eq_1: Two functions are considered equal with respect to a filter if they are equal for all inputs that eventually belong to that filter.

DenseRange.eq_1.description: The dense range of a function is equal to the property of density applied to its range.

explanatories.Rel: This defines a relation between two types as a set-valued function or partial multifunction.
explanatories.Filter.RTendsto: A relation between two types tends to a limit if every neighborhood of the limit is related to a neighborhood in the domain through the core of that neighborhood under the relation.
explanatories.Rel.core: This definition describes the core of a set with respect to a relation, which includes the elements that are exclusively related to the elements of that set.

rtendsto_nhds.description: This theorem establishes an equivalence between the convergence of a relation with respect to a filter and the condition that, for every open set containing a point, the core of that set is also included in the filter.

explanatories.PFun.preimage: This definition describes the preimage of a set under a partial function as the set of all inputs that map to elements within the specified set under the function.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

rtendsto'_nhds.description: This theorem characterizes the convergence of a relation with respect to a filter as being equivalent to the condition that, for every open set containing a point, the preimage of that set under the relation is also included in the filter.

  {motive : (a : Set α) → GenerateOpen g a → Prop} :
  ∀ {a : Set α} (t : GenerateOpen g a),
    (∀ (s : Set α) (a : s ∈ g), motive s ⋯) →

explanatories.DiscreteTopology.eq_bot: This theorem asserts that the topological structure on any type equipped with discrete topology is equivalent to the trivial topology.
explanatories.Embedding.discreteTopology: The topology induced on a space by an embedding from a discrete space is also discrete.

Sum.discreteTopology.fullDefinition: instance Sum.discreteTopology [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] [h : DiscreteTopology X]     [hY : DiscreteTopology Y] : DiscreteTopology (X ⊕ Y) :=   ⟨sup_eq_bot_iff.2 <| by simp [h.eq_bot, hY.eq_bot]⟩
Sum.discreteTopology.description: This definition establishes that the sum of two topological spaces, each with a discrete topology, also has a discrete topology.

induced_to_pi.description: This theorem shows that the topology induced by a function mapping to a product space is equivalent to the infimum of the topologies induced by the projections of that function.

inducing_iInf_to_pi.code:
inducing_iInf_to_pi.{u_5, u_6, u_8} {ι : Type u_5} {π : ι → Type u_6} [T : (i : ι) → TopologicalSpace (π i)]
  {X : Type u_8} (f : (i : ι) → X → π i) : Inducing fun x i => f i x
inducing_iInf_to_pi.comment:
Suppose `π i` is a family of topological spaces indexed by `i : ι`, and `X` is a type
endowed with a family of maps `f i : X → π i` for every `i : ι`, hence inducing a
map `g : X → Π i, π i`. This lemma shows that infimum of the topologies on `X` induced by
the `f i` as `i : ι` varies is simply the topology on `X` induced by `g : X → Π i, π i`
where `Π i, π i` is endowed with the usual product topology.
inducing_iInf_to_pi.description: This theorem establishes that the coarsest topology on a space, induced by a family of maps to a collection of topological spaces, coincides with the topology induced by the corresponding product space endowed with the usual product topology.

Pi.discreteTopology.comment: A finite product of discrete spaces is discrete.

explanatories.isOpen_discrete: This theorem states that every subset of a topological space with a discrete topology is open.
explanatories.Sum.discreteTopology: This definition establishes that the sum of two topological spaces, each with a discrete topology, also has a discrete topology.
explanatories.Sigma.discreteTopology: This defines a discrete topological structure on the sigma type formed from a family of discrete topological spaces, allowing each component to be treated independently.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Embedding.discreteTopology: The topology induced on a space by an embedding from a discrete space is also discrete.
explanatories.isOpen_set_pi: This theorem states that the product of a finite collection of open sets, indexed by a finite set, is itself an open set in the product topology of the respective spaces.
explanatories.singletons_open_iff_discrete: This theorem states that a topological space is discrete if and only if every singleton set is open.
explanatories.Set.univ_pi_singleton: The theorem states that the product of the universal set with respect to any function that maps indices to single-element sets is equal to that single-element set itself.
explanatories.Set.finite_univ: The universal set is finite if its elements belong to a finite type.

Pi.discreteTopology.fullDefinition: instance Pi.discreteTopology : DiscreteTopology (∀ i, π i) :=   singletons_open_iff_discrete.mp fun x => by     rw [← univ_pi_singleton]     exact isOpen_set_pi finite_univ fun i _ => (isOpen_discrete {x i})
Pi.discreteTopology.description: This definition asserts that the function space formed by a finite product of discrete topological spaces is itself endowed with the discrete topology.

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.
explanatories.Sigma.map: This defines a mapping for the components in a dependent pair structure.

open_embedding_sigma_map.description: This theorem states that the sigma map composed from two functions is an open embedding if and only if each component mapping is also an open embedding, under the condition that the first function is injective.

explanatories.TopologicalSpace.induced: The induced topology on a space is defined as the collection of sets that are the preimages of open sets in another space, ensuring that a given function remains continuous.

explanatories.ULift.down: This function retrieves the original value from a lifted container that holds a value of a specified type.
explanatories.nhdsWithin.eq_1: The neighborhood of a point within a set is equal to the intersection of the neighborhood of that point with the principal filter generated by the set.
explanatories.Filter.prod.eq_1: The product of two filters is equal to the intersection of the filters obtained by applying the first and second projections to the respective filters.
explanatories.instTopologicalSpaceProd.eq_1: This theorem establishes that the topological structure on the product of two spaces is equivalent to the intersection of the topologies induced by the projections onto each component.
explanatories.IsClopen.eq_1: This theorem demonstrates that a set in a topological space is clopen if and only if it is both closed and open simultaneously.

ULift.topologicalSpace.eq_1.description: This theorem demonstrates that the topology on a type derived from lifting is equivalent to the topology induced by a specific function that maps down to the original type.

explanatories.Inducing.isOpen_iff: A set in the domain is open if and only if there exists an open set in the codomain that is the image of that set under a function known to be an inducing map.

ULift.isOpen_iff.description: This theorem states that a subset of a type equipped with a topology is open if and only if its preimage under the upward lifting function is open in the base space.

LocallyFinite.exists_forall_eventually_e.comment:
Let `f : ℕ → Π a, β a` be a sequence of (dependent) functions on a topological space. Suppose
that the family of sets `s n = {x | f (n + 1) x ≠ f n x}` is locally finite. Then there exists a
function `F : Π a, β a` such that for any `x`, we have `f n x = F x` on the product of an infinite
interval `[N, +∞)` and a neighbourhood of `x`.

We formulate the conclusion in terms of the product of filter `Filter.atTop` and `𝓝 x`.

explanatories.Filter.atTop: This definition introduces a filter that captures the behavior of elements approaching infinity in an ordered set, generated by all sets containing elements greater than or equal to any given element.

LocallyFinite.exists_forall_eventually_e.description: If a family of sets associated with a sequence of functions in a topological space is locally finite, then there exists a function that equals the sequence on large intervals and near any point in the space.

TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.code: TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.{u} {α : Type u} [t : TopologicalSpace α] (s : Set α) : Prop
TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.comment:
A set `s` in a topological space is separable if it is contained in the closure of a countable
set `c`. Beware that this definition does not require that `c` is contained in `s` (to express the
latter, use `TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace s` or
`TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable (univ : Set s))`. In metric spaces, the two definitions are
equivalent, see `TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.separableSpace`.

TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable.comment:
In a second-countable space, an open set, given as a union of open sets,
is equal to the union of countably many of those sets.
In particular, any open covering of `α` has a countable subcover: α is a Lindelöf space.

connectedComponentIn.code: connectedComponentIn.{u} {α : Type u} [TopologicalSpace α] (F : Set α) (x : α) : Set α
connectedComponentIn.comment:
Given a set `F` in a topological space `α` and a point `x : α`, the connected
component of `x` in `F` is the connected component of `x` in the subtype `F` seen as
a set in `α`. This definition does not make sense if `x` is not in `F` so we return the
empty set in this case.

connectedComponentIn.description: This definition describes the connected component of a point within a given set in a topological space, returning the empty set if the point is not in the set.

PreconnectedSpace.induction₂'.code:
PreconnectedSpace.induction₂'.{u} {α : Type u} [TopologicalSpace α] [PreconnectedSpace α] (P : α → α → Prop)
  (h : ∀ (x : α), ∀ᶠ (y : α) in 𝓝 x, P x y ∧ P y x) (h' : Transitive P) (x y : α) : P x y
PreconnectedSpace.induction₂'.comment:
In a preconnected space, given a transitive relation `P`, if `P x y` and `P y x` are true
for `y` close enough to `x`, then `P x y` holds for all `x, y`. This is a version of the fact
that, if an equivalence relation has open classes, then it has a single equivalence class.

explanatories.Transitive: This defines a relation as transitive if the truth of one relationship implying another guarantees that the first relates to the third.

PreconnectedSpace.induction₂'.description: This theorem states that in a preconnected space, a transitive relation holds between any two points if it holds for points that are sufficiently close to one of them.

explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.

IsCompact.mem_nhdsSet_prod_of_forall.comment:
If `s : Set (X × Y)` belongs to `𝓝 x ×ˢ l` for all `x` from a compact set `K`,
then it belongs to `(𝓝ˢ K) ×ˢ l`,

IsCompact.mem_nhdsSet_prod_of_forall.description: If a set in the product space belongs to the neighborhood of each point from a compact set, then it belongs to the neighborhood of the entire compact set in the product space with another filter.

IsCompact.nhdsSet_prod_eq_biSup.description: The neighborhood of the product of a compact set and a filter is equal to the supremum of the neighborhoods of each point in the compact set, multiplied by the filter.

IsCompact.eventually_forall_of_forall_ev.comment:
To show that `∀ y ∈ K, P x y` holds for `x` close enough to `x₀` when `K` is compact,
it is sufficient to show that for all `y₀ ∈ K` there `P x y` holds for `(x, y)` close enough
to `(x₀, y₀)`.

Provided for backwards compatibility,
see `IsCompact.mem_prod_nhdsSet_of_forall` for a stronger statement.

IsCompact.nhdsSet_prod_eq.comment:
If `s` and `t` are compact sets, then the set neighborhoods filter of `s ×ˢ t`
is the product of set neighborhoods filters for `s` and `t`.

For general sets, only the `≤` inequality holds, see `nhdsSet_prod_le`.
IsCompact.nhdsSet_prod_eq.description: The neighborhood of the product of two compact sets is equal to the product of their individual neighborhoods.

generalized_tube_lemma.comment:
If `s` and `t` are compact sets and `n` is an open neighborhood of `s × t`, then there exist
open neighborhoods `u ⊇ s` and `v ⊇ t` such that `u × v ⊆ n`.

See also `IsCompact.nhdsSet_prod_eq`.

equal to the cocompact filter on `X`.

pi.locally_compact_space.fullDefinition: instance Pi.locallyCompactSpace [∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)] : LocallyCompactSpace (∀ i, X i) :=   ⟨fun t n hn => by     rw [nhds_pi, Filter.mem_pi] at hn     obtain ⟨s, hs, n', hn', hsub⟩ := hn     choose n'' hn'' hsub' hc using fun i =>       LocallyCompactSpace.local_compact_nhds (t i) (n' i) (hn' i)     refine ⟨s.pi n'', ?_, subset_trans (fun _ => ?_) hsub, ?_⟩     · exact (set_pi_mem_nhds_iff hs _).mpr fun i _ => hn'' i     · exact forall₂_imp fun i _ hi' => hsub' i hi'     · rw [← Set.univ_pi_ite]       refine isCompact_univ_pi fun i => ?_       by_cases h : i ∈ s       · rw [if_pos h]         exact hc i       · rw [if_neg h]         exact CompactSpace.isCompact_univ⟩

  (hU : IsOpen U) (hx : x ∈ U) : ∃ K, IsCompact K ∧ x ∈ interior K ∧ K ⊆ U
exists_compact_subset.comment:
A reformulation of the definition of locally compact space: In a locally compact space,
every open set containing `x` has a compact subset containing `x` in its interior.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.IsCompact: This defines the property of a set within a topological space being compact, which requires that for any nontrivial filter containing the set, there is an element within the set such that every set in the filter intersects with every neighborhood of that element.

exists_compact_subset.description: In a locally compact space, for every open set containing a point, there exists a compact subset that contains the point within its interior and is contained in the open set.

exists_mem_nhdsSet_isCompact_mapsTo.code:
exists_mem_nhdsSet_isCompact_mapsTo.{u_1, u_2} {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
  [LocallyCompactPair X Y] {f : X → Y} {K : Set X} {U : Set Y} (hf : Continuous f) (hK : IsCompact K) (hU : IsOpen U)
  (hKU : MapsTo f K U) : ∃ L ∈ 𝓝ˢ K, IsCompact L ∧ MapsTo f L U
exists_mem_nhdsSet_isCompact_mapsTo.comment:
If `f : X → Y` is a continuous map in a locally compact pair of topological spaces,
`K : set X` is a compact set, and `U` is an open neighbourhood of `f '' K`,
then there exists a compact neighbourhood `L` of `K` such that `f` maps `L` to `U`.

This is a generalization of `exists_mem_nhds_isCompact_mapsTo`.

explanatories.IsCompact: This defines the property of a set within a topological space being compact, which requires that for any nontrivial filter containing the set, there is an element within the set such that every set in the filter intersects with every neighborhood of that element.
explanatories.Set.MapsTo: A function maps to a set if the image of that set is contained within another specified set.

exists_mem_nhdsSet_isCompact_mapsTo.description: In a locally compact pair of topological spaces, a continuous map from a compact set to an open neighborhood guarantees the existence of a compact neighborhood that maps into that open set.

exists_compact_between.code:
exists_compact_between.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] [LocallyCompactSpace X] {K U : Set X}
  (hK : IsCompact K) (hU : IsOpen U) (h_KU : K ⊆ U) : ∃ L, IsCompact L ∧ K ⊆ interior L ∧ L ⊆ U
exists_compact_between.comment:
In a locally compact space, for every containment `K ⊆ U` of a compact set `K` in an open
set `U`, there is a compact neighborhood `L` such that `K ⊆ L ⊆ U`: equivalently, there is a
compact `L` such that `K ⊆ interior L` and `L ⊆ U`.
See also `exists_compact_closed_between`, in which one guarantees additionally that `L` is closed
if the space is regular.
