CompactExhaustion.choice.comment:
A choice of an
[exhaustion by compact sets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exhaustion_by_compact_sets)
of a weakly locally compact σ-compact space.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.IsCompact: This defines the property of a set within a topological space being compact, which requires that for any nontrivial filter containing the set, there is an element within the set such that every set in the filter intersects with every neighborhood of that element.
explanatories.isCompact_empty: The empty set is compact in any topological space.
explanatories.HasSubset.Subset.trans: A theorem indicating that this is an alternative name for the transitive property of set inclusion.
explanatories.SigmaCompactSpace: In a σ-compact space, the entire space is classified as σ-compact.
explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.
explanatories.Exists.choose: An existential statement guarantees the existence of an element satisfying a property, allowing for the extraction of such an element from the statement.
explanatories.compactCovering: This defines a sequence of sets that provides a monotone choice of compact coverings for a σ-compact space.
explanatories.Classical.choose_spec: Selecting an element that satisfies a property guarantees that this element indeed possesses that property.
explanatories.isCompact_compactCovering: The compact covering of a σ-compact space is itself compact for any non-negative integer.
explanatories.iUnion_compactCovering: The union of the compact coverings for a σ-compact space equals the entire space.
explanatories.Union.union: The union of two elements is defined as the combination of both elements into a single entity.
explanatories.IsCompact.union: The union of two compact sets in a topological space is also compact.
explanatories.Set.univ_subset_iff: A set is a superset of the universal set if and only if it is equal to the universal set itself.
explanatories.Set.Subset.trans: The transitive property of set inclusion states that if one set is included in a second set, and that second set is included in a third set, then the first set is also included in the third set.
explanatories.interior_mono: The interior of a subset is contained within the interior of a superset if the subset is included in the superset.
explanatories.Nat.recOn: This function defines a way to construct a proof or value for a specified type based on an initial case for zero and a rule for how to handle successor cases in the natural numbers.
explanatories.exists_compact_superset: In a weakly locally compact space, every compact set can be contained within the interior of another compact set.
explanatories.Exists.choose_spec: An element chosen from an existence assertion satisfies the property asserted by that existence statement.
explanatories.Set.subset_union_left: Any element of a set is also an element of the union of that set with another set.
explanatories.Set.iUnion_mono': If for every set in one collection there exists a set in another collection such that the first set is a subset of the corresponding second set, then the union of the first collection is a subset of the union of the second collection.
explanatories.Set.subset_union_right: Any set is a subset of the union of itself with another set.

CompactExhaustion.choice.fullDefinition: noncomputable def choice (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace X]     [SigmaCompactSpace X] : CompactExhaustion X := by   apply Classical.choice   let K : ℕ → { s : Set X // IsCompact s } := fun n =>     Nat.recOn n ⟨∅, isCompact_empty⟩ fun n s =>       ⟨(exists_compact_superset s.2).choose ∪ compactCovering X n,         (exists_compact_superset s.2).choose_spec.1.union (isCompact_compactCovering _ _)⟩   refine ⟨⟨fun n ↦ (K n).1, fun n => (K n).2, fun n ↦ ?_, ?_⟩⟩   · exact Subset.trans (exists_compact_superset (K n).2).choose_spec.2       (interior_mono subset_union_left)   · refine univ_subset_iff.1 (iUnion_compactCovering X ▸ ?_)     exact iUnion_mono' fun n => ⟨n + 1, subset_union_right⟩
CompactExhaustion.choice.description: A weakly locally compact σ-compact space admits a choice of an exhaustion by compact sets.

IsLindelof.code: IsLindelof.{u} {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] (s : Set X) : Prop
IsLindelof.comment:
A set `s` is Lindelöf if every nontrivial filter `f` with the countable intersection
property that contains `s`, has a clusterpoint in `s`. The filter-free definition is given by
`isLindelof_iff_countable_subcover`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.ClusterPt: This defines a condition for a point to be a cluster point of a given filter in topology, indicating that the intersection of the filter with the neighborhood of the point is non-empty.

IsLindelof.fullDefinition: def IsLindelof (s : Set X) :=   ∀ ⦃f⦄ [NeBot f] [CountableInterFilter f], f ≤ 𝓟 s → ∃ x ∈ s, ClusterPt x f
IsLindelof.description: A set is Lindelöf if every nontrivial filter containing it and having the countable intersection property also has a cluster point within the set.

IsLindelof.compl_mem_sets.code:
IsLindelof.compl_mem_sets.{u} {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] {s : Set X} (hs : IsLindelof s) {f : Filter X}
  [CountableInterFilter f] (hf : ∀ x ∈ s, sᶜ ∈ 𝓝 x ⊓ f) : sᶜ ∈ f
IsLindelof.compl_mem_sets.comment:
The complement to a Lindelöf set belongs to a filter `f` with the countable intersection
property if it belongs to each filter `𝓝 x ⊓ f`, `x ∈ s`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

IsLindelof.compl_mem_sets.description: The complement of a Lindelöf set is in a filter with the countable intersection property if it is contained in the intersection of that filter with the neighborhoods of each point in the set.

The complement to a Lindelöf set belongs to a filter `f` with the countable intersection

IsLindelof.compl_mem_sets_of_nhdsWithin.description: The complement of a Lindelöf set is in a filter with the countable intersection property if for every point in the set, there exists a neighborhood within the set whose complement is also in the filter.

  (hcountable_union : ∀ (S : Set (Set X)), S.Countable → (∀ s ∈ S, p s) → p (⋃₀ S))
  (hnhds : ∀ x ∈ s, ∃ t ∈ 𝓝[s] x, p t) : p s

of a Lindelöf set `s` has a neighborhood `t` within `s` such that `p t`, then `p s` holds.

refinement_of_locallyCompact_sigmaCompac.code:
refinement_of_locallyCompact_sigmaCompact_of_nhds_basis_set.{u, v} {X : Type v} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace X] [SigmaCompactSpace X] [T2Space X] {ι : X → Type u} {p : (x : X) → ι x → Prop}
  {B : (x : X) → ι x → Set X} {s : Set X} (hs : IsClosed s) (hB : ∀ x ∈ s, (𝓝 x).HasBasis (p x) (B x)) :
  ∃ α c r, (∀ (a : α), c a ∈ s ∧ p (c a) (r a)) ∧ s ⊆ ⋃ a, B (c a) (r a) ∧ LocallyFinite fun a => B (c a) (r a)
refinement_of_locallyCompact_sigmaCompac.comment:
Let `X` be a locally compact sigma compact Hausdorff topological space, let `s` be a closed set
in `X`. Suppose that for each `x ∈ s` the sets `B x : ι x → Set X` with the predicate
`p x : ι x → Prop` form a basis of the filter `𝓝 x`. Then there exists a locally finite covering
`fun i ↦ B (c i) (r i)` of `s` such that all “centers” `c i` belong to `s` and each `r i` satisfies
`p (c i)`.

The notation is inspired by the case `B x r = Metric.ball x r` but the theorem applies to
`nhds_basis_opens` as well. If the covering must be subordinate to some open covering of `s`, then
the user should use a basis obtained by `Filter.HasBasis.restrict_subset` or a similar lemma, see
the proof of `paracompact_of_locallyCompact_sigmaCompact` for an example.

The formalization is based on two [ncatlab](https://ncatlab.org/) proofs:
* [locally compact and sigma compact spaces are paracompact](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/locally+compact+and+sigma-compact+spaces+are+paracompact);
* [open cover of smooth manifold admits locally finite refinement by closed balls](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/partition+of+unity#ExistenceOnSmoothManifolds).

See also `refinement_of_locallyCompact_sigmaCompact_of_nhds_basis` for a version of this lemma
dealing with a covering of the whole space.

In most cases (namely, if `B c r ∪ B c r'` is again a set of the form `B c r''`) it is possible
to choose `α = X`. This fact is not yet formalized in `mathlib`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.ParacompactSpace: Every open cover of a paracompact space admits a locally finite refinement.
explanatories.isOpen_iUnion: The union of a collection of open sets is itself open if each individual set in the collection is open.
explanatories.Set.mem_iUnion: An element belongs to the union of a collection of sets if and only if it is an element of at least one set within that collection.
explanatories.precise_refinement_set: In a paracompact space, every open cover of a closed set has a locally finite refinement that is indexed by the same type.
explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.
explanatories.SetCoe.forall': The universal quantification over elements of a set with membership conditions is equivalent to universal quantification over the coerced version of that set.
explanatories.isClosed_closure: The closure of a set in a topological space is always a closed set.
explanatories.disjoint_compl_right: In a Heyting algebra, an element is disjoint from its complement.
explanatories.Disjoint.mono: If one element in a lattice is disjoint from another, then a smaller element is disjoint from a smaller element, provided their respective order relations hold.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.compl_le_compl: In a Heyting algebra, if one element is less than or equal to another, then the complement of the second is less than or equal to the complement of the first.
explanatories.subset_closure: Every set is contained within its closure in a topological space.
explanatories.LocallyFinite.closure_iUnion: The closure of the union of a locally finite family of sets is equal to the union of the closures of each set in the family.
explanatories.Set.compl_iUnion: The complement of the union of a family of sets is equal to the intersection of the complements of each set in that family.
explanatories.Set.subset_iInter_iff: A set is a subset of the intersection of other sets if and only if it is a subset of each individual set in that intersection.
explanatories.absurd: This establishes a principle that allows one to derive any statement from a proposition and its negation, highlighting the nature of contradictions in logic.
explanatories.closure_minimal: The closure of a subset is contained within a closed set if the subset is included in that closed set.
explanatories.isClosed_compl_iff: A set is closed if and only if its complement is open in a topological space.
explanatories.Disjoint.le_bot: If two elements in a lattice are disjoint, then their infimum is less than or equal to the least element of the lattice.
explanatories.Set.singleton_subset_iff: A singleton set is a subset of another set if and only if its single element is an element of that set.
explanatories.t2_separation: This theorem asserts that in a T2 space, any two distinct points can be separated by disjoint open sets containing each point.
explanatories.Disjoint.symm: If two elements in a lattice are disjoint, then the second element is also disjoint from the first, establishing the symmetry of disjointness.
explanatories.Disjoint.ne_of_mem: If two sets are disjoint, then any element from one set differs from any element in the other set.

T4Space.of_paracompactSpace_t2Space.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) T4Space.of_paracompactSpace_t2Space [T2Space X] [ParacompactSpace X] :     T4Space X := by   -- First we show how to go from points to a set on one side.   have : ∀ s t : Set X, IsClosed s →       (∀ x ∈ s, ∃ u v, IsOpen u ∧ IsOpen v ∧ x ∈ u ∧ t ⊆ v ∧ Disjoint u v) →       ∃ u v, IsOpen u ∧ IsOpen v ∧ s ⊆ u ∧ t ⊆ v ∧ Disjoint u v := fun s t hs H ↦ by     /- For each `x ∈ s` we choose open disjoint `u x ∋ x` and `v x ⊇ t`. The sets `u x` form an         open covering of `s`. We choose a locally finite refinement `u' : s → Set X`, then         `⋃ i, u' i` and `(closure (⋃ i, u' i))ᶜ` are disjoint open neighborhoods of `s` and `t`. -/     choose u v hu hv hxu htv huv using SetCoe.forall'.1 H     rcases precise_refinement_set hs u hu fun x hx ↦ mem_iUnion.2 ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, hxu _⟩ with       ⟨u', hu'o, hcov', hu'fin, hsub⟩     refine ⟨⋃ i, u' i, (closure (⋃ i, u' i))ᶜ, isOpen_iUnion hu'o, isClosed_closure.isOpen_compl,       hcov', ?_, disjoint_compl_right.mono le_rfl (compl_le_compl subset_closure)⟩     rw [hu'fin.closure_iUnion, compl_iUnion, subset_iInter_iff]     refine fun i x hxt hxu ↦       absurd (htv i hxt) (closure_minimal ?_ (isClosed_compl_iff.2 <| hv _) hxu)     exact fun y hyu hyv ↦ (huv i).le_bot ⟨hsub _ hyu, hyv⟩   -- Now we apply the lemma twice: first to `s` and `t`, then to `t` and each point of `s`.   refine { normal := fun s t hs ht hst ↦ this s t hs fun x hx ↦ ?_ }   rcases this t {x} ht fun y hy ↦ (by     simp_rw [singleton_subset_iff]     exact t2_separation (hst.symm.ne_of_mem hy hx))     with ⟨v, u, hv, hu, htv, hxu, huv⟩   exact ⟨u, v, hu, hv, singleton_subset_iff.1 hxu, htv, huv.symm⟩
T4Space.of_paracompactSpace_t2Space.description: A paracompact Hausdorff space is defined to be a normal space.

RestrictGenTopology.isOpen_iff.description: A set is open in a topological space if and only if the preimage of that set under the inclusion map from the subtypes is open for every element of a specified collection of sets.

explanatories.ContinuousOn: This defines a property indicating that a function between topological spaces is continuous at every point of a specified subset.

RestrictGenTopology.of_continuous_prop.description: A collection of sets is a topology if any function that is continuous on every set in the collection is also continuous overall.

RestrictGenTopology.continuous_iff.description: A function from one topological space to another is continuous if and only if it is continuous on every set in a specified collection of sets.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

RestrictGenTopology.enlarge.description: A collection of sets forms a topology if it can be expanded from another topology by ensuring every set in the first collection is contained within a set in the second collection.

RestrictGenTopology.of_isClosed.code:
RestrictGenTopology.of_isClosed.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] {S : Set (Set X)}

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

RestrictGenTopology.of_isClosed.description: A collection of sets forms a topology if any set that is the preimage of a closed set through the elements of the collection is also closed.

RestrictGenTopology.of_seq.code:
RestrictGenTopology.of_seq.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] {S : Set (Set X)} [SequentialSpace X]
  (h : ∀ ⦃u : ℕ → X⦄ ⦃x : X⦄, Tendsto u atTop (𝓝 x) → insert x (range u) ∈ S) : RestrictGenTopology S
RestrictGenTopology.of_seq.comment:
If `X` is a sequential space
and `S` contains each set of the form `insert x (Set.range u)`
where `u : ℕ → X` is a sequence and `x` is its limit,
then topology on `X` is generated by its restrictions to the sets of `S`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.Filter.atTop: This definition introduces a filter that captures the behavior of elements approaching infinity in an ordered set, generated by all sets containing elements greater than or equal to any given element.
explanatories.Insert.insert: An operation is defined that allows an element to be added to a collection of another type.

RestrictGenTopology.of_seq.description: A collection of sets generates a topology on a sequential space if it includes every set formed by inserting the limit of a converging sequence into the range of that sequence.

exterior.code: exterior.{u_3} {α : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace α] (s : Set α) : Set α
exterior.comment:
The *exterior* of a set is the intersection of all its neighborhoods. In an Alexandrov-discrete
space, this is the smallest neighborhood of the set.

Note that this construction is unnamed in the literature. We choose the name in analogy to
`interior`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Filter.ker: A definition describing the kernel of a filter as the intersection of all sets contained within that filter.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.ker: A theorem establishing that the kernel of a filter, given its basis, is equivalent to the intersection of the sets associated with all basis elements satisfying the filter's property.

exterior.fullDefinition: def exterior (s : Set α) : Set α := (𝓝ˢ s).ker
exterior.description: The exterior of a set in a topological space is defined as the intersection of all its neighborhoods, representing the smallest neighborhood of that set in an Alexandrov-discrete space.

exterior_def.code: exterior_def.{u_3} {α : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace α] (s : Set α) : exterior s = ⋂₀ {t | IsOpen t ∧ s ⊆ t}

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

exterior_def.description: The exterior of a set in a topological space is defined as the intersection of all open sets that contain the set.

subset_exterior_iff.code:
subset_exterior_iff.{u_3} {α : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace α] {s t : Set α} :
  s ⊆ exterior t ↔ ∀ (U : Set α), IsOpen U → t ⊆ U → s ⊆ U

UniformContinuous.code: UniformContinuous.{ua, ub} {α : Type ua} {β : Type ub} [UniformSpace α] [UniformSpace β] (f : α → β) : Prop
UniformContinuous.comment:
A function `f : α → β` is *uniformly continuous* if `(f x, f y)` tends to the diagonal
as `(x, y)` tends to the diagonal. In other words, if `x` is sufficiently close to `y`, then
`f x` is close to `f y` no matter where `x` and `y` are located in `α`.

explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.UniformSpace: The uniformity filter on a uniform space is a filter that captures the concept of uniform convergence and closeness of points in a given space.

UniformContinuous.fullDefinition: def UniformContinuous [UniformSpace β] (f : α → β) :=   Tendsto (fun x : α × α => (f x.1, f x.2)) (𝓤 α) (𝓤 β)
UniformContinuous.description: A function is uniformly continuous if the images of close points remain close, regardless of their locations in the original space.

explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.comap: A theorem asserting that if a filter has a basis, then the filter obtained by pulling back the basis through a function also has a basis characterized by the preimages of the original sets.
explanatories.uniformity: This defines a filter on the product of a uniform space with itself, derived from the structure of the uniform space.

explanatories.UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace: A uniform space can be associated with a topological space, establishing a connection between the two concepts.
explanatories.UniformSpace.Core.symm: The uniformity of a space is symmetric, meaning that if a set is in the uniformity, then its inverse under the swap operation is also in the uniformity.
explanatories.UniformSpace.symm: The symmetry property of the uniformity filter asserts that if a set is in the uniformity, then the set obtained by swapping the elements of each pair is also in the uniformity.

explanatories.le_trans: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second, and the second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.comp: A theorem stating that the composition of two functions that tend to maps between respective filters also results in a function that tends to map from the original filter to the final one.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.

explanatories.UniformContinuous.comp: The composition of two uniformly continuous functions is also uniformly continuous.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.induced: The induced topology on a space is defined as the collection of sets that are the preimages of open sets in another space, ensuring that a given function remains continuous.
explanatories.Filter.tendsto_comap_iff: A theorem stating that a function converges to a limit under a filter if and only if the composition of that function with another function also converges to a limit under a different filter derived from the second function.
explanatories.Filter.tendsto_comap: A theorem establishing that the limit of a function, when considered under the context of a filter's pullback, converges to the original filter.
explanatories.Filter.comap_lift'_eq: The theorem states that the operation of pulling back a lifted filter through a function is equivalent to lifting the filter after applying the preimage of that function to the set transformation.
explanatories.Filter.comap_lift'_eq2: The theorem establishes that the lifting operation applied to the preimage of a filter under a monotone function is equivalent to first transforming the filter and then performing the lift operation on that transformed set.
explanatories.Filter.lift'_mono': If one set of transformations is contained within another for all sets in a given filter, then the lifted filter defined by the first set of transformations is contained within the lifted filter defined by the second set.
explanatories.Filter.comap_mono: A theorem stating that the operation of mapping a filter through a function preserves the property of monotonicity.
explanatories.nhds_induced: This theorem states that the neighborhood filter of a point in a topological space is equal to the filter obtained by pulling back the neighborhood filter of the image of that point under a given function.

UniformSpace.comap.fullDefinition: abbrev UniformSpace.comap (f : α → β) (u : UniformSpace β) : UniformSpace α where   uniformity := 𝓤[u].comap fun p : α × α => (f p.1, f p.2)   symm := by     simp only [tendsto_comap_iff, Prod.swap, (· ∘ ·)]     exact tendsto_swap_uniformity.comp tendsto_comap   comp := le_trans     (by       rw [comap_lift'_eq, comap_lift'_eq2]       · exact lift'_mono' fun s _ ⟨a₁, a₂⟩ ⟨x, h₁, h₂⟩ => ⟨f x, h₁, h₂⟩       · exact monotone_id.compRel monotone_id)     (comap_mono u.comp)   toTopologicalSpace := u.toTopologicalSpace.induced f   nhds_eq_comap_uniformity x := by     simp only [nhds_induced, nhds_eq_comap_uniformity, comap_comap, Function.comp]

uniform_space.comap.code: UniformSpace.comap.{ua, ub} {α : Type ua} {β : Type ub} (f : α → β) (u : UniformSpace β) : UniformSpace α
uniform_space.comap.comment:
Given `f : α → β` and a uniformity `u` on `β`, the inverse image of `u` under `f`
is the inverse image in the filter sense of the induced function `α × α → β × β`.
See note [reducible non-instances].

explanatories.compRel: The composition of relations is defined as the set of pairs where the first element is related to an intermediate element, which in turn is related to the second element.
explanatories.Prod.swap: A function exists that exchanges the positions of the elements in a pair.
explanatories.Monotone.compRel: The composition of monotone functions results in another monotone function when applied to a preordered set.
explanatories.UniformSpace.Core.uniformity: The uniformity filter associated with a uniform space is a specific type of filter over pairs of elements that formalizes the notion of uniform convergence and structure.
explanatories.monotone_id: The theorem states that the identity function is monotone in any preorder.
explanatories.Filter.comap: A definition of a filter that is obtained by applying an inverse mapping to another filter, specifying how sets relate under this construction.
explanatories.UniformSpace.Core.toTopologicalSpace: A uniform space can be associated with a topological space that it generates.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.comap: A theorem asserting that if a filter has a basis, then the filter obtained by pulling back the basis through a function also has a basis characterized by the preimages of the original sets.
explanatories.uniformity: This defines a filter on the product of a uniform space with itself, derived from the structure of the uniform space.
explanatories.UniformSpace.Core.comp: For every element in a uniformity, there exists another element such that the composition of that element with itself is contained within the original element.
explanatories.UniformSpace.uniformity: The uniformity filter on a uniform space is a filter that captures the concept of uniform convergence and closeness of points in a given space.
explanatories.UniformSpace.nhds_eq_comap_uniformity: The neighborhoods in a uniform space at any point coincide with the filter obtained by applying an inverse mapping to the uniformity filter associated with that space.
explanatories.UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace: A uniform space can be associated with a topological space, establishing a connection between the two concepts.
explanatories.UniformSpace.Core.symm: The uniformity of a space is symmetric, meaning that if a set is in the uniformity, then its inverse under the swap operation is also in the uniformity.
explanatories.UniformSpace.symm: The symmetry property of the uniformity filter asserts that if a set is in the uniformity, then the set obtained by swapping the elements of each pair is also in the uniformity.
explanatories.UniformSpace.comp: The uniformity filter of a uniform space contains sets whose symmetric products are also included in the filter.
explanatories.nhds_eq_comap_uniformity: The neighborhood of a point in a uniform space is equal to the preimage of the uniformity structure under the function that pairs the point with elements of the space.
explanatories.tendsto_swap_uniformity: The operation that swaps the components of pairs converges in the uniform structure of a uniform space.
explanatories.le_trans: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second, and the second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.comp: A theorem stating that the composition of two functions that tend to maps between respective filters also results in a function that tends to map from the original filter to the final one.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.UniformContinuous.comp: The composition of two uniformly continuous functions is also uniformly continuous.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.induced: The induced topology on a space is defined as the collection of sets that are the preimages of open sets in another space, ensuring that a given function remains continuous.
explanatories.Filter.tendsto_comap_iff: A theorem stating that a function converges to a limit under a filter if and only if the composition of that function with another function also converges to a limit under a different filter derived from the second function.
explanatories.Filter.tendsto_comap: A theorem establishing that the limit of a function, when considered under the context of a filter's pullback, converges to the original filter.
explanatories.Filter.comap_lift'_eq: The theorem states that the operation of pulling back a lifted filter through a function is equivalent to lifting the filter after applying the preimage of that function to the set transformation.
explanatories.Filter.comap_lift'_eq2: The theorem establishes that the lifting operation applied to the preimage of a filter under a monotone function is equivalent to first transforming the filter and then performing the lift operation on that transformed set.
explanatories.Filter.lift'_mono': If one set of transformations is contained within another for all sets in a given filter, then the lifted filter defined by the first set of transformations is contained within the lifted filter defined by the second set.
explanatories.Filter.comap_mono: A theorem stating that the operation of mapping a filter through a function preserves the property of monotonicity.
explanatories.nhds_induced: This theorem states that the neighborhood filter of a point in a topological space is equal to the filter obtained by pulling back the neighborhood filter of the image of that point under a given function.

explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.

explanatories.UniformSpace.Core.ext: Two uniform spaces are equal if their associated uniformity filters are the same.

explanatories.uniformity: This defines a filter on the product of a uniform space with itself, derived from the structure of the uniform space.

explanatories.UniformSpace.uniformity: The uniformity filter on a uniform space is a filter that captures the concept of uniform convergence and closeness of points in a given space.
explanatories.UniformSpace.nhds_eq_comap_uniformity: The neighborhoods in a uniform space at any point coincide with the filter obtained by applying an inverse mapping to the uniformity filter associated with that space.
explanatories.UniformSpace.Core.symm: The uniformity of a space is symmetric, meaning that if a set is in the uniformity, then its inverse under the swap operation is also in the uniformity.
explanatories.UniformSpace.ext: If two uniform spaces on the same type have equivalent entourages, then they are equal as uniform spaces.
explanatories.UniformSpace.symm: The symmetry property of the uniformity filter asserts that if a set is in the uniformity, then the set obtained by swapping the elements of each pair is also in the uniformity.
explanatories.UniformSpace.comp: The uniformity filter of a uniform space contains sets whose symmetric products are also included in the filter.
explanatories.nhds_eq_comap_uniformity: The neighborhood of a point in a uniform space is equal to the preimage of the uniformity structure under the function that pairs the point with elements of the space.

explanatories.symm_le_uniformity: The image of the uniformity filter under the swapping function is a subset of the uniformity filter itself, indicating a certain invariance under exchange of elements.
explanatories.comp_mem_uniformity_sets: If a set is part of the uniformity filter of a uniform space, then there exists another set in the uniformity filter such that the composition of that set with itself is contained within the original set.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.comp: A theorem stating that the composition of two functions that tend to maps between respective filters also results in a function that tends to map from the original filter to the final one.
explanatories.Functor.map: This defines a function that applies a mapping operation to a value wrapped in a context, transforming it from one type to another while preserving the structure of the context.

explanatories.Filter.mem_comap: A theorem stating that a set belongs to the pullback of a filter if and only if there exists a set in the original filter whose preimage under a function is included in the original set.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.UniformContinuous.comp: The composition of two uniformly continuous functions is also uniformly continuous.
explanatories.Prod.map: A mapping function transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.
explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.UniformContinuous₂.comp: The composition of two uniformly continuous functions is uniformly continuous when both individual functions are uniformly continuous.
explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function constructs a sum type from an element of the first type.

Sum.instUniformSpace.fullDefinition: instance Sum.instUniformSpace : UniformSpace (α ⊕ β) where   uniformity := map (fun p : α × α => (inl p.1, inl p.2)) (𝓤 α) ⊔     map (fun p : β × β => (inr p.1, inr p.2)) (𝓤 β)   symm := fun s hs ↦ ⟨symm_le_uniformity hs.1, symm_le_uniformity hs.2⟩   comp := fun s hs ↦ by     rcases comp_mem_uniformity_sets hs.1 with ⟨tα, htα, Htα⟩     rcases comp_mem_uniformity_sets hs.2 with ⟨tβ, htβ, Htβ⟩     filter_upwards [mem_lift' (union_mem_sup (image_mem_map htα) (image_mem_map htβ))]     rintro ⟨_, _⟩ ⟨z, ⟨⟨a, b⟩, hab, ⟨⟩⟩ | ⟨⟨a, b⟩, hab, ⟨⟩⟩, ⟨⟨_, c⟩, hbc, ⟨⟩⟩ | ⟨⟨_, c⟩, hbc, ⟨⟩⟩⟩     exacts [@Htα (_, _) ⟨b, hab, hbc⟩, @Htβ (_, _) ⟨b, hab, hbc⟩]   nhds_eq_comap_uniformity x := by     ext     cases x <;> simp [mem_comap', -mem_comap, nhds_inl, nhds_inr, nhds_eq_comap_uniformity,       Prod.ext_iff]

  (hKU : K ⊆ U) : ∃ V ∈ 𝓤 α, IsOpen V ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, ball x V ⊆ U
lebesgue_number_of_compact_open.comment:
A useful consequence of the Lebesgue number lemma: given any compact set `K` contained in an
open set `U`, we can find an (open) entourage `V` such that the ball of size `V` about any point of
`K` is contained in `U`.

Cauchy.code: Cauchy.{u} {α : Type u} [uniformSpace : UniformSpace α] (f : Filter α) : Prop
Cauchy.comment:
A filter `f` is Cauchy if for every entourage `r`, there exists an
`s ∈ f` such that `s × s ⊆ r`. This is a generalization of Cauchy
sequences, because if `a : ℕ → α` then the filter of sets containing
cofinitely many of the `a n` is Cauchy iff `a` is a Cauchy sequence.
Cauchy.fullDefinition: def Cauchy (f : Filter α) :=   NeBot f ∧ f ×ˢ f ≤ 𝓤 α
Cauchy.description: A filter is Cauchy if for every entourage, there exists a set in the filter such that the product of the set with itself is contained within that entourage, generalizing the concept of Cauchy sequences.

  [SeparableSpace α] : SecondCountableTopology α
UniformSpace.secondCountable_of_separabl.comment:
A separable uniform space with countably generated uniformity filter is second countable:
one obtains a countable basis by taking the balls centered at points in a dense subset,
and with rational "radii" from a countable open symmetric antitone basis of `𝓤 α`. We do not
register this as an instance, as there is already an instance going in the other direction
from second countable spaces to separable spaces, and we want to avoid loops.
UniformSpace.secondCountable_of_separabl.description: A separable uniform space with a countably generated uniformity filter has a second countable topology, which allows for the construction of a countable basis using balls centered at points from a dense subset with rational radii.

TendstoUniformlyOnFilter.code:
TendstoUniformlyOnFilter.{u, v, x} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {ι : Type x} [UniformSpace β] (F : ι → α → β) (f : α → β)
  (p : Filter ι) (p' : Filter α) : Prop
TendstoUniformlyOnFilter.comment:
A sequence of functions `Fₙ` converges uniformly on a filter `p'` to a limiting function `f`
with respect to the filter `p` if, for any entourage of the diagonal `u`, one has
`p ×ˢ p'`-eventually `(f x, Fₙ x) ∈ u`.

explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Prod.fst: This defines a function that retrieves the first element from a given pair of values.

TendstoUniformlyOnFilter.description: A sequence of functions converges uniformly to a limiting function on a given filter if, for every entourage of the diagonal, the pairs of their values become arbitrarily close in the uniform space with respect to the specified filters.

A sequence of functions `Fₙ` converges uniformly on a filter `p'` to a limiting function `f` w.r.t.
filter `p` iff the function `(n, x) ↦ (f x, Fₙ x)` converges along `p ×ˢ p'` to the uniformity.

TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.code:
TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.{u, v, x} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {ι : Type x} [UniformSpace β] [TopologicalSpace α]
  (F : ι → α → β) (f : α → β) (p : Filter ι) (s : Set α) : Prop
TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.comment:
A sequence of functions `Fₙ` converges locally uniformly on a set `s` to a limiting function
`f` with respect to a filter `p` if, for any entourage of the diagonal `u`, for any `x ∈ s`, one
has `p`-eventually `(f y, Fₙ y) ∈ u` for all `y` in a neighborhood of `x` in `s`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.fullDefinition: def TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn (F : ι → α → β) (f : α → β) (p : Filter ι) (s : Set α) :=   ∀ u ∈ 𝓤 β, ∀ x ∈ s, ∃ t ∈ 𝓝[s] x, ∀ᶠ n in p, ∀ y ∈ t, (f y, F n y) ∈ u
TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.description: A sequence of functions converges locally uniformly to a limiting function on a set with respect to a filter if, for any neighborhood around a point in the set, the functions and the limiting function become arbitrarily close outside of a negligible set defined by the filter.

  {ι : Sort u_1} {ι' : Sort u_2} {p : ι → Prop} {p' : ι' → Prop} {s : ι → Set (α × α)} {s' : ι' → Set (β × β)}

  UniformInducing f ↔

comap_uniformity_of_spaced_out.{v, u_1} {β : Type v} [UniformSpace β] {α : Type u_1} {f : α → β} {s : Set (β × β)}
  (hs : s ∈ 𝓤 β) (hf : Pairwise fun x y => (f x, f y) ∉ s) : comap (Prod.map f f) (𝓤 β) = 𝓟 idRel
comap_uniformity_of_spaced_out.comment:
If a map `f : α → β` sends any two distinct points to point that are **not** related by a fixed
`s ∈ 𝓤 β`, then `f` is uniform inducing with respect to the discrete uniformity on `α`:
the preimage of `𝓤 β` under `Prod.map f f` is the principal filter generated by the diagonal in
`α × α`.

UniformEquiv.changeInv.fullDefinition: def changeInv (f : α ≃ᵤ β) (g : β → α) (hg : Function.RightInverse g f) : α ≃ᵤ β :=   have : g = f.symm :=     funext fun x => calc       g x = f.symm (f (g x)) := (f.left_inv (g x)).symm       _ = f.symm x := by rw [hg x]   { toFun := f     invFun := g     left_inv := by convert f.left_inv     right_inv := by convert f.right_inv using 1     uniformContinuous_toFun := f.uniformContinuous     uniformContinuous_invFun := by convert f.symm.uniformContinuous }

UniformFun.isBasis_gen.code:
UniformFun.isBasis_gen.{u_1, u_2} (α : Type u_1) (β : Type u_2) (𝓑 : Filter (β × β)) :
  IsBasis (fun V => V ∈ 𝓑) (UniformFun.gen α β)
UniformFun.isBasis_gen.comment:
If `𝓕` is a filter on `β × β`, then the set of all `UniformFun.gen α β V` for
`V ∈ 𝓕` is a filter basis on `(α →ᵤ β) × (α →ᵤ β)`. This will only be applied to `𝓕 = 𝓤 β` when
`β` is equipped with a `UniformSpace` structure, but it is useful to define it for any filter in
order to be able to state that it has a lower adjoint (see `UniformFun.gc`).

UniformFun.gc.code:
UniformFun.gc.{u_1, u_2} (α : Type u_1) (β : Type u_2) :
  GaloisConnection (fun 𝓐 => map (UniformFun.phi α β) (𝓐 ×ˢ ⊤)) fun 𝓕 => UniformFun.filter α β 𝓕
UniformFun.gc.comment:
The function `UniformFun.filter α β : Filter (β × β) → Filter ((α →ᵤ β) × (α →ᵤ β))`
has a lower adjoint `l` (in the sense of `GaloisConnection`). The exact definition of `l` is not
interesting; we will only use that it exists (in `UniformFun.mono` and
`UniformFun.iInf_eq`) and that
`l (Filter.map (Prod.map f f) 𝓕) = Filter.map (Prod.map ((∘) f) ((∘) f)) (l 𝓕)` for each
`𝓕 : Filter (γ × γ)` and `f : γ → α` (in `UniformFun.comap_eq`).

UniformFun.mono.comment:
If `u₁` and `u₂` are two uniform structures on `γ` and `u₁ ≤ u₂`, then
`𝒰(α, γ, u₁) ≤ 𝒰(α, γ, u₂)`.

explanatories.Monotone: A function is considered monotone if it preserves the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output will not exceed the corresponding output of the larger input.
explanatories.DirectedOn.mono: If a set is directed with respect to one relation, it remains directed with respect to another relation that is at least as strong as the first.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.mono: If a non-empty set is a subset of another set, then the larger set is also non-empty.

UniformFun.mono.description: This theorem asserts that if one uniform structure is finer than another, the associated uniform spaces of functions generated from these structures will also maintain this order of fineness.

UniformFun.uniformEquivProdArrow.fullDefinition: protected def uniformEquivProdArrow [UniformSpace γ] : (α →ᵤ β × γ) ≃ᵤ (α →ᵤ β) × (α →ᵤ γ) :=   -- Denote `φ` this bijection. Equiv.toUniformEquivOfUniformInducing (Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow _ _ _) <| by     constructor     change       comap (Prod.map (Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow _ _ _) (Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow _ _ _))           _ = _     simp_rw [UniformFun]     rw [← uniformity_comap]     congr     unfold instUniformSpaceProd     rw [UniformSpace.comap_inf, ← UniformSpace.comap_comap, ← UniformSpace.comap_comap]     have := (@UniformFun.inf_eq α (β × γ)       (UniformSpace.comap Prod.fst ‹_›) (UniformSpace.comap Prod.snd ‹_›)).symm     rwa [UniformFun.comap_eq, UniformFun.comap_eq] at this

uniform_fun.uniform_equiv_prod_arrow.fullDefinition: protected def uniformEquivProdArrow [UniformSpace γ] : (α →ᵤ β × γ) ≃ᵤ (α →ᵤ β) × (α →ᵤ γ) :=   -- Denote `φ` this bijection. We want to show that   -- `comap φ (𝒰(α, β, uβ) × 𝒰(α, γ, uγ)) = 𝒰(α, β × γ, uβ × uγ)`.   -- But `uβ × uγ` is defined as `comap fst uβ ⊓ comap snd uγ`, so we just have to apply   -- `UniformFun.inf_eq` and `UniformFun.comap_eq`, which leaves us to check   -- that some square commutes.   Equiv.toUniformEquivOfUniformInducing (Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow _ _ _) <| by     constructor     change       comap (Prod.map (Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow _ _ _) (Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow _ _ _))           _ = _     simp_rw [UniformFun]     rw [← uniformity_comap]     congr     unfold instUniformSpaceProd     rw [UniformSpace.comap_inf, ← UniformSpace.comap_comap, ← UniformSpace.comap_comap]     have := (@UniformFun.inf_eq α (β × γ)       (UniformSpace.comap Prod.fst ‹_›) (UniformSpace.comap Prod.snd ‹_›)).symm     rwa [UniformFun.comap_eq, UniformFun.comap_eq] at this
uniform_fun.uniform_equiv_prod_arrow.description: This defines a uniform isomorphism between the space of uniformly continuous functions from one type to a product of two types and the Cartesian product of the spaces of uniformly continuous functions to each of those types separately.

UniformFun.uniformEquivPiComm.fullDefinition: protected def uniformEquivPiComm : UniformEquiv (α →ᵤ ∀ i, δ i) (∀ i, α →ᵤ δ i) :=   -- Denote `φ` this bijection. We want to show that     -- `comap φ (Π i, 𝒰(α, δ i, uδ i)) = 𝒰(α, (Π i, δ i), (Π i, uδ i))`.     -- But `Π i, uδ i` is defined as `⨅ i, comap (eval i) (uδ i)`, so we just have to apply     -- `UniformFun.iInf_eq` and `UniformFun.comap_eq`, which leaves us to check     -- that some square commutes.     @Equiv.toUniformEquivOfUniformInducing     _ _ 𝒰(α, ∀ i, δ i, Pi.uniformSpace δ)     (@Pi.uniformSpace ι (fun i => α → δ i) fun i => 𝒰(α, δ i, _)) (Equiv.piComm _) <| by       refine @UniformInducing.mk ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_       change comap (Prod.map Function.swap Function.swap) _ = _       rw [← uniformity_comap]       congr       unfold Pi.uniformSpace       rw [UniformSpace.ofCoreEq_toCore, UniformSpace.ofCoreEq_toCore,         UniformSpace.comap_iInf, UniformFun.iInf_eq]       refine iInf_congr fun i => ?_       rw [← UniformSpace.comap_comap, UniformFun.comap_eq]       rfl
UniformFun.uniformEquivPiComm.description: This establishes a uniform isomorphism between the space of uniformly continuous functions from one type to a product of types and the product of uniformly continuous functions from the first type to each member of the target types.

UniformOnFun.gen.code:
UniformOnFun.gen.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (𝔖 : Set (Set α)) (S : Set α) (V : Set (β × β)) :
  Set ((α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) × (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β))
UniformOnFun.gen.comment:
Basis sets for the uniformity of `𝔖`-convergence: for `S : Set α` and `V : Set (β × β)`,
`gen 𝔖 S V` is the set of pairs `(f, g)` of functions `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β` such that
`∀ x ∈ S, (f x, g x) ∈ V`. Note that the family `𝔖 : Set (Set α)` is only used to specify which
type alias of `α → β` to use here.

UniformOnFun.gen_eq_preimage_restrict.code:
UniformOnFun.gen_eq_preimage_restrict.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {𝔖 : Set (Set α)} (S : Set α)
  (V : Set (β × β)) :
  UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 S V =
    Prod.map (S.restrict ∘ ⇑UniformFun.toFun) (S.restrict ∘ ⇑UniformFun.toFun) ⁻¹' UniformFun.gen (↑S) β V
UniformOnFun.gen_eq_preimage_restrict.comment:
For `S : Set α` and `V : Set (β × β)`, we have
`UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 S V = (S.restrict × S.restrict) ⁻¹' (UniformFun.gen S β V)`.
This is the crucial fact for proving that the family `UniformOnFun.gen S V` for `S ∈ 𝔖` and
`V ∈ 𝓤 β` is indeed a basis for the uniformity `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β` endowed with `𝒱(α, β, 𝔖, uβ)`
the uniform structure of `𝔖`-convergence, as defined in `UniformOnFun.uniformSpace`.

UniformOnFun.isBasis_gen.code:
UniformOnFun.isBasis_gen.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (𝔖 : Set (Set α)) (h : 𝔖.Nonempty)
  (h' : DirectedOn (fun x x_1 => x ⊆ x_1) 𝔖) (𝓑 : FilterBasis (β × β)) :
  IsBasis (fun SV => SV.1 ∈ 𝔖 ∧ SV.2 ∈ 𝓑) fun SV => UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 SV.1 SV.2
UniformOnFun.isBasis_gen.comment:
If `𝔖 : Set (Set α)` is nonempty and directed and `𝓑` is a filter basis on `β × β`, then the
family `UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 S V` for `S ∈ 𝔖` and `V ∈ 𝓑` is a filter basis on
`(α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) × (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β)`.
We will show in `has_basis_uniformity_of_basis` that, if `𝓑` is a basis for `𝓤 β`, then the
corresponding filter is the uniformity of `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β`.

UniformOnFun.isBasis_gen.description: If a nonempty and directed set of subsets is provided alongside a filter basis on pairs of another type, then the functions generated by those subsets form a filter basis on the space of uniformly continuous functions.

uniform_on_fun.is_basis_gen.code:
UniformOnFun.isBasis_gen.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (𝔖 : Set (Set α)) (h : 𝔖.Nonempty)
  (h' : DirectedOn (fun x x_1 => x ⊆ x_1) 𝔖) (𝓑 : FilterBasis (β × β)) :
  IsBasis (fun SV => SV.1 ∈ 𝔖 ∧ SV.2 ∈ 𝓑) fun SV => UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 SV.1 SV.2
uniform_on_fun.is_basis_gen.comment:
If `𝔖 : Set (Set α)` is nonempty and directed and `𝓑` is a filter basis on `β × β`, then the
family `UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 S V` for `S ∈ 𝔖` and `V ∈ 𝓑` is a filter basis on
`(α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) × (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β)`.
We will show in `has_basis_uniformity_of_basis` that, if `𝓑` is a basis for `𝓤 β`, then the
corresponding filter is the uniformity of `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β`.

UniformOnFun.uniformSpace.code:
UniformOnFun.uniformSpace.{u_1, u_2} (α : Type u_1) (β : Type u_2) [UniformSpace β] (𝔖 : Set (Set α)) :
  UniformSpace (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β)
UniformOnFun.uniformSpace.comment:
Uniform structure of `𝔖`-convergence, i.e uniform convergence on the elements of `𝔖`,
declared as an instance on `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β`. It is defined as the infimum, for `S ∈ 𝔖`, of the pullback
by `S.restrict`, the map of restriction to `S`, of the uniform structure `𝒰(s, β, uβ)` on
`↥S →ᵤ β`. We will denote it `𝒱(α, β, 𝔖, uβ)`, where `uβ` is the uniform structure on `β`.

UniformOnFun.hasBasis_uniformity_of_cove.comment:
Let `t i` be a nonempty directed subfamily of `𝔖`
such that every `s ∈ 𝔖` is included in some `t i`.
Let `V` bounded by `p` be a basis of entourages of `β`.

Then `UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 (t i) (V j)` bounded by `p j` is a basis of entourages of `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β`.

such that each `s ∈ 𝔖` is included in some `t n`

UniformOnFun.precomp_uniformContinuous.code:
UniformOnFun.precomp_uniformContinuous.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} [UniformSpace β]
  {𝔖 : Set (Set α)} {𝔗 : Set (Set γ)} {f : γ → α} (hf : MapsTo (fun x => f '' x) 𝔗 𝔖) :
  UniformContinuous fun g => (ofFun 𝔗) ((toFun 𝔖) g ∘ f)
UniformOnFun.precomp_uniformContinuous.comment:
Let `f : γ → α`, `𝔖 : Set (Set α)`, `𝔗 : Set (Set γ)`, and assume that `∀ T ∈ 𝔗, f '' T ∈ 𝔖`.
Then, the function `(fun g ↦ g ∘ f) : (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) → (γ →ᵤ[𝔗] β)` is uniformly continuous.

Note that one can easily see that assuming `∀ T ∈ 𝔗, ∃ S ∈ 𝔖, f '' T ⊆ S` would work too, but
we will get this for free when we prove that `𝒱(α, β, 𝔖, uβ) = 𝒱(α, β, 𝔖', uβ)` where `𝔖'` is the
***noncovering*** bornology generated by `𝔖`.

UniformOnFun.precomp_uniformContinuous.description: If a mapping from one set to another ensures that the image of any element under this mapping brings corresponding subsets from the second set into the first set, then the composed function will maintain uniform continuity.

that of pointwise convergence.

UniformOnFun.uniformEquivProdArrow.fullDefinition: protected def uniformEquivProdArrow [UniformSpace γ] :     (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β × γ) ≃ᵤ (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) × (α →ᵤ[𝔖] γ) :=   -- Denote `φ` this bijection. We want to show that   -- `comap φ (𝒱(α, β, 𝔖, uβ) × 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, uγ)) = 𝒱(α, β × γ, 𝔖, uβ × uγ)`.   -- But `uβ × uγ` is defined as `comap fst uβ ⊓ comap snd uγ`, so we just have to apply   -- `UniformOnFun.inf_eq` and `UniformOnFun.comap_eq`,   -- which leaves us to check that some square commutes.   -- We could also deduce this from `UniformFun.uniformEquivProdArrow`,   -- but it turns out to be more annoying.   ((UniformOnFun.ofFun 𝔖).symm.trans <|     (Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow _ _ _).trans <|       (UniformOnFun.ofFun 𝔖).prodCongr (UniformOnFun.ofFun 𝔖)).toUniformEquivOfUniformInducing <| by       constructor       rw [uniformity_prod, comap_inf, comap_comap, comap_comap]       have H := @UniformOnFun.inf_eq α (β × γ) 𝔖         (UniformSpace.comap Prod.fst ‹_›) (UniformSpace.comap Prod.snd ‹_›)       apply_fun (fun u ↦ @uniformity (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β × γ) u) at H       convert H.symm using 1       rw [UniformOnFun.comap_eq, UniformOnFun.comap_eq]       erw [inf_uniformity]       rw [uniformity_comap, uniformity_comap]       rfl -- the relevant diagram commutes by definition
UniformOnFun.uniformEquivProdArrow.description: This establishes a uniform isomorphism between the space of uniformly continuous functions mapping to a product of types and the product of spaces of uniformly continuous functions mapping to those types individually.

We want to show that   -- `comap φ (Π i, 𝒱(α, δ i, 𝔖, uδ i)) = 𝒱(α, (Π i, δ i), 𝔖, (Π i, uδ i))`.   -- But `Π i, uδ i` is defined as `⨅ i, comap (eval i) (uδ i)`, so we just have to apply   -- `UniformOnFun.iInf_eq` and `UniformOnFun.comap_eq`,   -- which leaves us to check that some square commutes.   -- We could also deduce this from `UniformFun.uniformEquivPiComm`, but it turns out   -- to be more annoying.   @Equiv.toUniformEquivOfUniformInducing (α →ᵤ[𝔖] ((i : ι) → δ i)) ((i : ι) → α →ᵤ[𝔖] δ i)       _ _ (Equiv.piComm _) <| by     constructor     change comap (Prod.map Function.swap Function.swap) _ = _     erw [← uniformity_comap]     congr     rw [Pi.uniformSpace, UniformSpace.ofCoreEq_toCore, Pi.uniformSpace,       UniformSpace.ofCoreEq_toCore, UniformSpace.comap_iInf, UniformOnFun.iInf_eq]     refine iInf_congr fun i => ?_     rw [← UniformSpace.comap_comap, UniformOnFun.comap_eq]     rfl -- Like in the previous lemma, the diagram actually commutes by definition
UniformOnFun.uniformEquivPiComm.description: This defines a uniform isomorphism that establishes a natural correspondence between the space of uniformly continuous functions on a product type and the product of spaces of uniformly continuous functions.

UniformOnFun.uniformEquivUniformFun.fullDefinition: def uniformEquivUniformFun (h : univ ∈ 𝔖) : (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) ≃ᵤ (α →ᵤ β) where   toFun f := UniformFun.ofFun <| toFun _ f   invFun f := ofFun _ <| UniformFun.toFun f   left_inv _ := rfl   right_inv _ := rfl   uniformContinuous_toFun := by     simp only [UniformContinuous, (UniformFun.hasBasis_uniformity _ _).tendsto_right_iff]     intro U hU     filter_upwards [UniformOnFun.gen_mem_uniformity _ _ h hU] with f hf x using hf x (mem_univ _)   uniformContinuous_invFun := uniformContinuous_ofUniformFun _ _
UniformOnFun.uniformEquivUniformFun.description: This definition establishes a uniform equivalence between the space of functions that are uniformly continuous with respect to a set of subsets and the space of all uniformly continuous functions, given that the universal set is included in that collection.

CauchyFilter.comment:
Space of Cauchy filters

This is essentially the completion of a uniform space. The embeddings are the neighbourhood filters.
This space is not minimal, the separated uniform space (i.e. quotiented on the intersection of all
entourages) is necessary for this.

UniformSpace.Completion.completionSepara.fullDefinition: def completionSeparationQuotientEquiv (α : Type u) [UniformSpace α] :     Completion (SeparationQuotient α) ≃ Completion α := by   refine ⟨Completion.extension (lift' ((↑) : α → Completion α)),     Completion.map SeparationQuotient.mk, fun a ↦ ?_, fun a ↦ ?_⟩   · refine induction_on a (isClosed_eq (continuous_map.comp continuous_extension) continuous_id) ?_     refine SeparationQuotient.surjective_mk.forall.2 fun a ↦ ?_     rw [extension_coe (uniformContinuous_lift' _), lift'_mk (uniformContinuous_coe α),       map_coe uniformContinuous_mk]   · refine induction_on a       (isClosed_eq (continuous_extension.comp continuous_map) continuous_id) fun a ↦ ?_     rw [map_coe uniformContinuous_mk, extension_coe (uniformContinuous_lift' _),       lift'_mk (uniformContinuous_coe _)]

ContinuousMap.tendsto_iff_forall_compact.comment:
Compact-open topology on `C(α, β)` agrees with the topology of uniform convergence on compacts:
a family of continuous functions `F i` tends to `f` in the compact-open topology
if and only if the `F i` tends to `f` uniformly on all compact sets.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.IsCompact: This defines the property of a set within a topological space being compact, which requires that for any nontrivial filter containing the set, there is an element within the set such that every set in the filter intersects with every neighborhood of that element.
explanatories.TendstoUniformlyOn: A sequence of functions converges uniformly to a limiting function on a set if, for every entourage of the diagonal, the pairs of their values become arbitrarily close in the uniform space at points within that set with respect to the specified filter.

ContinuousMap.compactConvergenceUniformS.code:
ContinuousMap.compactConvergenceUniformSpace.{u₁, u₂} {α : Type u₁} {β : Type u₂} [TopologicalSpace α]
  [UniformSpace β] : UniformSpace C(α, β)
ContinuousMap.compactConvergenceUniformS.comment:
Uniform space structure on `C(α, β)`.

The uniformity comes from `α →ᵤ[{K | IsCompact K}] β` (i.e., `UniformOnFun α β {K | IsCompact K}`)
which defines topology of uniform convergence on compact sets.
We use `ContinuousMap.tendsto_iff_forall_compact_tendstoUniformlyOn`
to show that the induced topology agrees with the compact-open topology
and replace the topology with `compactOpen` to avoid non-defeq diamonds,
see Note [forgetful inheritance].

explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.tendsto_iff_forall_compact: This theorem establishes that a family of continuous functions converges to a function in the compact-open topology if and only if it converges uniformly on compact sets.

explanatories.UniformSpace.replaceTopology: This defines a method to replace the topology in a uniform space instance with another topology that is propositionally equivalent to the original one.
explanatories.UniformSpace.comap: The inverse image of a uniformity on a uniform space under a function generates a new uniform space that captures the structure of the original space.
explanatories.eq_of_forall_le_iff: A theorem stating that in a partially ordered structure, if two elements are related to every other element in the same way, then the two elements are equal.
explanatories.Filter.tendsto_id': A theorem stating that a filter converges to itself if and only if it is less than or equal to another filter.
explanatories.nhds_induced: This theorem states that the neighborhood filter of a point in a topological space is equal to the filter obtained by pulling back the neighborhood filter of the image of that point under a given function.
explanatories.Filter.tendsto_comap_iff: A theorem stating that a function converges to a limit under a filter if and only if the composition of that function with another function also converges to a limit under a different filter derived from the second function.
explanatories.UniformOnFun.tendsto_iff_tendstoUniforml: The theorem establishes that convergence of a sequence of functions in the uniform topology is equivalent to uniform convergence on the subsets specified by a certain collection of sets.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.comap: A theorem asserting that if a filter has a basis, then the filter obtained by pulling back the basis through a function also has a basis characterized by the preimages of the original sets.
explanatories.Filter.HasAntitoneBasis.comap: A theorem stating that if a filter has an antitone basis, then the filter formed by the preimage of a mapping maintains the antitone basis property under the transformation.

ContinuousMap.compactConvergenceUniformS.fullDefinition: instance compactConvergenceUniformSpace : UniformSpace C(α, β) :=   .replaceTopology (.comap toUniformOnFunIsCompact inferInstance) <| by     refine TopologicalSpace.ext_nhds fun f ↦ eq_of_forall_le_iff fun l ↦ ?_     simp_rw [← tendsto_id', tendsto_iff_forall_compact_tendstoUniformlyOn,       nhds_induced, tendsto_comap_iff, UniformOnFun.tendsto_iff_tendstoUniformlyOn]     rfl
ContinuousMap.compactConvergenceUniformS.description: This definition establishes a uniform space structure on the space of continuous functions, defined by the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets.

EquicontinuousAt.{u_1, u_3, u_7} {ι : Type u_1} {X : Type u_3} {α : Type u_7} [tX : TopologicalSpace X]
  [uα : UniformSpace α] (F : ι → X → α) (x₀ : X) : Prop
EquicontinuousAt.comment:
A family `F : ι → X → α` of functions from a topological space to a uniform space is
*equicontinuous at `x₀ : X`* if, for all entourages `U ∈ 𝓤 α`, there is a neighborhood `V` of `x₀`
such that, for all `x ∈ V` and for all `i : ι`, `F i x` is `U`-close to `F i x₀`.
EquicontinuousAt.fullDefinition: def EquicontinuousAt (F : ι → X → α) (x₀ : X) : Prop :=   ∀ U ∈ 𝓤 α, ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 x₀, ∀ i, (F i x₀, F i x) ∈ U
EquicontinuousAt.description: A family of functions from a topological space to a uniform space is considered equicontinuous at a specific point if, for every entourage, there exists a neighborhood around that point where the function values remain close to each other.

EquicontinuousWithinAt.closure'.code:
EquicontinuousWithinAt.closure'.{u_3, u_5, u_7} {X : Type u_3} {Y : Type u_5} {α : Type u_7} [tX : TopologicalSpace X]
  [tY : TopologicalSpace Y] [uα : UniformSpace α] {A : Set Y} {u : Y → X → α} {S : Set X} {x₀ : X}
  (hA : EquicontinuousWithinAt (u ∘ Subtype.val) S x₀) (hu₁ : Continuous (S.restrict ∘ u))
  (hu₂ : Continuous (eval x₀ ∘ u)) : EquicontinuousWithinAt (u ∘ Subtype.val) S x₀
EquicontinuousWithinAt.closure'.comment:
If a set of functions is equicontinuous at some `x₀` within a set `S`, the same is true for its
closure in *any* topology for which evaluation at any `x ∈ S ∪ {x₀}` is continuous. Since
this will be applied to `DFunLike` types, we state it for any topological space whith a map
to `X → α` satisfying the right continuity conditions. See also `Set.EquicontinuousWithinAt.closure`
for a more familiar (but weaker) statement.

Note: This could *technically* be called `EquicontinuousWithinAt.closure` without name clashes
with `Set.EquicontinuousWithinAt.closure`, but we don't do it because, even with a `protected`
marker, it would introduce ambiguities while working in namespace `Set` (e.g, in the proof of
any theorem called `Set.something`).

EquicontinuousAt.tendsto_of_mem_closure.comment:
If `F : ι → X → α` is a family of functions equicontinuous at `x`,
it tends to `f y` along a filter `l` for any `y ∈ s`,
the limit function `f` tends to `z` along `𝓝[s] x`, and `x ∈ closure s`,
then `(F · x)` tends to `z` along `l`.

In some sense, this is a converse of `EquicontinuousAt.closure`.

explanatories.UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace: A uniform space can be associated with a topological space, establishing a connection between the two concepts.

unique_uniformity_of_compact.description: In a compact space, any two uniform structures that induce the same topology must be identical.

explanatories.Set.diagonal: The diagonal of a type consists of all pairs where both elements are identical.
explanatories.uniformity: This defines a filter on the product of a uniform space with itself, derived from the structure of the uniform space.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.comap: A theorem asserting that if a filter has a basis, then the filter obtained by pulling back the basis through a function also has a basis characterized by the preimages of the original sets.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.nhdsSet_diagonal: The neighborhood of the diagonal in the product space is equal to the supremum of the neighborhoods of each point on the diagonal.
explanatories.continuous_swap: This theorem shows that the function that interchanges the components of pairs in a product of topological spaces is continuous.
explanatories.Continuous.tendsto_nhdsSet: The image under a continuous function of the neighborhood of a set is a neighborhood of the image of that set.
explanatories.Filter.lift': The definition describes a method for transforming a filter from one type to another by applying a function that maps sets of the first type to sets of the second type.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Filter.le_iff_forall_inf_principal_compl: A theorem stating that one filter is a refinement of another if and only if the intersection of the first filter with the complements of sets in the second filter yields the trivial filter.
explanatories.ClusterPt: This defines a condition for a point to be a cluster point of a given filter in topology, indicating that the intersection of the filter with the neighborhood of the point is non-empty.
explanatories.exists_clusterPt_of_compactSpace: In a compact topological space, any non-empty filter has a cluster point.
explanatories.ClusterPt.of_inf_right: If a point is a cluster point of the intersection of two filters, then it is also a cluster point of one of those filters.
explanatories.mem_closure_iff_clusterPt: A point is in the closure of a set if and only if it is a cluster point of that set.
explanatories.closure_compl: The closure of the complement of a set in a topological space is equal to the complement of the interior of the set.
explanatories.subset_interior_iff_mem_nhdsSet: A set is a subset of the interior of another set if and only if the second set is in the neighborhood of the first set.
explanatories.mt: If a true implication leads to a false conclusion, then the antecedent must also be false.
explanatories.disjoint_nested_nhds: This theorem guarantees that in a T3 space, for any two distinct points, one can find disjoint neighborhoods around each point with the neighborhoods being open and their corresponding closures being closed.
explanatories.Union.union: The union of two elements is defined as the combination of both elements into a single entity.
explanatories.IsClosed.union: The union of two closed sets in a topological space is also a closed set.
explanatories.mem_nhdsSet_iff_forall: A set is in the neighborhood of another set if and only if it is in the neighborhood of every point of the second set.
explanatories.IsOpen.mem_nhds: If a set is open in a topological space and contains a point, then that set is a neighborhood of that point.
explanatories.IsOpen.union: The union of two open sets in a topological space is also an open set.
explanatories.IsOpen.prod: This theorem establishes that the Cartesian product of two open sets in topological spaces is also an open set in the product topology.
explanatories.Set.mem_union: An element belongs to the union of two sets if and only if it belongs to at least one of those sets.
explanatories.Set.mem_prod: An ordered pair belongs to the Cartesian product of two sets if and only if its first and second components belong to the respective sets.
explanatories.and_self_iff: The conjunction of a proposition with itself is equivalent to the proposition itself.
explanatories.em: This theorem states that for any proposition, either it is true or its negation is true, reflecting the principle of excluded middle.
explanatories.Or.imp_left: The theorem shows that if one proposition implies another, then the disjunction of that proposition with a third proposition implies the disjunction of the second proposition with the same third proposition.
explanatories.Set.union_subset_union: The union of two sets is a subset of the union of two other sets if each of the original sets is a subset of the corresponding sets.
explanatories.Filter.mem_lift': The theorem states that if a given set belongs to a filter, then the image of that set under a specified function will belong to the lift of the filter with respect to that function.
explanatories.prod_mem_nhds: This theorem states that if a set is in the neighborhood of one point in a topological space and another set is in the neighborhood of a different point, then the Cartesian product of these two sets is in the neighborhood of the pair of those two points.
explanatories.clusterPt_iff: A point is a cluster point of a filter if and only if every neighborhood of that point intersects with every set in the filter non-emptily.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.ClusterPt.of_inf_left: If a point is a cluster point of the intersection of two filters, then it is also a cluster point of each of the individual filters.
explanatories.Or.resolve_right: This theorem states that if at least one of two propositions is true and the second proposition is false, then the first proposition must be true.
explanatories.Or.inl: If a proposition is true, then it can be included in a disjunction, demonstrating how to inject it into the logical framework of 'or'.
explanatories.Disjoint.le_bot: If two elements in a lattice are disjoint, then their infimum is less than or equal to the least element of the lattice.
explanatories.Or.inr: If there is a proof of a proposition, it can be included in a disjunction as the second option.
explanatories.Or.resolve_left: This theorem states that if one has a disjunction and knows that one of the propositions is false, then the other proposition must be true.
explanatories.Filter.comap_iSup: A theorem stating that the filter obtained by mapping through a function and taking the supremum of a family of filters is equal to the supremum of the results of mapping through that function on each filter individually.
explanatories.nhds_prod_eq: This theorem states that the neighborhood of a point in the product space is equal to the product of the neighborhoods of the individual points in each space.
explanatories.Filter.comap_prod: The comap of a function that produces pairs from a filter on the first component is equal to the infimum of the comaps of the projections of that function with respect to the corresponding filters on the second and third components.
explanatories.Filter.comap_id': A theorem asserting that applying the identity function in the comap operation on a filter returns the filter itself unchanged.
explanatories.iSup_split_single: This theorem states that the supremum of a function over a set can be expressed as the maximum of the function evaluated at a specific element and the supremum of the function evaluated at all other elements in the set.
explanatories.Filter.comap_const_of_mem: A theorem stating that if a constant element is a member of every set in a filter, then the filter's comap with respect to that constant element is the filter containing all sets.
explanatories.mem_of_mem_nhds: If a set is a member of the neighborhood of a point, then that point must be an element of the set.
explanatories.Filter.comap: A definition of a filter that is obtained by applying an inverse mapping to another filter, specifying how sets relate under this construction.
explanatories.Filter.comap_const_of_not_mem: A theorem stating that if a set does not contain a specific element and belongs to a filter, then the filter's comap with respect to that element is the bottom filter.
explanatories.compl_singleton_mem_nhds: This theorem states that in a T1 space, the complement of a singleton set containing a point belongs to the neighborhood of any other distinct point.
explanatories.not_not_intro: From any proposition that is true, it can be concluded that its negation is false, thereby establishing the principle of double negation introduction.
explanatories.IsCompact.prod: The Cartesian product of two compact sets is also compact.
explanatories.Set.Subset.rfl: Every set is a subset of itself.

uniformSpaceOfCompactT2.fullDefinition: def uniformSpaceOfCompactT2 [TopologicalSpace γ] [CompactSpace γ] [T2Space γ] : UniformSpace γ where   uniformity := 𝓝ˢ (diagonal γ)   symm := continuous_swap.tendsto_nhdsSet fun x => Eq.symm   comp := by     /-  This is the difficult part of the proof. We need to prove that, for each neighborhood `W`         of the diagonal `Δ`, there exists a smaller neighborhood `V` such that `V ○ V ⊆ W`.         -/     set 𝓝Δ := 𝓝ˢ (diagonal γ)     -- The filter of neighborhoods of Δ     set F := 𝓝Δ.lift' fun s : Set (γ × γ) => s ○ s     -- Compositions of neighborhoods of Δ     -- If this weren't true, then there would be V ∈ 𝓝Δ such that F ⊓ 𝓟 Vᶜ ≠ ⊥     rw [le_iff_forall_inf_principal_compl]     intro V V_in     by_contra H     haveI : NeBot (F ⊓ 𝓟 Vᶜ) := ⟨H⟩     -- Hence compactness would give us a cluster point (x, y) for F ⊓ 𝓟 Vᶜ     obtain ⟨⟨x, y⟩, hxy⟩ : ∃ p : γ × γ, ClusterPt p (F ⊓ 𝓟 Vᶜ) := exists_clusterPt_of_compactSpace _     -- In particular (x, y) is a cluster point of 𝓟 Vᶜ, hence is not in the interior of V,     -- and a fortiori not in Δ, so x ≠ y     have clV : ClusterPt (x, y) (𝓟 <| Vᶜ) := hxy.of_inf_right     have : (x, y) ∉ interior V := by       have : (x, y) ∈ closure Vᶜ := by rwa [mem_closure_iff_clusterPt]       rwa [closure_compl] at this     have diag_subset : diagonal γ ⊆ interior V := subset_interior_iff_mem_nhdsSet.2 V_in     have x_ne_y : x ≠ y := mt (@diag_subset (x, y)) this     -- Since γ is compact and Hausdorff, it is T₄, hence T₃.     -- So there are closed neighborhoods V₁ and V₂ of x and y contained in     -- disjoint open neighborhoods U₁ and U₂.     obtain       ⟨U₁, _, V₁, V₁_in, U₂, _, V₂, V₂_in, V₁_cl, V₂_cl, U₁_op, U₂_op, VU₁, VU₂, hU₁₂⟩ :=       disjoint_nested_nhds x_ne_y     -- We set U₃ := (V₁ ∪ V₂)ᶜ so that W := U₁ ×ˢ U₁ ∪ U₂ ×ˢ U₂ ∪ U₃ ×ˢ U₃ is an open     -- neighborhood of Δ.     let U₃ := (V₁ ∪ V₂)ᶜ     have U₃_op : IsOpen U₃ := (V₁_cl.union V₂_cl).isOpen_compl     let W := U₁ ×ˢ U₁ ∪ U₂ ×ˢ U₂ ∪ U₃ ×ˢ U₃     have W_in : W ∈ 𝓝Δ := by       rw [mem_nhdsSet_iff_forall]       rintro ⟨z, z'⟩ (rfl : z = z')       refine IsOpen.mem_nhds ?_ ?_       · apply_rules [IsOpen.union, IsOpen.prod]       · simp only [W, mem_union, mem_prod, and_self_iff]         exact (_root_.em _).imp_left fun h => union_subset_union VU₁ VU₂ h     -- So W ○ W ∈ F by definition of F     have : W ○ W ∈ F := @mem_lift' _ _ _ (fun s => s ○ s) _ W_in       -- Porting note: was `by simpa only using mem_lift' W_in`     -- And V₁ ×ˢ V₂ ∈ 𝓝 (x, y)     have hV₁₂ : V₁ ×ˢ V₂ ∈ 𝓝 (x, y) := prod_mem_nhds V₁_in V₂_in     -- But (x, y) is also a cluster point of F so (V₁ ×ˢ V₂) ∩ (W ○ W) ≠ ∅     -- However the construction of W implies (V₁ ×ˢ V₂) ∩ (W ○ W) = ∅.     -- Indeed assume for contradiction there is some (u, v) in the intersection.     obtain ⟨⟨u, v⟩, ⟨u_in, v_in⟩, w, huw, hwv⟩ := clusterPt_iff.mp hxy.of_inf_left hV₁₂ this     -- So u ∈ V₁, v ∈ V₂, and there exists some w such that (u, w) ∈ W and (w ,v) ∈ W.     -- Because u is in V₁ which is disjoint from U₂ and U₃, (u, w) ∈ W forces (u, w) ∈ U₁ ×ˢ U₁.     have uw_in : (u, w) ∈ U₁ ×ˢ U₁ :=       (huw.resolve_right fun h => h.1 <| Or.inl u_in).resolve_right fun h =>         hU₁₂.le_bot ⟨VU₁ u_in, h.1⟩     -- Similarly, because v ∈ V₂, (w ,v) ∈ W forces (w, v) ∈ U₂ ×ˢ U₂.     have wv_in : (w, v) ∈ U₂ ×ˢ U₂ :=       (hwv.resolve_right fun h => h.2 <| Or.inr v_in).resolve_left fun h =>         hU₁₂.le_bot ⟨h.2, VU₂ v_in⟩     -- Hence w ∈ U₁ ∩ U₂ which is empty.     -- So we have a contradiction     exact hU₁₂.le_bot ⟨uw_in.2, wv_in.1⟩   nhds_eq_comap_uniformity x := by     simp_rw [nhdsSet_diagonal, comap_iSup, nhds_prod_eq, comap_prod, (· ∘ ·), comap_id']     rw [iSup_split_single _ x, comap_const_of_mem fun V => mem_of_mem_nhds]     suffices ∀ y ≠ x, comap (fun _ : γ ↦ x) (𝓝 y) ⊓ 𝓝 y ≤ 𝓝 x by simpa     intro y hxy     simp [comap_const_of_not_mem (compl_singleton_mem_nhds hxy) (not_not_intro rfl)]

Equicontinuous.comap_uniformFun_eq.code:
Equicontinuous.comap_uniformFun_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {X : Type u_2} {α : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [UniformSpace α] {F : ι → X → α} [CompactSpace X] (F_eqcont : Equicontinuous F) :
  UniformSpace.comap F (UniformFun.uniformSpace X α) = UniformSpace.comap F (Pi.uniformSpace fun i => α)
Equicontinuous.comap_uniformFun_eq.comment:
Let `X` be a compact topological space, `α` a uniform space, and `F : ι → (X → α)` an
equicontinuous family. Then, the uniform structures of uniform convergence and pointwise
convergence induce the same uniform structure on `ι`.

In other words, pointwise convergence and uniform convergence coincide on an equicontinuous
subset of `X → α`.

Consider using `Equicontinuous.uniformInducing_uniformFun_iff_pi` and
`Equicontinuous.inducing_uniformFun_iff_pi` instead, to avoid rewriting instances.

explanatories.UniformFun.uniformSpace: This defines a uniform space structure on the space of uniformly continuous functions from one type to another, based on the uniform space of the codomain.
explanatories.UniformSpace.comap: The inverse image of a uniformity on a uniform space under a function generates a new uniform space that captures the structure of the original space.
explanatories.Pi.uniformSpace: A uniform space can be defined for the space of functions indexed by a set, where each target type is itself equipped with a uniform structure.
explanatories.Filter.comap: A definition of a filter that is obtained by applying an inverse mapping to another filter, specifying how sets relate under this construction.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.comap: A theorem asserting that if a filter has a basis, then the filter obtained by pulling back the basis through a function also has a basis characterized by the preimages of the original sets.
explanatories.Set.Equicontinuous: A set of functions is considered equicontinuous if the family of functions formed by that set maintains equicontinuity.
explanatories.UniformOnFun.uniformSpace: This defines a uniform structure for functions from one type to another based on a set of convergence criteria, specifically capturing uniform convergence with respect to those criteria.

Equicontinuous.comap_uniformFun_eq.description: The uniform structures induced by uniform convergence and pointwise convergence on an equicontinuous family of functions from a compact topological space to a uniform space are equivalent.

Equicontinuous.inducing_uniformFun_iff_p.comment:
Let `X` be a compact topological space, `α` a uniform space, and `F : ι → (X → α)` an
equicontinuous family. Then, the topologies of uniform convergence and pointwise convergence induce
the same topology on `ι`.

In other words, pointwise convergence and uniform convergence coincide on an equicontinuous
subset of `X → α`.

This is a consequence of `Equicontinuous.comap_uniformFun_eq`, stated in terms of `Inducing`
for convenuence.

explanatories.UniformFun.ofFun: This provides a way to reinterpret a function from one type to another as a function that satisfies the uniform structure associated with uniform convergence.

explanatories.UniformOnFun.ofFun: This establishes a method to reinterpret a function from one type to another as a function that adheres to a uniform structure constrained by a specific set of subsets.

Equicontinuous.inducing_uniformFun_iff_p.description: The topologies induced by pointwise convergence and uniform convergence are equivalent for an equicontinuous family of functions from a compact topological space to a uniform space.

  [UniformSpace α] {F : ι → X → α} {𝔖 : Set (Set X)} (𝔖_compact : ∀ K ∈ 𝔖, IsCompact K)
  (F_eqcont : ∀ K ∈ 𝔖, EquicontinuousOn F K) :
  UniformSpace.comap F (UniformOnFun.uniformSpace X α 𝔖) =
    UniformSpace.comap ((⋃₀ 𝔖).restrict ∘ F) (Pi.uniformSpace fun i => α)
EquicontinuousOn.comap_uniformOnFun_eq.comment:
Let `X` be a topological space, `𝔖` a family of compact subsets of `X`, `α` a uniform space,
and `F : ι → (X → α)` a family which is equicontinuous on each `K ∈ 𝔖`. Then, the uniform
structures of uniform convergence on `𝔖` and pointwise convergence on `⋃₀ 𝔖` induce the same
uniform structure on `ι`.

In particular, pointwise convergence and compact convergence coincide on an equicontinuous
subset of `X → α`.

Consider using `EquicontinuousOn.uniformInducing_uniformOnFun_iff_pi'` and
`EquicontinuousOn.inducing_uniformOnFun_iff_pi'` instead to avoid rewriting instances,
as well as their unprimed versions in case `𝔖` covers `X`.

Let `X` be a compact topological space, `α` a uniform space, `F : ι → (X → α)` an
