  (hinv : Tendsto (fun x => x⁻¹) (𝓝 1) (𝓝 1)) (hleft : ∀ (x₀ : G), 𝓝 x₀ = map (fun x => x₀ * x) (𝓝 1))
  (hconj : ∀ (x₀ : G), Tendsto (fun x => x₀ * x * x₀⁻¹) (𝓝 1) (𝓝 1)) : ContinuousInv G

explanatories.Specializes.map: The theorem demonstrates that if one point specializes another in a topological space and a continuous function maps these points, then the image of the first point under this function specializes the image of the second point.
explanatories.Inseparable.map: The theorem states that if two points in a topological space are inseparable and a continuous function maps them, then their images under that function are also inseparable.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.Filter.map: A definition describing a transformation of a filter through a function that maps elements from one type to another.
explanatories.Subgroup.map: This definition states that the image of a subgroup through a monoid homomorphism is itself a subgroup of the target group.
explanatories.ContinuousMul.of_nhds_one: A monoid equipped with a topology is structured to have a continuous multiplication operation if the multiplication converges at the identity element and the neighborhoods around any element can be represented through translations involving the neighborhoods of the identity.
explanatories.Ultrafilter.map: An ultrafilter can be transformed into another ultrafilter through a function mapping elements from one type to another.

ContinuousInv.of_nhds_one.description: A topological group has a continuous inversion operation if the inversion function converges at the identity and for every element, the neighborhood around it can be transformed through multiplication by that element.

topological_add_group_quotient.fullDefinition: instance topologicalGroup_quotient [N.Normal] : TopologicalGroup (G ⧸ N) where   continuous_mul := by     have cont : Continuous (((↑) : G → G ⧸ N) ∘ fun p : G × G ↦ p.fst * p.snd) :=       continuous_quot_mk.comp continuous_mul     have quot : QuotientMap fun p : G × G ↦ ((p.1 : G ⧸ N), (p.2 : G ⧸ N)) := by       apply IsOpenMap.to_quotientMap       · exact (QuotientGroup.isOpenMap_coe N).prod (QuotientGroup.isOpenMap_coe N)       · exact continuous_quot_mk.prod_map continuous_quot_mk       · exact (surjective_quot_mk _).prodMap (surjective_quot_mk _)     exact quot.continuous_iff.2 cont   continuous_inv := by     have quot := IsOpenMap.to_quotientMap       (QuotientGroup.isOpenMap_coe N) continuous_quot_mk (surjective_quot_mk _)     rw [quot.continuous_iff]     exact continuous_quot_mk.comp continuous_inv

TopologicalGroup.exists_antitone_basis_n.code:
TopologicalGroup.exists_antitone_basis_nhds_one.{w} (G : Type w) [TopologicalSpace G] [Group G] [TopologicalGroup G]
  [FirstCountableTopology G] : ∃ u, (𝓝 1).HasAntitoneBasis u ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), u (n + 1) * u (n + 1) ⊆ u n
TopologicalGroup.exists_antitone_basis_n.comment:
Any first countable topological group has an antitone neighborhood basis `u : ℕ → Set G` for
which `(u (n + 1)) ^ 2 ⊆ u n`. The existence of such a neighborhood basis is a key tool for
`QuotientGroup.completeSpace`
TopologicalGroup.exists_antitone_basis_n.description: In any first countable topological group, there exists a neighborhood basis such that the square of each set in the basis is contained in the preceding set.

explanatories.mul_one: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element in a multiplicative structure by one results in that same element.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.continuous_mul: The multiplication operation in a topological space is continuous when the space has a multiplication structure that ensures continuity.
explanatories.subset_closure: Every set is contained within its closure in a topological space.
explanatories.isClosed_closure: The closure of a set in a topological space is always a closed set.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.interior_subset: The interior of a set is contained within the set itself in a topological space.
explanatories.isOpen_interior: The interior of a set in a topological space is always an open set.
explanatories.Set.image_subset_iff: The image of a set under a function is a subset of another set if and only if the original set is a subset of the preimage of that other set, illustrating a Galois connection between image and preimage.
explanatories.Set.mul_subset_mul_left: The theorem states that if one set is a subset of another, then scaling both sets by a fixed set leads to a new set that is a subset of the scaled version of the second set.
explanatories.IsOpen.closure_mul: The closure of the product of a set with an open set in a topological group is equal to the product of the closure of the set and the open set itself.
explanatories.RegularSpace.of_exists_mem_nhds_isClosed: This theorem states that if every neighborhood of a point in a topological space contains a closed subset that is also contained in that neighborhood, then the space is a regular space.
explanatories.Continuous.tendsto': If a function is continuous at a point, then it tends to the value of that function at that point as the input approaches it.
explanatories.mem_nhds_prod_iff: This theorem characterizes membership in the neighborhood of a point in the product space as the existence of neighborhoods around each component whose product is contained within the set.
explanatories.Set.image_prod: The image of a product of two sets under a binary function is equal to the image obtained by applying the function to all pairs formed from the elements of those sets.
explanatories.Filter.mem_of_superset: A theorem stating that if a set belongs to a filter and is a subset of another set, then that other set also belongs to the filter.
explanatories.Set.subset_mul_left: The theorem states that if one set is non-empty and contains the multiplicative identity, then any subset of that set, when multiplied by the non-empty set, is included in the resulting set.
explanatories.mem_interior_iff_mem_nhds: A point is in the interior of a set if and only if the set contains a neighborhood around that point.

TopologicalGroup.regularSpace.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) TopologicalGroup.regularSpace : RegularSpace G := by   refine .of_exists_mem_nhds_isClosed_subset fun a s hs ↦ ?_   have : Tendsto (fun p : G × G => p.1 * p.2) (𝓝 (a, 1)) (𝓝 a) :=     continuous_mul.tendsto' _ _ (mul_one a)   rcases mem_nhds_prod_iff.mp (this hs) with ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hUV⟩   rw [← image_subset_iff, image_prod] at hUV   refine ⟨closure U, mem_of_superset hU subset_closure, isClosed_closure, ?_⟩   calc     closure U ⊆ closure U * interior V := subset_mul_left _ (mem_interior_iff_mem_nhds.2 hV)     _ = U * interior V := isOpen_interior.closure_mul U     _ ⊆ U * V := mul_subset_mul_left interior_subset     _ ⊆ s := hUV
TopologicalGroup.regularSpace.description: A topological group is considered a regular space, meaning that any closed set and a point not in that set can be separated by neighborhoods.

  [TopologicalGroup G] (S : Subgroup G) (hS : Tendsto (⇑S.subtype) cofinite (cocompact G)) :

Subgroup.properlyDiscontinuousSMul_of_te.comment:
A subgroup `S` of a topological group `G` acts on `G` properly discontinuously on the left, if
it is discrete in the sense that `S ∩ K` is finite for all compact `K`. (See also
`DiscreteTopology`.)

explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.Filter.cofinite: A definition describing the cofinite filter as consisting of subsets whose complements are finite.

Subgroup.properlyDiscontinuousSMul_of_te.description: If a subgroup of a topological group tends to map cofinite sets to the cocompact topology, then it acts on the group properly discontinuously.

`DiscreteTopology`.)

If `G` is Hausdorff, this can be combined with `t2Space_of_properlyDiscontinuousSMul_of_t2Space`
to show that the quotient group `G ⧸ S` is Hausdorff.

compact_open_separated_mul_right.comment:

such that `K * V ⊆ U`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.IsCompact: This defines the property of a set within a topological space being compact, which requires that for any nontrivial filter containing the set, there is an element within the set such that every set in the filter intersects with every neighborhood of that element.

compact_open_separated_mul_right.description: For a compact set contained within an open set in a topological group, there exists an open neighborhood around the identity such that the product of the compact set with this neighborhood is still contained in the open set.

explanatories.Equiv.mulLeft: Left multiplication by an element in a group defines a permutation of the group's elements.
explanatories.Homeomorph.mulLeft: The action of multiplying by an element on the left in a topological group establishes a homeomorphism between the group and itself.
explanatories.Equiv.mulRight: Right multiplication by an element in a group defines a permutation of the group's elements.
explanatories.Homeomorph.mulRight: The action of multiplying by an element on the right in a topological group establishes a homeomorphism between the group and itself.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Continuous.continuousAt: If a function is continuous on its entire domain, then it is also continuous at any specific point in that domain.
explanatories.Inducing.continuous: An inducing map between two topological spaces is a continuous function.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.True.intro: The statement establishes that the proposition of truth is inherently valid, with a specific proof confirming its truth.
explanatories.Set.Subset.rfl: Every set is a subset of itself.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.
explanatories.WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace.exists_compact: In a weakly locally compact space, every point has a neighborhood that is both compact and contains the point.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.denseSeq: A dense sequence is a sequence of elements from a non-empty separable topological space that is used to approximate every point in the space.
explanatories.Homeomorph.isCompact_preimage: This theorem states that a set is compact if and only if its preimage under a homeomorphism is compact as well.
explanatories.Set.iUnion_eq_univ_iff: The union of a family of sets equals the universal set if and only if every element in the universal set belongs to at least one of the sets in the family.
explanatories.Homeomorph.apply_symm_apply: Applying a homeomorphism to the result of its inverse yields the original element, confirming that the inverse effectively reverses the mapping.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.denseRange_denseSeq: The countable dense sequence in a separable topological space has a range that is dense in the space.
explanatories.Dense.inter_nhds_nonempty: If a set is dense in a topological space and another set contains a neighborhood of a point, then their intersection is nonempty.

explanatories.continuous_const: The constant function from one topological space to another is continuous.
explanatories.Continuous.mul: The pointwise multiplication of two continuous functions from a topological space to a space with a continuous multiplication structure is itself continuous.
explanatories.continuous_id: The identity function is continuous in any topological space.
explanatories.ContinuousAt.mul: If two functions are continuous at a certain point in a topological space, then their pointwise multiplication is also continuous at that same point.

toUnits_homeomorph.comment: If `G` is a group with topological `⁻¹`, then it is homeomorphic to its units.

explanatories.Inducing.continuous_iff: A function is continuous if and only if its composition with another function, which is an inducing map, is also continuous.
explanatories.QuotientMap.continuous_iff: A quotient map is continuous if and only if the composition of that map with another function is also continuous.
explanatories.MulEquiv.toEquiv: The underlying equivalence of a multiplicative equivalence is a structure that connects two multiplicative types.
explanatories.Units.continuous_iff: A function from a topological space to the units of a monoid is continuous if and only if the function that extracts the underlying values is continuous and the function that takes the inverse of those values is also continuous.
explanatories.Units.continuous_val: The mapping that assigns each element of a monoid to its corresponding unit is continuous in the context of topological spaces.

toUnits_homeomorph.fullDefinition: def toUnits_homeomorph [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [ContinuousInv G] : G ≃ₜ Gˣ where   toEquiv := toUnits.toEquiv   continuous_toFun := Units.continuous_iff.2 ⟨continuous_id, continuous_inv⟩   continuous_invFun := Units.continuous_val
toUnits_homeomorph.description: A group equipped with a topological inverse is homeomorphic to its group of units.

  [TopologicalSpace β] : (α × β)ˣ ≃ₜ αˣ × βˣ
Units.Homeomorph.prodUnits.comment:
The topological group isomorphism between the units of a product of two monoids, and the product
of the units of each monoid.

explanatories.Continuous.fst': This theorem establishes that the composition of a continuous function with the first projection of a product space remains continuous.
explanatories.Continuous.prod_mk: This theorem establishes that the product of two continuous functions is also a continuous function in the context of topological spaces.
explanatories.Continuous.snd': This theorem states that if a function is continuous, then the function obtained by applying it to the second component of ordered pairs is also continuous.
explanatories.Inducing.continuous_iff: A function is continuous if and only if its composition with another function, which is an inducing map, is also continuous.
explanatories.Prod.fst: This defines a function that retrieves the first element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.continuous_fst: This theorem asserts that the first projection function from a product space to one of its component spaces is continuous.
explanatories.continuous_snd: This theorem asserts that the second projection map from the Cartesian product of two topological spaces is continuous.
explanatories.QuotientMap.continuous_iff: A quotient map is continuous if and only if the composition of that map with another function is also continuous.
explanatories.MulEquiv.toEquiv: The underlying equivalence of a multiplicative equivalence is a structure that connects two multiplicative types.
explanatories.Units.continuous_iff: A function from a topological space to the units of a monoid is continuous if and only if the function that extracts the underlying values is continuous and the function that takes the inverse of those values is also continuous.
explanatories.Units.continuous_val: The mapping that assigns each element of a monoid to its corresponding unit is continuous in the context of topological spaces.
explanatories.Units.continuous_coe_inv: The mapping that takes a unit in a monoid and gives its inverse is continuous in the context of a topological space.
explanatories.MulEquiv.prodUnits: There is a monoid isomorphism between the group of units of the product of two monoids and the product of the groups of units of the individual monoids.
explanatories.Continuous.units_map: The composition of a continuous homomorphism from one monoid to another, when restricted to the units of the source monoid, remains continuous.
explanatories.MonoidHom.fst: The natural projection homomorphism from the product of two monoids to the first monoid is defined.
explanatories.MonoidHom.snd: The natural projection homomorphism maps pairs from the product of two monoids to the second component of each pair.

Units.Homeomorph.prodUnits.fullDefinition: def Homeomorph.prodUnits : (α × β)ˣ ≃ₜ αˣ × βˣ where   continuous_toFun :=     (continuous_fst.units_map (MonoidHom.fst α β)).prod_mk       (continuous_snd.units_map (MonoidHom.snd α β))   continuous_invFun :=     Units.continuous_iff.2       ⟨continuous_val.fst'.prod_mk continuous_val.snd',         continuous_coe_inv.fst'.prod_mk continuous_coe_inv.snd'⟩   toEquiv := MulEquiv.prodUnits.toEquiv
Units.Homeomorph.prodUnits.description: The structure establishes a topological isomorphism between the units of a product of two monoids and the product of the units of each individual monoid.

explanatories.MulEquiv.prodUnits: There is a monoid isomorphism between the group of units of the product of two monoids and the product of the groups of units of the individual monoids.
explanatories.Continuous.units_map: The composition of a continuous homomorphism from one monoid to another, when restricted to the units of the source monoid, remains continuous.
explanatories.MonoidHom.fst: The natural projection homomorphism from the product of two monoids to the first monoid is defined.
explanatories.MonoidHom.snd: The natural projection homomorphism maps pairs from the product of two monoids to the second component of each pair.

AddUnits.Homeomorph.sumAddUnits.description: The structure establishes a topological isomorphism between the units of a product of two monoids and the product of the units of each individual monoid.

GroupTopology.coinduced.comment:

topology such that `f` is continuous and `β` is a topological group.

explanatories.TopologicalSpace.coinduced: The coinduced topology on a space is defined such that a set is considered open if the preimage of that set under a given function is open, thus ensuring that the function remains continuous while providing the finest topology.

GroupTopology.coinduced.fullDefinition: def coinduced {α β : Type*} [t : TopologicalSpace α] [Group β] (f : α → β) : GroupTopology β :=   sInf { b : GroupTopology β | TopologicalSpace.coinduced f t ≤ b.toTopologicalSpace }
GroupTopology.coinduced.description: The coinduced group topology on a group is the most refined topology that ensures a given mapping from one space is continuous while maintaining the structure of a topological group.

TopologicalAbelianization.comment:
The topological abelianization of `absoluteGaloisGroup`, that is, the quotient of
`absoluteGaloisGroup` by the topological closure of its commutator subgroup.

explanatories.Subgroup.topologicalClosure: The topological closure of a subgroup in a topological group is also a subgroup.

TopologicalAbelianization.description: This defines the topological abelianization of a group, which is obtained by taking the quotient of the group by the topological closure of its commutator subgroup.

smul_singleton_mem_nhds_of_sigmaCompact.code:
smul_singleton_mem_nhds_of_sigmaCompact.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {X : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace G]
  [TopologicalSpace X] [Group G] [TopologicalGroup G] [MulAction G X] [SigmaCompactSpace G] [BaireSpace X] [T2Space X]
  [ContinuousSMul G X] [IsPretransitive G X] {U : Set G} (hU : U ∈ 𝓝 1) (x : X) : U • {x} ∈ 𝓝 x
smul_singleton_mem_nhds_of_sigmaCompact.comment:
Consider a sigma-compact group acting continuously and transitively on a Baire space. Then
the orbit map is open around the identity. It follows in `isOpenMap_smul_of_sigmaCompact` that it
is open around any point.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

smul_singleton_mem_nhds_of_sigmaCompact.description: The action of a sigma-compact topological group on a Baire space is such that the image of a neighborhood of the identity under the group action includes a neighborhood around any point in the space.

isOpenMap_smul_of_sigmaCompact.code:
isOpenMap_smul_of_sigmaCompact.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {X : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace G] [TopologicalSpace X]
  [Group G] [TopologicalGroup G] [MulAction G X] [SigmaCompactSpace G] [BaireSpace X] [T2Space X] [ContinuousSMul G X]
  [IsPretransitive G X] (x : X) : IsOpenMap fun g => g • x
isOpenMap_smul_of_sigmaCompact.comment:
Consider a sigma-compact group acting continuously and transitively on a Baire space. Then
the orbit map is open. This is a version of the open mapping theorem, valid notably for the
action of a sigma-compact locally compact group on a locally compact space.
isOpenMap_smul_of_sigmaCompact.description: The action of a sigma-compact topological group on a Baire space defines an open mapping for the orbit function at any point in the space.

QuotientGroup.continuousSMul.{w} {G : Type w} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [TopologicalGroup G] {Γ : Subgroup G}
  [LocallyCompactSpace G] : ContinuousSMul G (G ⧸ Γ)

explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.Prod.mk: A pair is constructed from two given terms, resulting in a tuple that combines them.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.mk: This definition indicates a procedure for mapping elements of a group to their corresponding equivalence classes in the quotient group formed by a specified subgroup.
explanatories.continuous_coinduced_rng: This theorem asserts that a function is continuous with respect to the coinduced topology on the target space if it is continuous from the original topological space.
explanatories.Continuous.comp: The composition of two continuous functions in topological spaces is itself continuous.
explanatories.continuous_mul: The multiplication operation in a topological space is continuous when the space has a multiplication structure that ensures continuity.
explanatories.QuotientMap.continuous_lift_prod_right: The theorem establishes that if there is a quotient map from one topological space to another and a continuous function defined on the product of spaces, then this function is also continuous.
explanatories.quotientMap_quotient_mk': This theorem demonstrates that the quotient map induced by a setoid on a topological space is a quotient map.

QuotientGroup.continuousSMul.fullDefinition: instance QuotientGroup.continuousSMul [LocallyCompactSpace G] : ContinuousSMul G (G ⧸ Γ) where   continuous_smul := by     let F : G × G ⧸ Γ → G ⧸ Γ := fun p => p.1 • p.2     change Continuous F     have H : Continuous (F ∘ fun p : G × G => (p.1, QuotientGroup.mk p.2)) := by       change Continuous fun p : G × G => QuotientGroup.mk (p.1 * p.2)       exact continuous_coinduced_rng.comp continuous_mul     exact QuotientMap.continuous_lift_prod_right quotientMap_quotient_mk' H
QuotientGroup.continuousSMul.description: The quotient of a topological group by a subgroup is equipped with a continuous scalar multiplication.

ContinuousAt.comp_div_cases.code:
ContinuousAt.comp_div_cases.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {G₀ : Type u_3} [GroupWithZero G₀]
  [TopologicalSpace G₀] [HasContinuousInv₀ G₀] [ContinuousMul G₀] [TopologicalSpace α] [TopologicalSpace β] {a : α}
  {f g : α → G₀} (h : α → G₀ → β) (hf : ContinuousAt f a) (hg : ContinuousAt g a)
  (hh : g a ≠ 0 → ContinuousAt (↿h) (a, f a / g a)) (h2h : g a = 0 → Tendsto (↿h) (𝓝 a ×ˢ ⊤) (𝓝 (h a 0))) :
  ContinuousAt (fun x => h x (f x / g x)) a
ContinuousAt.comp_div_cases.comment:
The function `f x / g x` is discontinuous when `g x = 0`. However, under appropriate
conditions, `h x (f x / g x)` is still continuous.  The condition is that if `g a = 0` then `h x y`
must tend to `h a 0` when `x` tends to `a`, with no information about `y`. This is represented by
the `⊤` filter.  Note: `tendsto_prod_top_iff` characterizes this convergence in uniform spaces.  See
also `Filter.prod_top` and `Filter.mem_prod_top`.

explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.HasContinuousInv₀: The inverse function is continuous at all points except zero.

ContinuousAt.comp_div_cases.description: The continuity of a function that combines two other functions divided by a variable term is maintained under certain conditions, particularly when the denominator approaches zero, by ensuring the function behaves predictably at that point.

SubmodulesBasis.toModuleFilterBasis.fullDefinition: def toModuleFilterBasis : ModuleFilterBasis R M where   sets := { U | ∃ i, U = B i }   nonempty := by     inhabit ι     exact ⟨B default, default, rfl⟩   inter_sets := by     rintro _ _ ⟨i, rfl⟩ ⟨j, rfl⟩     cases' hB.inter i j with k hk     use B k     constructor     · use k     · exact hk   zero' := by     rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩     exact (B i).zero_mem   add' := by     rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩     use B i     constructor     · use i     · rintro x ⟨y, y_in, z, z_in, rfl⟩       exact (B i).add_mem y_in z_in   neg' := by     rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩     use B i     constructor     · use i     · intro x x_in       exact (B i).neg_mem x_in   conj' := by     rintro x₀ _ ⟨i, rfl⟩     use B i     constructor     · use i     · simp   smul' := by     rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩     use univ     constructor     · exact univ_mem     · use B i       constructor       · use i       · rintro _ ⟨a, -, m, hm, rfl⟩         exact (B i).smul_mem _ hm   smul_left' := by     rintro x₀ _ ⟨i, rfl⟩     use B i     constructor     · use i     · intro m       exact (B i).smul_mem _   smul_right' := by     rintro m₀ _ ⟨i, rfl⟩     exact hB.smul m₀ i

explanatories.UniformContinuous.comp: The composition of two uniformly continuous functions is also uniformly continuous.
explanatories.UniformContinuous.inv: The inverse of a uniformly continuous function is also uniformly continuous, ensuring that the closeness of points is maintained.
explanatories.uniformity: This defines a filter on the product of a uniform space with itself, derived from the structure of the uniform space.
explanatories.UniformSpace.comap: The inverse image of a uniformity on a uniform space under a function generates a new uniform space that captures the structure of the original space.
explanatories.UniformAddGroup.comap: The composition of a uniform group homomorphism with a uniform space yields a uniform group on the initial group.
explanatories.UniformGroup.comap: The composition of a uniform group homomorphism with a uniform space yields a uniform group on the initial group.
explanatories.Filter.comap: A definition of a filter that is obtained by applying an inverse mapping to another filter, specifying how sets relate under this construction.
explanatories.nhds_eq_comap_uniformity: The neighborhood of a point in a uniform space is equal to the preimage of the uniformity structure under the function that pairs the point with elements of the space.
explanatories.Filter.comap_comap: A theorem demonstrating that the composition of two filter transformations is equivalent to applying the composition of the corresponding functions within a single transformation on the filter.
explanatories.Filter.mem_map: A theorem establishing that a set belongs to the image of a filter under a function if and only if the preimage of that set belongs to the original filter.
explanatories.Filter.mem_of_superset: A theorem stating that if a set belongs to a filter and is a subset of another set, then that other set also belongs to the filter.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.comap: A theorem asserting that if a filter has a basis, then the filter obtained by pulling back the basis through a function also has a basis characterized by the preimages of the original sets.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.Filter.tendsto_comap_iff: A theorem stating that a function converges to a limit under a filter if and only if the composition of that function with another function also converges to a limit under a different filter derived from the second function.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.comp: A theorem stating that the composition of two functions that tend to maps between respective filters also results in a function that tends to map from the original filter to the final one.
explanatories.Filter.tendsto_comap: A theorem establishing that the limit of a function, when considered under the context of a filter's pullback, converges to the original filter.
explanatories.Filter.tendsto_id: A theorem stating that the identity function converges with respect to a given filter if the filter itself converges.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.inv: The convergence of a function to a value in a topological group implies that the convergence of its inverse occurs to the inverse of that value.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.le_comap: A theorem asserting that if a function converges with respect to one filter to a limit defined by another filter, then the first filter is dominated by the filter obtained by taking the preimage of the second filter through the function.
explanatories.exists_nhds_one_split: If a set contains a neighborhood of the identity element in a topological space with continuous multiplication, then there exists a smaller neighborhood around the identity such that the product of any two points within it remains in the original set.
explanatories.Filter.mem_lift': The theorem states that if a given set belongs to a filter, then the image of that set under a specified function will belong to the lift of the filter with respect to that function.
explanatories.Filter.preimage_mem_comap: A theorem stating that the preimage of a set belonging to a filter is also a member of the filter's comap under a given function.
explanatories.nhds_translation_div: The neighborhood of the identity element in a topological group under translation by a specific element corresponds to the neighborhood of that element itself when considering division by that element.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Continuous.comp: The composition of two continuous functions in topological spaces is itself continuous.

TopologicalGroup.toUniformSpace.fullDefinition: def TopologicalGroup.toUniformSpace : UniformSpace G where   uniformity := comap (fun p : G × G => p.2 / p.1) (𝓝 1)   symm :=     have : Tendsto (fun p : G × G ↦ (p.2 / p.1)⁻¹) (comap (fun p : G × G ↦ p.2 / p.1) (𝓝 1))       (𝓝 1⁻¹) := tendsto_id.inv.comp tendsto_comap     by simpa [tendsto_comap_iff]   comp := Tendsto.le_comap fun U H ↦ by     rcases exists_nhds_one_split H with ⟨V, V_nhds, V_mul⟩     refine mem_map.2 (mem_of_superset (mem_lift' <| preimage_mem_comap V_nhds) ?_)     rintro ⟨x, y⟩ ⟨z, hz₁, hz₂⟩     simpa using V_mul _ hz₂ _ hz₁   nhds_eq_comap_uniformity _ := by simp only [comap_comap, (· ∘ ·), nhds_translation_div]
TopologicalGroup.toUniformSpace.description: A topological group can be equipped with a uniform structure that corresponds to its group operations and topology.

DenseInducing.extend_Z_bilin.comment:
Bourbaki GT III.6.5 Theorem I:
ℤ-bilinear continuous maps from dense images into a complete Hausdorff group extend by continuity.
Note: Bourbaki assumes that α and β are also complete Hausdorff, but this is not necessary.
DenseInducing.extend_Z_bilin.description: Continuous maps that are bilinear and defined on dense images can be extended by continuity into a complete uniform space.

QuotientGroup.completeSpace'.code:
QuotientGroup.completeSpace'.{u} (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [TopologicalGroup G]
  [FirstCountableTopology G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] [CompleteSpace G] : CompleteSpace (G ⧸ N)
QuotientGroup.completeSpace'.comment:
The quotient `G ⧸ N` of a complete first countable topological group `G` by a normal subgroup
is itself complete. [N. Bourbaki, *General Topology*, IX.3.1 Proposition 4][bourbaki1966b]

Because a topological group is not equipped with a `UniformSpace` instance by default, we must
explicitly provide it in order to consider completeness. See `QuotientGroup.completeSpace` for a
version in which `G` is already equipped with a uniform structure.

explanatories.inv_inv: This theorem demonstrates that taking the inverse of an element twice in a group retrieves the original element.
explanatories.Continuous.comp: The composition of two continuous functions in topological spaces is itself continuous.
explanatories.Filter.NeBot.map: A theorem stating that if a filter is non-empty, then the image of that filter under any mapping is also non-empty.
explanatories.TopologicalGroup.exists_antitone_basis_n: In any first countable topological group, there exists a neighborhood basis such that the square of each set in the basis is contained in the preceding set.
explanatories.Filter.HasAntitoneBasis.map: A theorem stating that the image of a filter with an antitone basis under a function also has an antitone basis formed by the images of the sets in that basis.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.nhds_eq: The neighborhood of an element in a quotient group is equal to the image under the group homomorphism of the neighborhood of the corresponding element in the original group.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.mk_one: The theorem establishes that the image of the identity element of a group in its quotient by a normal subgroup is the identity element of the quotient group.
explanatories.UniformSpace.complete_of_cauchySeq_tends: A uniform space with a countable basis is complete if every Cauchy sequence converges to some limit within the space.
explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.cauchySeq_iff: A sequence is Cauchy if and only if for every basis element, there exists a threshold beyond which all pairs of sequence terms lie within the corresponding entourage.
explanatories.ge_iff_le: The relation of one element being greater than or equal to another is equivalent to the latter being less than or equal to the former.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.forall_true_left: This theorem states that for any property dependent on a true proposition, it is equivalent to asserting that the property holds for the specific instance of true.
explanatories.Set.mem_image: An element is in the image of a set under a function if and only if there exists an element in the original set that maps to it via the function.
explanatories.le_max_left: This theorem states that in a linear order, any element is less than or equal to the maximum of itself and another element.
explanatories.LE.le.trans_lt: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is strictly less than the third.
explanatories.lt_add_one: This theorem establishes that any element in a partially ordered set that includes zero and one is always less than that element plus one.
explanatories.le_max_right: This theorem asserts that in a linear order, any element is less than or equal to the maximum of itself and another element.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.LT.lt.le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than a second, then it is also less than or equal to that second element.
explanatories.mul_inv_cancel_left: This theorem states that in a group, multiplying an element by the inverse of itself followed by another element yields the second element unchanged.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.mk_mul: The theorem establishes that the product of two elements in a group, when taken in the context of a normal subgroup, corresponds to the product of their respective equivalence classes in the quotient group.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.mk_inv: The theorem asserts that the inverse of an element in a group is equivalent to the inverse of its image in the quotient group formed by a normal subgroup.
explanatories.inv_div: The theorem asserts that the inverse of the quotient of two elements in a division monoid is equal to the quotient of the second element by the first.
explanatories.div_mul_cancel: In a group, dividing an element by another and then multiplying by the same divisor returns the original element.
explanatories.Nat.recOn: This function defines a way to construct a proof or value for a specified type based on an initial case for zero and a rule for how to handle successor cases in the natural numbers.
explanatories.Classical.choose: The existence of an element satisfying a property guarantees the ability to select one such element.
explanatories.Classical.choose_spec: Selecting an element that satisfies a property guarantees that this element indeed possesses that property.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.mk_surjective: This theorem establishes that the function mapping elements of a group to their corresponding equivalence classes in the quotient group is surjective.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.

explanatories.PSigma.snd: The second component of a dependent pair provides the value associated with the first element of that pair.

explanatories.Nat.decreasingInduction': There is no definition or content to summarize.
explanatories.div_mul_div_cancel': In a group, dividing one element by another and then multiplying by a third element divided by the same second results in dividing the first element by the third element.
explanatories.div_self': In a group, the division of any element by itself yields the identity element.
explanatories.mem_of_mem_nhds: If a set is a member of the neighborhood of a point, then that point must be an element of the set.
explanatories.Filter.HasAntitoneBasis.mem: A theorem stating that if a filter has an antitone basis, then each set associated with that basis is an element of the filter.
explanatories.cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete: A Cauchy sequence in a complete uniform space converges to some limit.
explanatories.tendsto_nhds_of_cauchySeq_of_subseq: If a Cauchy sequence has a convergent subsequence, then the original sequence also converges to the same limit.
explanatories.strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ: A function defined on natural numbers is strictly monotone if it preserves the order such that each value is less than the value of the subsequent integer.
explanatories.StrictMono.tendsto_atTop: This theorem states that a strictly increasing function defined on natural numbers approaches positive infinity as its input approaches positive infinity.
explanatories.continuous_coinduced_rng: This theorem asserts that a function is continuous with respect to the coinduced topology on the target space if it is continuous from the original topological space.
explanatories.funext: If two functions yield the same output for every input, then those functions are considered equal.

Moreover, we may choose a     sequential antitone neighborhood basis `u` for `𝓝 (1 : G)` so that `(u (n + 1)) ^ 2 ⊆ u n`, and     this descends to an antitone neighborhood basis `v` for `𝓝 (1 : G ⧸ N)`. Since `𝓤 (G ⧸ N)` is     countably generated, it suffices to show any Cauchy sequence `x` converges. -/   letI : UniformSpace (G ⧸ N) := TopologicalGroup.toUniformSpace (G ⧸ N)   letI : UniformSpace G := TopologicalGroup.toUniformSpace G   haveI : (𝓤 (G ⧸ N)).IsCountablyGenerated := comap.isCountablyGenerated _ _   obtain ⟨u, hu, u_mul⟩ := TopologicalGroup.exists_antitone_basis_nhds_one G   obtain ⟨hv, v_anti⟩ := hu.map ((↑) : G → G ⧸ N)   rw [← QuotientGroup.nhds_eq N 1, QuotientGroup.mk_one] at hv   refine UniformSpace.complete_of_cauchySeq_tendsto fun x hx => ?_   /- Given `n : ℕ`, for sufficiently large `a b : ℕ`, given any lift of `x b`, we can find a lift     of `x a` such that the quotient of the lifts lies in `u n`. -/   have key₀ : ∀ i j : ℕ, ∃ M : ℕ, j < M ∧ ∀ a b : ℕ, M ≤ a → M ≤ b →       ∀ g : G, x b = g → ∃ g' : G, g / g' ∈ u i ∧ x a = g' := by     have h𝓤GN : (𝓤 (G ⧸ N)).HasBasis (fun _ ↦ True) fun i ↦ { x | x.snd / x.fst ∈ (↑) '' u i } := by       simpa [uniformity_eq_comap_nhds_one'] using hv.comap _     rw [h𝓤GN.cauchySeq_iff] at hx     simp only [ge_iff_le, mem_setOf_eq, forall_true_left, mem_image] at hx     intro i j     rcases hx i with ⟨M, hM⟩     refine ⟨max j M + 1, (le_max_left _ _).trans_lt (lt_add_one _), fun a b ha hb g hg => ?_⟩     obtain ⟨y, y_mem, hy⟩ :=       hM a (((le_max_right j _).trans (lt_add_one _).le).trans ha) b         (((le_max_right j _).trans (lt_add_one _).le).trans hb)     refine       ⟨y⁻¹ * g, by         simpa only [div_eq_mul_inv, mul_inv_rev, inv_inv, mul_inv_cancel_left] using y_mem, ?_⟩     rw [QuotientGroup.mk_mul, QuotientGroup.mk_inv, hy, hg, inv_div, div_mul_cancel]   /- Inductively construct a subsequence `φ : ℕ → ℕ` using `key₀` so that if `a b : ℕ` exceed     `φ (n + 1)`, then we may find lifts whose quotients lie within `u n`. -/   set φ : ℕ → ℕ := fun n => Nat.recOn n (choose <| key₀ 0 0) fun k yk => choose <| key₀ (k + 1) yk   have hφ :     ∀ n : ℕ,       φ n < φ (n + 1) ∧ construct a sequence `x' n : G` of lifts of `x (φ (n + 1))` such that quotients of     successive terms lie in `x' n / x' (n + 1) ∈ u (n + 1)`. We actually need the proofs that each     term is a lift to construct the next term, so we use a Σ-type. -/   set x' : ∀ n, PSigma fun g : G => x (φ (n + 1)) = g := fun n =>     Nat.recOn n       ⟨choose (QuotientGroup.mk_surjective (x (φ 1))),         (choose_spec (QuotientGroup.mk_surjective (x (φ 1)))).symm⟩       fun k hk =>       ⟨choose <| (hφ k).2 _ _ (hφ (k + 1)).1.le le_rfl hk.fst hk.snd,         (choose_spec <| (hφ k).2 _ _ (hφ (k + 1)).1.le le_rfl hk.fst hk.snd).2⟩   have hx' : ∀ n : ℕ, (x' n).fst / (x' (n + 1)).fst ∈ u (n + 1) := fun n =>     (choose_spec <| (hφ n).2 _ _ (hφ (n + 1)).1.le le_rfl (x' n).fst (x' n).snd).1   /- The sequence `x'` is Cauchy. This is where we exploit the condition on `u`. The key idea     is to show by decreasing induction that `x' m / x' n ∈ u m` if `m ≤ n`. -/   have x'_cauchy : CauchySeq fun n => (x' n).fst := by     have h𝓤G : (𝓤 G).HasBasis (fun _ => True) fun i => { x | x.snd / x.fst ∈ u i } := by       simpa [uniformity_eq_comap_nhds_one'] using hu.toHasBasis.comap _     rw [h𝓤G.cauchySeq_iff']     simp only [ge_iff_le, mem_setOf_eq, forall_true_left]     exact fun m =>       ⟨m, fun n hmn =>         Nat.decreasingInduction'           (fun k _ _ hk => u_mul k ⟨_, hx' k, _, hk, div_mul_div_cancel' _ _ _⟩) hmn           (by simpa only [div_self'] using mem_of_mem_nhds (hu.mem _))⟩   /- Since `G` is complete, `x'` converges to some `x₀`, and so the image of this sequence under     the quotient map converges to `↑x₀`. quotient_group.complete_space'.completeS.code:
QuotientGroup.completeSpace'.{u} (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [TopologicalGroup G]
  [FirstCountableTopology G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] [CompleteSpace G] : CompleteSpace (G ⧸ N)
quotient_group.complete_space'.completeS.comment:
The quotient `G ⧸ N` of a complete first countable topological group `G` by a normal subgroup
is itself complete. [N. Bourbaki, *General Topology*, IX.3.1 Proposition 4][bourbaki1966b]

Because a topological group is not equipped with a `UniformSpace` instance by default, we must
explicitly provide it in order to consider completeness. See `QuotientGroup.completeSpace` for a
version in which `G` is already equipped with a uniform structure.

QuotientGroup.completeSpace'.completeSpa.comment:
The quotient `G ⧸ N` of a complete first countable topological group `G` by a normal subgroup
is itself complete. [N. Bourbaki, *General Topology*, IX.3.1 Proposition 4][bourbaki1966b]

Because a topological group is not equipped with a `UniformSpace` instance by default, we must
explicitly provide it in order to consider completeness. See `QuotientGroup.completeSpace` for a
version in which `G` is already equipped with a uniform structure.

explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.comp: A theorem stating that the composition of two functions that tend to maps between respective filters also results in a function that tends to map from the original filter to the final one.
explanatories.ContinuousAt.tendsto: If a function is continuous at a point, then it has the property that its value approaches the function's output at that point when the input approaches the point.
explanatories.Continuous.tendsto: A continuous function at a point preserves the convergence of sequences by ensuring that the limit of the function's output at that point is the image of the limit of the input.

explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.

explanatories.mul_inv_rev: This theorem asserts that the inverse of the product of two elements in a division monoid is equal to the product of their individual inverses in reverse order.
explanatories.inv_inv: This theorem demonstrates that taking the inverse of an element twice in a group retrieves the original element.
explanatories.Continuous.comp: The composition of two continuous functions in topological spaces is itself continuous.
explanatories.Filter.NeBot.map: A theorem stating that if a filter is non-empty, then the image of that filter under any mapping is also non-empty.

explanatories.Filter.HasAntitoneBasis.map: A theorem stating that the image of a filter with an antitone basis under a function also has an antitone basis formed by the images of the sets in that basis.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.nhds_eq: The neighborhood of an element in a quotient group is equal to the image under the group homomorphism of the neighborhood of the corresponding element in the original group.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.mk_one: The theorem establishes that the image of the identity element of a group in its quotient by a normal subgroup is the identity element of the quotient group.
explanatories.UniformSpace.complete_of_cauchySeq_tends: A uniform space with a countable basis is complete if every Cauchy sequence converges to some limit within the space.
explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.cauchySeq_iff: A sequence is Cauchy if and only if for every basis element, there exists a threshold beyond which all pairs of sequence terms lie within the corresponding entourage.
explanatories.ge_iff_le: The relation of one element being greater than or equal to another is equivalent to the latter being less than or equal to the former.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.forall_true_left: This theorem states that for any property dependent on a true proposition, it is equivalent to asserting that the property holds for the specific instance of true.

explanatories.le_max_left: This theorem states that in a linear order, any element is less than or equal to the maximum of itself and another element.
explanatories.LE.le.trans_lt: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is strictly less than the third.
explanatories.lt_add_one: This theorem establishes that any element in a partially ordered set that includes zero and one is always less than that element plus one.
explanatories.le_max_right: This theorem asserts that in a linear order, any element is less than or equal to the maximum of itself and another element.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.LT.lt.le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than a second, then it is also less than or equal to that second element.
explanatories.mul_inv_cancel_left: This theorem states that in a group, multiplying an element by the inverse of itself followed by another element yields the second element unchanged.

explanatories.QuotientGroup.mk_inv: The theorem asserts that the inverse of an element in a group is equivalent to the inverse of its image in the quotient group formed by a normal subgroup.
explanatories.inv_div: The theorem asserts that the inverse of the quotient of two elements in a division monoid is equal to the quotient of the second element by the first.
explanatories.div_mul_cancel: In a group, dividing an element by another and then multiplying by the same divisor returns the original element.
explanatories.Nat.recOn: This function defines a way to construct a proof or value for a specified type based on an initial case for zero and a rule for how to handle successor cases in the natural numbers.
explanatories.Classical.choose: The existence of an element satisfying a property guarantees the ability to select one such element.
explanatories.Classical.choose_spec: Selecting an element that satisfies a property guarantees that this element indeed possesses that property.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.mk_surjective: This theorem establishes that the function mapping elements of a group to their corresponding equivalence classes in the quotient group is surjective.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.PSigma.fst: The first component of a dependent pair provides the underlying element from the pair structure.
explanatories.PSigma.snd: The second component of a dependent pair provides the value associated with the first element of that pair.
explanatories.Filter.HasAntitoneBasis.toHasBasis: A theorem that establishes that a filter with an antitone basis also satisfies the condition of having a basis that is trivially true for every element in the corresponding sets.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.cauchySeq_iff': A sequence is Cauchy if and only if for every basis element, there exists a threshold beyond which all pairs of sequence terms and a fixed subsequent term lie within the corresponding entourage.
explanatories.Nat.decreasingInduction': There is no definition or content to summarize.
explanatories.div_mul_div_cancel': In a group, dividing one element by another and then multiplying by a third element divided by the same second results in dividing the first element by the third element.
explanatories.div_self': In a group, the division of any element by itself yields the identity element.
explanatories.mem_of_mem_nhds: If a set is a member of the neighborhood of a point, then that point must be an element of the set.
explanatories.Filter.HasAntitoneBasis.mem: A theorem stating that if a filter has an antitone basis, then each set associated with that basis is an element of the filter.
explanatories.cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete: A Cauchy sequence in a complete uniform space converges to some limit.
explanatories.tendsto_nhds_of_cauchySeq_of_subseq: If a Cauchy sequence has a convergent subsequence, then the original sequence also converges to the same limit.
explanatories.strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ: A function defined on natural numbers is strictly monotone if it preserves the order such that each value is less than the value of the subsequent integer.
explanatories.StrictMono.tendsto_atTop: This theorem states that a strictly increasing function defined on natural numbers approaches positive infinity as its input approaches positive infinity.
explanatories.continuous_coinduced_rng: This theorem asserts that a function is continuous with respect to the coinduced topology on the target space if it is continuous from the original topological space.
explanatories.funext: If two functions yield the same output for every input, then those functions are considered equal.

:= TopologicalGroup.toUniformSpace G   haveI : (𝓤 (G ⧸ N)).IsCountablyGenerated := comap.isCountablyGenerated _ _   obtain ⟨u, hu, u_mul⟩ := TopologicalGroup.exists_antitone_basis_nhds_one G   obtain ⟨hv, v_anti⟩ := hu.map ((↑) : G → G ⧸ N)   rw [← QuotientGroup.nhds_eq N 1, QuotientGroup.mk_one] at hv   refine UniformSpace.complete_of_cauchySeq_tendsto fun x hx => ?_   /- Given `n : ℕ`, for sufficiently large `a b : ℕ`, given any lift of `x b`, we can find a lift     of `x a` such that the quotient of the lifts lies in `u n`. -/   have key₀ : ∀ i j : ℕ, ∃ M : ℕ, j < M ∧ ∀ a b : ℕ, M ≤ a → M ≤ b →       ∀ g : G, x b = g → ∃ g' : G, g / g' ∈ u i ∧ x a = g' := by     have h𝓤GN : (𝓤 (G ⧸ N)).HasBasis (fun _ ↦ True) fun i ↦ { x | x.snd / x.fst ∈ (↑) '' u i } := by       simpa [uniformity_eq_comap_nhds_one'] using hv.comap _     rw [h𝓤GN.cauchySeq_iff] at hx     simp only [ge_iff_le, mem_setOf_eq, forall_true_left, mem_image] at hx     intro i j     rcases hx i with ⟨M, hM⟩ construct a sequence `x' n : G` of lifts of `x (φ (n + 1))` such that quotients of     successive terms lie in `x' n / x' (n + 1) ∈ u (n + 1)`. We actually need the proofs that each     term is a lift to construct the next term, so we use a Σ-type. -/   set x' : ∀ n, PSigma fun g : G => x (φ (n + 1)) = g := fun n =>     Nat.recOn n       ⟨choose (QuotientGroup.mk_surjective (x (φ 1))),         (choose_spec (QuotientGroup.mk_surjective (x (φ 1)))).symm⟩       fun k hk =>       ⟨choose <| (hφ k).2 _ _ (hφ (k + 1)).1.le le_rfl hk.fst hk.snd,         (choose_spec <| (hφ k).2 _ _ (hφ (k + 1)).1.le le_rfl hk.fst hk.snd).2⟩   have hx' : ∀ n : ℕ, (x' n).fst / (x' (n + 1)).fst ∈ u (n + 1) := fun n =>     (choose_spec <| (hφ n).2 _ _ (hφ (n + 1)).1.le le_rfl (x' n).fst (x' n).snd).1   /- The sequence `x'` is Cauchy. explanatories.mul_inv_cancel_left: This theorem states that in a group, multiplying an element by the inverse of itself followed by another element yields the second element unchanged.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.mk_mul: The theorem establishes that the product of two elements in a group, when taken in the context of a normal subgroup, corresponds to the product of their respective equivalence classes in the quotient group.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.mk_inv: The theorem asserts that the inverse of an element in a group is equivalent to the inverse of its image in the quotient group formed by a normal subgroup.
explanatories.inv_div: The theorem asserts that the inverse of the quotient of two elements in a division monoid is equal to the quotient of the second element by the first.
explanatories.div_mul_cancel: In a group, dividing an element by another and then multiplying by the same divisor returns the original element.
explanatories.Nat.recOn: This function defines a way to construct a proof or value for a specified type based on an initial case for zero and a rule for how to handle successor cases in the natural numbers.
explanatories.Classical.choose: The existence of an element satisfying a property guarantees the ability to select one such element.
explanatories.Classical.choose_spec: Selecting an element that satisfies a property guarantees that this element indeed possesses that property.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.mk_surjective: This theorem establishes that the function mapping elements of a group to their corresponding equivalence classes in the quotient group is surjective.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.PSigma.fst: The first component of a dependent pair provides the underlying element from the pair structure.
explanatories.PSigma.snd: The second component of a dependent pair provides the value associated with the first element of that pair.
explanatories.Filter.HasAntitoneBasis.toHasBasis: A theorem that establishes that a filter with an antitone basis also satisfies the condition of having a basis that is trivially true for every element in the corresponding sets.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.cauchySeq_iff': A sequence is Cauchy if and only if for every basis element, there exists a threshold beyond which all pairs of sequence terms and a fixed subsequent term lie within the corresponding entourage.
explanatories.Nat.decreasingInduction': There is no definition or content to summarize.
explanatories.div_mul_div_cancel': In a group, dividing one element by another and then multiplying by a third element divided by the same second results in dividing the first element by the third element.
explanatories.div_self': In a group, the division of any element by itself yields the identity element.
explanatories.mem_of_mem_nhds: If a set is a member of the neighborhood of a point, then that point must be an element of the set.
explanatories.Filter.HasAntitoneBasis.mem: A theorem stating that if a filter has an antitone basis, then each set associated with that basis is an element of the filter.
explanatories.cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete: A Cauchy sequence in a complete uniform space converges to some limit.
explanatories.tendsto_nhds_of_cauchySeq_of_subseq: If a Cauchy sequence has a convergent subsequence, then the original sequence also converges to the same limit.
explanatories.strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ: A function defined on natural numbers is strictly monotone if it preserves the order such that each value is less than the value of the subsequent integer.
explanatories.StrictMono.tendsto_atTop: This theorem states that a strictly increasing function defined on natural numbers approaches positive infinity as its input approaches positive infinity.
explanatories.continuous_coinduced_rng: This theorem asserts that a function is continuous with respect to the coinduced topology on the target space if it is continuous from the original topological space.
explanatories.funext: If two functions yield the same output for every input, then those functions are considered equal.

:= TopologicalGroup.toUniformSpace G   haveI : (𝓤 (G ⧸ N)).IsCountablyGenerated := comap.isCountablyGenerated _ _   obtain ⟨u, hu, u_mul⟩ := TopologicalGroup.exists_antitone_basis_nhds_one G   obtain ⟨hv, v_anti⟩ := hu.map ((↑) : G → G ⧸ N)   rw [← QuotientGroup.nhds_eq N 1, QuotientGroup.mk_one] at hv   refine UniformSpace.complete_of_cauchySeq_tendsto fun x hx => ?_   /- Given `n : ℕ`, for sufficiently large `a b : ℕ`, given any lift of `x b`, we can find a lift     of `x a` such that the quotient of the lifts lies in `u n`. -/   have key₀ : ∀ i j : ℕ, ∃ M : ℕ, j < M ∧ ∀ a b : ℕ, M ≤ a → M ≤ b →       ∀ g : G, x b = g → ∃ g' : G, g / g' ∈ u i ∧ x a = g' := by     have h𝓤GN : (𝓤 (G ⧸ N)).HasBasis (fun _ ↦ True) fun i ↦ { x | x.snd / x.fst ∈ (↑) '' u i } := by       simpa [uniformity_eq_comap_nhds_one'] using hv.comap _     rw [h𝓤GN.cauchySeq_iff] at hx     simp only [ge_iff_le, mem_setOf_eq, forall_true_left, mem_image] at hx     intro i j     rcases hx i with ⟨M, hM⟩ [QuotientGroup.mk_mul, QuotientGroup.mk_inv, hy, hg, inv_div, div_mul_cancel]   /- Inductively construct a subsequence `φ : ℕ → ℕ` using `key₀` so that if `a b : ℕ` exceed     `φ (n + 1)`, then we may QuotientAddGroup.completeSpace'.complete.code:
QuotientGroup.completeSpace'.{u} (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [TopologicalGroup G]
  [FirstCountableTopology G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] [CompleteSpace G] : CompleteSpace (G ⧸ N)
QuotientAddGroup.completeSpace'.complete.comment:
The quotient `G ⧸ N` of a complete first countable topological group `G` by a normal subgroup
is itself complete. [N. Bourbaki, *General Topology*, IX.3.1 Proposition 4][bourbaki1966b]

Because a topological group is not equipped with a `UniformSpace` instance by default, we must
explicitly provide it in order to consider completeness. See `QuotientGroup.completeSpace` for a
version in which `G` is already equipped with a uniform structure.

QuotientAddGroup.completeSpace'.code:
QuotientAddGroup.completeSpace'.{u} (G : Type u) [AddGroup G] [TopologicalSpace G] [TopologicalAddGroup G]

QuotientAddGroup.completeSpace'.comment:
The quotient `G ⧸ N` of a complete first countable topological additive group
`G` by a normal additive subgroup is itself complete. Consequently, quotients of Banach spaces by
subspaces are complete. [N. Bourbaki, *General Topology*, IX.3.1 Proposition 4][bourbaki1966b]

Because an additive topological group is not equipped with a `UniformSpace` instance by default,
we must explicitly provide it in order to consider completeness. See
`QuotientAddGroup.completeSpace` for a version in which `G` is already equipped with a uniform
structure.

  (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] [hG : CompleteSpace G] : CompleteSpace (G ⧸ N)
QuotientGroup.completeSpace.comment:
The quotient `G ⧸ N` of a complete first countable uniform group `G` by a normal subgroup
is itself complete. In contrast to `QuotientGroup.completeSpace'`, in this version `G` is
already equipped with a uniform structure.
[N. Bourbaki, *General Topology*, IX.3.1 Proposition 4][bourbaki1966b]

Even though `G` is equipped with a uniform structure, the quotient `G ⧸ N` does not inherit a
uniform structure, so it is still provided manually via `TopologicalGroup.toUniformSpace`.
In the most common use cases, this coincides (definitionally) with the uniform structure on the
quotient obtained via other means.

  [TopologicalSpace M] [AddCommGroup M] [ContinuousAdd M] [Module R M] [ContinuousSMul R M]

Submodule.eq_top_of_nonempty_interior'.comment:
If `M` is a topological module over `R` and `0` is a limit of invertible elements of `R`, then
`⊤` is the only submodule of `M` with a nonempty interior.
This is the case, e.g., if `R` is a nontrivially normed field.

explanatories.IsUnit: An element in a monoid is defined as a unit if there exists another element in the monoid that serves as its two-sided inverse.

Submodule.eq_top_of_nonempty_interior'.description: If a submodule of a topological module has a nonempty interior and zero is approached by invertible elements, then that submodule must be the entire space.

Module.punctured_nhds_neBot.code:
Module.punctured_nhds_neBot.{u_1, u_2} (R : Type u_1) (M : Type u_2) [Ring R] [TopologicalSpace R] [TopologicalSpace M]
  [AddCommGroup M] [ContinuousAdd M] [Module R M] [ContinuousSMul R M] [Nontrivial M] [(𝓝[≠] 0).NeBot]
  [NoZeroSMulDivisors R M] (x : M) : (𝓝[≠] x).NeBot
Module.punctured_nhds_neBot.comment:
Let `R` be a topological ring such that zero is not an isolated point (e.g., a nontrivially
normed field, see `NormedField.punctured_nhds_neBot`). Let `M` be a nontrivial module over `R`
such that `c • x = 0` implies `c = 0 ∨ x = 0`. Then `M` has no isolated points. We formulate this
using `NeBot (𝓝[≠] x)`.

This lemma is not an instance because Lean would need to find `[ContinuousSMul ?m_1 M]` with
unknown `?m_1`. We register this as an instance for `R = ℝ` in `Real.punctured_nhds_module_neBot`.
One can also use `haveI := Module.punctured_nhds_neBot R M` in a proof.
Module.punctured_nhds_neBot.description: In a nontrivial module over a topological ring where zero is not isolated, the punctured neighborhood around any nonzero point is a nonempty filter, indicating that the module does not have isolated points.

for the definition, although in applications `M` and `M₂` will be topological modules over the
topological semiring `R`.

ContinuousSemilinearEquivClass.map_conti.comment:
`ContinuousSemilinearEquivClass F σ M M₂` asserts `F` is a type of bundled continuous
`σ`-semilinear equivs `M → M₂`.  See also `ContinuousLinearEquivClass F R M M₂` for the case
where `σ` is the identity map on `R`.  A map `f` between an `R`-module and an `S`-module over a ring
homomorphism `σ : R →+* S` is semilinear if it satisfies the two properties `f (x + y) = f x + f y`
and `f (c • x) = (σ c) • f x`.

explanatories.outParam: This defines a mechanism to create output parameters in type classes, allowing type inference to determine specific types based on other known values.
explanatories.ContinuousMapClass.map_continuous: This theorem asserts that a mapping defined by a continuous map preserves the property of continuity when applied to a topological space.

ContinuousSemilinearEquivClass.map_conti.description: If a type represents a continuous semilinear equivalence between two modules, then the function associated with this type is continuous.

`R`-linear equivs `M → M₂`. This is an abbreviation for
`ContinuousSemilinearEquivClass F (RingHom.id R) M M₂`.

explanatories.RingHom.id: This definition describes the identity ring homomorphism that maps each element of a semiring to itself.
explanatories.outParam: This defines a mechanism to create output parameters in type classes, allowing type inference to determine specific types based on other known values.
explanatories.LinearMap.id: This definition specifies the identity linear map for a module over a semiring that maps each element to itself.
explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged and can be used to explicitly assign a type to an expression for typeclass inference purposes.
explanatories.IsOpenMap.id: The identity function is an open map for any topological space.

linearMapOfMemClosureRangeCoe.{u_1, u_2, u_4, u_5} {M₁ : Type u_1} {M₂ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} {S : Type u_5}
  [TopologicalSpace M₂] [T2Space M₂] [Semiring R] [Semiring S] [AddCommMonoid M₁] [AddCommMonoid M₂] [Module R M₁]
  [Module S M₂] [ContinuousConstSMul S M₂] [ContinuousAdd M₂] {σ : R →+* S} (f : M₁ → M₂)
  (hf : f ∈ closure (Set.range DFunLike.coe)) : M₁ →ₛₗ[σ] M₂
linearMapOfMemClosureRangeCoe.comment:
Constructs a bundled linear map from a function and a proof that this function belongs to the
closure of the set of linear maps.

explanatories.LinearMap.range: This definition states that the range of a linear map between modules is a submodule of the codomain module.
explanatories.map_smul: This theorem states that a morphism that is equivariant with respect to the actions of a monoid preserves the action when applied to the product of an element from the monoid and an element from the type.
explanatories.Set.MapsTo.closure: If a continuous function maps a set to another set, then it also maps the closure of the first set to the closure of the second set.
explanatories.SemilinearEquivClass.map_smulₛₗ: This theorem establishes that applying a semilinear equivalence to the scalar multiplication of an element in a module results in a transformed scalar multiplication of the image of that element under the equivalence.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.
explanatories.addMonoidHomOfMemClosureRangeCoe: A function that lies in the closure of the range of a bundled monoid homomorphism can be transformed into a monoid homomorphism between two monoids within a topological space.
explanatories.isClosed_setOf_map_smul: The set of functions that satisfy a given condition related to scalar multiplication is a closed set in the topological space.
explanatories.IsClosed.closure_subset_iff: A closed set contains the closure of another set if and only if the original set is entirely contained within the closed set.
explanatories.Set.range_subset_iff: The range of a function is a subset of a set if and only if every value in the range is included in that set.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smulₛₗ: This theorem states that applying a linear map to a scalar multiplied by a vector yields the same result as multiplying the result of the linear map by the scalar.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul': This theorem asserts that a specific linear map interacts with scalar multiplication in such a way that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is equivalent to multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar's image under a specified semiring homomorphism.
explanatories.LinearMap.CompatibleSMul.map_smul: This theorem shows that scalar multiplication in one module can be interchanged with a linear map to another module.
explanatories.Set.EqOn.closure: This theorem states that if two continuous functions are equal on a set, they remain equal on the closure of that set in a T2 topological space.

linearMapOfMemClosureRangeCoe.fullDefinition: def linearMapOfMemClosureRangeCoe (f : M₁ → M₂)     (hf : f ∈ closure (Set.range ((↑) : (M₁ →ₛₗ[σ] M₂) → M₁ → M₂))) : M₁ →ₛₗ[σ] M₂ :=   { addMonoidHomOfMemClosureRangeCoe f hf with     map_smul' := (isClosed_setOf_map_smul M₁ M₂ σ).closure_subset_iff.2       (Set.range_subset_iff.2 LinearMap.map_smulₛₗ) hf }
linearMapOfMemClosureRangeCoe.description: This defines a way to create a bundled linear map from a function, given that the function is in the closure of linear maps.

  [ContinuousSMul S M₂] (c : M₁ →L[R] S) (f : M₂) : M₁ →L[R] M₂
ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight.comment:
The linear map `fun x => c x • f`.  Associates to a scalar-valued linear map and an element of
`M₂` the `M₂`-valued linear map obtained by multiplying the two (a.k.a. tensoring by `M₂`).
See also `ContinuousLinearMap.smulRightₗ` and `ContinuousLinearMap.smulRightL`.

ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight.description: The construction defines a continuous linear map that takes a scalar-valued linear map and an element from a module, producing a new linear map by scaling the output by the given element.

explanatories.Homeomorph.continuous_invFun: This theorem establishes that the inverse of a homeomorphism between two topological spaces is itself a continuous function.
explanatories.IsOpenMap.prod: This theorem establishes that if two mappings are open, then the mapping formed by taking their respective outputs from a product of their domains is also an open map.

ContinuousLinearEquiv.skewProd.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {R : Type u_1} [Semiring R] {M : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace M]
  [AddCommGroup M] {M₂ : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace M₂] [AddCommGroup M₂] {M₃ : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace M₃]
  [AddCommGroup M₃] {M₄ : Type u_5} [TopologicalSpace M₄] [AddCommGroup M₄] [Module R M] [Module R M₂] [Module R M₃]
  [Module R M₄] [TopologicalAddGroup M₄] (e : M ≃L[R] M₂) (e' : M₃ ≃L[R] M₄) (f : M →L[R] M₄) : (M × M₃) ≃L[R] M₂ × M₄
ContinuousLinearEquiv.skewProd.comment:
Equivalence given by a block lower diagonal matrix. `e` and `e'` are diagonal square blocks,
and `f` is a rectangular block below the diagonal.

ContinuousLinearEquiv.equivOfRightInverse.{u_1, u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_1} [Ring R] {M : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace M]
  [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {M₂ : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace M₂] [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂]
  [TopologicalAddGroup M] (f₁ : M →L[R] M₂) (f₂ : M₂ →L[R] M) (h : Function.RightInverse ⇑f₂ ⇑f₁) :
  M ≃L[R] M₂ × ↥(LinearMap.ker f₁)
ContinuousLinearEquiv.equivOfRightInvers.comment:
A pair of continuous linear maps such that `f₁ ∘ f₂ = id` generates a continuous
linear equivalence `e` between `M` and `M₂ × f₁.ker` such that `(e x).2 = x` for `x ∈ f₁.ker`,
`(e x).1 = f₁ x`, and `(e (f₂ y)).2 = 0`. The map is given by `e x = (f₁ x, x - f₂ (f₁ x))`.

ContinuousLinearEquiv.equivOfRightInvers.fullDefinition: def equivOfRightInverse (f₁ : M →L[R] M₂) (f₂ : M₂ →L[R] M) (h : Function.RightInverse f₂ f₁) :     M ≃L[R] M₂ × ker f₁ :=   equivOfInverse (f₁.prod (f₁.projKerOfRightInverse f₂ h)) (f₂.coprod (ker f₁).subtypeL)     (fun x => by simp) fun ⟨x, y⟩ => by       -- Porting note: `simp` timeouts.       rw [ContinuousLinearMap.coprod_apply,         Submodule.subtypeL_apply, _root_.map_add, ContinuousLinearMap.prod_apply, h x,         ContinuousLinearMap.projKerOfRightInverse_comp_inv,         ContinuousLinearMap.prod_apply, LinearMap.map_coe_ker,         ContinuousLinearMap.projKerOfRightInverse_apply_idem, Prod.mk_add_mk, add_zero, zero_add]

continuous_linear_equiv.equiv_of_right_i.comment:
A pair of continuous linear maps such that `f₁ ∘ f₂ = id` generates a continuous
linear equivalence `e` between `M` and `M₂ × f₁.ker` such that `(e x).2 = x` for `x ∈ f₁.ker`,
`(e x).1 = f₁ x`, and `(e (f₂ y)).2 = 0`. The map is given by `e x = (f₁ x, x - f₂ (f₁ x))`.

ContinuousLinearMap.inverse.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {M₂ : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace M]
  [TopologicalSpace M₂] [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M₂] [Module R M₂] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] :
  (M →L[R] M₂) → M₂ →L[R] M
ContinuousLinearMap.inverse.comment:
Introduce a function `inverse` from `M →L[R] M₂` to `M₂ →L[R] M`, which sends `f` to `f.symm` if
`f` is a continuous linear equivalence and to `0` otherwise.  This definition is somewhat ad hoc,
but one needs a fully (rather than partially) defined inverse function for some purposes, including
for calculus.

explanatories.Or.symm: The disjunction operation is symmetric, meaning that if one proposition is true or the other, then the order of these propositions can be reversed.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm: The inverse of a continuous linear equivalence between two modules also forms a continuous linear equivalence between those modules.
explanatories.Homeomorph.symm: This definition establishes the inverse of a homeomorphism, mapping a homeomorphism from one topological space to its corresponding homeomorphism in the reverse direction.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Classical.choose: The existence of an element satisfying a property guarantees the ability to select one such element.
explanatories.Ring.inverse: This defines a function that maps each element of a monoid with zero to its inverse if it is invertible, and to zero if it is not.
explanatories.MulEquiv.symm: The inverse of a multiplicative isomorphism is itself a multiplicative isomorphism between the two types.

ContinuousLinearMap.inverse.fullDefinition: noncomputable def inverse : (M →L[R] M₂) → M₂ →L[R] M := fun f =>   if h : ∃ e : M ≃L[R] M₂, (e : M →L[R] M₂) = f then ((Classical.choose h).symm : M₂ →L[R] M) else 0
ContinuousLinearMap.inverse.description: The definition introduces a function that maps a continuous linear map to its inverse if it represents a continuous linear equivalence, and to zero otherwise.

In the specific case of continuous multilinear maps on spaces indexed by `Fin (n+1)`, where one
can build an element of `(i : Fin (n+1)) → M i` using `cons`, one can express directly the
additivity of a multilinear map along the first variable.

explanatories.Nat.succ: This states the successor function for natural numbers, which yields the next integer by adding one to a given natural number.
explanatories.List.cons: The construction of a list adds a specified element at the beginning, followed by the remaining elements of an existing list.
explanatories.Fin.succ: The successor of a finite number is produced by increasing its upper limit, resulting in a new finite number that is one greater.

ContinuousMultilinearMap.cons_add.description: This theorem establishes that a continuous multilinear map is additive with respect to its first argument when constructed from spaces indexed by finite types, allowing the addition of two inputs to be expressed through the evaluation of the map.

If `f` is continuous multilinear, then `f (Σ_{j₁ ∈ A₁} g₁ j₁, ..., Σ_{jₙ ∈ Aₙ} gₙ jₙ)` is the
sum of `f (g₁ (r 1), ..., gₙ (r n))` where `r` ranges over all functions with `r 1 ∈ A₁`, ...,
`r n ∈ Aₙ`. This follows from multilinearity by expanding successively with respect to each
coordinate.

ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_sum_finset.description: This theorem demonstrates that for a continuous multilinear map, the output obtained from summing over a collection of inputs is equivalent to summing the values of the map evaluated at each combination of those inputs.

ContinuousMultilinearMap.restrictScalars.comment:
Reinterpret an `A`-multilinear map as an `R`-multilinear map, if `A` is an algebra over `R`
and their actions on all involved modules agree with the action of `R` on `A`.

explanatories.ContinuousMultilinearMap.cont: The theorem states that a continuous multilinear map from a family of modules to another module is itself continuous with respect to the topology of the involved spaces.
explanatories.ContinuousMultilinearMap.toMultilinearMa: This definition converts a continuous multilinear map into a general multilinear map between specified modules over a semiring.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.cont: A continuous linear map between two modules is continuous with respect to their topological structures.

ContinuousMultilinearMap.restrictScalars.description: This definition describes a process for interpreting a multilinear map over one algebra as a multilinear map over another algebra when the associated actions on the involved modules are compatible.

Bornology.IsVonNBounded.image_multilinea.comment:
The image of a von Neumann bounded set under a continuous multilinear map
is von Neumann bounded.

This version does not assume that the topologies on the domain and on the codomain
agree with the vector space structure in any way
but it assumes that `ι` is nonempty.

Bornology.IsVonNBounded.image_multilinea.description: The theorem establishes that the image of a von Neumann bounded set under a continuous multilinear map remains von Neumann bounded, without requiring alignment of topological structures between the domain and codomain.

ContinuousMultilinearMap.toUniformOnFun.description: This definition establishes a way to define a topology on continuous multilinear maps by associating them with functions that are uniformly bounded, given a set of input elements from a family of spaces.
