FiberBundle.prod.fullDefinition: noncomputable instance FiberBundle.prod : FiberBundle (F₁ × F₂) (E₁ ×ᵇ E₂) where   totalSpaceMk_inducing' b := by     rw [← (Prod.inducing_diag F₁ E₁ F₂ E₂).of_comp_iff]     exact (totalSpaceMk_inducing F₁ E₁ b).prod_map (totalSpaceMk_inducing F₂ E₂ b)   trivializationAtlas' := { e |     ∃ (e₁ : Trivialization F₁ (π F₁ E₁)) (e₂ : Trivialization F₂ (π F₂ E₂))       (_ : MemTrivializationAtlas e₁) (_ : MemTrivializationAtlas e₂),       e = Trivialization.prod e₁ e₂ }   trivializationAt' b := (trivializationAt F₁ E₁ b).prod (trivializationAt F₂ E₂ b)   mem_baseSet_trivializationAt' b :=     ⟨mem_baseSet_trivializationAt F₁ E₁ b, mem_baseSet_trivializationAt F₂ E₂ b⟩   trivialization_mem_atlas' b :=     ⟨trivializationAt F₁ E₁ b, trivializationAt F₂ E₂ b, inferInstance, inferInstance, rfl⟩

Trivialization.pullback.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Trivialization.pullback (e : Trivialization F (π F E)) (f : K) :     Trivialization F (π F ((f : B' → B) *ᵖ E)) where   toFun z := (z.proj, (e (Pullback.lift f z)).2)   invFun y := @TotalSpace.mk _ F (f *ᵖ E) y.1 (e.symm (f y.1) y.2)   source := Pullback.lift f ⁻¹' e.source   baseSet := f ⁻¹' e.baseSet   target := (f ⁻¹' e.baseSet) ×ˢ univ   map_source' x h := by     simp_rw [e.source_eq, mem_preimage, Pullback.lift_proj] at h     simp_rw [prod_mk_mem_set_prod_eq, mem_univ, and_true_iff, mem_preimage, h]   map_target' y h := by     rw [mem_prod, mem_preimage] at h     simp_rw [e.source_eq, mem_preimage, Pullback.lift_proj, h.1]   left_inv' x h := by     simp_rw [mem_preimage, e.mem_source, Pullback.lift_proj] at h     simp_rw [Pullback.lift, e.symm_apply_apply_mk h]   right_inv' x h := by     simp_rw [mem_prod, mem_preimage, mem_univ, and_true_iff] at h     simp_rw [Pullback.lift_mk, e.apply_mk_symm h]   open_source := by     simp_rw [e.source_eq, ← preimage_comp]     exact e.open_baseSet.preimage ((map_continuous f).comp <| Pullback.continuous_proj F E f)   open_target := ((map_continuous f).isOpen_preimage _ e.open_baseSet).prod isOpen_univ   open_baseSet := (map_continuous f).isOpen_preimage _ e.open_baseSet   continuousOn_toFun :=     (Pullback.continuous_proj F E f).continuousOn.prod       (continuous_snd.comp_continuousOn <|         e.continuousOn.comp (Pullback.continuous_lift F E f).continuousOn Subset.rfl)   continuousOn_invFun := by     dsimp only     simp_rw [(inducing_pullbackTotalSpaceEmbedding F E f).continuousOn_iff, Function.comp,       pullbackTotalSpaceEmbedding]     refine       continuousOn_fst.prod         (e.continuousOn_symm.comp ((map_continuous f).prod_map continuous_id).continuousOn           Subset.rfl)   source_eq := by     dsimp only     rw [e.source_eq]     rfl   target_eq := rfl   proj_toFun y _ := rfl
Trivialization.pullback.description: A fiber bundle trivialization can be adapted to correspond to a trivialization on the pullback bundle via a continuous map from a base space.

ContinuousMap.exists_lift_sigma.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {X : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {Y : ι → Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [(i : ι) → TopologicalSpace (Y i)] [ConnectedSpace X] (f : C(X, (i : ι) × Y i)) : ∃ i g, f = (sigmaMk i).comp g
ContinuousMap.exists_lift_sigma.comment:
Every continuous map from a connected topological space to the disjoint union of a family of
topological spaces is a composition of the embedding `ContinuousMap.sigmMk i : C(Y i, Σ i, Y i)` for
some `i` and a continuous map `g : C(X, Y i)`. See also `Continuous.exists_lift_sigma` for a version
with unbundled functions and `ContinuousMap.sigmaCodHomeomorph` for a homeomorphism defined using
this fact.

TopologicalSpace.eq_induced_by_maps_to_s.description: This theorem states that the topology on a given space is equal to the infimum of the topologies induced by maps that represent membership in open sets of the Sierpiński space.

Set.SeparatesPointsStrongly.code:
Set.SeparatesPointsStrongly.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace α] {𝕜 : Type u_5} [TopologicalSpace 𝕜]
  (s : Set C(α, 𝕜)) : Prop
Set.SeparatesPointsStrongly.comment:
A set of continuous maps "separates points strongly"
if for each pair of distinct points there is a function with specified values on them.

We give a slightly unusual formulation, where the specified values are given by some
function `v`, and we ask `f x = v x ∧ f y = v y`. This avoids needing a hypothesis `x ≠ y`.

In fact, this definition would work perfectly well for a set of non-continuous functions,
but as the only current use case is in the Stone-Weierstrass theorem,
writing it this way avoids having to deal with casts inside the set.
(This may need to change if we do Stone-Weierstrass on non-compact spaces,
where the functions would be continuous functions vanishing at infinity.)
Set.SeparatesPointsStrongly.fullDefinition: def Set.SeparatesPointsStrongly (s : Set C(α, 𝕜)) : Prop :=   ∀ (v : α → 𝕜) (x y : α), ∃ f ∈ s, (f x : 𝕜) = v x ∧ f y = v y
Set.SeparatesPointsStrongly.description: This definition establishes that a set of continuous maps strongly separates points if, for every pair of distinct points, there exists a function that assigns specified values to each point.

Subalgebra.SeparatesPoints.strongly.comment:
Working in continuous functions into a topological field,
a subalgebra of functions that separates points also separates points strongly.

By the hypothesis, we can find a function `f` so `f x ≠ f y`.
By an affine transformation in the field we can arrange so that `f x = a` and `f x = b`.

ContinuousMap.compStarAlgHom'.comment:
The functorial map taking `f : C(X, Y)` to `C(Y, A) →⋆ₐ[𝕜] C(X, A)` given by pre-composition
with the continuous function `f`. See `ContinuousMap.compMonoidHom'` and
`ContinuousMap.compAddMonoidHom'`, `ContinuousMap.compRightAlgHom` for bundlings of

explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.zero_comp: This theorem states that composing any continuous map with the identity continuous map results in the identity continuous map of the codomain.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.one_comp: This theorem states that composing any continuous map with the identity continuous map results in the identity continuous map of the codomain.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.comp: This definition states that the composition of morphisms between additive monoids results in a morphism that also operates within the framework of additive monoids.
explanatories.ZeroHom.map_zero': This theorem asserts that a zero homomorphism maps the zero element of one type to the zero element of another type, thereby preserving the zero value.
explanatories.Algebra.commutes': This theorem asserts that in an algebra over a commutative semiring, the ring homomorphism corresponding to an element commutes with multiplication in the algebra.
explanatories.AlgHom.commutes': This theorem states that for an algebra homomorphism between two algebras over a commutative semiring, applying the ring homomorphism form of the algebra homomorphism to an element mapped from the semiring reproduces the mapping of that element in the target algebra.
explanatories.StarAlgHom.comp: This definition describes the process of composing two star algebra homomorphisms to create a new star algebra homomorphism that connects the first algebra to the third through the second.
explanatories.MonoidHom.map_mul': This theorem states that a certain function maintains the operation of multiplication across the elements it acts upon.
explanatories.RingHom.map_add': This theorem asserts that a ring homomorphism preserves the operation of addition when applied to the sum of two elements.
explanatories.StarAlgHom.map_star': This theorem asserts that a star algebra homomorphism carries the property of preserving the star operation when transforming elements between two algebras.

ContinuousMap.compStarAlgHom'.description: This defines a functorial mapping that takes a continuous function between two topological spaces and associates it with a continuous star algebra homomorphism from the space of continuous mappings into a star algebra back to the original space.

cfcHom.code:
cfcHom.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {p : A → Prop} [CommSemiring R] [StarRing R] [MetricSpace R]
  [TopologicalSemiring R] [ContinuousStar R] [TopologicalSpace A] [Ring A] [StarRing A] [Algebra R A]
  [ContinuousFunctionalCalculus R p] {a : A} (ha : p a) : C(↑(spectrum R a), R) →⋆ₐ[R] A
cfcHom.comment:
The star algebra homomorphism underlying a instance of the continuous functional calculus;
a version for continuous functions on the spectrum.

In this case, the user must supply the fact that `a` satisfies the predicate `p`, for otherwise it
may be the case that no star algebra homomorphism exists. For instance if `R := ℝ` and `a` is an
element whose spectrum (in `ℂ`) is disjoint from `ℝ`, then `spectrum ℝ a = ∅` and so there can be
no star algebra homomorphism between these spaces.

While `ContinuousFunctionalCalculus` is stated in terms of these homomorphisms, in practice the
user should instead prefer `cfc` over `cfcHom`.

cfc.code:
cfc.{u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_3} {A : Type u_4} {p : A → Prop} [CommSemiring R] [StarRing R] [MetricSpace R]
  [TopologicalSemiring R] [ContinuousStar R] [TopologicalSpace A] [Ring A] [StarRing A] [Algebra R A]
  [ContinuousFunctionalCalculus R p] (f : R → R) (a : A) : A
cfc.comment:
This is the *continuous functional calculus* of an element `a : A` applied to bare functions.
When either `a` does not satisfy the predicate `p` (i.e., `a` is not `IsStarNormal`,
`IsSelfAdjoint`, or `0 ≤ a` when `R` is `ℂ`, `ℝ`, or `ℝ≥0`, respectively), or when `f : R → R` is
not continuous on the spectrum of `a`, then `cfc f a` returns the junk value `0`.

This is the primary declaration intended for widespread use of the continuous functional calculus,
and all the API applies to this declaration. For more information, see the module documentation
for `Topology.ContinuousFunction.FunctionalCalculus`.

ContinuousMap.unitsLift.comment:
Equivalence between continuous maps into the units of a monoid with continuous multiplication
and the units of the monoid of continuous maps.

explanatories.Units.continuous_val: The mapping that assigns each element of a monoid to its corresponding unit is continuous in the context of topological spaces.
explanatories.Continuous.comp: The composition of two continuous functions in topological spaces is itself continuous.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.continuous: This theorem states that a continuous map between two topological spaces induces a continuous function when viewed as a function.
explanatories.Inv.inv: This expression defines a function that computes the inverse of an element within a specified type.
explanatories.ContinuousInv.continuous_inv: The inversion operation in a topological group is continuous.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.ext: This theorem asserts that if two continuous maps agree on every point in their domain, then they are identical as functions.
explanatories.Units.mul_inv: The product of a unit element and its inverse in a monoid equals one.
explanatories.Units.inv_mul: The inverse of a unit element in a monoid, when multiplied by the unit itself, equals the identity element of the monoid.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.congr_fun: This theorem asserts that if two continuous maps are equal, then they produce the same output for any input from their domain.
explanatories.continuous_induced_rng: This theorem establishes that a function composed with another function is continuous if and only if the second function is continuous.
explanatories.Continuous.prod_mk: This theorem establishes that the product of two continuous functions is also a continuous function in the context of topological spaces.
explanatories.MulOpposite.continuous_op: The mapping related to the operation of reversing the multiplication in a topological space is continuous.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.ContinuousAt.comp: If one function is continuous at a point and another function is continuous at the image of that point under the first function, then their composition is also continuous at that original point.

ContinuousMap.unitsLift.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between continuous maps into the units of a monoid with continuous multiplication and the units of the monoid of continuous maps.

explanatories.ContinuousMap.starOrderedRing_of_sqrt: This theorem establishes that a certain structure, characterized by a continuous square root function and specific properties of a ring, results in a star-ordered ring of continuous functions mapping from a topological space to the ring.
explanatories.Real.sqrt: The square root function is defined for real numbers, returning zero for negative inputs.
explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.
explanatories.RCLike.star_def: This theorem establishes that the conjugate operation in a relational structure corresponds to the action of a specific endomorphism.
explanatories.RCLike.nonneg_iff: This theorem states that a number in a relational structure is non-negative if and only if its real part is non-negative and its imaginary part is zero.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.And.right: This theorem allows for the extraction of the second component from a conjunction when given a proof of that conjunction.
explanatories.RCLike.conj_eq_iff_im: This theorem establishes an equivalence stating that a particular mapping of an element to itself occurs if and only if the image of that element is trivial, or zero.
explanatories.RCLike.conj_eq_iff_re: This theorem asserts that a complex element in a relational structure is equal to its conjugate if and only if its real part is equal to the element itself.
explanatories.RCLike.conj_ofReal: This theorem demonstrates that the operation defined for complex conjugation in a relational structure leaves real numbers unchanged.
explanatories.RCLike.ofReal_mul: This theorem states that the mapping of the product of two real numbers in a relational structure is equal to the product of their corresponding relational structure representations.
explanatories.Real.mul_self_sqrt: The product of the square root of a nonnegative real number with itself equals that original nonnegative number.
explanatories.And.left: From a conjunction of two propositions, it is possible to extract and prove the first proposition.
explanatories.NNReal.sqrt: This defines an order-preserving equivalence between nonnegative real numbers and their square roots.
explanatories.StarOrderedRing.nonneg_iff: This theorem states that a non-negative element in a star-ordered ring can be characterized as belonging to the additive closure of the set formed by the products of the star operation applied to other elements with themselves.

ContinuousMap.instStarOrderedRingRCLike.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) instStarOrderedRingRCLike {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] :     StarOrderedRing C(α, 𝕜) :=   starOrderedRing_of_sqrt ((↑) ∘ Real.sqrt ∘ re) (by fun_prop) fun x hx ↦ by     simp only [Function.comp_apply,star_def]     obtain hx' := nonneg_iff.mp hx |>.right     rw [← conj_eq_iff_im, conj_eq_iff_re] at hx'     rw [conj_ofReal, ← ofReal_mul, Real.mul_self_sqrt, hx']     rw [nonneg_iff]     simpa using nonneg_iff.mp hx |>.left

explanatories.Star.star: This definition introduces a unary operation on a type that possesses a star structure, mapping an element to another element within the same type.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.le_def: This theorem states that one continuous map is less than or equal to another if and only if it is less than or equal to the other map at every point in the domain.
explanatories.star_mul_self_nonneg: This theorem asserts that for any element in a star-ordered ring, the product of that element with its star results in a non-negative value.
explanatories.RCLike.nonneg_iff: This theorem states that a number in a relational structure is non-negative if and only if its real part is non-negative and its imaginary part is zero.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.coe_coe: This theorem confirms that coercing a continuous map into a function yields the same result as directly evaluating the continuous map as a function.
explanatories.StarOrderedRing.le_iff: This theorem characterizes the order relation in a star-ordered ring by stating that one element is less than or equal to another if and only if the second element can be expressed as the sum of the first element and a certain positive element from an additive submonoid.
explanatories.AddSubmonoid.closure_induction_left: Any property that holds for zero and is preserved under the addition of an element from a set and the result of applying closure to that set also holds for every element in the closure of the set.
explanatories.AddSubmonoid.one: The additive submonoid contains the element representing one if the underlying additive monoid has a multiplicative identity.
explanatories.ZeroMemClass.zero_mem: Any element of a set that belongs to a zero-member class contains the zero element.
explanatories.add_assoc: This theorem states that the addition operation is associative, meaning that the grouping of three elements being added does not affect the result.
explanatories.StarOrderedRing.nonneg_iff: This theorem states that a non-negative element in a star-ordered ring can be characterized as belonging to the additive closure of the set formed by the products of the star operation applied to other elements with themselves.
explanatories.le_antisymm: This theorem establishes that in a partial order, if one element is less than or equal to another and vice versa, then the two elements must be equal.
explanatories.le_add_of_nonneg_right: This theorem states that if one element is non-negative, then any element is less than or equal to the sum of itself and that non-negative element.
explanatories.AddMemClass.add_mem: This theorem states that a set defined by an addition property is closed under the operation of addition.
explanatories.AddSubmonoid.subset_closure: The closure of a set in an additive submonoid includes the entire set.
explanatories.AddSubmonoid.closure_induction': This theorem provides a method to prove properties about elements in the additive closure of a set using induction based on the operations within the additive structure.
explanatories.AddSubmonoid.mul: The multiplication of additive submonoids in a semiring is defined as the smallest submodule containing all products of elements from the two submonoids.

ContinuousMapZero.instStarOrderedRing.fullDefinition: instance instStarOrderedRing {R : Type*}     [TopologicalSpace R] [OrderedCommSemiring R] [NoZeroDivisors R] [StarRing R] [StarOrderedRing R]     [TopologicalSemiring R] [ContinuousStar R] [StarOrderedRing C(α, R)] :     StarOrderedRing C(α, R)₀ where   le_iff f g := by     constructor     · rw [le_def, ← ContinuousMap.coe_coe, ← ContinuousMap.coe_coe g, ← ContinuousMap.le_def,         StarOrderedRing.le_iff]       rintro ⟨p, hp_mem, hp⟩       induction hp_mem using AddSubmonoid.closure_induction_left generalizing f g with       | one => exact ⟨0, zero_mem _, by ext x; congrm($(hp) x)⟩       | mul_left s s_mem p p_mem hp' =>         obtain ⟨s, rfl⟩ := s_mem         simp only at *         have h₀ : (star s * s + p) 0 = 0 := by simpa using congr($(hp) 0).symm         rw [← add_assoc] at hp         have p'₀ : 0 ≤ p 0 := by rw [← StarOrderedRing.nonneg_iff] at p_mem; exact p_mem 0         have s₉ : (star s * s) 0 = 0 := le_antisymm ((le_add_of_nonneg_right p'₀).trans_eq h₀)           (star_mul_self_nonneg (s 0))         have s₀' : s 0 = 0 := by aesop         let s' : C(α, R)₀ := ⟨s, s₀'⟩         obtain ⟨p', hp'_mem, rfl⟩ := hp' (f + star s' * s') g hp         refine ⟨star s' * s' + p', ?_, by rw [add_assoc]⟩         exact add_mem (AddSubmonoid.subset_closure ⟨s', rfl⟩) hp'_mem     · rintro ⟨p, hp, rfl⟩       induction hp using AddSubmonoid.closure_induction' generalizing f with       | mem s s_mem =>         obtain ⟨s, rfl⟩ := s_mem         exact fun x ↦ le_add_of_nonneg_right (star_mul_self_nonneg (s x))       | one => simp       | mul g₁ _ g₂ _ h₁ h₂ => calc           f ≤ f + g₁ := h₁ f           _ ≤ (f + g₁) + g₂ := h₂ (f + g₁)           _ = f + (g₁ + g₂) := add_assoc _ _ _

When `α` is compact and `𝕜` is a normed field,

ContinuousMap.idealOfSet.comment:

which vanish on the complement of `s`.

explanatories.Ideal: An ideal in a semiring is an additive submonoid that is closed under multiplication by elements from the semiring.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.coe_add: This theorem asserts that the evaluation of the product of two continuous maps in a topological space corresponds to the product of their individual evaluations.
explanatories.Pi.add_apply: This theorem examines the behavior of function composition involving a constant function that returns the "one" value.
explanatories.add_zero: This theorem states that in any additive structure with a zero element, adding zero to any element results in that same element.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.MulZeroClass.mul_zero: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by zero results in zero, indicating that zero is an absorbing element in multiplication.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Set.Subset.rfl: Every set is a subset of itself.

ContinuousMap.idealOfSet.fullDefinition: def idealOfSet (s : Set X) : Ideal C(X, R) where   carrier := {f : C(X, R) | ∀ x ∈ sᶜ, f x = 0}   add_mem' {f g} hf hg x hx := by simp [hf x hx, hg x hx, coe_add, Pi.add_apply, add_zero]   zero_mem' _ _ := rfl   smul_mem' c f hf x hx := mul_zero (c x) ▸ congr_arg (fun y => c x * y) (hf x hx)
ContinuousMap.idealOfSet.description: This definition describes how to create an ideal in the space of continuous functions that vanish outside a specified subset of a topological space, given a topological ring.

ContinuousMap.idealOpensGI.fullDefinition: def idealOpensGI :     GaloisInsertion (opensOfIdeal : Ideal C(X, 𝕜) → Opens X) fun s => idealOfSet 𝕜 s where   choice I _ := opensOfIdeal I.closure   gc I s := ideal_gc X 𝕜 I s   le_l_u s := (setOfIdeal_ofSet_of_isOpen 𝕜 s.isOpen).ge   choice_eq I hI :=     congr_arg _ <|       Ideal.ext         (Set.ext_iff.mp           (isClosed_of_closure_subset <|               (idealOfSet_ofIdeal_eq_closure I ▸ hI : I.closure ≤ I)).closure_eq)
ContinuousMap.idealOpensGI.description: This definition establishes a Galois insertion relationship between the open sets associated with ideals of continuous functions and the ideals of sets in a compact Hausdorff topological space.

cfcₙHom.comment:
The non-unital star algebra homomorphism underlying a instance of the continuous functional
calculus for non-unital algebras; a version for continuous functions on the quasispectrum.

In this case, the user must supply the fact that `a` satisfies the predicate `p`.

While `NonUnitalContinuousFunctionalCalculus` is stated in terms of these homomorphisms, in practice
the user should instead prefer `cfcₙ` over `cfcₙHom`.

cfcₙ.code:
cfcₙ.{u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_3} {A : Type u_4} {p : A → Prop} [CommSemiring R] [Nontrivial R] [StarRing R]
  [MetricSpace R] [TopologicalSemiring R] [ContinuousStar R] [NonUnitalRing A] [StarRing A] [TopologicalSpace A]
  [Module R A] [IsScalarTower R A A] [SMulCommClass R A A] [NonUnitalContinuousFunctionalCalculus R p] (f : R → R)
  (a : A) : A
cfcₙ.comment:
This is the *continuous functional calculus* of an element `a : A` in a non-unital algebra
applied to bare functions.  When either `a` does not satisfy the predicate `p` (i.e., `a` is not
`IsStarNormal`, `IsSelfAdjoint`, or `0 ≤ a` when `R` is `ℂ`, `ℝ`, or `ℝ≥0`, respectively), or when
`f : R → R` is not continuous on the quasispectrum of `a` or `f 0 ≠ 0`, then `cfcₙ f a` returns the
junk value `0`.

This is the primary declaration intended for widespread use of the continuous functional calculus
for non-unital algebras, and all the API applies to this declaration. For more information, see the
module documentation for `Topology.ContinuousFunction.FunctionalCalculus`.

cfcₙ_def.{u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_3} {A : Type u_4} {p : A → Prop} [CommSemiring R] [Nontrivial R] [StarRing R]

  [Module R A] [IsScalarTower R A A] [SMulCommClass R A A] [NonUnitalContinuousFunctionalCalculus R p] (f : R → R)
  (a : A) :
  cfcₙ f a =
    if h : p a ∧ ContinuousOn f (σₙ R a) ∧ f 0 = 0 then
      (cfcₙHom ⋯) { toFun := (σₙ R a).restrict f, continuous_toFun := ⋯, map_zero' := ⋯ }
    else 0

The non-unital continuous functional calculus obtained by restricting a unital calculus
to functions that map zero to zero. This is an auxiliary definition and is not
intended for use outside this file. The equality between the non-unital and unital
calculi in this case is encoded in the lemma `cfcₙ_eq_cfc`.

explanatories.ContinuousMapZero.comp: This definition describes the composition of two continuous maps that map the zero element in one space to the zero element in another, resulting in a continuous map between the first and the final space.
explanatories.NonUnitalStarAlgHom.comp: This definition describes the composition of two non-unital star algebra homomorphisms, producing another non-unital star algebra homomorphism that maps elements from the first algebra directly to the final algebra through the intermediate one.

explanatories.ContinuousMapZero.toContinuousMapHom: This definition describes a non-unital star algebra homomorphism that represents a coercion from a specific type of continuous maps to a broader class of continuous maps between two topological spaces.

explanatories.spectrum_subset_quasispectrum: This theorem asserts that the spectrum of an element in a commutative semiring is a subset of its quasispectrum.

explanatories.ClosedEmbedding.comp: The composition of two closed embeddings results in another closed embedding between the corresponding topological spaces.

ContinuousMap.attachBound.comment:
Turn a function `f : C(X, ℝ)` into a continuous map into `Set.Icc (-‖f‖) (‖f‖)`,

explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.neg_norm_le_apply: This theorem states that for a continuous function defined on a compact space, the negative norm of the function is less than or equal to the function's value at any point in its domain.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.apply_le_norm: This theorem asserts that for a continuous function defined on a compact space, the value of the function at any point does not exceed its norm.

ContinuousMap.attachBound.fullDefinition: def attachBound (f : C(X, ℝ)) : C(X, Set.Icc (-‖f‖) ‖f‖) where   toFun x := ⟨f x, ⟨neg_norm_le_apply f x, apply_le_norm f x⟩⟩
ContinuousMap.attachBound.description: This definition describes a continuous map that transforms a continuous function into a new map whose values are constrained within specified bounds based on the function's norm.

  (A : Subalgebra ℝ C(X, ℝ)) (f : ↥A) (g : ℝ[X]) : (g.toContinuousMapOn (Set.Icc (-‖f‖) ‖f‖)).comp (↑f).attachBound ∈ A
ContinuousMap.polynomial_comp_attachBoun.comment:
Given a continuous function `f` in a subalgebra of `C(X, ℝ)`, postcomposing by a polynomial
gives another function in `A`.

This lemma proves something slightly more subtle than this:
we take `f`, and think of it as a function into the restricted target `Set.Icc (-‖f‖) ‖f‖)`,
and then postcompose with a polynomial function on that interval.
This is in fact the same situation as above, and so also gives a function in `A`.

ContinuousMap.continuousMap_mem_subalgeb.code:
ContinuousMap.continuousMap_mem_subalgebra_closure_of_separatesPoints.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [CompactSpace X] (A : Subalgebra ℝ C(X, ℝ)) (w : A.SeparatesPoints) (f : C(X, ℝ)) : f ∈ A.topologicalClosure
ContinuousMap.continuousMap_mem_subalgeb.comment:
An alternative statement of the Stone-Weierstrass theorem.

If `A` is a subalgebra of `C(X, ℝ)` which separates points (and `X` is compact),
every real-valued continuous function on `X` is a uniform limit of elements of `A`.

explanatories.Subalgebra.restrictScalars: A subalgebra of a larger algebra can be restricted to a smaller base field, allowing it to be viewed as a subalgebra with respect to that field while preserving the algebraic structure.
explanatories.Subalgebra.comap: The preimage of a subalgebra under an algebra homomorphism is defined as a new subalgebra in the original algebraic structure.
explanatories.RCLike.ofRealAm: This definition describes a linear map that relates real numbers to a type equipped with a relational structure.
explanatories.AlgHom.compLeftContinuous: This definition specifies a way to create a homomorphism between continuous maps from one topological algebra to another, by applying a continuous algebra homomorphism on the left.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.compLeftContinuous: This definition establishes a linear map that represents the composition of continuous maps from one topological space to another, specifically allowing for left multiplication by a continuous linear map.
explanatories.Submodule.restrictScalars: This definition describes the process of forming an S-submodule from an R-submodule by restricting the scalar multiplication from the semiring R to the semiring S.
explanatories.Submodule.comap: This definition introduces the pullback of a submodule through a semilinear map, producing a corresponding submodule in the original space.
explanatories.Polynomial.X: This definition introduces the polynomial variable, also known as the indeterminate, for polynomials over a semiring.

Subalgebra.SeparatesPoints.rclike_to_rea.description: The theorem establishes that if a star subalgebra separates points, then its corresponding real-valued subalgebra will also separate points.

explanatories.ContinuousMapZero.toNNReal_add_add_neg_a: The conversion to non-negative reals of the sum of two continuous functions, combined with the transformations of their negations, equals the conversion to non-negative reals of the negation of that sum added to the conversions of each function.
explanatories.ContinuousMapZero.toNNReal_mul_add_neg_m: The equation establishes a specific algebraic relationship showing that the conversion to non-negative reals of the product of two continuous functions, along with their individual negated transformations, is equivalent to the conversion to non-negative reals of the negation of that product added to the products of their non-negative transformations.

NonUnitalStarAlgHom.realContinuousMapZer.fullDefinition: noncomputable def realContinuousMapZeroOfNNReal (φ : C(X, ℝ≥0)₀ →⋆ₙₐ[ℝ≥0] A) :     C(X, ℝ)₀ →⋆ₙₐ[ℝ] A where   toFun f := φ f.toNNReal - φ (-f).toNNReal   map_zero' := by simp   map_mul' f g := by     have := congr(φ $(f.toNNReal_mul_add_neg_mul_add_mul_neg_eq g))     simp only [map_add, map_mul, sub_mul, mul_sub] at this ⊢     rw [← sub_eq_zero] at this ⊢     rw [← this]     abel   map_add' f g := by     have := congr(φ $(f.toNNReal_add_add_neg_add_neg_eq g))     simp only [map_add, map_mul, sub_mul, mul_sub] at this ⊢     rw [← sub_eq_zero] at this ⊢     rw [← this]     abel   map_smul' r f := by     simp only [MonoidHom.id_apply]     by_cases hr : 0 ≤ r     · lift r to ℝ≥0 using hr       simp only [← smul_def, toNNReal_smul, map_smul, toNNReal_neg_smul, smul_sub]     · rw [not_le, ← neg_pos] at hr       rw [← neg_smul]       nth_rw 1 [← neg_neg r]       nth_rw 3 [← neg_neg r]       lift -r to ℝ≥0 using hr.le with r       simp only [neg_smul, ← smul_def, toNNReal_neg_smul, map_smul, toNNReal_smul, smul_sub,         sub_neg_eq_add]       rw [sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm]   map_star' f := by simp only [star_trivial, star_sub, ← map_star]

explanatories.pow_left_strictMonoOn: The function that raises a number to a non-zero power is strictly monotonic when restricted to the non-negative elements of a strict ordered semiring.
explanatories.zero_le: This theorem states that in a canonically ordered additive commutative monoid, any element is greater than or equal to zero.
explanatories.Continuous.pow: The function raising a continuous mapping to a monoid to a natural number preserves the continuity of the resulting function.
explanatories.Continuous.surjective: This theorem states that a continuous function that approaches infinity in both directions is surjective.

explanatories.Filter.OrderBot.atBot_eq: This theorem states that the filter capturing the behavior of elements approaching the least element in a partially ordered set is equivalent to the filter generated by that least element itself.
explanatories.pos_iff_ne_zero: This theorem establishes that in a canonically ordered additive commutative monoid, an element is positive if and only if it is not equal to zero.

NNReal.powOrderIso.description: This definition characterizes the function that raises non-negative real numbers to a positive integer power as an order isomorphism within the space of non-negative real numbers.

  [ContinuousSMul A E] : IsScalarTower ℝ A E
Real.isScalarTower.comment:
A topological group carries at most one structure of a topological `ℝ`-module, so for any
topological `ℝ`-algebra `A` (e.g. `A = ℂ`) and any topological group that is both a topological
`ℝ`-module and a topological `A`-module, these structures agree.

explanatories.map_real_smul: This theorem confirms that a continuous additive map between two vector spaces over the reals preserves scalar multiplication, meaning it behaves linearly with respect to real coefficients.

edist_le_tsum_of_edist_le_of_tendsto.code:
edist_le_tsum_of_edist_le_of_tendsto.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [PseudoEMetricSpace α] {f : ℕ → α} (d : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞)
  (hf : ∀ (n : ℕ), edist (f n) (f n.succ) ≤ d n) {a : α} (ha : Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 a)) (n : ℕ) :
  edist (f n) a ≤ ∑' (m : ℕ), d (n + m)
edist_le_tsum_of_edist_le_of_tendsto.comment:
If `edist (f n) (f (n+1))` is bounded above by a function `d : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞`,
then the distance from `f n` to the limit is bounded by `∑'_{k=n}^∞ d k`.

explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.Filter.atTop: This definition introduces a filter that captures the behavior of elements approaching infinity in an ordered set, generated by all sets containing elements greater than or equal to any given element.
explanatories.EDist.edist: A distance function is defined on a type, returning non-negative extended real numbers between pairs of its elements.
explanatories.Continuous.edist: This theorem asserts that the pointwise distance between two continuous functions is also a continuous function.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.edist: This theorem states that if two functions converge to two points in a pseudometric space as their input approaches a filter, then the distance between the outputs of these functions also converges to the distance between those two points.
explanatories.Nat.succ: This states the successor function for natural numbers, which yields the next integer by adding one to a given natural number.

edist_le_tsum_of_edist_le_of_tendsto.description: This theorem asserts that if the distances between consecutive terms of a sequence are bounded by a function, then the distance from any term in the sequence to its limit is also bounded by the sum of that function evaluated at indices beyond the term in question.

AddCircle.partialHomeomorphCoe.fullDefinition: @[simps] def partialHomeomorphCoe [DiscreteTopology (zmultiples p)] :     PartialHomeomorph 𝕜 (AddCircle p) where   toFun := (↑)   invFun := fun x ↦ equivIco p a x   source := Ioo a (a + p)   target := {↑a}ᶜ   map_source' := by     intro x hx hx'     exact hx.1.ne' ((coe_eq_coe_iff_of_mem_Ico (Ioo_subset_Ico_self hx)       (left_mem_Ico.mpr (lt_add_of_pos_right a hp.out))).mp hx')   map_target' := by     intro x hx     exact (eq_left_or_mem_Ioo_of_mem_Ico (equivIco p a x).2).resolve_left       (hx ∘ ((equivIco p a).symm_apply_apply x).symm.trans ∘ congrArg _)   left_inv' :=     fun x hx ↦ congrArg _ ((equivIco p a).apply_symm_apply ⟨x, Ioo_subset_Ico_self hx⟩)   right_inv' := fun x _ ↦ (equivIco p a).symm_apply_apply x   open_source := isOpen_Ioo   open_target := isOpen_compl_singleton   continuousOn_toFun := (AddCircle.continuous_mk' p).continuousOn   continuousOn_invFun := by     exact ContinuousAt.continuousOn       (fun _ ↦ continuousAt_subtype_val.comp ∘ continuousAt_equivIco p a)

AddCircle.setAddOrderOfEquiv.fullDefinition: def setAddOrderOfEquiv {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :     { u : AddCircle p | addOrderOf u = n } ≃ { m | m < n ∧ m.gcd n = 1 } :=   Equiv.symm <|     Equiv.ofBijective (fun m => ⟨↑((m : 𝕜) / n * p), addOrderOf_div_of_gcd_eq_one hn m.prop.2⟩)       (by         refine ⟨fun m₁ m₂ h => Subtype.ext ?_, fun u => ?_⟩         · simp_rw [Subtype.ext_iff] at h           rw [← sub_eq_zero, ← coe_sub, ← sub_mul, ← sub_div, ← Int.cast_natCast m₁,             ← Int.cast_natCast m₂, ← Int.cast_sub, coe_eq_zero_iff] at h           obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := h           rw [← mul_div_right_comm, eq_div_iff, mul_comm, ← zsmul_eq_mul, mul_smul_comm, ←             nsmul_eq_mul, ← natCast_zsmul, smul_smul,             (zsmul_strictMono_left hp.out).injective.eq_iff, mul_comm] at hm           swap           · exact Nat.cast_ne_zero.2 hn.ne'           rw [← @Nat.cast_inj ℤ, ← sub_eq_zero]           refine Int.eq_zero_of_abs_lt_dvd ⟨_, hm.symm⟩ (abs_sub_lt_iff.2 ⟨?_, ?_⟩) <;>             apply (Int.sub_le_self _ <| Nat.cast_nonneg _).trans_lt (Nat.cast_lt.2 _)           exacts [m₁.2.1, m₂.2.1]         obtain ⟨m, hmn, hg, he⟩ := (addOrderOf_eq_pos_iff hn).mp u.2         exact ⟨⟨m, hmn, hg⟩, Subtype.ext he⟩)

satisfies `0 ≤ m < n`.

explanatories.AddCircle.coe_add_period: The theorem states that in a linear ordered additive group, adding a specific point to another element results in an equivalent representation of that element within a particular context.
explanatories.Fact.out: This theorem asserts that the property represented by a fact can be retrieved from its corresponding instance.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This theorem states that for any element and a property it satisfies, one can construct a subtype consisting of elements that possess that property.
explanatories.Equiv.right_inv: This theorem states that the inverse function of an equivalence relation has a right inverse that retrieves the original function.
explanatories.Subtype.val: The value of a subtype is the underlying element from the base type that satisfies a given property.
explanatories.Equiv.symm_apply_apply: This theorem shows that applying an equivalence and then its inverse will return the original element from the first type.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.lt_add_of_pos_right: This theorem states that if a positive quantity is added to another quantity, the result will be strictly greater than the original quantity.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Set.Ico_subset_Icc_self: This theorem establishes that the left-open right-closed interval defined by two elements is contained within the left-closed right-closed interval defined by the same elements in a preorder structure.
explanatories.QuotientAddGroup.congr: This definition describes how to lift an isomorphism between two groups to an isomorphism between their respective quotient groups, assuming that the isomorphism preserves the normal subgroups involved.
explanatories.AddEquiv.symm: The definition states that the inverse of an additive isomorphism is also an additive isomorphism.
explanatories.Homeomorph.mk: This theorem establishes a function that creates a homeomorphism between two topological spaces from an equivalence between those spaces, ensuring the functions involved are continuous.
explanatories.Homeomorph.symm: This definition establishes the inverse of a homeomorphism, mapping a homeomorphism from one topological space to its corresponding homeomorphism in the reverse direction.
explanatories.QuotientAddGroup.mk: This definition indicates a procedure for mapping elements of a group to their corresponding equivalence classes in the quotient group formed by a specified subgroup.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.

explanatories.Set.inclusion: The inclusion function maps each element of a subset to its corresponding element in a larger set, assuming the subset is contained within the larger set.
explanatories.Quot.liftOn: The process of lifting a function onto the quotient of a set, while ensuring that equivalent elements map to the same value, can be rearranged so that the quotient appears as the first argument.
explanatories.ne_or_eq: This theorem asserts that for any two elements, they are either not equal or equal, affirming the principle of excluded middle in equality.
explanatories.LE.le.lt_of_ne: A theorem stating that in a partially ordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and they are not equal, then the first element is strictly less than the second.
explanatories.AddCircle.EndpointIdent.mk: This theorem establishes a relationship between specific endpoints within a circular structure and their representation in terms of a given additive group.
explanatories.le_refl: This theorem confirms that in a preorder, any element is related to itself under the less than or equal relation.

AddCircle.equivIccQuot.fullDefinition: def equivIccQuot : 𝕋 ≃ Quot (EndpointIdent p a) where   toFun x := Quot.mk _ <| inclusion Ico_subset_Icc_self (equivIco _ _ x)   invFun x :=     Quot.liftOn x (↑) <| by       rintro _ _ ⟨_⟩       exact (coe_add_period p a).symm   left_inv := (equivIco p a).symm_apply_apply   right_inv :=     Quot.ind <| by       rintro ⟨x, hx⟩       rcases ne_or_eq x (a + p) with (h | rfl)       · revert x         dsimp only         intro x hx h         congr         ext1         apply congr_arg Subtype.val ((equivIco p a).right_inv ⟨x, hx.1, hx.2.lt_of_ne h⟩)       · rw [← Quot.sound EndpointIdent.mk]         dsimp only         congr         ext1         apply congr_arg Subtype.val           ((equivIco p a).right_inv ⟨a, le_refl a, lt_add_of_pos_right a hp.out⟩)
AddCircle.equivIccQuot.description: This definition describes a structural equivalence between an additive circle and the quotient space formed by identifying the endpoints of an interval defined by two points in a linear ordered additive group.

explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.continuous_right_toIcoMod: The theorem establishes that a specific mapping from a linear ordered additive group to a closed interval is continuous at a given point under certain positive conditions.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.Continuous.continuousAt: If a function is continuous on its entire domain, then it is also continuous at any specific point in that domain.
explanatories.ContinuousAt.comp_continuousWithinAt: The composition of a continuous function with another function that is continuous within a set at a point is also continuous within that set at the same point.
explanatories.ContinuousWithinAt.comp: If a function is continuous at a point within a set and it maps that set into another, then the composition of these functions is also continuous at that point within the first set.
explanatories.continuous_left_toIocMod: The theorem establishes that a specific mapping from a linear ordered additive group to an open interval is continuous at a given point under certain positive conditions.
explanatories.continuousAt_iff_continuous_left_right: This theorem indicates that a function is continuous at a point if and only if it is continuous when approached from both the left and the right at that point in a linear order.
explanatories.AddCircle.continuous_mk': The theorem establishes that the canonical map from a quotient of the additive group of multiples of a specific element to the entire space is continuous under the topology of the linear ordered additive group.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.Continuous.comp: The composition of two continuous functions in topological spaces is itself continuous.
explanatories.continuous_subtype_val: This theorem states that the value function of a subtype in a topological space is continuous.
explanatories.ContinuousAt.comp: If one function is continuous at a point and another function is continuous at the image of that point under the first function, then their composition is also continuous at that original point.
explanatories.AddCircle.equivIccQuot: This definition describes a structural equivalence between an additive circle and the quotient space formed by identifying the endpoints of an interval defined by two points in a linear ordered additive group.
explanatories.AddCircle.equivIccQuot_comp_mk_eq_toIcoM: The theorem asserts that the composition of a specific equivalence function and a quotient mapping results in a function that produces distinct representatives from a bounded interval using a particular structure of endpoints.
explanatories.AddCircle.equivIccQuot_comp_mk_eq_toIocM: This theorem illustrates the composition of an equivalence transformation related to specific intervals in a linear ordered additive group, equating it to a function that applies a quotient followed by a mapping that identifies endpoints.
explanatories.quotientMap_quotient_mk': This theorem demonstrates that the quotient map induced by a setoid on a topological space is a quotient map.
explanatories.QuotientMap.continuous_iff: A quotient map is continuous if and only if the composition of that map with another function is also continuous.
explanatories.continuous_iff_continuousAt: A function is continuous if and only if it is continuous at every point in its domain.
explanatories.continuous_quot_mk: This theorem states that the canonical map that takes elements from a topological space to their equivalence classes under a given relation is continuous.
explanatories.inducing_subtype_val: This theorem establishes that the inclusion map corresponding to the value function of a subtype is an inducing map for the topology on that subtype.
explanatories.Inducing.continuousWithinAt_iff: A function is continuous at a point within a set if and only if the composition of that function with another inducing function is also continuous at the same point within the set.
explanatories.continuous_quot_lift: This theorem states that if a function is continuous and identifies points in its domain according to a certain equivalence relation, then the induced function on the quotient space is also continuous.
explanatories.Homeomorph.continuous_toFun: This theorem states that the forward function of a homeomorphism between two topological spaces is a continuous function.

AddCircle.homeoIccQuot.fullDefinition: def homeoIccQuot : 𝕋 ≃ₜ Quot (EndpointIdent p a) where   toEquiv := equivIccQuot p a   continuous_toFun := by     -- Porting note: was `simp_rw`     rw [quotientMap_quotient_mk'.continuous_iff]     simp_rw [continuous_iff_continuousAt,       continuousAt_iff_continuous_left_right]     intro x; constructor     on_goal 1 => erw [equivIccQuot_comp_mk_eq_toIocMod]     on_goal 2 => erw [equivIccQuot_comp_mk_eq_toIcoMod]     all_goals       apply continuous_quot_mk.continuousAt.comp_continuousWithinAt       rw [inducing_subtype_val.continuousWithinAt_iff]     · apply continuous_left_toIocMod     · apply continuous_right_toIcoMod   continuous_invFun :=     continuous_quot_lift _ ((AddCircle.continuous_mk' p).comp continuous_subtype_val)
AddCircle.homeoIccQuot.description: The definition describes a homeomorphism between the space formed by a closed interval with identified endpoints and the quotient of the additive group of real numbers by integer multiples of a positive real number.

CompactT2.Projective.comment:
The assertion `CompactT2.Projective` states that given continuous maps
`f : X → Z` and `g : Y → Z` with `g` surjective between `t_2`, compact topological spaces,
there exists a continuous lift `h : X → Y`, such that `f = g ∘ h`.

explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.

CompactT2.Projective.description: This definition specifies a property asserting that there exists a continuous map that allows for the lifting of continuous functions between compact, T2 topological spaces under certain conditions.

tendsto_nhds_iff_seq_tendsto.code:
tendsto_nhds_iff_seq_tendsto.{u_1, u_2} {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
  [FrechetUrysohnSpace X] {f : X → Y} {a : X} {b : Y} :
  Tendsto f (𝓝 a) (𝓝 b) ↔ ∀ (u : ℕ → X), Tendsto u atTop (𝓝 a) → Tendsto (f ∘ u) atTop (𝓝 b)
tendsto_nhds_iff_seq_tendsto.comment:
If the domain of a function `f : α → β` is a Fréchet-Urysohn space, then convergence
is equivalent to sequential convergence. See also `Filter.tendsto_iff_seq_tendsto` for a version
that works for any pair of filters assuming that the filter in the domain is countably generated.

This property is equivalent to the definition of `FrechetUrysohnSpace`, see
`FrechetUrysohnSpace.of_seq_tendsto_imp_tendsto`.

tendsto_nhds_iff_seq_tendsto.description: This theorem states that in a Fréchet-Urysohn space, the convergence of a function to a limit is equivalent to the convergence of sequences mapping to that function.

PartialHomeomorph.toFun'.comment:
Coercion of a partial homeomorphisms to a function. We don't use `e.toFun` because it is
actually `e.toPartialEquiv.toFun`, so `simp` will apply lemmas about `toPartialEquiv`.
While we may want to switch to this behavior later, doing it mid-port will break a lot of proofs.

PartialHomeomorph.ext.code:
PartialHomeomorph.ext.{u_1, u_3} {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
  (e e' : PartialHomeomorph X Y) (h : ∀ (x : X), ↑e x = ↑e' x) (hinv : ∀ (x : Y), ↑e.symm x = ↑e'.symm x)
  (hs : e.source = e'.source) : e = e'
PartialHomeomorph.ext.comment:
Two partial homeomorphisms are equal when they have equal `toFun`, `invFun` and `source`.
It is not sufficient to have equal `toFun` and `source`, as this only determines `invFun` on
the target. This would only be true for a weaker notion of equality, arguably the right one,
called `EqOnSource`.

PartialHomeomorph.preimage_eventuallyEq_.comment:
This lemma is useful in the manifold library in the case that `e` is a chart. It states that
locally around `e x` the set `e.symm ⁻¹' s` is the same as the set intersected with the target
of `e` and some other neighborhood of `f x` (which will be the source of a chart on `Z`).

PartialHomeomorph.piecewise.code:
PartialHomeomorph.piecewise.{u_1, u_3} {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
  (e e' : PartialHomeomorph X Y) (s : Set X) (t : Set Y) [(x : X) → Decidable (x ∈ s)] [(y : Y) → Decidable (y ∈ t)]
  (H : e.IsImage s t) (H' : e'.IsImage s t) (Hs : e.source ∩ frontier s = e'.source ∩ frontier s)
  (Heq : EqOn (↑e) (↑e') (e.source ∩ frontier s)) : PartialHomeomorph X Y
PartialHomeomorph.piecewise.comment:
Combine two `PartialHomeomorph`s using `Set.piecewise`. The source of the new
`PartialHomeomorph` is `s.ite e.source e'.source = e.source ∩ s ∪ e'.source \ s`, and similarly for
target.  The function sends `e.source ∩ s` to `e.target ∩ t` using `e` and
`e'.source \ s` to `e'.target \ t` using `e'`, and similarly for the inverse function.
To ensure the maps `toFun` and `invFun` are inverse of each other on the new `source` and `target`,
the definition assumes that the sets `s` and `t` are related both by `e.is_image` and `e'.is_image`.
To ensure that the new maps are continuous on `source`/`target`, it also assumes that `e.source` and
`e'.source` meet `frontier s` on the same set and `e x = e' x` on this intersection.

PartialHomeomorph.disjointUnion.comment:
Combine two `PartialHomeomorph`s with disjoint sources and disjoint targets. We reuse
`PartialHomeomorph.piecewise` then override `toPartialEquiv` to `PartialEquiv.disjointUnion`.
This way we have better definitional equalities for `source` and `target`.

PartialHomeomorph.disjointUnion.fullDefinition: def disjointUnion (e e' : PartialHomeomorph X Y) [∀ x, Decidable (x ∈ e.source)]     [∀ y, Decidable (y ∈ e.target)] (Hs : Disjoint e.source e'.source)     (Ht : Disjoint e.target e'.target) : PartialHomeomorph X Y :=   (e.piecewise e' e.source e.target e.isImage_source_target         (e'.isImage_source_target_of_disjoint e Hs.symm Ht.symm)         (by rw [e.open_source.inter_frontier_eq, (Hs.symm.frontier_right e'.open_source).inter_eq])         (by           rw [e.open_source.inter_frontier_eq]           exact eqOn_empty _ _)).replaceEquiv     (e.toPartialEquiv.disjointUnion e'.toPartialEquiv Hs Ht)     (PartialEquiv.disjointUnion_eq_piecewise _ _ _ _).symm

PartialHomeomorph.homeomorphOfImageSubse.fullDefinition: def homeomorphOfImageSubsetSource {s : Set X} {t : Set Y} (hs : s ⊆ e.source) (ht : e '' s = t) :     s ≃ₜ t :=   have h₁ : MapsTo e s t := mapsTo'.2 ht.subset   have h₂ : t ⊆ e.target := ht ▸ e.image_source_eq_target ▸ image_subset e hs   have h₃ : MapsTo e.symm t s := ht ▸ forall_mem_image.2 fun _x hx =>       (e.left_inv (hs hx)).symm ▸ hx   { toFun := MapsTo.restrict e s t h₁     invFun := MapsTo.restrict e.symm t s h₃     left_inv := fun a => Subtype.ext (e.left_inv (hs a.2))     right_inv := fun b => Subtype.eq <| e.right_inv (h₂ b.2)     continuous_toFun := (e.continuousOn.mono hs).restrict_mapsTo h₁     continuous_invFun := (e.continuousOn_symm.mono h₂).restrict_mapsTo h₃ }

OnePoint.continuousMapDiscreteEquiv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def continuousMapDiscreteEquiv (Y : Type*) [DiscreteTopology X] [TopologicalSpace Y]     [T2Space Y] [Infinite X] :     C(OnePoint X, Y) ≃ { f : X → Y // ∃ L, Tendsto (fun x : X ↦ f x) cofinite (𝓝 L) } where   toFun f := ⟨(f ·), ⟨f ∞, continuous_iff_from_discrete _ |>.mp (map_continuous f)⟩⟩   invFun f :=     { toFun := fun x => match x with         | ∞ => Classical.choose f.2         | some x => f.1 x       continuous_toFun := continuous_iff_from_discrete _ |>.mpr <| Classical.choose_spec f.2 }   left_inv f := by     ext x     refine OnePoint.rec ?_ ?_ x     · refine tendsto_nhds_unique ?_ (continuous_iff_from_discrete _ |>.mp <| map_continuous f)       let f' : { f : X → Y // ∃ L, Tendsto (fun x : X ↦ f x) cofinite (𝓝 L) } :=         ⟨fun x ↦ f x, ⟨f ∞, continuous_iff_from_discrete f |>.mp <| map_continuous f⟩⟩       exact Classical.choose_spec f'.property     · simp   right_inv f := rfl

Continuous.homeoOfEquivCompactToT2.t1_co.comment:
A concrete counterexample shows that `Continuous.homeoOfEquivCompactToT2`
cannot be generalized from `T2Space` to `T1Space`.

Let `α = OnePoint ℕ` be the one-point compactification of `ℕ`, and let `β` be the same space
`OnePoint ℕ` with the cofinite topology.  Then `α` is compact, `β` is T1, and the identity map
`id : α → β` is a continuous equivalence that is not a homeomorphism.

explanatories.dite_eq_right_iff: This theorem shows that a decision-based expression equaling a constant value is equivalent to asserting that the condition implies the given function results in that constant value.

LocallyConstant.piecewise.fullDefinition: def piecewise {C₁ C₂ : Set X} (h₁ : IsClosed C₁) (h₂ : IsClosed C₂) (h : C₁ ∪ C₂ = Set.univ)     (f : LocallyConstant C₁ Z) (g : LocallyConstant C₂ Z)     (hfg : ∀ (x : X) (hx : x ∈ C₁ ∩ C₂), f ⟨x, hx.1⟩ = g ⟨x, hx.2⟩)     [DecidablePred (· ∈ C₁)] : LocallyConstant X Z where   toFun i := if hi : i ∈ C₁ then f ⟨i, hi⟩ else g ⟨i, (Set.compl_subset_iff_union.mpr h) hi⟩   isLocallyConstant := by     let dZ : TopologicalSpace Z := ⊥     haveI : DiscreteTopology Z := discreteTopology_bot Z     obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := f     obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := g     rw [IsLocallyConstant.iff_continuous] at hf hg ⊢     dsimp only [coe_mk]     rw [Set.union_eq_iUnion] at h     refine (locallyFinite_of_finite _).continuous h (fun i ↦ ?_) (fun i ↦ ?_)     · cases i <;> [exact h₂; exact h₁]     · cases i <;> rw [continuousOn_iff_continuous_restrict]       · convert hg         ext x         simp only [cond_false, restrict_apply, Subtype.coe_eta, dite_eq_right_iff]         exact fun hx ↦ hfg x ⟨hx, x.prop⟩       · simp only [cond_true, restrict_dite, Subtype.coe_eta]         exact hf
LocallyConstant.piecewise.description: A piecewise defined locally constant function can be constructed on a topological space when two closed sets cover the space and the locally constant functions defined on these sets agree on their intersection.

LocallyConstant.piecewise'.fullDefinition: def piecewise' {C₀ C₁ C₂ : Set X} (h₀ : C₀ ⊆ C₁ ∪ C₂) (h₁ : IsClosed C₁)     (h₂ : IsClosed C₂) (f₁ : LocallyConstant C₁ Z) (f₂ : LocallyConstant C₂ Z)     [DecidablePred (· ∈ C₁)] (hf : ∀ x (hx : x ∈ C₁ ∩ C₂), f₁ ⟨x, hx.1⟩ = f₂ ⟨x, hx.2⟩) :     LocallyConstant C₀ Z :=   letI : ∀ j : C₀, Decidable (j ∈ Subtype.val ⁻¹' C₁) := fun j ↦ decidable_of_iff (↑j ∈ C₁) Iff.rfl   piecewise (h₁.preimage continuous_subtype_val) (h₂.preimage continuous_subtype_val)     (by simpa [eq_univ_iff_forall] using h₀)     (f₁.comap ⟨(restrictPreimage C₁ ((↑) : C₀ → X)), continuous_subtype_val.restrictPreimage⟩)     (f₂.comap ⟨(restrictPreimage C₂ ((↑) : C₀ → X)), continuous_subtype_val.restrictPreimage⟩) <| by       rintro ⟨x, hx₀⟩ ⟨hx₁ : x ∈ C₁, hx₂ : x ∈ C₂⟩       simpa using hf x ⟨hx₁, hx₂⟩

LocallyConstant.piecewise'.eq_1.code:
LocallyConstant.piecewise'.eq_1.{u_1, u_3} {X : Type u_1} {Z : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace X] {C₀ C₁ C₂ : Set X}
  (h₀ : C₀ ⊆ C₁ ∪ C₂) (h₁ : IsClosed C₁) (h₂ : IsClosed C₂) (f₁ : LocallyConstant (↑C₁) Z)
  (f₂ : LocallyConstant (↑C₂) Z) [DecidablePred fun x => x ∈ C₁]
  (hf : ∀ (x : X) (hx : x ∈ C₁ ∩ C₂), f₁ ⟨x, ⋯⟩ = f₂ ⟨x, ⋯⟩) :
  piecewise' h₀ h₁ h₂ f₁ f₂ hf =
    piecewise ⋯ ⋯ ⋯ (comap { toFun := C₁.restrictPreimage Subtype.val, continuous_toFun := ⋯ } f₁)
      (comap { toFun := C₂.restrictPreimage Subtype.val, continuous_toFun := ⋯ } f₂) ⋯

IsQuasiSeparated.comment:
A subset `s` of a topological space is quasi-separated if the intersections of any pairs of
compact open subsets of `s` are still compact.

Note that this is equivalent to `s` being a `QuasiSeparatedSpace` only when `s` is open.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.IsCompact: This defines the property of a set within a topological space being compact, which requires that for any nontrivial filter containing the set, there is an element within the set such that every set in the filter intersects with every neighborhood of that element.

IsQuasiSeparated.fullDefinition: def IsQuasiSeparated (s : Set α) : Prop :=   ∀ U V : Set α, U ⊆ s → IsOpen U → IsCompact U → V ⊆ s → IsOpen V → IsCompact V → IsCompact (U ∩ V)
IsQuasiSeparated.description: A subset of a topological space is considered quasi-separated if the intersection of any two compact open subsets of that subset remains compact.

explanatories.ENNReal.half_pos: This theorem states that for a nonzero nonnegative extended real number, half of it is positive.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne': A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then the two elements cannot be equal.
explanatories.ENNReal.add_lt_add: This theorem states that if one nonnegative extended real number is less than another and a second pair of such numbers also holds the same condition, then the sum of the first two is less than the sum of the second two.
explanatories.ENNReal.add_halves: This theorem shows that dividing a nonnegative extended real number into two equal parts and then adding those parts together results in the original number.

uniformSpaceOfEDist.fullDefinition: def uniformSpaceOfEDist (edist : α → α → ℝ≥0∞) (edist_self : ∀ x : α, edist x x = 0)     (edist_comm : ∀ x y : α, edist x y = edist y x)     (edist_triangle : ∀ x y z : α, edist x z ≤ edist x y + edist y z) : UniformSpace α :=   .ofFun edist edist_self edist_comm edist_triangle fun ε ε0 =>     ⟨ε / 2, ENNReal.half_pos ε0.ne', fun _ h₁ _ h₂ =>       (ENNReal.add_lt_add h₁ h₂).trans_eq (ENNReal.add_halves _)⟩
uniformSpaceOfEDist.description: A uniform space is established from an extended distance function that satisfies properties of identity, symmetry, and the triangle inequality.

Given `f : β → ℝ≥0∞`, if `f` sends `{i | p i}` to a set of positive numbers

`uniformity_basis_edist_nnreal`, and `uniformity_basis_edist_inv_nat`.

  UniformContinuousOn f s ↔

explanatories.UniformContinuousOn: A function is considered uniformly continuous on a set if points that are close together in that set map to points that are also close together in the target space.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.uniformContinuousOn_iff: A function is uniformly continuous on a specified set if and only if for every neighborhood structure in the codomain, there exists a neighborhood structure in the domain such that the mappings of points from the domain that are close enough remain within the neighborhood in the codomain.

EMetric.uniformContinuousOn_iff.description: A function is uniformly continuous on a set in a pseudo-metric space if, for every positive distance, there exists a smaller distance such that whenever points within the set are closer than this smaller distance, their images under the function are closer than the original distance.

EMetric.controlled_of_uniformEmbedding.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [PseudoEMetricSpace α] [PseudoEMetricSpace β]
  {f : α → β} (h : UniformEmbedding f) :
  (∀ ε > 0, ∃ δ > 0, ∀ {a b : α}, edist a b < δ → edist (f a) (f b) < ε) ∧
    ∀ δ > 0, ∃ ε > 0, ∀ {a b : α}, edist (f a) (f b) < ε → edist a b < δ
EMetric.controlled_of_uniformEmbedding.comment:
If a map between pseudoemetric spaces is a uniform embedding then the edistance between `f x`
and `f y` is controlled in terms of the distance between `x` and `y`.

In fact, this lemma holds for a `UniformInducing` map.

If a map between pseudoemetric spaces is a uniform embedding then the edistance between `f x`
and `f y` is controlled in terms of the distance between `x` and `y`.

In fact, this lemma holds for a `UniformInducing` map.

EMetric.complete_of_convergent_controlle.code:
EMetric.complete_of_convergent_controlled_sequences.{u} {α : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace α] (B : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞)
  (hB : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < B n)
  (H : ∀ (u : ℕ → α), (∀ (N n m : ℕ), N ≤ n → N ≤ m → edist (u n) (u m) < B N) → ∃ x, Tendsto u atTop (𝓝 x)) :
  CompleteSpace α
EMetric.complete_of_convergent_controlle.comment:
A very useful criterion to show that a space is complete is to show that all sequences
which satisfy a bound of the form `edist (u n) (u m) < B N` for all `n m ≥ N` are
converging. This is often applied for `B N = 2^{-N}`, i.e., with a very fast convergence to
`0`, which makes it possible to use arguments of converging series, while this is impossible
to do in general for arbitrary Cauchy sequences.

explanatories.UniformSpace.complete_of_convergent_cont: A uniform space is complete if it has a countable basis for its uniformity filter and every controlled Cauchy sequence converges.

EMetric.complete_of_convergent_controlle.description: A pseudo-metric space is complete if every sequence that is controlled by a specific converging bound also converges to a limit point in that space.

pseudoEMetricSpacePi.comment:
The product of a finite number of pseudoemetric spaces, with the max distance, is still
a pseudoemetric space.
This construction would also work for infinite products, but it would not give rise
to the product topology. Hence, we only formalize it in the good situation of finitely many
spaces.

pseudoEMetricSpacePi.fullDefinition: instance pseudoEMetricSpacePi [∀ b, PseudoEMetricSpace (π b)] : PseudoEMetricSpace (∀ b, π b) where   edist_self f := bot_unique <| Finset.sup_le <| by simp   edist_comm f g := by simp [edist_pi_def, edist_comm]   edist_triangle f g h := edist_pi_le_iff.2 fun b => le_trans (edist_triangle _ (g b) _)     (add_le_add (edist_le_pi_edist _ _ _) (edist_le_pi_edist _ _ _))   toUniformSpace := Pi.uniformSpace _   uniformity_edist := by     simp only [Pi.uniformity, PseudoEMetricSpace.uniformity_edist, comap_iInf, gt_iff_lt,       preimage_setOf_eq, comap_principal, edist_pi_def]     rw [iInf_comm]; congr; funext ε     rw [iInf_comm]; congr; funext εpos     simp [setOf_forall, εpos]

explanatories.EDist.edist: A distance function is defined on a type, returning non-negative extended real numbers between pairs of its elements.
explanatories.PseudoEMetricSpace.edist_self: The distance between any element and itself in a pseudo-metric space is equal to zero.
explanatories.PseudoEMetricSpace.edist_comm: The distance function in a pseudo-metric space is commutative, meaning the distance between two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.PseudoEMetricSpace.edist_triangle: The triangle inequality for the distance function in a pseudo-metric space asserts that the distance from one point to another is less than or equal to the sum of the distances between the first point to a third point and the second point to that third point.
explanatories.lt_of_le_of_lt: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is also strictly less than the third.

continuousOn_prod_of_subset_closure_cont.comment:
Consider a function `f : α × β → γ`. Suppose that it is continuous on each “vertical fiber”
`{a} × t`, `a ∈ s`, and is Lipschitz continuous on each “horizontal fiber” `s × {b}`, `b ∈ t`
with the same Lipschitz constant `K`. Then it is continuous on `s × t`. Moreover, it suffices
to require continuity on vertical fibers for `a` from a subset `s' ⊆ s` that is dense in `s`.

The actual statement uses (Lipschitz) continuity of `fun y ↦ f (a, y)` and `fun x ↦ f (x, b)`
instead of continuity of `f` on subsets of the product space.

continuousOn_prod_of_subset_closure_cont.description: If a function is continuous on vertical fibers and Lipschitz continuous on horizontal fibers within a product space, then it is continuous on the entire product of those sets given certain density conditions.

The actual statement uses (Lipschitz) continuity of `fun y ↦ f (a, y)` and `fun x ↦ f (x, b)`
instead of continuity of `f` on subsets of the product space.

explanatories.LipschitzWith: A function is Lipschitz continuous with a non-negative constant if the distance between its outputs is bounded by the constant multiplied by the distance between its inputs.

continuous_prod_of_continuous_lipschitz.description: If a function defined on a product of two spaces is continuous in one variable while being Lipschitz continuous in the other variable, then the function is continuous on the entire product space.

explanatories.ENNReal.pow_pos: This theorem indicates that if a nonnegative extended real number is positive, then raising it to any natural number power will also yield a positive result.
explanatories.ENNReal.inv_pos: This theorem establishes that the reciprocal of a positive extended nonnegative real number is positive if and only if that number is not infinity.
explanatories.ENNReal.two_ne_top: This theorem asserts that the number two is not equal to infinity in the context of extended nonnegative real numbers.
explanatories.pow_le_pow_right_of_le_one': This theorem concludes that if an element in a monoid is less than or equal to one and one non-negative integer is less than or equal to another, then raising the element to the power of the second integer results in a value that is less than or equal to raising it to the power of the first integer.
explanatories.ENNReal.inv_le_one: This theorem states that the reciprocal of a nonnegative extended real number is less than or equal to one if and only if that number is greater than or equal to one.
explanatories.ENNReal.one_lt_two: This theorem simply states that one is less than two.
explanatories.LT.lt.le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than a second, then it is also less than or equal to that second element.
explanatories.pow_succ': This theorem states that in a monoid, raising an element to the power of one plus a natural number is equivalent to multiplying the element by itself raised to the power of that natural number.
explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.
explanatories.ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel: This theorem asserts that for a nonzero and finite extended nonnegative real number, the product of the number and its reciprocal equals one.
explanatories.two_ne_zero: This theorem asserts that the number two is not equal to zero in any type that permits both zero and the natural representation of two, assuming two is non-zero.
explanatories.Set.iUnion_eq_univ_iff: The union of a family of sets equals the universal set if and only if every element in the universal set belongs to at least one of the sets in the family.
explanatories.linearOrderOfSTO: A definition stating that a strict total order can be used to create a linear order structure.
explanatories.WellOrderingRel: This definition describes a relation that allows any type to be equipped with a well-order derived from the well-order of cardinals through an embedding.
explanatories.IsWellFounded.wf: A theorem stating that if a relation is well-founded on a type, then it is classified as a well-founded relation.
explanatories.WellFounded.min: This definition specifies the concept of a minimal element in a nonempty set that is ordered by a well-founded relation.
explanatories.WellFounded.min_mem: This theorem asserts that the minimal element of a nonempty set, as determined by a well-founded relation, belongs to that set.
explanatories.WellFounded.not_lt_min: This theorem states that in a nonempty set with respect to a well-founded relation, an element cannot be related to its minimum element.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.trivial: The statement confirms that the proposition asserting truth is indeed valid and can be proven simply.

TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf.code: TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : TopCat} (F : Presheaf C X) : Prop
TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf.comment:
The sheaf condition has several different equivalent formulations.
The official definition chosen here is in terms of grothendieck topologies so that the results on
sites could be applied here easily, and this condition does not require additional constraints on
the value category.
The equivalent formulations of the sheaf condition on `presheaf C X` are as follows :

1. `TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf`: (the official definition)
  It is a sheaf with respect to the grothendieck topology on `opens X`, which is to say:
  For each open cover `{ Uᵢ }` of `U`, and a family of compatible functions `A ⟶ F(Uᵢ)` for an
  `A : X`, there exists a unique gluing `A ⟶ F(U)` compatible with the restriction.

2. `TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafEqualizerProducts`: (requires `C` to have all products)
  For each open cover `{ Uᵢ }` of `U`, `F(U) ⟶ ∏ᶜ F(Uᵢ)` is the equalizer of the two morphisms
  `∏ᶜ F(Uᵢ) ⟶ ∏ᶜ F(Uᵢ ∩ Uⱼ)`.
  See `TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafEqualizerProducts`.

3. `TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafOpensLeCover`:
  For each open cover `{ Uᵢ }` of `U`, `F(U)` is the limit of the diagram consisting of arrows
  `F(V₁) ⟶ F(V₂)` for every pair of open sets `V₁ ⊇ V₂` that are contained in some `Uᵢ`.
  See `TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafOpensLeCover`.

4. `TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafPairwiseIntersections`:
  For each open cover `{ Uᵢ }` of `U`, `F(U)` is the limit of the diagram consisting of arrows
  from `F(Uᵢ)` and `F(Uⱼ)` to `F(Uᵢ ∩ Uⱼ)` for each pair `(i, j)`.
  See `TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafPairwiseIntersections`.

The following requires `C` to be concrete and complete, and `forget C` to reflect isomorphisms and
preserve limits. This applies to most "algebraic" categories, e.g. groups, abelian groups and rings.

5. `TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafUniqueGluing`:
  (requires `C` to be concrete and complete; `forget C` to reflect isomorphisms and preserve limits)
  For each open cover `{ Uᵢ }` of `U`, and a compatible family of elements `x : F(Uᵢ)`, there exists
  a unique gluing `x : F(U)` that restricts to the given elements.
  See `TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafUniqueGluing`.

6. The underlying sheaf of types is a sheaf.
  See `TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp` and
  `CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget`.

TopCat.Presheaf.coveringOfPresieve.code:

  (V : Opens ↑X) × { f // R f } → Opens ↑X
TopCat.Presheaf.coveringOfPresieve.comment:
Given a presieve `R` on `U`, we obtain a covering family of open sets in `X`, by taking as index
type the type of dependent pairs `(V, f)`, where `f : V ⟶ U` is in `R`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presieve: This definition describes a presieve as a collection of morphisms that all have a common codomain in a given category.

TopCat.Presheaf.coveringOfPresieve.fullDefinition: def coveringOfPresieve (U : Opens X) (R : Presieve U) : (ΣV, { f : V ⟶ U // R f }) → Opens X :=   fun f => f.1
TopCat.Presheaf.coveringOfPresieve.description: A covering family of open sets in a topological space is derived from a given presieve by considering dependent pairs formed by the open sets and the morphisms in the presieve.

TopCat.Presheaf.presieveOfCoveringAux.code: TopCat.Presheaf.presieveOfCoveringAux.{w, v} {X : TopCat} {ι : Type v} (U : ι → Opens ↑X) (Y : Opens ↑X) : Presieve Y
TopCat.Presheaf.presieveOfCoveringAux.comment:
Given a family of opens `U : ι → Opens X` and any open `Y : Opens X`, we obtain a presieve
on `Y` by declaring that a morphism `f : V ⟶ Y` is a member of the presieve if and only if
there exists an index `i : ι` such that `V = U i`.

TopCat.Presheaf.presieveOfCoveringAux.description: A presieve on an open set is constructed from a family of open sets by including morphisms that originate from any one of those sets in the family.

TopCat.Presheaf.covering_presieve_eq_sel.code:
TopCat.Presheaf.covering_presieve_eq_self.{w} {X : TopCat} {Y : Opens ↑X} (R : Presieve Y) :
  presieveOfCoveringAux (coveringOfPresieve Y R) Y = R
TopCat.Presheaf.covering_presieve_eq_sel.comment:
Given a presieve `R` on `Y`, if we take its associated family of opens via
`coveringOfPresieve` (which may not cover `Y` if `R` is not covering), and take
the presieve on `Y` associated to the family of opens via `presieveOfCoveringAux`,
then we get back the original presieve `R`.

TopCat.Presheaf.presieveOfCovering.homOf.description: An index from a family of open sets can be represented as a dependent pair consisting of an open set and a morphism from that open set to the supremum of the family, which satisfies the conditions of the associated presieve.

TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafOpensLeCover.code: TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafOpensLeCover.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : TopCat} (F : Presheaf C X) : Prop
TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafOpensLeCover.comment:
An equivalent formulation of the sheaf condition
(which we prove equivalent to the usual one below as
`isSheaf_iff_isSheafOpensLeCover`).

A presheaf is a sheaf if `F` sends the cone `(opensLeCoverCocone U).op` to a limit cone.
(Recall `opensLeCoverCocone U`, has cone point `iSup U`,
mapping down to any `V` which is contained in some `U i`.)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapCone: This definition describes how to obtain a new cone in one category from an existing cone in another category by applying a functor that maps between the two categories.

TopCat.Presheaf.generateEquivalenceOpens.comment:
Given a family of opens `U` and an open `Y` equal to the union of opens in `U`, we may
take the presieve on `Y` associated to `U` and the sieve generated by it, and form the
full subcategory (subposet) of opens contained in `Y` (`over Y`) consisting of arrows
in the sieve. This full subcategory is equivalent to `OpensLeCover U`, the (poset)
category of opens contained in some `U i`.

Top.presheaf.whisker_iso_map_generate_co.fullDefinition: def whiskerIsoMapGenerateCocone :     (F.mapCone (opensLeCoverCocone U).op).whisker (generateEquivalenceOpensLe U hY).op.functor ≅       F.mapCone (Sieve.generate (presieveOfCoveringAux U Y)).arrows.cocone.op where   hom :=     { hom := F.map (eqToHom (congr_arg op hY.symm))       w := fun j => by         erw [← F.map_comp]         dsimp         congr 1 }   inv :=     { hom := F.map (eqToHom (congr_arg op hY))       w := fun j => by         erw [← F.map_comp]         dsimp         congr 1 }   hom_inv_id := by     ext     simp [eqToHom_map]   inv_hom_id := by     ext     simp [eqToHom_map] set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

TopCat.Presheaf.isLimitOpensLeEquivGener.code:
TopCat.Presheaf.isLimitOpensLeEquivGenerate₁.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : TopCat} (F : Presheaf C X)
  {ι : Type w} (U : ι → Opens ↑X) {Y : Opens ↑X} (hY : Y = iSup U) :
  IsLimit (Functor.mapCone F (opensLeCoverCocone U).op) ≃
    IsLimit (Functor.mapCone F (Sieve.generate (presieveOfCoveringAux U Y)).arrows.cocone.op)
TopCat.Presheaf.isLimitOpensLeEquivGener.comment:
Given a presheaf `F` on the topological space `X` and a family of opens `U` of `X`,
the natural cone associated to `F` and `U` used in the definition of
`F.IsSheafOpensLeCover` is a limit cone iff the natural cone associated to `F`
and the sieve generated by the presieve associated to `U` is a limit cone.
