TopCat.Presheaf.isLimitOpensLeEquivGener.code:
TopCat.Presheaf.isLimitOpensLeEquivGenerate₂.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : TopCat} (F : Presheaf C X)
  {Y : Opens ↑X} (R : Presieve Y) (hR : Sieve.generate R ∈ (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↑X).sieves Y) :
  IsLimit (Functor.mapCone F (opensLeCoverCocone (coveringOfPresieve Y R)).op) ≃
    IsLimit (Functor.mapCone F (Sieve.generate R).arrows.cocone.op)
TopCat.Presheaf.isLimitOpensLeEquivGener.comment:
Given a presheaf `F` on the topological space `X` and a presieve `R` whose generated sieve
is covering for the associated Grothendieck topology (equivalently, the presieve is covering
for the associated pretopology), the natural cone associated to `F` and the family of opens
associated to `R` is a limit cone iff the natural cone associated to `F` and the generated
sieve is a limit cone.
Since only the existence of a 1-1 correspondence will be used, the exact definition does
not matter, so tactics are used liberally.

TopCat.Presheaf.isLimitOpensLeEquivGener.fullDefinition: def isLimitOpensLeEquivGenerate₂ (R : Presieve Y)     (hR : Sieve.generate R ∈ Opens.grothendieckTopology X Y) :     IsLimit (F.mapCone (opensLeCoverCocone (coveringOfPresieve Y R)).op) ≃       IsLimit (F.mapCone (Sieve.generate R).arrows.cocone.op) := by   convert isLimitOpensLeEquivGenerate₁ F (coveringOfPresieve Y R)       (coveringOfPresieve.iSup_eq_of_mem_grothendieck Y R hR).symm using 1   rw [covering_presieve_eq_self R] set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafOpens.code:
TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafOpensLeCover.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : TopCat}
  (F : Presheaf C X) : F.IsSheaf ↔ F.IsSheafOpensLeCover
TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafOpens.comment:
A presheaf `(opens X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ C` on a topological space `X` is a sheaf on the site `opens X` iff
it satisfies the `IsSheafOpensLeCover` sheaf condition. The latter is not the
official definition of sheaves on spaces, but has the advantage that it does not
require `has_products C`.

explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafOpensLeCover: This defines a condition that characterizes a presheaf as a sheaf by requiring it to send a specified cone of covering families to a limit cone.
explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf: A presheaf is defined as a sheaf if it satisfies the sheaf condition with respect to the Grothendieck topology on the open sets of a topological space.

TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafOpens.description: A presheaf on a topological space is a sheaf according to a specific condition if and only if it meets the requirement of being a sheaf under a different, less restrictive condition that does not necessitate the existence of products in the category.

TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafPairwiseIntersect.code:
TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafPairwiseIntersections.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : TopCat}
  (F : Presheaf C X) : Prop
TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafPairwiseIntersect.comment:
An alternative formulation of the sheaf condition
(which we prove equivalent to the usual one below as
`isSheaf_iff_isSheafPairwiseIntersections`).

A presheaf is a sheaf if `F` sends the cone `(pairwise.cocone U).op` to a limit cone.
(Recall `Pairwise.cocone U` has cone point `supr U`, mapping down to the `U i` and the `U i ⊓ U j`.)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapCone: This definition describes how to obtain a new cone in one category from an existing cone in another category by applying a functor that maps between the two categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Pairwise.cocone: This definition establishes that for a given function from a type to a complete lattice, the supremum of that function yields a cocone over the corresponding diagram.
explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.Bool.false: The boolean value false is a specific representation of the false state in boolean logic.

TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafPairwiseIntersect.fullDefinition: def IsSheafPairwiseIntersections (F : Presheaf C X) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃ι : Type w⦄ (U : ι → Opens X), Nonempty (IsLimit (F.mapCone (Pairwise.cocone U).op)) set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafPairwiseIntersect.description: A presheaf is considered a sheaf if it satisfies a condition related to the limit cone formed by the mappings from overlaps of open sets within any family of open sets.

TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafPreservesLimitPairwiseIntersections.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : TopCat}
  (F : Presheaf C X) : Prop
TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafPreservesLimitPai.comment:
An alternative formulation of the sheaf condition
(which we prove equivalent to the usual one below as
`isSheaf_iff_isSheafPreservesLimitPairwiseIntersections`).

A presheaf is a sheaf if `F` preserves the limit of `Pairwise.diagram U`.
(Recall `Pairwise.diagram U` is the diagram consisting of the pairwise intersections
`U i ⊓ U j` mapping into the open sets `U i`. This diagram has limit `supr U`.)

in terms of a limit diagram over all `{ V : opens X // ∃ i, V ≤ U i }`
is equivalent to the reformulation
in terms of a limit diagram over `U i` and `U i ⊓ U j`.

TopCat.Sheaf.interUnionPullbackCone.comment:
For a sheaf `F`, `F(U ⊔ V)` is the pullback of `F(U) ⟶ F(U ⊓ V)` and `F(V) ⟶ F(U ⊓ V)`.

TopCat.Sheaf.interUnionPullbackConeLift.fullDefinition: def interUnionPullbackConeLift : s.pt ⟶ F.1.obj (op (U ⊔ V)) := by   let ι : ULift.{w} WalkingPair → Opens X := fun j => WalkingPair.casesOn j.down U V   have hι : U ⊔ V = iSup ι := by     ext     rw [Opens.coe_iSup, Set.mem_iUnion]     constructor     · rintro (h | h)       exacts [⟨⟨WalkingPair.left⟩, h⟩, ⟨⟨WalkingPair.right⟩, h⟩]     · rintro ⟨⟨_ | _⟩, h⟩       exacts [Or.inl h, Or.inr h]   refine     (F.presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafPairwiseIntersections.mp F.2 ι).some.lift         ⟨s.pt,           { app := ?_             naturality := ?_ }⟩ ≫       F.1.map (eqToHom hι).op   · rintro ((_ | _) | (_ | _))     exacts [s.fst, s.snd, s.fst ≫ F.1.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op,       s.snd ≫ F.1.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op]   rintro ⟨i⟩ ⟨j⟩ f   let g : j ⟶ i := f.unop   have : f = g.op := rfl   clear_value g   subst this   rcases i with (⟨⟨_ | _⟩⟩ | ⟨⟨_ | _⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩) <;>   rcases j with (⟨⟨_ | _⟩⟩ | ⟨⟨_ | _⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩) <;>   rcases g with ⟨⟩ <;>   dsimp [Pairwise.diagram] <;>   simp only [Category.id_comp, s.condition, CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id, Category.comp_id]   rw [← cancel_mono (F.1.map (eqToHom <| inf_comm U V : U ⊓ V ⟶ _).op), Category.assoc,     Category.assoc, ← F.1.map_comp, ← F.1.map_comp]   exact s.condition.symm set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

Top.sheaf.inter_union_pullback_cone_lift.fullDefinition: def interUnionPullbackConeLift : s.pt ⟶ F.1.obj (op (U ⊔ V)) := by   let ι : ULift.{w} WalkingPair → Opens X := fun j => WalkingPair.casesOn j.down U V   have hι : U ⊔ V = iSup ι := by     ext     rw [Opens.coe_iSup, Set.mem_iUnion]     constructor     · rintro (h | h)       exacts [⟨⟨WalkingPair.left⟩, h⟩, ⟨⟨WalkingPair.right⟩, h⟩]     · rintro ⟨⟨_ | _⟩, h⟩       exacts [Or.inl h, Or.inr h]   refine     (F.presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafPairwiseIntersections.mp F.2 ι).some.lift         ⟨s.pt,           { app := ?_             naturality := ?_ }⟩ ≫       F.1.map (eqToHom hι).op   · rintro ((_ | _) | (_ | _))     exacts [s.fst, s.snd, s.fst ≫ F.1.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op,       s.snd ≫ F.1.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op]   rintro ⟨i⟩ ⟨j⟩ f   let g : j ⟶ i := f.unop   have : f = g.op := rfl   clear_value g   subst this   rcases i with (⟨⟨_ | _⟩⟩ | ⟨⟨_ | _⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩) <;>   rcases j with (⟨⟨_ | _⟩⟩ | ⟨⟨_ | _⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩) <;>   rcases g with ⟨⟩ <;>   dsimp [Pairwise.diagram] <;>   simp only [Category.id_comp, s.condition, CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id, Category.comp_id]   rw [← cancel_mono (F.1.map (eqToHom <| inf_comm U V : U ⊓ V ⟶ _).op), Category.assoc,     Category.assoc, ← F.1.map_comp, ← F.1.map_comp]   exact s.condition.symm set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
Top.sheaf.inter_union_pullback_cone_lift.description: For a sheaf over the union of two open sets, any cone formed by mappings from the sheaf's values over these sets and their intersection can be lifted to a morphism into the sheaf's value over their union.

TopCat.Sheaf.isLimitPullbackCone.fullDefinition: def isLimitPullbackCone : IsLimit (interUnionPullbackCone F U V) := by   let ι : ULift.{w} WalkingPair → Opens X := fun ⟨j⟩ => WalkingPair.casesOn j U V   have hι : U ⊔ V = iSup ι := by     ext     rw [Opens.coe_iSup, Set.mem_iUnion]     constructor     · rintro (h | h)       exacts [⟨⟨WalkingPair.left⟩, h⟩, ⟨⟨WalkingPair.right⟩, h⟩]     · rintro ⟨⟨_ | _⟩, h⟩       exacts [Or.inl h, Or.inr h]   apply PullbackCone.isLimitAux'   intro s   use interUnionPullbackConeLift F U V s   refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩   · apply interUnionPullbackConeLift_left   · apply interUnionPullbackConeLift_right   · intro m h₁ h₂     rw [← cancel_mono (F.1.map (eqToHom hι.symm).op)]     apply (F.presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafPairwiseIntersections.mp F.2 ι).some.hom_ext     rintro ((_ | _) | (_ | _)) <;>     rw [Category.assoc, Category.assoc]     · erw [← F.1.map_comp]       convert h₁       apply interUnionPullbackConeLift_left     · erw [← F.1.map_comp]       convert h₂       apply interUnionPullbackConeLift_right     all_goals       dsimp only [Functor.op, Pairwise.cocone_ι_app, Functor.mapCone_π_app, Cocone.op,         Pairwise.coconeιApp, unop_op, op_comp, NatTrans.op]       simp_rw [F.1.map_comp, ← Category.assoc]       congr 1       simp_rw [Category.assoc, ← F.1.map_comp]     · convert h₁       apply interUnionPullbackConeLift_left     · convert h₂       apply interUnionPullbackConeLift_right set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

Top.sheaf.is_limit_pullback_cone.fullDefinition: def isLimitPullbackCone : IsLimit (interUnionPullbackCone F U V) := by   let ι : ULift.{w} WalkingPair → Opens X := fun ⟨j⟩ => WalkingPair.casesOn j U V   have hι : U ⊔ V = iSup ι := by     ext     rw [Opens.coe_iSup, Set.mem_iUnion]     constructor     · rintro (h | h)       exacts [⟨⟨WalkingPair.left⟩, h⟩, ⟨⟨WalkingPair.right⟩, h⟩]     · rintro ⟨⟨_ | _⟩, h⟩       exacts [Or.inl h, Or.inr h]   apply PullbackCone.isLimitAux'   intro s   use interUnionPullbackConeLift F U V s   refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩   · apply interUnionPullbackConeLift_left   · apply interUnionPullbackConeLift_right   · intro m h₁ h₂     rw [← cancel_mono (F.1.map (eqToHom hι.symm).op)]     apply (F.presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafPairwiseIntersections.mp F.2 ι).some.hom_ext     rintro ((_ | _) | (_ | _)) <;>     rw [Category.assoc, Category.assoc]     · erw [← F.1.map_comp]       convert h₁       apply interUnionPullbackConeLift_left     · erw [← F.1.map_comp]       convert h₂       apply interUnionPullbackConeLift_right     all_goals       dsimp only [Functor.op, Pairwise.cocone_ι_app, Functor.mapCone_π_app, Cocone.op,         Pairwise.coconeιApp, unop_op, op_comp, NatTrans.op]       simp_rw [F.1.map_comp, ← Category.assoc]       congr 1       simp_rw [Category.assoc, ← F.1.map_comp]     · convert h₁       apply interUnionPullbackConeLift_left     · convert h₂       apply interUnionPullbackConeLift_right set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
Top.sheaf.is_limit_pullback_cone.description: For a sheaf, the value at the union of two open sets is the limit of the pullback cone defined by its values over the individual open sets and their intersection.

  (F : Presheaf C X) : Prop
TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafUniqueGluing.comment:
The sheaf condition in terms of unique gluings. A presheaf `F : presheaf C X` satisfies this sheaf
condition if and only if, for every compatible family of sections `sf : Π i : ι, F.obj (op (U i))`,
there exists a unique gluing `s : F.obj (op (supr U))`.

We prove this to be equivalent to the usual one below in
`TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafUniqueGluing`

  (F : Presheaf C X) : Prop
TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafEqualizerProducts.comment:
The sheaf condition for a `F : presheaf C X` requires that the morphism
`F.obj U ⟶ ∏ᶜ F.obj (U i)` (where `U` is some open set which is the union of the `U i`)
is the equalizer of the two morphisms
`∏ᶜ F.obj (U i) ⟶ ∏ᶜ F.obj (U i) ⊓ (U j)`.

TopCat.Presheaf.SheafConditionPairwiseIn.fullDefinition: def coneEquivInverseObj (c : Limits.Cone (SheafConditionEqualizerProducts.diagram F U)) :     Limits.Cone ((diagram U).op ⋙ F) where   pt := c.pt   π :=     { app := by         intro x         induction x using Opposite.rec' with | h x => ?_         rcases x with (⟨i⟩ | ⟨i, j⟩)         · exact c.π.app WalkingParallelPair.zero ≫ Pi.π _ i         · exact c.π.app WalkingParallelPair.one ≫ Pi.π _ (i, j)       naturality := by         intro x y f         induction x using Opposite.rec' with | h x => ?_         induction y using Opposite.rec' with | h y => ?_         have ef : f = f.unop.op := rfl         revert ef         generalize f.unop = f'         rintro rfl         rcases x with (⟨i⟩ | ⟨⟩) <;> rcases y with (⟨⟩ | ⟨j, j⟩) <;> rcases f' with ⟨⟩         · dsimp           erw [F.map_id]           simp         · dsimp           simp only [Category.id_comp, Category.assoc]           have h := c.π.naturality WalkingParallelPairHom.left           dsimp [SheafConditionEqualizerProducts.leftRes] at h           simp only [Category.id_comp] at h           have h' := h =≫ Pi.π _ (i, j)           rw [h']           simp only [Category.assoc, limit.lift_π, Fan.mk_π_app]           rfl         · dsimp           simp only [Category.id_comp, Category.assoc]           have h := c.π.naturality WalkingParallelPairHom.right           dsimp [SheafConditionEqualizerProducts.rightRes] at h           simp only [Category.id_comp] at h           have h' := h =≫ Pi.π _ (j, i)           rw [h']           simp           rfl         · dsimp           erw [F.map_id]           simp } set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

TopCat.continuousFunctions.map.comment:
A homomorphism of topological rings can be postcomposed with functions from a source space `X`;
this is a ring homomorphism (with respect to the pointwise ring operations on functions).

explanatories.ContinuousMap.ext: This theorem asserts that if two continuous maps agree on every point in their domain, then they are identical as functions.
explanatories.RingHom.map_one: This theorem states that a ring homomorphism must map the multiplicative identity element of its domain to the multiplicative identity element of its codomain.
explanatories.RingHom.map_mul: This theorem states that ring homomorphisms maintain the multiplication structure by ensuring the image of a product equals the product of the images.
explanatories.RingHom.map_zero: This theorem establishes that a ring homomorphism must send the additive identity from the domain to the additive identity in the codomain.
explanatories.RingHom.map_add: This theorem indicates that a ring homomorphism maintains the property of addition by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements is equal to the sum of their images.

TopCat.continuousFunctions.map.description: This definition establishes that a homomorphism between topological rings can be combined with functions from a topological space, resulting in a new mapping that preserves the ring structure through pointwise operations.

Top.presheaf.stalk_pushforward.comment:
For a presheaf `F` on a space `X`, a continuous map `f : X ⟶ Y` induces a morphisms between the
stalk of `f _ * F` at `f x` and the stalk of `F` at `x`.

Top.presheaf.stalk_pushforward.fullDefinition: def stalkPushforward (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : X.Presheaf C) (x : X) : (f _* F).stalk (f x) ⟶ F.stalk x := by   -- This is a hack; Lean doesn't like to elaborate the term written directly.   -- Porting note: The original proof was `trans; swap`, but `trans` does nothing.   refine ?_ ≫ colimit.pre _ (OpenNhds.map f x).op   exact colim.map (whiskerRight (NatTrans.op (OpenNhds.inclusionMapIso f x).inv) F) set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

preserves limits and filtered colimits. Then two sections who agree on every stalk must be equal.

TopCat.Presheaf.app_surjective_of_inject.code:
TopCat.Presheaf.app_surjective_of_injective_of_locally_surjective.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]

  [PreservesLimits (forget C)] [(forget C).ReflectsIsomorphisms] {F G : Sheaf C X} (f : F ⟶ G) (U : Opens ↑X)
  (hinj : ∀ (x : ↥U), Function.Injective ⇑((stalkFunctor C ↑x).map f.val))
  (hsurj :
    ∀ (t : (forget C).obj (G.val.obj (op U))) (x : ↥U),
      ∃ V, ∃ (_ : ↑x ∈ V), ∃ iVU s, (f.val.app (op V)) s = (G.val.map iVU.op) t) :
  Function.Surjective ⇑(f.val.app (op U))
TopCat.Presheaf.app_surjective_of_inject.comment:
For surjectivity, we are given an arbitrary section `t` and need to find a preimage for it.
We claim that it suffices to find preimages *locally*. That is, for each `x : U` we construct
a neighborhood `V ≤ U` and a section `s : F.obj (op V))` such that `f.app (op V) s` and `t`
agree on `V`.

TopCat.Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective.code:
TopCat.Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [ConcreteCategory C] {X : TopCat}
  {ℱ 𝒢 : Presheaf C X} (T : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢) : Prop
TopCat.Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective.comment:
A map of presheaves `T : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` is **locally surjective** if for any open set `U`,
section `t` over `U`, and `x ∈ U`, there exists an open set `x ∈ V ⊆ U` and a section `s` over `V`
such that `$T_*(s_V) = t|_V$`.

See `TopCat.Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff` below.

explanatories.Opens.grothendieckTopology: This defines a Grothendieck topology that is derived from a given topological space.

TopCat.Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective.fullDefinition: def IsLocallySurjective (T : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢) :=   CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) T set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
TopCat.Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective.description: The definition describes a map between presheaves as locally surjective if, for any open set and section, there exists a smaller open set where the image under the map corresponds to the restriction of the section.

TopCat.Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff.code:
TopCat.Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [ConcreteCategory C] {X : TopCat}
  {ℱ 𝒢 : Presheaf C X} (T : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢) :
  IsLocallySurjective T ↔
    ∀ (U : Opens ↑X) (t : (forget C).obj (𝒢.obj (op U))), ∀ x ∈ U, ∃ V ι, (∃ s, (T.app (op V)) s = t |_ₕ ι) ∧ x ∈ V

explanatories.CommRingCat: This definition refers to the category consisting of commutative rings and their morphisms.
explanatories.CommRingCat.of: This definition creates a bundled category of commutative rings from a specified type that adheres to the properties of a commutative ring.
explanatories.Localization: This definition introduces the concept of the localization of a commutative monoid at a submonoid, represented as a quotient type.
explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.SubmonoidPresheaf.obj: This definition describes a construction that assigns a submonoid to each open set of a topological space, based on a given presheaf of objects in a category.
explanatories.CommRingCat.ofHom: This definition allows a ring homomorphism between two commutative rings to be viewed as a morphism in the category of commutative rings.
explanatories.IsLocalization.map: This definition outlines a way to map a homomorphism from one localized semiring to another while ensuring that the image of the submonoid under the first semiring is contained within the submonoid of the second semiring.
explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.SubmonoidPresheaf.map: This theorem states that for any morphism between open sets in a topological space, the submonoid assigned to the first open set is contained within the preimage of the submonoid assigned to the second open set under the associated presheaf mapping.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id: A functor preserves identity morphisms by ensuring that the image of an identity morphism in one category is the identity morphism of the corresponding object in the mapped category.
explanatories.IsLocalization.map_id: The theorem shows that applying the identity map to an element of the localized semiring results in that same element, establishing the preservation of elements under the localization process.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp: A functor maintains the composition of morphisms when mapping them from one category to another.
explanatories.CommRingCat.comp_eq_ring_hom_comp: This theorem states that the composition of two ring homomorphisms is equal to the application of the comp operator used to combine them in the category of commutative rings.
explanatories.IsLocalization.map_comp_map: The theorem establishes that the composition of localization maps induced by two homomorphisms equates to the localization map induced by the composition of those homomorphisms when certain conditions regarding submonoids are satisfied.
explanatories.IsLocalization.map_comp: The theorem states that the composition of the localization map and the algebra map from one commutative semiring to another can be represented equivalently as the composition of the algebra map and a morphism mapping to a different semiring under certain conditions involving submonoids.

TopCat.Presheaf.SubmonoidPresheaf.locali.fullDefinition: protected noncomputable def SubmonoidPresheaf.localizationPresheaf : X.Presheaf CommRingCat where   obj U := CommRingCat.of <| Localization (G.obj U)   map {U V} i := CommRingCat.ofHom <| IsLocalization.map _ (F.map i) (G.map i)   map_id U := by     simp_rw [F.map_id]     ext x     -- Porting note: `M` and `S` needs to be specified manually     exact IsLocalization.map_id (M := G.obj U) (S := Localization (G.obj U)) x   map_comp {U V W} i j := by     delta CommRingCat.ofHom CommRingCat.of Bundled.of     simp_rw [F.map_comp, CommRingCat.comp_eq_ring_hom_comp]     rw [IsLocalization.map_comp_map]

explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res: The theorem asserts a relationship between the germ of a presheaf at a point within an open set and its image under a morphism of open sets, demonstrating how the presheaf behaves under restriction.

TopCat.Presheaf.submonoidPresheafOfStalk.fullDefinition: noncomputable def submonoidPresheafOfStalk (S : ∀ x : X, Submonoid (F.stalk x)) :     F.SubmonoidPresheaf where   obj U := ⨅ x : U.unop, Submonoid.comap (F.germ x) (S x)   map {U V} i := by     intro s hs     simp only [Submonoid.mem_comap, Submonoid.mem_iInf] at hs ⊢     intro x     change (F.map i.unop.op ≫ F.germ x) s ∈ _     rw [F.germ_res]     exact hs _
TopCat.Presheaf.submonoidPresheafOfStalk.description: This definition describes how to create a submonoid presheaf from a given presheaf and a specified submonoid at each stalk, ensuring that sections of the presheaf restrict to the defined submonoid at each point.

skyscraperPresheaf.code:
skyscraperPresheaf.{u, v, w} {X : TopCat} (p₀ : ↑X) [(U : Opens ↑X) → Decidable (p₀ ∈ U)] {C : Type v}
  [Category.{w, v} C] [HasTerminal C] (A : C) : Presheaf C X
skyscraperPresheaf.comment:
A skyscraper presheaf is a presheaf supported at a single point: if `p₀ ∈ X` is a specified
point, then the skyscraper presheaf `𝓕` with value `A` is defined by `U ↦ A` if `p₀ ∈ U` and
`U ↦ *` if `p₀ ∉ A` where `*` is some terminal object.

skyscraperPresheaf.fullDefinition: def skyscraperPresheaf : Presheaf C X where   obj U := if p₀ ∈ unop U then A else terminal C   map {U V} i :=     if h : p₀ ∈ unop V then eqToHom <| by dsimp; erw [if_pos h, if_pos (leOfHom i.unop h)]     else ((if_neg h).symm.ndrec terminalIsTerminal).from _   map_id U :=     (em (p₀ ∈ U.unop)).elim (fun h => dif_pos h) fun h =>       ((if_neg h).symm.ndrec terminalIsTerminal).hom_ext _ _   map_comp {U V W} iVU iWV := by     by_cases hW : p₀ ∈ unop W     · have hV : p₀ ∈ unop V := leOfHom iWV.unop hW       simp only [dif_pos hW, dif_pos hV, eqToHom_trans]     · dsimp; rw [dif_neg hW]; apply ((if_neg hW).symm.ndrec terminalIsTerminal).hom_ext

skyscraperPresheaf.{u, v, w} {X : TopCat} (p₀ : ↑X) [(U : Opens ↑X) → Decidable (p₀ ∈ U)] {C : Type v}
  [Category.{w, v} C] [HasTerminal C] (A : C) : Presheaf C X
skyscraper_presheaf.comment:
A skyscraper presheaf is a presheaf supported at a single point: if `p₀ ∈ X` is a specified
point, then the skyscraper presheaf `𝓕` with value `A` is defined by `U ↦ A` if `p₀ ∈ U` and
`U ↦ *` if `p₀ ∉ A` where `*` is some terminal object.

skyscraperPresheafFunctor.description: The skyscraper presheaf functor captures the process of associating to each object in a category a skyscraper presheaf centered at a specified point in a topological space, with morphisms being transformed accordingly based on their relation to that point.

skyscraper_presheaf_functor.comment:
Taking skyscraper presheaf at a point is functorial: `c ↦ skyscraper p₀ c` defines a functor by
sending every `f : a ⟶ b` to the natural transformation `α` defined as: `α(U) = f : a ⟶ b` if
`p₀ ∈ U` and the unique morphism to a terminal object in `C` if `p₀ ∉ U`.

explanatories.SkyscraperPresheafFunctor.map': The functorial property of the skyscraper presheaf at a point is established by mapping morphisms between values to corresponding natural transformations that either reflect the morphism or lead to a unique morphism to a terminal object based on the inclusion of a specified point in the open set.

skyscraper_sheaf_functor.fullDefinition: def skyscraperSheafFunctor : C ⥤ Sheaf C X where   obj c := skyscraperSheaf p₀ c   map f := Sheaf.Hom.mk <| (skyscraperPresheafFunctor p₀).map f   map_id _ := Sheaf.Hom.ext _ _ <| (skyscraperPresheafFunctor p₀).map_id _   map_comp _ _ := Sheaf.Hom.ext _ _ <| (skyscraperPresheafFunctor p₀).map_comp _ _
skyscraper_sheaf_functor.description: The skyscraper sheaf functor establishes a functorial correspondence between objects in a category and the skyscraper sheaves at a specified point in a topological space, mapping morphisms according to their inclusion with respect to that point.

StalkSkyscraperPresheafAdjunctionAuxs.to.fullDefinition: def toSkyscraperPresheaf {𝓕 : Presheaf C X} {c : C} (f : 𝓕.stalk p₀ ⟶ c) :     𝓕 ⟶ skyscraperPresheaf p₀ c where   app U :=     if h : p₀ ∈ U.unop then 𝓕.germ ⟨p₀, h⟩ ≫ f ≫ eqToHom (if_pos h).symm     else ((if_neg h).symm.ndrec terminalIsTerminal).from _   naturality U V inc := by     -- Porting note: don't know why original proof fell short of working, add `aesop_cat` finished     -- the proofs anyway     dsimp     by_cases hV : p₀ ∈ V.unop     · have hU : p₀ ∈ U.unop := leOfHom inc.unop hV       split_ifs       erw [← Category.assoc, 𝓕.germ_res inc.unop, Category.assoc, Category.assoc, eqToHom_trans]     · split_ifs       exact ((if_neg hV).symm.ndrec terminalIsTerminal).hom_ext ..

TopCat.PrelocalPredicate.sheafify.fullDefinition: def PrelocalPredicate.sheafify {T : X → Type v} (P : PrelocalPredicate T) : LocalPredicate T where   pred {U} f := ∀ x : U, ∃ (V : Opens X) (_ : x.1 ∈ V) (i : V ⟶ U), P.pred fun x : V => f (i x : U)   res {V U} i f w x := by     specialize w (i x)     rcases w with ⟨V', m', i', p⟩     refine ⟨V ⊓ V', ⟨x.2, m'⟩, Opens.infLELeft _ _, ?_⟩     convert P.res (Opens.infLERight V V') _ p   locality {U} f w x := by     specialize w x     rcases w with ⟨V, m, i, p⟩     specialize p ⟨x.1, m⟩     rcases p with ⟨V', m', i', p'⟩     exact ⟨V', m', i' ≫ i, p'⟩ set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
TopCat.PrelocalPredicate.sheafify.description: A prelocal predicate can be transformed into a local predicate by requiring that its condition is satisfied in the neighborhoods around every point.

Top.stalk_to_fiber.fullDefinition: def stalkToFiber (P : LocalPredicate T) (x : X) : (subsheafToTypes P).presheaf.stalk x ⟶ T x := by   refine     colimit.desc _       { pt := T x         ι :=           { app := fun U f => ?_             naturality := ?_ } }   · exact f.1 ⟨x, (unop U).2⟩   · aesop set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
Top.stalk_to_fiber.description: A canonical map exists that connects the stalk of a presheaf to the original fiber by evaluating its sections.

TopCat.stalkToFiber_injective.code:
TopCat.stalkToFiber_injective.{v} {X : TopCat} {T : ↑X → Type v} (P : LocalPredicate T) (x : ↑X)
  (w :
    ∀ (U V : OpenNhds x) (fU : (y : ↥U.obj) → T ↑y),
      P.pred fU →
        ∀ (fV : (y : ↥V.obj) → T ↑y),
          P.pred fV →
            fU ⟨x, ⋯⟩ = fV ⟨x, ⋯⟩ →
              ∃ W iU iV, ∀ (w : ↥W.obj), fU ((fun x_4 => ⟨↑x_4, ⋯⟩) w) = fV ((fun x_4 => ⟨↑x_4, ⋯⟩) w)) :
  Function.Injective (stalkToFiber P x)
TopCat.stalkToFiber_injective.comment:
The `stalkToFiber` map is injective at `x` if any two allowed sections which agree at `x`
agree on some neighborhood of `x`.

explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply: The theorem shows that the application of the germ of a presheaf at a point within an open set, paired with the action of a morphism of open sets on a section, equals the germ of a corresponding local section at that point when considered under the presheaf's operations.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.FullSubcategory.obj: This definition specifies the object type within a category that is identified as a full subcategory, which includes all objects that satisfy a certain property.

TopCat.Presheaf.Sheafify.isGerm.description: A germ of a presheaf at a point is defined as a concept indicating that the behavior of the presheaf functions locally around that point is consistent with their values in the stalk at that point.

Bornology.ofDist.fullDefinition: abbrev Bornology.ofDist {α : Type*} (dist : α → α → ℝ) (dist_comm : ∀ x y, dist x y = dist y x)     (dist_triangle : ∀ x y z, dist x z ≤ dist x y + dist y z) : Bornology α :=   Bornology.ofBounded { s : Set α | ∃ C, ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → ∀ ⦃y⦄, y ∈ s → dist x y ≤ C }     ⟨0, fun x hx y => hx.elim⟩ (fun s ⟨c, hc⟩ t h => ⟨c, fun x hx y hy => hc (h hx) (h hy)⟩)     (fun s hs t ht => by       rcases s.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | ⟨x, hx⟩       · rwa [empty_union]       rcases t.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | ⟨y, hy⟩       · rwa [union_empty]       rsuffices ⟨C, hC⟩ : ∃ C, ∀ z ∈ s ∪ t, dist x z ≤ C       · refine ⟨C + C, fun a ha b hb => (dist_triangle a x b).trans ?_⟩         simpa only [dist_comm] using add_le_add (hC _ ha) (hC _ hb)       rcases hs with ⟨Cs, hs⟩; rcases ht with ⟨Ct, ht⟩       refine ⟨max Cs (dist x y + Ct), fun z hz => hz.elim         (fun hz => (hs hx hz).trans (le_max_left _ _))         (fun hz => (dist_triangle x y z).trans <|           (add_le_add le_rfl (ht hy hz)).trans (le_max_right _ _))⟩)     fun z => ⟨dist z z, forall_eq.2 <| forall_eq.2 le_rfl⟩

PseudoMetricSpace.ofDistTopology.fullDefinition: def PseudoMetricSpace.ofDistTopology {α : Type u} [TopologicalSpace α] (dist : α → α → ℝ)     (dist_self : ∀ x : α, dist x x = 0) (dist_comm : ∀ x y : α, dist x y = dist y x)     (dist_triangle : ∀ x y z : α, dist x z ≤ dist x y + dist y z)     (H : ∀ s : Set α, IsOpen s ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ∃ ε > 0, ∀ y, dist x y < ε → y ∈ s) :     PseudoMetricSpace α :=   { dist := dist     dist_self := dist_self     dist_comm := dist_comm     dist_triangle := dist_triangle     toUniformSpace :=       (UniformSpace.ofDist dist dist_self dist_comm dist_triangle).replaceTopology <|         TopologicalSpace.ext_iff.2 fun s ↦ (H s).trans <| forall₂_congr fun x _ ↦           ((UniformSpace.hasBasis_ofFun (exists_gt (0 : ℝ)) dist dist_self dist_comm dist_triangle             UniformSpace.ofDist_aux).comap (Prod.mk x)).mem_iff.symm     uniformity_dist := rfl     toBornology := Bornology.ofDist dist dist_comm dist_triangle     cobounded_sets := rfl }

PseudoMetricSpace.toPseudoEMetricSpace.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) PseudoMetricSpace.toPseudoEMetricSpace : PseudoEMetricSpace α :=   { ‹PseudoMetricSpace α› with     edist_self := by simp [edist_dist]     edist_comm := fun _ _ => by simp only [edist_dist, dist_comm]     edist_triangle := fun x y z => by       simp only [edist_dist, ← ENNReal.ofReal_add, dist_nonneg]       rw [ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff _]       · exact dist_triangle _ _ _       · simpa using add_le_add (dist_nonneg : 0 ≤ dist x y) dist_nonneg     uniformity_edist := Metric.uniformity_edist }

explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.

PseudoEMetricSpace.toPseudoMetricSpaceOf.comment:
One gets a pseudometric space from an emetric space if the edistance
is everywhere finite, by pushing the edistance to reals. We set it up so that the edist and the
uniformity are defeq in the pseudometric space and the pseudoemetric space. In this definition, the
distance is given separately, to be able to prescribe some expression which is not defeq to the
push-forward of the edistance to reals. See note [reducible non-instances].

PseudoEMetricSpace.toPseudoMetricSpaceOf.fullDefinition: abbrev PseudoEMetricSpace.toPseudoMetricSpaceOfDist {α : Type u} [e : PseudoEMetricSpace α]     (dist : α → α → ℝ) (edist_ne_top : ∀ x y : α, edist x y ≠ ⊤)     (h : ∀ x y, dist x y = ENNReal.toReal (edist x y)) : PseudoMetricSpace α where   dist := dist   dist_self x := by simp [h]   dist_comm x y := by simp [h, edist_comm]   dist_triangle x y z := by     simp only [h]     exact ENNReal.toReal_le_add (edist_triangle _ _ _) (edist_ne_top _ _) (edist_ne_top _ _)   edist := edist   edist_dist _ _ := by simp only [h, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal (edist_ne_top _ _)]   toUniformSpace := e.toUniformSpace   uniformity_dist := e.uniformity_edist.trans <| by     simpa only [ENNReal.coe_toNNReal (edist_ne_top _ _), h]       using (Metric.uniformity_edist_aux fun x y : α => (edist x y).toNNReal).symm
PseudoEMetricSpace.toPseudoMetricSpaceOf.description: A pseudometric space can be derived from an e-metric space by translating the defining e-distance into real numbers, under the condition that the e-distance is always finite.

explanatories.Dist.dist: A distance function that defines how to measure the separation between elements of a type can be created when the type adheres to the properties of a distance metric.
explanatories.PseudoMetricSpace.dist_self: The distance from any point to itself is zero in a pseudo-metric space.
explanatories.PseudoMetricSpace.dist_comm: In a pseudo-metric space, the distance between two points is symmetric, meaning that the distance from the first point to the second is equal to the distance from the second point back to the first.
explanatories.PseudoMetricSpace.dist_triangle: The distance between any two points in a pseudo-metric space satisfies the triangle inequality.
explanatories.PseudoMetricSpace.edist: The function defines a way to compute the extended non-negative distance between points in a pseudo-metric space.
explanatories.PseudoMetricSpace.edist_dist: The extended non-negative distance between any two points in a pseudo-metric space is equal to the non-negative real distance between those points as defined by the space's distance function.
explanatories.UniformSpace.comap: The inverse image of a uniformity on a uniform space under a function generates a new uniform space that captures the structure of the original space.
explanatories.PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace: A pseudo-metric space can be transformed into a uniform space.
explanatories.Metric.uniformity_basis_dist: The uniform structure of a pseudo-metric space can be characterized by a basis consisting of sets containing pairs of points that are closer than a specified distance.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.comap: A theorem asserting that if a filter has a basis, then the filter obtained by pulling back the basis through a function also has a basis characterized by the preimages of the original sets.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.eq_biInf: A theorem stating that a filter defined by a basis can be expressed as the infimum of the principal filters generated by the sets associated with the indices that satisfy the basis properties.
explanatories.Bornology.induced: This defines a bornology on a set by taking the inverse image of a bornological space through a function.
explanatories.Filter.mem_comap_iff_compl: A theorem stating that a set belongs to the preimage filter of a function if and only if the complement of the image of the set also belongs to the original filter.
explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.
explanatories.Bornology.isBounded_def: A set is bounded with respect to a bornology if and only if its complement belongs to the filter of cobounded sets in that bornological space.
explanatories.Metric.isBounded_iff: A set in a pseudo-metric space is bounded if and only if there exists a constant such that the distance between any two points in the set does not exceed that constant.
explanatories.Set.forall_mem_image: The condition that a property holds for all images of elements from a set under a function is equivalent to saying that the property holds for the function's output applied to every element of that set.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf: An element is in the set of all elements satisfying a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.dist_self: The theorem states that the distance from any point to itself in a pseudo-metric space is zero.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.

PseudoMetricSpace.induced.fullDefinition: abbrev PseudoMetricSpace.induced {α β} (f : α → β) (m : PseudoMetricSpace β) :     PseudoMetricSpace α where   dist x y := dist (f x) (f y)   dist_self x := dist_self _   dist_comm x y := dist_comm _ _   dist_triangle x y z := dist_triangle _ _ _   edist x y := edist (f x) (f y)   edist_dist x y := edist_dist _ _   toUniformSpace := UniformSpace.comap f m.toUniformSpace   uniformity_dist := (uniformity_basis_dist.comap _).eq_biInf   toBornology := Bornology.induced f   cobounded_sets := Set.ext fun s => mem_comap_iff_compl.trans <| by     simp only [← isBounded_def, isBounded_iff, forall_mem_image, mem_setOf]

explanatories.PseudoMetricSpace.edist: The function defines a way to compute the extended non-negative distance between points in a pseudo-metric space.
explanatories.PseudoMetricSpace.edist_dist: The extended non-negative distance between any two points in a pseudo-metric space is equal to the non-negative real distance between those points as defined by the space's distance function.
explanatories.UniformSpace.comap: The inverse image of a uniformity on a uniform space under a function generates a new uniform space that captures the structure of the original space.
explanatories.PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace: A pseudo-metric space can be transformed into a uniform space.
explanatories.Metric.uniformity_basis_dist: The uniform structure of a pseudo-metric space can be characterized by a basis consisting of sets containing pairs of points that are closer than a specified distance.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.comap: A theorem asserting that if a filter has a basis, then the filter obtained by pulling back the basis through a function also has a basis characterized by the preimages of the original sets.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.eq_biInf: A theorem stating that a filter defined by a basis can be expressed as the infimum of the principal filters generated by the sets associated with the indices that satisfy the basis properties.
explanatories.Bornology.induced: This defines a bornology on a set by taking the inverse image of a bornological space through a function.
explanatories.Filter.mem_comap_iff_compl: A theorem stating that a set belongs to the preimage filter of a function if and only if the complement of the image of the set also belongs to the original filter.
explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.
explanatories.Bornology.isBounded_def: A set is bounded with respect to a bornology if and only if its complement belongs to the filter of cobounded sets in that bornological space.
explanatories.Metric.isBounded_iff: A set in a pseudo-metric space is bounded if and only if there exists a constant such that the distance between any two points in the set does not exceed that constant.
explanatories.Set.forall_mem_image: The condition that a property holds for all images of elements from a set under a function is equivalent to saying that the property holds for the function's output applied to every element of that set.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf: An element is in the set of all elements satisfying a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.dist_self: The theorem states that the distance from any point to itself in a pseudo-metric space is zero.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.

pseudo_metric_space.induced.fullDefinition: abbrev PseudoMetricSpace.induced {α β} (f : α → β) (m : PseudoMetricSpace β) :     PseudoMetricSpace α where   dist x y := dist (f x) (f y)   dist_self x := dist_self _   dist_comm x y := dist_comm _ _   dist_triangle x y z := dist_triangle _ _ _   edist x y := edist (f x) (f y)   edist_dist x y := edist_dist _ _   toUniformSpace := UniformSpace.comap f m.toUniformSpace   uniformity_dist := (uniformity_basis_dist.comap _).eq_biInf   toBornology := Bornology.induced f   cobounded_sets := Set.ext fun s => mem_comap_iff_compl.trans <| by     simp only [← isBounded_def, isBounded_iff, forall_mem_image, mem_setOf]

explanatories.Dist.dist: A distance function that defines how to measure the separation between elements of a type can be created when the type adheres to the properties of a distance metric.
explanatories.Set.forall_mem_image: The condition that a property holds for all images of elements from a set under a function is equivalent to saying that the property holds for the function's output applied to every element of that set.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.max_le_iff: An element is less than or equal to the maximum of two others if and only if it is less than or equal to both of those two elements.
explanatories.PseudoEMetricSpace.toPseudoMetricSpaceOf: A pseudometric space can be derived from an e-metric space by translating the defining e-distance into real numbers, under the condition that the e-distance is always finite.
explanatories.max_lt: This theorem states that if two elements are both less than a third element in a linear order, then the maximum of the first two elements is also less than the third element.
explanatories.edist_lt_top: In a pseudo-metric space, the extended distance between any two points is always finite.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne: A theorem indicating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then they must be distinct.
explanatories.sup_eq_max: The supremum of two elements in a linear order is equal to the maximum of those two elements.
explanatories.dist_edist: The distance between two points in a pseudo-metric space can be expressed as the real value derived from their extended distance.
explanatories.ENNReal.toReal_max: This theorem establishes that for two non-infinite positive extended nonnegative real numbers, the conversion of their maximum to a real number is equal to the maximum of their individual conversions to real numbers.
explanatories.edist_ne_top: In a pseudometric space, the extended distance between any two elements is always finite.
explanatories.Prod.edist_eq: The distance between two ordered pairs from different pseudo-metric spaces is given by the maximum distance between their corresponding elements.
explanatories.PseudoMetricSpace.replaceBornology: A new pseudo-metric space is constructed from an existing one while ensuring that the bornology defined for it is equivalent to a specified bornology structure.
explanatories.Bornology.isBounded_image_fst_and_snd: The image of the first and second components of a set of ordered pairs is bounded if and only if the original set is bounded in the context of the given bornological spaces.
explanatories.Metric.isBounded_iff_eventually: A set is bounded in a pseudo-metric space if and only if there exists a real number such that the distance between any two points in the set does not exceed that number as one approaches infinity.
explanatories.Filter.eventually_and: A theorem stating that a property holds for almost all elements with respect to a filter if and only if both component properties hold for almost all elements.
explanatories.forall_and: The universal quantification of a conjunction of two properties is equivalent to the conjunction of the universal quantifications of each property individually.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.

Prod.pseudoMetricSpaceMax.fullDefinition: instance Prod.pseudoMetricSpaceMax : PseudoMetricSpace (α × β) :=   let i := PseudoEMetricSpace.toPseudoMetricSpaceOfDist     (fun x y : α × β => dist x.1 y.1 ⊔ dist x.2 y.2)     (fun x y => (max_lt (edist_lt_top _ _) (edist_lt_top _ _)).ne) fun x y => by       simp only [sup_eq_max, dist_edist, ← ENNReal.toReal_max (edist_ne_top _ _) (edist_ne_top _ _),         Prod.edist_eq]   i.replaceBornology fun s => by     simp only [← isBounded_image_fst_and_snd, isBounded_iff_eventually, forall_mem_image, ←       eventually_and, ← forall_and, ← max_le_iff]     rfl

pseudoMetricSpacePi.fullDefinition: instance pseudoMetricSpacePi : PseudoMetricSpace (∀ b, π b) := by   /- we construct the instance from the pseudoemetric space instance to avoid checking again that     the uniformity is the same as the product uniformity, but we register nevertheless a nice     formula for the distance -/   let i := PseudoEMetricSpace.toPseudoMetricSpaceOfDist     (fun f g : ∀ b, π b => ((sup univ fun b => nndist (f b) (g b) : ℝ≥0) : ℝ))     (fun f g => ((Finset.sup_lt_iff bot_lt_top).2 fun b _ => edist_lt_top _ _).ne)     (fun f g => by       simp only [edist_pi_def, edist_nndist, ← ENNReal.coe_finset_sup, ENNReal.coe_toReal])   refine i.replaceBornology fun s => ?_   simp only [← isBounded_def, isBounded_iff_eventually, ← forall_isBounded_image_eval_iff,     forall_mem_image, ← Filter.eventually_all, Function.eval_apply, @dist_nndist (π _)]   refine eventually_congr ((eventually_ge_atTop 0).mono fun C hC ↦ ?_)   lift C to ℝ≥0 using hC   refine ⟨fun H x hx y hy ↦ NNReal.coe_le_coe.2 <| Finset.sup_le fun b _ ↦ H b hx hy,     fun H b x hx y hy ↦ NNReal.coe_le_coe.2 ?_⟩   simpa only using Finset.sup_le_iff.1 (NNReal.coe_le_coe.1 <| H hx hy) b (Finset.mem_univ b)

IsMetricSeparated.comment:
Two sets in an (extended) metric space are called *metric separated* if the (extended) distance
between `x ∈ s` and `y ∈ t` is bounded from below by a positive constant.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.EDist.edist: A distance function is defined on a type, returning non-negative extended real numbers between pairs of its elements.

IsMetricSeparated.fullDefinition: def IsMetricSeparated {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] (s t : Set X) :=   ∃ r, r ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ t, r ≤ edist x y
IsMetricSeparated.description: Two sets in an extended metric space are considered metric separated if there is a positive lower bound on the distance between any point in one set and any point in the other set.

complete_of_proper.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) complete_of_proper [ProperSpace α] : CompleteSpace α :=   ⟨fun {f} hf => by     /- We want to show that the Cauchy filter `f` is converging. It suffices to find a closed       ball (therefore compact by properness) where it is nontrivial. -/     obtain ⟨t, t_fset, ht⟩ : ∃ t ∈ f, ∀ x ∈ t, ∀ y ∈ t, dist x y < 1 :=       (Metric.cauchy_iff.1 hf).2 1 zero_lt_one     rcases hf.1.nonempty_of_mem t_fset with ⟨x, xt⟩     have : closedBall x 1 ∈ f := mem_of_superset t_fset fun y yt => (ht y yt x xt).le     rcases (isCompact_iff_totallyBounded_isComplete.1 (isCompact_closedBall x 1)).2 f hf         (le_principal_iff.2 this) with       ⟨y, -, hy⟩     exact ⟨y, hy⟩⟩

  (H : ∀ (u : ℕ → α), (∀ (N n m : ℕ), N ≤ n → N ≤ m → dist (u n) (u m) < B N) → ∃ x, Tendsto u atTop (𝓝 x)) :
  CompleteSpace α
Metric.complete_of_convergent_controlled.comment:
A very useful criterion to show that a space is complete is to show that all sequences
which satisfy a bound of the form `dist (u n) (u m) < B N` for all `n m ≥ N` are
converging. This is often applied for `B N = 2^{-N}`, i.e., with a very fast convergence to
`0`, which makes it possible to use arguments of converging series, while this is impossible
to do in general for arbitrary Cauchy sequences.

indexed by the same type.

  (hR : ∀ (x : α), 0 < R x) :
  ∃ ι c r r',
    (∀ (i : ι), 0 < r i ∧ r i < r' i ∧ r' i < R (c i)) ∧
      (LocallyFinite fun i => ball (c i) (r' i)) ∧ ⋃ i, ball (c i) (r i) = univ
exists_locallyFinite_iUnion_eq_ball_radi.comment:
Let `R : α → ℝ` be a (possibly discontinuous) positive function on a proper metric space. Then
there exists a collection of pairs of balls `Metric.ball (c i) (r i)`, `Metric.ball (c i) (r' i)`
such that

* for all `i` we have `0 < r i < r' i < R (c i)`;
* the family of balls `Metric.ball (c i) (r' i)` is locally finite;
* the balls `Metric.ball (c i) (r i)` cover the whole space.

This is a simple corollary of `refinement_of_locallyCompact_sigmaCompact_of_nhds_basis`
and `exists_iUnion_ball_eq_radius_pos_lt` or `exists_locallyFinite_subset_iUnion_ball_radius_lt`.

AntilipschitzWith.comment:
We say that `f : α → β` is `AntilipschitzWith K` if for any two points `x`, `y` we have
`edist x y ≤ K * edist (f x) (f y)`.

explanatories.EDist.edist: A distance function is defined on a type, returning non-negative extended real numbers between pairs of its elements.

AntilipschitzWith.fullDefinition: def AntilipschitzWith [PseudoEMetricSpace α] [PseudoEMetricSpace β] (K : ℝ≥0) (f : α → β) :=   ∀ x y, edist x y ≤ K * edist (f x) (f y)
AntilipschitzWith.description: A function is classified as an Antilipschitz map if the distance between any two points in the domain is at most a constant multiple of the distance between their images in the codomain.

explanatories.add_le_add: This theorem states that if two pairs of elements each satisfy an order relation, then the sum of the first pair is less than or equal to the sum of the second pair, preserving the order.
explanatories.dist_smul_pair: The distance between two scaled elements in a pseudo-metric space is bounded by the product of the distance from one of the scaling factors to zero and the distance between the two original elements.
explanatories.dist_pair_smul: The distance between the results of scaling two elements by a common factor in two pseudo-metric spaces is bounded by the product of the distance between those elements and the distance from the scaled factor to zero.
explanatories.Metric.continuous_iff: A function in a pseudo-metric space is continuous if and only if, for every point and positive distance, there exists a smaller positive distance such that points within that smaller distance from the original point map to points within the specified positive distance under the function.
explanatories.Continuous.tendsto': If a function is continuous at a point, then it tends to the value of that function at that point as the input approaches it.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.eventually: A theorem stating that if a function converges to a certain filter, and a property holds for almost all values under a second filter, then the property also holds for almost all values under the first filter after applying the function.
explanatories.gt_mem_nhds: This theorem asserts that in an order topology, for any two elements where one is less than the other, there exists a neighborhood around the smaller element that contains only elements less than the larger element.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.exists_gt: This theorem asserts that in a topological space with a preorder, if a property holds for infinitely many points in a neighborhood of a point, then there exists a point within that neighborhood that is greater than the given point and satisfies the property.
explanatories.max_lt_iff: An element is less than the maximum of two others if and only if it is less than each of those two elements.
explanatories.dist_triangle: The triangle inequality states that in a pseudo-metric space, the distance from one point to another cannot exceed the sum of the distances from the first point to a third point and from that third point to the second point.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.add_le_add_right: This theorem states that if one element is less than or equal to another, then adding a common element to the right side of the inequality preserves that relationship.
explanatories.LT.lt.le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than a second, then it is also less than or equal to that second element.
explanatories.Eq.le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if two elements are equal, then one is less than or equal to the other.

BoundedSMul.continuousSMul.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) BoundedSMul.continuousSMul : ContinuousSMul α β where   continuous_smul := by     rw [Metric.continuous_iff]     rintro ⟨a, b⟩ ε ε0     obtain ⟨δ, δ0, hδε⟩ : ∃ δ > 0, δ * (δ + dist b 0) + dist a 0 * δ < ε := by       have : Continuous fun δ ↦ δ * (δ + dist b 0) + dist a 0 * δ := by fun_prop       refine ((this.tendsto' _ _ ?_).eventually (gt_mem_nhds ε0)).exists_gt       simp     refine ⟨δ, δ0, fun (a', b') hab' => ?_⟩     obtain ⟨ha, hb⟩ := max_lt_iff.1 hab'     calc dist (a' • b') (a • b)         ≤ dist (a' • b') (a • b') + dist (a • b') (a • b) := dist_triangle ..       _ ≤ dist a' a * dist b' 0 + dist a 0 * dist b' b :=         add_le_add (dist_pair_smul _ _ _) (dist_smul_pair _ _ _)       _ ≤ δ * (δ + dist b 0) + dist a 0 * δ := by           have : dist b' 0 ≤ δ + dist b 0 := (dist_triangle _ _ _).trans <| add_le_add_right hb.le _           gcongr       _ < ε := hδε

explanatories.add_le_add: This theorem states that if two pairs of elements each satisfy an order relation, then the sum of the first pair is less than or equal to the sum of the second pair, preserving the order.
explanatories.dist_smul_pair: The distance between two scaled elements in a pseudo-metric space is bounded by the product of the distance from one of the scaling factors to zero and the distance between the two original elements.
explanatories.dist_pair_smul: The distance between the results of scaling two elements by a common factor in two pseudo-metric spaces is bounded by the product of the distance between those elements and the distance from the scaled factor to zero.
explanatories.Metric.continuous_iff: A function in a pseudo-metric space is continuous if and only if, for every point and positive distance, there exists a smaller positive distance such that points within that smaller distance from the original point map to points within the specified positive distance under the function.
explanatories.Continuous.tendsto': If a function is continuous at a point, then it tends to the value of that function at that point as the input approaches it.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.eventually: A theorem stating that if a function converges to a certain filter, and a property holds for almost all values under a second filter, then the property also holds for almost all values under the first filter after applying the function.
explanatories.gt_mem_nhds: This theorem asserts that in an order topology, for any two elements where one is less than the other, there exists a neighborhood around the smaller element that contains only elements less than the larger element.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.exists_gt: This theorem asserts that in a topological space with a preorder, if a property holds for infinitely many points in a neighborhood of a point, then there exists a point within that neighborhood that is greater than the given point and satisfies the property.
explanatories.max_lt_iff: An element is less than the maximum of two others if and only if it is less than each of those two elements.
explanatories.dist_triangle: The triangle inequality states that in a pseudo-metric space, the distance from one point to another cannot exceed the sum of the distances from the first point to a third point and from that third point to the second point.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.add_le_add_right: This theorem states that if one element is less than or equal to another, then adding a common element to the right side of the inequality preserves that relationship.

  MetricSpace (X ⊕ Y)
Metric.glueMetricApprox.comment:
Given two maps `Φ` and `Ψ` intro metric spaces `X` and `Y` such that the distances between
`Φ p` and `Φ q`, and between `Ψ p` and `Ψ q`, coincide up to `2 ε` where `ε > 0`, one can almost
glue the two spaces `X` and `Y` along the images of `Φ` and `Ψ`, so that `Φ p` and `Ψ p` are
at distance `ε`.

Metric.Sum.dist.code: Metric.Sum.dist.{u, v} {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} [MetricSpace X] [MetricSpace Y] : X ⊕ Y → X ⊕ Y → ℝ
Metric.Sum.dist.comment:
Distance on a disjoint union. There are many (noncanonical) ways to put a distance compatible
with each factor.
If the two spaces are bounded, one can say for instance that each point in the first is at distance
`diam X + diam Y + 1` of each point in the second.
Instead, we choose a construction that works for unbounded spaces, but requires basepoints,
chosen arbitrarily.
We embed isometrically each factor, set the basepoints at distance 1,
arbitrarily, and say that the distance from `a` to `b` is the sum of the distances of `a` and `b` to
their respective basepoints, plus the distance 1 between the basepoints.
Since there is an arbitrary choice in this construction, it is not an instance by default.

metric.sigma.dist.comment:
Distance on a disjoint union. There are many (noncanonical) ways to put a distance compatible
with each factor.
We choose a construction that works for unbounded spaces, but requires basepoints,
chosen arbitrarily.
We embed isometrically each factor, set the basepoints at distance 1, arbitrarily,
and say that the distance from `a` to `b` is the sum of the distances of `a` and `b` to
their respective basepoints, plus the distance 1 between the basepoints.
Since there is an arbitrary choice in this construction, it is not an instance by default.

Metric.inductivePremetric.fullDefinition: def inductivePremetric (I : ∀ n, Isometry (f n)) : PseudoMetricSpace (Σn, X n) where   dist := inductiveLimitDist f   dist_self x := by simp [dist, inductiveLimitDist]   dist_comm x y := by     let m := max x.1 y.1     have hx : x.1 ≤ m := le_max_left _ _     have hy : y.1 ≤ m := le_max_right _ _     unfold dist; simp only     rw [inductiveLimitDist_eq_dist I x y m hx hy, inductiveLimitDist_eq_dist I y x m hy hx,       dist_comm]   dist_triangle x y z := by     let m := max (max x.1 y.1) z.1     have hx : x.1 ≤ m := le_trans (le_max_left _ _) (le_max_left _ _)     have hy : y.1 ≤ m := le_trans (le_max_right _ _) (le_max_left _ _)     have hz : z.1 ≤ m := le_max_right _ _     calc       inductiveLimitDist f x z = dist (leRecOn hx (f _) x.2 : X m) (leRecOn hz (f _) z.2 : X m) :=         inductiveLimitDist_eq_dist I x z m hx hz       _ ≤ dist (leRecOn hx (f _) x.2 : X m) (leRecOn hy (f _) y.2 : X m) +             dist (leRecOn hy (f _) y.2 : X m) (leRecOn hz (f _) z.2 : X m) :=         (dist_triangle _ _ _)       _ = inductiveLimitDist f x y + inductiveLimitDist f y z := by         rw [inductiveLimitDist_eq_dist I x y m hx hy, inductiveLimitDist_eq_dist I y z m hy hz]

ContractingWith.exists_fixedPoint.code:
ContractingWith.exists_fixedPoint.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [EMetricSpace α] [cs : CompleteSpace α] {K : ℝ≥0} {f : α → α}
  (hf : ContractingWith K f) (x : α) (hx : edist x (f x) ≠ ⊤) :
  ∃ y,
    IsFixedPt f y ∧
      Tendsto (fun n => f^[n] x) atTop (𝓝 y) ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), edist (f^[n] x) y ≤ edist x (f x) * ↑K ^ n / (1 - ↑K)
ContractingWith.exists_fixedPoint.comment:
Banach fixed-point theorem, contraction mapping theorem, `EMetricSpace` version.
A contracting map on a complete metric space has a fixed point.
We include more conclusions in this theorem to avoid proving them again later.

The main API for this theorem are the functions `efixedPoint` and `fixedPoint`,
and lemmas about these functions.

explanatories.Filter.atTop: This definition introduces a filter that captures the behavior of elements approaching infinity in an ordered set, generated by all sets containing elements greater than or equal to any given element.

ContractingWith.exists_fixedPoint.description: In a complete metric space, a contracting map guarantees the existence of a fixed point, and the iterates of any initial point converge to this fixed point while their distances to it are bounded by a factor involving the contraction constant.

ContractingWith.efixedPoint_eq_of_edist_.comment:
If a globally contracting map `f` has two complete forward-invariant sets `s`, `t`,
and `x ∈ s` is at a finite distance from `y ∈ t`, then the `efixedPoint'` constructed by `x`
is the same as the `efixedPoint'` constructed by `y`.

This lemma takes additional arguments stating that `f` contracts on `s` and `t` because this way
it can be used to prove the desired equality with non-trivial proofs of these facts.

PiNat.metricSpace.comment:
Metric space structure on `Π (n : ℕ), E n` when the spaces `E n` have the discrete topology,
where the distance is given by `dist x y = (1/2)^n`, where `n` is the smallest index where `x` and
`y` differ. Not registered as a global instance by default.
Warning: this definition makes sure that the topology is defeq to the original product topology,
but it does not take care of a possible uniformity. If the `E n` have a uniform structure, then
there will be two non-defeq uniform structures on `Π n, E n`, the product one and the one coming
from the metric structure. In this case, use `metricSpaceOfDiscreteUniformity` instead.

explanatories.PiNat.eq_of_dist_eq_zero: If the distance between two sequences is zero, then the sequences are identical.

PiNat.metricSpaceOfDiscreteUniformity.fullDefinition: protected def metricSpaceOfDiscreteUniformity {E : ℕ → Type*} [∀ n, UniformSpace (E n)]     (h : ∀ n, uniformity (E n) = 𝓟 idRel) : MetricSpace (∀ n, E n) :=   haveI : ∀ n, DiscreteTopology (E n) := fun n => discreteTopology_of_discrete_uniformity (h n)   { dist_triangle := PiNat.dist_triangle     dist_comm := PiNat.dist_comm     dist_self := PiNat.dist_self     eq_of_dist_eq_zero := PiNat.eq_of_dist_eq_zero _ _     toUniformSpace := Pi.uniformSpace _     uniformity_dist := by       simp [Pi.uniformity, comap_iInf, gt_iff_lt, preimage_setOf_eq, comap_principal,         PseudoMetricSpace.uniformity_dist, h, idRel]       apply le_antisymm       · simp only [le_iInf_iff, le_principal_iff]         intro ε εpos         obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ : ∃ n, (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ n < ε := exists_pow_lt_of_lt_one εpos (by norm_num)         apply           @mem_iInf_of_iInter _ _ _ _ _ (Finset.range n).finite_toSet fun i =>             { p : (∀ n : ℕ, E n) × ∀ n : ℕ, E n | p.fst i = p.snd i }         · simp only [mem_principal, setOf_subset_setOf, imp_self, imp_true_iff]         · rintro ⟨x, y⟩ hxy           simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_range, iInter_coe_set, mem_iInter, mem_setOf_eq]             at hxy           apply lt_of_le_of_lt _ hn           rw [← mem_cylinder_iff_dist_le, mem_cylinder_iff]           exact hxy       · simp only [le_iInf_iff, le_principal_iff]         intro n         refine mem_iInf_of_mem ((1 / 2) ^ n : ℝ) ?_         refine mem_iInf_of_mem (by positivity) ?_         simp only [mem_principal, setOf_subset_setOf, Prod.forall]         intro x y hxy         exact apply_eq_of_dist_lt hxy le_rfl }

explanatories.LT.lt.le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than a second, then it is also less than or equal to that second element.

explanatories.uniformity: This defines a filter on the product of a uniform space with itself, derived from the structure of the uniform space.
explanatories.Pi.uniformSpace: A uniform space can be defined for the space of functions indexed by a set, where each target type is itself equipped with a uniform structure.
explanatories.Pi.uniformity: The uniformity on the function space indexed by a set is equivalent to the infimum of the comap of the uniformities from each component space.
explanatories.Filter.comap_iInf: A theorem asserting that the filter created by transforming an infimum of a collection of filters through a function is equivalent to the infimum of the filters obtained by transforming each filter individually through the same function.

explanatories.Filter.comap_principal: A theorem stating that the filter obtained by applying a function to the principal filter corresponds to the principal filter of the preimage of a set under that function.
explanatories.PseudoMetricSpace.uniformity_dist: The uniform structure of a pseudo-metric space can be characterized as the infimum of the collections of entourages based on distances less than positive values.
explanatories.le_antisymm: This theorem establishes that in a partial order, if one element is less than or equal to another and vice versa, then the two elements must be equal.
explanatories.le_iInf_iff: This theorem states that a certain value is less than or equal to the infimum of a family of functions if and only if it is less than or equal to each individual function in that family.
explanatories.Filter.le_principal_iff: A theorem stating that a filter is less than or equal to the principal filter generated by a set if and only if that set belongs to the filter.
explanatories.Filter.mem_iInf_of_iInter: A theorem stating that a set belongs to the infimum of a collection of filters if it is contained in the intersection of finite sets, each of which is associated with the corresponding filters in that collection.
explanatories.Prod.fst: This defines a function that retrieves the first element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Filter.mem_principal: A theorem that equates membership in the principal filter generated by a set with the condition that the set is a subset of another set.
explanatories.Set.setOf_subset_setOf: The inclusion of the set of elements satisfying one property in the set of elements satisfying another property is equivalent to stating that whenever an element satisfies the first property, it must also satisfy the second property.
explanatories.imp_self: If a proposition is true, then it implies itself and is equivalent to the truth of any statement.
explanatories.Finset.mem_range: This theorem states that an integer is a member of the range of another integer if and only if it is less than that integer.
explanatories.Set.mem_iInter: An element belongs to the indexed intersection of sets if and only if it is included in every set specified by the indexing collection.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.Filter.mem_iInf_of_mem: A theorem stating that if a set belongs to a specific filter indexed by an element, then it also belongs to the infimum of all those filters.

explanatories.add_le_add: This theorem states that if two pairs of elements each satisfy an order relation, then the sum of the first pair is less than or equal to the sum of the second pair, preserving the order.
explanatories.dist_le_zero: The distance between two points in a metric space is less than or equal to zero if and only if those points are identical.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.add: The product of two functions that converge to respective limits in a topological space with a continuous multiplication structure also converges to the product of those limits.

explanatories.min_le_left: This theorem establishes that the minimum of two elements in a linear order is less than or equal to the first element.
explanatories.summable_geometric_two_encode: The infinite sum of the terms formed by taking half raised to the power of the encoding of each element in a countable set is convergent.

explanatories.dist_comm: The distance between two points in a pseudo-metric space is symmetric, meaning it is the same regardless of the order of the points.
explanatories.min_le_min: If one element is less than or equal to a second element and another element is less than or equal to a fourth element, then the minimum of the first two elements is less than or equal to the minimum of the last two elements.
explanatories.dist_triangle: The triangle inequality states that in a pseudo-metric space, the distance from one point to another cannot exceed the sum of the distances from the first point to a third point and from that third point to the second point.
explanatories.min_add_distrib: This theorem states that in a canonically linear ordered additive commutative monoid, the minimum of an element and the sum of two other elements is equal to the minimum of the first element and the sum of the minimums of the two other elements.
explanatories.min_le_right: This theorem demonstrates that the minimum of two elements in a linear order is less than or equal to the second element.
explanatories.tsum_le_tsum: If one series is term-wise less than or equal to another series and both are summable, then the sum of the first series is also less than or equal to the sum of the second series.

explanatories.tendsto_order: This theorem characterizes the convergence of a function in an order topology by stating that it approaches a limit if for every element less than the limit, the function eventually exceeds that element, and for every element greater than the limit, the function eventually remains below that element.
explanatories.tendsto_tsum_compl_atTop_zero: The sum of a function evaluated on the complement of an increasing subset converges to zero as that subset grows to include the entire space.
explanatories.half_pos: This theorem asserts that in a linear ordered semifield, if an element is positive, then half of that element is also positive.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.exists: A theorem stating that if a property holds for almost all elements in a non-empty filter, then there exists at least one element for which the property holds.
explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.
explanatories.exists_pos_mul_lt: This theorem states that in a linear ordered semifield, if an element is positive, then there exists a positive element such that the product of it and another element is less than the positive element.

explanatories.Finset.sum_le_sum: This theorem asserts that in an ordered additive commutative monoid, if each element of one finite sum is less than or equal to the corresponding element of another, then the total sum of the first set of elements is less than or equal to the total sum of the second set.

explanatories.add_le_add_right: This theorem states that if one element is less than or equal to another, then adding a common element to the right side of the inequality preserves that relationship.
explanatories.Finset.sum_const: The theorem establishes that the sum of a constant value over a finite set equals the product of the constant value and the cardinality of that set.

explanatories.add_halves: This theorem asserts that in a linear ordered semifield, the sum of half of any element and half of the same element equals the original element itself.
