pi_countable.metric_space.code:
PiCountable.metricSpace.{u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_2} [Encodable ι] {F : ι → Type u_3} [(i : ι) → MetricSpace (F i)] :
  MetricSpace ((i : ι) → F i)
pi_countable.metric_space.comment:
Given a countable family of metric spaces, one may put a distance on their product `Π i, E i`,
defining the right topology and uniform structure. It is highly non-canonical, though, and therefore
not registered as a global instance.
The distance we use here is `dist x y = ∑' n, min (1/2)^(encode i) (dist (x n) (y n))`.

explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Min.min: This defines a minimum operation that takes two elements and returns the lesser of the two.
explanatories.lt_min_iff: An element is less than the minimum of two others if and only if it is less than each of those two elements.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.PiNat.dist: The distance function on a product space is defined based on the first index at which two sequences differ, assigning a decreasing value based on the difference.
explanatories.Dist.dist: A distance function that defines how to measure the separation between elements of a type can be created when the type adheres to the properties of a distance metric.
explanatories.PiNat.dist_self: The distance between a sequence and itself is zero.
explanatories.PiNat.dist_comm: The distance between two sequences is symmetric, meaning it is the same regardless of the order in which the sequences are considered.
explanatories.PiNat.dist_triangle: The distance between two sequences is less than or equal to the sum of the distances between each of the sequences and a third sequence.
explanatories.PiNat.eq_of_dist_eq_zero: If the distance between two sequences is zero, then the sequences are identical.
explanatories.Finset.finite_toSet: A finite set can be constructed from a finite collection of elements, confirming it is also a finite set when regarded as a simple set.
explanatories.Finset.mem_coe: This theorem establishes that an element is a member of a finite set when considered as a subset of a larger set if and only if it is a member of the finite set itself.
explanatories.LT.lt.le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than a second, then it is also less than or equal to that second element.
explanatories.PiNat.metricSpace: A sequence of types with a discrete topology is endowed with a metric space structure where the distance between sequences is determined by the first index at which they differ.
explanatories.uniformity: This defines a filter on the product of a uniform space with itself, derived from the structure of the uniform space.
explanatories.Pi.uniformSpace: A uniform space can be defined for the space of functions indexed by a set, where each target type is itself equipped with a uniform structure.
explanatories.Pi.uniformity: The uniformity on the function space indexed by a set is equivalent to the infimum of the comap of the uniformities from each component space.
explanatories.Filter.comap_iInf: A theorem asserting that the filter created by transforming an infimum of a collection of filters through a function is equivalent to the infimum of the filters obtained by transforming each filter individually through the same function.
explanatories.gt_iff_lt: The relationship between greater than and less than for any two elements states that one element being greater than another is equivalent to the latter being less than the former.
explanatories.Set.preimage_setOf_eq: The preimage of the set of elements satisfying a property under a function is equal to the set of elements in the domain that map to elements satisfying that property.
explanatories.Filter.comap_principal: A theorem stating that the filter obtained by applying a function to the principal filter corresponds to the principal filter of the preimage of a set under that function.
explanatories.PseudoMetricSpace.uniformity_dist: The uniform structure of a pseudo-metric space can be characterized as the infimum of the collections of entourages based on distances less than positive values.
explanatories.le_antisymm: This theorem establishes that in a partial order, if one element is less than or equal to another and vice versa, then the two elements must be equal.
explanatories.le_iInf_iff: This theorem states that a certain value is less than or equal to the infimum of a family of functions if and only if it is less than or equal to each individual function in that family.
explanatories.Filter.le_principal_iff: A theorem stating that a filter is less than or equal to the principal filter generated by a set if and only if that set belongs to the filter.
explanatories.Filter.mem_iInf_of_iInter: A theorem stating that a set belongs to the infimum of a collection of filters if it is contained in the intersection of finite sets, each of which is associated with the corresponding filters in that collection.
explanatories.Prod.fst: This defines a function that retrieves the first element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Filter.mem_principal: A theorem that equates membership in the principal filter generated by a set with the condition that the set is a subset of another set.
explanatories.Set.setOf_subset_setOf: The inclusion of the set of elements satisfying one property in the set of elements satisfying another property is equivalent to stating that whenever an element satisfies the first property, it must also satisfy the second property.
explanatories.imp_self: If a proposition is true, then it implies itself and is equivalent to the truth of any statement.
explanatories.Finset.mem_range: This theorem states that an integer is a member of the range of another integer if and only if it is less than that integer.
explanatories.Set.mem_iInter: An element belongs to the indexed intersection of sets if and only if it is included in every set specified by the indexing collection.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.Filter.mem_iInf_of_mem: A theorem stating that if a set belongs to a specific filter indexed by an element, then it also belongs to the infimum of all those filters.
explanatories.Prod.forall: There is no mathematical statement or concept to summarize as no input was provided.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.add_le_add: This theorem states that if two pairs of elements each satisfy an order relation, then the sum of the first pair is less than or equal to the sum of the second pair, preserving the order.
explanatories.dist_le_zero: The distance between two points in a metric space is less than or equal to zero if and only if those points are identical.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.add: The product of two functions that converge to respective limits in a topological space with a continuous multiplication structure also converges to the product of those limits.
explanatories.Encodable.encode: This defines a method for encoding elements from a specific type into natural numbers.
explanatories.PiCountable.dist: A distance can be defined for the product of a countable family of metric spaces using a specific summation formula that involves the distances of individual elements from the spaces.
explanatories.PiCountable.dist_eq_tsum: The distance between two sequences is equal to the sum of the minimum distances of their corresponding elements, each weighted by a decreasing factor based on their indices.
explanatories.min_le_left: This theorem establishes that the minimum of two elements in a linear order is less than or equal to the first element.
explanatories.summable_geometric_two_encode: The infinite sum of the terms formed by taking half raised to the power of the encoding of each element in a countable set is convergent.
explanatories.PiCountable.dist_summable: The sum of distances between two sequences in a countable metric space, weighted by a diminishing geometric factor, is finite.
explanatories.PiCountable.dist_le_dist_pi_of_dist_lt: If the distance between two sequences is less than a certain decreasing value based on their indices, then the distance between the corresponding elements of those sequences is less than or equal to the overall distance between the two sequences.
explanatories.dist_comm: The distance between two points in a pseudo-metric space is symmetric, meaning it is the same regardless of the order of the points.
explanatories.min_le_min: If one element is less than or equal to a second element and another element is less than or equal to a fourth element, then the minimum of the first two elements is less than or equal to the minimum of the last two elements.
explanatories.dist_triangle: The triangle inequality states that in a pseudo-metric space, the distance from one point to another cannot exceed the sum of the distances from the first point to a third point and from that third point to the second point.
explanatories.min_add_distrib: This theorem states that in a canonically linear ordered additive commutative monoid, the minimum of an element and the sum of two other elements is equal to the minimum of the first element and the sum of the minimums of the two other elements.
explanatories.min_le_right: This theorem demonstrates that the minimum of two elements in a linear order is less than or equal to the second element.
explanatories.tsum_le_tsum: If one series is term-wise less than or equal to another series and both are summable, then the sum of the first series is also less than or equal to the sum of the second series.
explanatories.Summable.add: The sum of two summable functions is itself summable when the addition operation is continuous.
explanatories.tsum_add: The sum of the pointwise addition of two summable functions equals the sum of each function's individual sums when the underlying space is both T2 and supports continuous addition.
explanatories.tendsto_order: This theorem characterizes the convergence of a function in an order topology by stating that it approaches a limit if for every element less than the limit, the function eventually exceeds that element, and for every element greater than the limit, the function eventually remains below that element.
explanatories.tendsto_tsum_compl_atTop_zero: The sum of a function evaluated on the complement of an increasing subset converges to zero as that subset grows to include the entire space.
explanatories.half_pos: This theorem asserts that in a linear ordered semifield, if an element is positive, then half of that element is also positive.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.exists: A theorem stating that if a property holds for almost all elements in a non-empty filter, then there exists at least one element for which the property holds.
explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.
explanatories.exists_pos_mul_lt: This theorem states that in a linear ordered semifield, if an element is positive, then there exists a positive element such that the product of it and another element is less than the positive element.
explanatories.Set.Subset.rfl: Every set is a subset of itself.
explanatories.SetCoe.forall: The universal quantification over elements of a coerced subset is equivalent to universal quantification over the original set with membership constraints.
explanatories.sum_add_tsum_compl: The sum of a function over a finite set plus the sum of the function over the complement of that set equals the total sum of the function.
explanatories.Finset.sum_le_sum: This theorem asserts that in an ordered additive commutative monoid, if each element of one finite sum is less than or equal to the corresponding element of another, then the total sum of the first set of elements is less than or equal to the total sum of the second set.
explanatories.Summable.subtype: If a function is summable over its domain, then its restriction to a subtype formed by a specific set is also summable.
explanatories.add_lt_add_of_le_of_lt: This theorem demonstrates that if one element is less than or equal to another and a different element is strictly less than another, then adding these pairs of elements preserves the strict inequality in the sum.
explanatories.add_le_add_right: This theorem states that if one element is less than or equal to another, then adding a common element to the right side of the inequality preserves that relationship.
explanatories.Finset.sum_const: The theorem establishes that the sum of a constant value over a finite set equals the product of the constant value and the cardinality of that set.
explanatories.nsmul_eq_mul: This theorem establishes that the scalar multiplication of a natural number with an element of a non-associative semiring is equivalent to the multiplication of that natural number cast into the semiring with the element.
explanatories.add_halves: This theorem asserts that in a linear ordered semifield, the sum of half of any element and half of the same element equals the original element itself.
explanatories.lt_min: This theorem asserts that if an element is less than two other elements in a linear order, then it is also less than the minimum of those two elements.
explanatories.and_imp: The theorem states that the implication resulting from the conjunction of two propositions leading to a third proposition is equivalent to the scenario where each of the two propositions separately implies the third proposition.

EMetric.Closeds.emetricSpace.comment:
In emetric spaces, the Hausdorff edistance defines an emetric space structure
on the type of closed subsets

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.EMetric.hausdorffEdist: The Hausdorff extended distance between two sets is defined as the smallest radius such that each set is within that radius from the other set.
explanatories.EMetric.hausdorffEdist_self: The Hausdorff distance of a set to itself is zero.
explanatories.EMetric.hausdorffEdist_comm: The Hausdorff extended distances between two sets are symmetric, meaning the distance from the first set to the second is equal to the distance from the second set to the first.
explanatories.EMetric.hausdorffEdist_triangle: The Hausdorff distance between a set and a third set is less than or equal to the sum of the Hausdorff distances between the first set and a second set and between the second set and the third set, thus satisfying the triangle inequality.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.Closeds.ext: This theorem states that if two closed sets in a topological space are equal as sets, then they are also equal as bundled objects.
explanatories.EMetric.hausdorffEdist_zero_iff_eq_of_cl: Two closed sets have a Hausdorff distance of zero if and only if they are identical.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.Closeds.closed: This theorem demonstrates that the set associated with a bundled object representing closed sets in a topological space is itself confirmed to be closed.
explanatories.EDist.edist: A distance function is defined on a type, returning non-negative extended real numbers between pairs of its elements.
explanatories.PseudoEMetricSpace.edist_triangle: The triangle inequality for the distance function in a pseudo-metric space asserts that the distance from one point to another is less than or equal to the sum of the distances between the first point to a third point and the second point to that third point.
explanatories.PseudoEMetricSpace.edist_comm: The distance function in a pseudo-metric space is commutative, meaning the distance between two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.NonemptyCompacts.ext: This theorem asserts that if two nonempty compact sets are equal as subsets of a topological space, then they are also equal as nonempty compact sets.

EMetric.Closeds.emetricSpace.description: In emetric spaces, the structure of an emetric space is established on the collection of closed subsets using the Hausdorff distance.

explanatories.Nat.add_zero: Adding zero to a natural number does not change its value.
explanatories.Nat.zero_eq: Zero is equal to the natural number zero.

explanatories.cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete: A Cauchy sequence in a complete uniform space converges to some limit.

explanatories.mem_closure_of_tendsto: If a sequence of points converges to a point and those points eventually belong to a set, then that point is in the closure of the set.

explanatories.Filter.eventually_atTop: This theorem states that a property holds eventually for elements approaching positive infinity if and only if there exists an element such that the property holds for all elements greater than or equal to it in a semilattice structure.
explanatories.Set.mem_preimage: An element is in the preimage of a set under a function if and only if the image of that element is in the original set.
explanatories.Set.preimage_iUnion: The preimage of the union of a collection of sets under a function is equal to the union of the preimages of each individual set.

explanatories.zero_le: This theorem states that in a canonically ordered additive commutative monoid, any element is greater than or equal to zero.
explanatories.edist_le_of_edist_le_geometric_two_of_te: If the distance between consecutive terms in a sequence decreases geometrically, then the distance from the first term to the limit of the sequence is at most double the upper bound of the distances.
explanatories.le_refl: This theorem confirms that in a preorder, any element is related to itself under the less than or equal relation.

explanatories.two_mul: This theorem demonstrates that multiplying an element by two in a non-associative semiring is equivalent to adding the element to itself.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.

explanatories.Filter.atTop: This definition introduces a filter that captures the behavior of elements approaching infinity in an ordered set, generated by all sets containing elements greater than or equal to any given element.

explanatories.ENNReal.tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_l: The function that maps natural numbers to the powers of a non-negative extended real number less than one converges to zero as the natural numbers tend to infinity.
explanatories.ENNReal.one_lt_two: This theorem simply states that one is less than two.
explanatories.Or.inr: If there is a proof of a proposition, it can be included in a disjunction as the second option.
explanatories.MulZeroClass.mul_zero: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by zero results in zero, indicating that zero is an absorbing element in multiplication.

EMetric.Closeds.completeSpace.fullDefinition: instance Closeds.completeSpace [CompleteSpace α] : CompleteSpace (Closeds α) := by   /- We will show that, if a sequence of sets `s n` satisfies     `edist (s n) (s (n+1)) < 2^{-n}`, then it converges. This is enough to guarantee     completeness, by a standard completeness criterion.     We use the shorthand `B n = 2^{-n}` in ennreal. -/   let B : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞ := fun n => 2⁻¹ ^ n   have B_pos : ∀ n, (0 : ℝ≥0∞) < B n := by simp [B, ENNReal.pow_pos]   have B_ne_top : ∀ n, B n ≠ ⊤ := by simp [B, ENNReal.pow_ne_top]   /- Consider a sequence of closed sets `s n` with `edist (s n) (s (n+1)) < B n`.     We will show that it converges. The limit set is `t0 = ⋂n, closure (⋃m≥n, s m)`.     We will have to show that a point in `s n` is close to a point in `t0`, and a point     in `t0` is close to a point in `s n`. The completeness then follows from a     standard criterion. -/   refine complete_of_convergent_controlled_sequences B B_pos fun s hs => ?_   let t0 := ⋂ n, closure (⋃ m ≥ n, s m : Set α)   let t : Closeds α := ⟨t0, isClosed_iInter fun _ => isClosed_closure⟩   use t   -- The inequality is written this way to agree with `edist_le_of_edist_le_geometric_of_tendsto₀`   have I1 : ∀ n, ∀ x ∈ s n, ∃ y ∈ t0, edist x y ≤ 2 * B n := by     /- This is the main difficulty of the proof. Starting from `x ∈ s n`, we want            to find a point in `t0` which is close to `x`. Define inductively a sequence of            points `z m` with `z n = x` and `z m ∈ s m` and `edist (z m) (z (m+1)) ≤ B m`. This is            possible since the Hausdorff distance between `s m` and `s (m+1)` is at most `B m`.            This sequence is a Cauchy sequence, therefore converging as the space is complete, to            a limit which satisfies the required properties. -/     intro n x hx     obtain ⟨z, hz₀, hz⟩ :       ∃ z : ∀ l, s (n + l), (z 0 : α) = x ∧ ∀ k, edist (z k : α) (z (k + 1) : α) ≤ B n / 2 ^ k := by       -- We prove existence of the sequence by induction.       have : ∀ (l) (z : s (n + l)), ∃ z' : s (n + l + 1), edist (z : α) z' ≤ B n / 2 ^ l := by         intro l z         obtain ⟨z', z'_mem, hz'⟩ : ∃ z' ∈ s (n + l + 1), edist (z : α) z' < B n / 2 ^ l := by           refine exists_edist_lt_of_hausdorffEdist_lt (s := s (n + l)) z.2 ?_           simp only [ENNReal.inv_pow, div_eq_mul_inv]           rw [← pow_add]           apply hs <;> simp         exact ⟨⟨z', z'_mem⟩, le_of_lt hz'⟩       use fun k => Nat.recOn k ⟨x, hx⟩ fun l z => (this l z).choose       simp only [Nat.add_zero, Nat.zero_eq, Nat.rec_zero, Nat.rec_add_one, true_and]       exact fun k => (this k _).choose_spec     -- it follows from the previous bound that `z` is a Cauchy sequence     have : CauchySeq fun k => (z k : α) := cauchySeq_of_edist_le_geometric_two (B n) (B_ne_top n) hz     -- therefore, it converges     rcases cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete this with ⟨y, y_lim⟩     use y     -- the limit point `y` will be the desired point, in `t0` and close to our initial point `x`.     -- First, we check it belongs to `t0`.     have : y ∈ t0 :=       mem_iInter.2 fun k =>         mem_closure_of_tendsto y_lim           (by             simp only [exists_prop, Set.mem_iUnion, Filter.eventually_atTop, Set.mem_preimage,               Set.preimage_iUnion]             exact ⟨k, fun m hm => ⟨n + m, zero_add k ▸ add_le_add (zero_le n) hm, (z m).2⟩⟩)     use this     -- Then, we check that `y` is close to `x = z n`. This follows from the fact that `y`     -- is the limit of `z k`, and the distance between `z n` and `z k` has already been estimated.     rw [← hz₀]     exact edist_le_of_edist_le_geometric_two_of_tendsto₀ (B n) hz y_lim   have I2 : ∀ n, ∀ x ∈ t0, ∃ y ∈ s n, edist x y ≤ 2 * B n := by     /- For the (much easier) reverse inequality, we start from a point `x ∈ t0` and we want             to find a point `y ∈ s n` which is close to `x`.             `x` belongs to `t0`, the intersection of the closures. In particular, it is well             approximated by a point `z` in `⋃m≥n, s m`, say in `s m`. Since `s m` and             `s n` are close, this point is itself well approximated by a point `y` in `s n`,             as required. -/     intro n x xt0     have : x ∈ closure (⋃ m ≥ n, s m : Set α) := by apply mem_iInter.1 xt0 n     obtain ⟨z : α, hz, Dxz : edist x z < B n⟩ := mem_closure_iff.1 this (B n) (B_pos n)     simp only [exists_prop, Set.mem_iUnion] at hz     obtain ⟨m : ℕ, m_ge_n : m ≥ n, hm : z ∈ (s m : Set α)⟩ := hz     have : hausdorffEdist (s m : Set α) (s n) < B n := hs n m n m_ge_n (le_refl n)     obtain ⟨y : α, hy : y ∈ (s n : Set α), Dzy : edist z y < B n⟩ :=       exists_edist_lt_of_hausdorffEdist_lt hm this     exact       ⟨y, hy,         calc           edist x y ≤ edist x z + edist z y := edist_triangle _ _ _           _ ≤ B n + B n := add_le_add (le_of_lt Dxz) (le_of_lt Dzy)           _ = 2 * B n := (two_mul _).symm           ⟩   -- Deduce from the above inequalities that the distance between `s n` and `t0` is at most `2 B n`.   have main : ∀ n : ℕ, edist (s n) t ≤ 2 * B n := fun n =>     hausdorffEdist_le_of_mem_edist (I1 n) (I2 n)   -- from this, the convergence of `s n` to `t0` follows.   refine tendsto_atTop.2 fun ε εpos => ?_   have : Tendsto (fun n => 2 * B n) atTop (𝓝 (2 * 0)) :=     ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul (ENNReal.tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one <|       by simp [ENNReal.one_lt_two]) (Or.inr <| by simp)   rw [mul_zero] at this   obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ : ∃ N, ∀ b ≥ N, ε > 2 * B b :=     ((tendsto_order.1 this).2 ε εpos).exists_forall_of_atTop   exact ⟨N, fun n hn => lt_of_le_of_lt (main n) (hN n hn)⟩

EMetric.Closeds.compactSpace.fullDefinition: instance Closeds.compactSpace [CompactSpace α] : CompactSpace (Closeds α) :=   ⟨by     /- by completeness, it suffices to show that it is totally bounded,         i.e., for all ε>0, there is a finite set which is ε-dense.         start from a set `s` which is ε-dense in α. Then the subsets of `s`         are finitely many, and ε-dense for the Hausdorff distance. -/     refine       isCompact_of_totallyBounded_isClosed (EMetric.totallyBounded_iff.2 fun ε εpos => ?_)         isClosed_univ     rcases exists_between εpos with ⟨δ, δpos, δlt⟩     obtain ⟨s : Set α, fs : s.Finite, hs : univ ⊆ ⋃ y ∈ s, ball y δ⟩ :=       EMetric.totallyBounded_iff.1         (isCompact_iff_totallyBounded_isComplete.1 (@isCompact_univ α _ _)).1 δ δpos     -- we first show that any set is well approximated by a subset of `s`.     have main : ∀ u : Set α, ∃ v ⊆ s, hausdorffEdist u v ≤ δ := by       intro u       let v := { x : α | x ∈ s ∧ ∃ y ∈ u, edist x y < δ }       exists v, (fun x hx => hx.1 : v ⊆ s)       refine hausdorffEdist_le_of_mem_edist ?_ ?_       · intro x hx         have : x ∈ ⋃ y ∈ s, ball y δ := hs (by simp)         rcases mem_iUnion₂.1 this with ⟨y, ys, dy⟩         have : edist y x < δ := by simp at dy; rwa [edist_comm] at dy         exact ⟨y, ⟨ys, ⟨x, hx, this⟩⟩, le_of_lt dy⟩       · rintro x ⟨_, ⟨y, yu, hy⟩⟩         exact ⟨y, yu, le_of_lt hy⟩     -- introduce the set F of all subsets of `s` (seen as members of `Closeds α`).     let F := { f : Closeds α | (f : Set α) ⊆ s }     refine ⟨F, ?_, fun u _ => ?_⟩     -- `F` is finite     · apply @Finite.of_finite_image _ _ F _       · apply fs.finite_subsets.subset fun b => _         · exact fun s => (s : Set α)         simp only [F, and_imp, Set.mem_image, Set.mem_setOf_eq, exists_imp]         intro _ x hx hx'         rwa [hx'] at hx       · exact SetLike.coe_injective.injOn     -- `F` is ε-dense     · obtain ⟨t0, t0s, Dut0⟩ := main u       have : IsClosed t0 := (fs.subset t0s).isCompact.isClosed       let t : Closeds α := ⟨t0, this⟩       have : t ∈ F := t0s       have : edist u t < ε := lt_of_le_of_lt Dut0 δlt       apply mem_iUnion₂.2       exact ⟨t, ‹t ∈ F›, this⟩⟩

EMetric.NonemptyCompacts.emetricSpace.fullDefinition: instance NonemptyCompacts.emetricSpace : EMetricSpace (NonemptyCompacts α) where   edist s t := hausdorffEdist (s : Set α) t   edist_self s := hausdorffEdist_self   edist_comm s t := hausdorffEdist_comm   edist_triangle s t u := hausdorffEdist_triangle   eq_of_edist_eq_zero {s t} h := NonemptyCompacts.ext <| by     have : closure (s : Set α) = closure t := hausdorffEdist_zero_iff_closure_eq_closure.1 h     rwa [s.isCompact.isClosed.closure_eq, t.isCompact.isClosed.closure_eq] at this

EMetric.NonemptyCompacts.secondCountable.fullDefinition: instance NonemptyCompacts.secondCountableTopology [SecondCountableTopology α] :     SecondCountableTopology (NonemptyCompacts α) :=   haveI : SeparableSpace (NonemptyCompacts α) := by     /- To obtain a countable dense subset of `NonemptyCompacts α`, start from         a countable dense subset `s` of α, and then consider all its finite nonempty subsets.         This set is countable and made of nonempty compact sets. It turns out to be dense:         by total boundedness, any compact set `t` can be covered by finitely many small balls, and         approximations in `s` of the centers of these balls give the required finite approximation         of `t`. -/     rcases exists_countable_dense α with ⟨s, cs, s_dense⟩     let v0 := { t : Set α | t.Finite ∧ t ⊆ s }     let v : Set (NonemptyCompacts α) := { t : NonemptyCompacts α | (t : Set α) ∈ v0 }     refine ⟨⟨v, ?_, ?_⟩⟩     · have : v0.Countable := countable_setOf_finite_subset cs       exact this.preimage SetLike.coe_injective     · refine fun t => mem_closure_iff.2 fun ε εpos => ?_       -- t is a compact nonempty set, that we have to approximate uniformly by a a set in `v`.       rcases exists_between εpos with ⟨δ, δpos, δlt⟩       have δpos' : 0 < δ / 2 := ENNReal.half_pos δpos.ne'       -- construct a map F associating to a point in α an approximating point in s, up to δ/2.       have Exy : ∀ x, ∃ y, y ∈ s ∧ edist x y < δ / 2 := by         intro x         rcases mem_closure_iff.1 (s_dense x) (δ / 2) δpos' with ⟨y, ys, hy⟩         exact ⟨y, ⟨ys, hy⟩⟩       let F x := (Exy x).choose       have Fspec : ∀ x, F x ∈ s ∧ edist x (F x) < δ / 2 := fun x => (Exy x).choose_spec       -- cover `t` with finitely many balls. Their centers form a set `a`       have : TotallyBounded (t : Set α) := t.isCompact.totallyBounded       obtain ⟨a : Set α, af : Set.Finite a, ta : (t : Set α) ⊆ ⋃ y ∈ a, ball y (δ / 2)⟩ :=         totallyBounded_iff.1 this (δ / 2) δpos'       -- replace each center by a nearby approximation in `s`, giving a new set `b`       let b := F '' a       have : b.Finite := af.image _       have tb : ∀ x ∈ t, ∃ y ∈ b, edist x y < δ := by         intro x hx         rcases mem_iUnion₂.1 (ta hx) with ⟨z, za, Dxz⟩         exists F z, mem_image_of_mem _ za         calc           edist x (F z) ≤ edist x z + edist z (F z) := edist_triangle _ _ _           _ < δ / 2 + δ / 2 := ENNReal.add_lt_add Dxz (Fspec z).2           _ = δ := ENNReal.add_halves _       -- keep only the points in `b` that are close to point in `t`, yielding a new set `c`       let c := { y ∈ b | ∃ x ∈ t, edist x y < δ }       have : c.Finite := ‹b.Finite›.subset fun x hx => hx.1       -- points in `t` are well approximated by points in `c`       have tc : ∀ x ∈ t, ∃ y ∈ c, edist x y ≤ δ := by         intro x hx         rcases tb x hx with ⟨y, yv, Dxy⟩         have : y ∈ c := by simp [c, -mem_image]; exact ⟨yv, ⟨x, hx, Dxy⟩⟩         exact ⟨y, this, le_of_lt Dxy⟩       -- points in `c` are well approximated by points in `t`       have ct : ∀ y ∈ c, ∃ x ∈ t, edist y x ≤ δ := by         rintro y ⟨_, x, xt, Dyx⟩         have : edist y x ≤ δ :=           calc             edist y x = edist x y := edist_comm _ _             _ ≤ δ := le_of_lt Dyx         exact ⟨x, xt, this⟩       -- it follows that their Hausdorff distance is small       have : hausdorffEdist (t : Set α) c ≤ δ := hausdorffEdist_le_of_mem_edist tc ct       have Dtc : hausdorffEdist (t : Set α) c < ε := this.trans_lt δlt       -- the set `c` is not empty, as it is well approximated by a nonempty set       have hc : c.Nonempty := nonempty_of_hausdorffEdist_ne_top t.nonempty (ne_top_of_lt Dtc)       -- let `d` be the version of `c` in the type `NonemptyCompacts α`       let d : NonemptyCompacts α := ⟨⟨c, ‹c.Finite›.isCompact⟩, hc⟩       have : c ⊆ s := by         intro x hx         rcases (mem_image _ _ _).1 hx.1 with ⟨y, ⟨_, yx⟩⟩         rw [← yx]         exact (Fspec y).1       have : d ∈ v := ⟨‹c.Finite›, this⟩       -- we have proved that `d` is a good approximation of `t` as requested       exact ⟨d, ‹d ∈ v›, Dtc⟩   UniformSpace.secondCountable_of_separable (NonemptyCompacts α)

TopologicalSpace.Opens.CompleteCopy.inst.comment:
A distance on an open subset `s` of a metric space, designed to make it complete.  It is given
by `dist' x y = dist x y + |1 / dist x sᶜ - 1 / dist y sᶜ|`, where the second term blows up close to
the boundary to ensure that Cauchy sequences for `dist'` remain well inside `s`.

explanatories.Dist.dist: A distance function that defines how to measure the separation between elements of a type can be created when the type adheres to the properties of a distance metric.

explanatories.Metric.infDist: The minimal distance from a point to a set in a pseudo-metric space is defined.
explanatories.MetricSpace.ofT0PseudoMetricSpace: A pseudometric space that satisfies the T0 separation axiom can be regarded as a metric space.
explanatories.PseudoMetricSpace.ofDistTopology: A pseudo-metric space structure can be formed by ensuring that a given distance function, satisfying standard metric properties, aligns with an existing topological structure's definition of open sets.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.Opens.CompleteCopy.dist: This theorem states that the distance between two points in a complete copy of an open subset of a metric space is given by the sum of their original distance and an adjustment based on their proximity to the boundary.
explanatories.dist_self: The theorem states that the distance from any point to itself in a pseudo-metric space is zero.
explanatories.one_div: The reciprocal of an element in a division inverse monoid is equal to its inverse.
explanatories.sub_self: In an additive group, subtracting an element from itself results in the identity element.
explanatories.abs_zero: This theorem asserts that the absolute value of zero is equal to zero within the framework of a lattice and additive group structure.
explanatories.add_zero: This theorem states that in any additive structure with a zero element, adding zero to any element results in that same element.
explanatories.dist_comm: The distance between two points in a pseudo-metric space is symmetric, meaning it is the same regardless of the order of the points.
explanatories.abs_sub_comm: This theorem asserts that the absolute value of the difference between two elements is symmetric, meaning that the order of subtraction does not affect its absolute value in the context of a lattice and additive group.
explanatories.add_le_add: This theorem states that if two pairs of elements each satisfy an order relation, then the sum of the first pair is less than or equal to the sum of the second pair, preserving the order.
explanatories.dist_triangle: The triangle inequality states that in a pseudo-metric space, the distance from one point to another cannot exceed the sum of the distances from the first point to a third point and from that third point to the second point.
explanatories.add_add_add_comm: The sum of four elements can be rearranged by grouping them in different ways within a commutative additive semigroup.
explanatories.isOpen_iff_mem_nhds: A set is open in a topological space if and only if every point in the set is contained in a neighborhood that is also entirely within the set.
explanatories.Metric.isOpen_iff: A set in a pseudo-metric space is open if and only if every point in the set has a neighborhood that is entirely contained within the set.
explanatories.Eq.trans_lt: A theorem that states that in a totally ordered structure, if one element is equal to a second and that second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is also strictly less than the third.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.Opens.CompleteCopy.dist: The distance between points in the complete copy of an open set does not exceed the distance between those points in the original metric space.
explanatories.LE.le.trans_lt: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is strictly less than the third.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.tendsto_const_nhds: The constant function that maps every input to a specific point tends to that point in the neighborhood as the filter approaches it.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.dist: The convergence of two functions towards different points in a pseudometric space guarantees that the distance between their outputs also converges to the distance between those points.
explanatories.continuous_subtype_val: This theorem states that the value function of a subtype in a topological space is continuous.
explanatories.Continuous.continuousAt: If a function is continuous on its entire domain, then it is also continuous at any specific point in that domain.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.add: The product of two functions that converge to respective limits in a topological space with a continuous multiplication structure also converges to the product of those limits.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.sub: If two functions converge to elements in a topological group, then the quotient of those functions also converges to the quotient of those elements.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.abs: If a function converges to a certain value, then the absolute value of that function also converges to the absolute value of that target value.
explanatories.ContinuousAt.comp: If one function is continuous at a point and another function is continuous at the image of that point under the first function, then their composition is also continuous at that original point.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.Opens.isOpen: This theorem states that the open set represented by a bundled object in a topological space is indeed an open set according to the topological structure.
explanatories.IsOpen.isClosed_compl: If a set is open in a topological space, then its complement is closed.
explanatories.IsClosed.closure_eq: The closure of a closed set in a topological space is equal to the set itself.
explanatories.Set.mem_compl_iff: An element is in the complement of a set if and only if it is not in the original set.
explanatories.Classical.not_not: The Double Negation Theorem states that the negation of the negation of a proposition is equivalent to the proposition itself.
explanatories.zero_add: This theorem establishes that adding zero to any element in an additive structure results in that same element.
explanatories.Filter.mem_of_superset: A theorem stating that if a set belongs to a filter and is a subset of another set, then that other set also belongs to the filter.
explanatories.gt_mem_nhds: This theorem asserts that in an order topology, for any two elements where one is less than the other, there exists a neighborhood around the smaller element that contains only elements less than the larger element.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.comp: A theorem stating that the composition of two functions that tend to maps between respective filters also results in a function that tends to map from the original filter to the final one.

TopologicalSpace.Opens.CompleteCopy.inst.fullDefinition: instance instMetricSpace : MetricSpace (CompleteCopy s) := by   refine @MetricSpace.ofT0PseudoMetricSpace (CompleteCopy s)     (.ofDistTopology dist (fun _ ↦ ?_) (fun _ _ ↦ ?_) (fun x y z ↦ ?_) fun t ↦ ?_) _   · simp only [dist_eq, dist_self, one_div, sub_self, abs_zero, add_zero]   · simp only [dist_eq, dist_comm, abs_sub_comm]   · calc       dist x z = dist x.1 z.1 + |1 / infDist x.1 sᶜ - 1 / infDist z.1 sᶜ| := rfl       _ ≤ dist x.1 y.1 + dist y.1 z.1 + (|1 / infDist x.1 sᶜ - 1 / infDist y.1 sᶜ| +             |1 / infDist y.1 sᶜ - 1 / infDist z.1 sᶜ|) :=         add_le_add (dist_triangle _ _ _) (dist_triangle (1 / infDist _ _) _ _)       _ = dist x y + dist y z := add_add_add_comm ..   · refine ⟨fun h x hx ↦ ?_, fun h ↦ isOpen_iff_mem_nhds.2 fun x hx ↦ ?_⟩     · rcases (Metric.isOpen_iff (α := s)).1 h x hx with ⟨ε, ε0, hε⟩       exact ⟨ε, ε0, fun y hy ↦ hε <| (dist_comm _ _).trans_lt <| (dist_val_le_dist _ _).trans_lt hy⟩     · rcases h x hx with ⟨ε, ε0, hε⟩       simp only [dist_eq, one_div] at hε       have : Tendsto (fun y : s ↦ dist x.1 y.1 + |(infDist x.1 sᶜ)⁻¹ - (infDist y.1 sᶜ)⁻¹|)           (𝓝 x) (𝓝 (dist x.1 x.1 + |(infDist x.1 sᶜ)⁻¹ - (infDist x.1 sᶜ)⁻¹|)) := by         refine (tendsto_const_nhds.dist continuous_subtype_val.continuousAt).add           (tendsto_const_nhds.sub <| ?_).abs         refine (continuousAt_inv_infDist_pt ?_).comp continuous_subtype_val.continuousAt         rw [s.isOpen.isClosed_compl.closure_eq, mem_compl_iff, not_not]         exact x.2       simp only [dist_self, sub_self, abs_zero, zero_add] at this       exact mem_of_superset (this <| gt_mem_nhds ε0) hε

polish_space.complete_copy_metric_space.fullDefinition: instance instMetricSpace : MetricSpace (CompleteCopy s) := by   refine @MetricSpace.ofT0PseudoMetricSpace (CompleteCopy s)     (.ofDistTopology dist (fun _ ↦ ?_) (fun _ _ ↦ ?_) (fun x y z ↦ ?_) fun t ↦ ?_) _   · simp only [dist_eq, dist_self, one_div, sub_self, abs_zero, add_zero]   · simp only [dist_eq, dist_comm, abs_sub_comm]   · calc       dist x z = dist x.1 z.1 + |1 / infDist x.1 sᶜ - 1 / infDist z.1 sᶜ| := rfl       _ ≤ dist x.1 y.1 + dist y.1 z.1 + (|1 / infDist x.1 sᶜ - 1 / infDist y.1 sᶜ| +             |1 / infDist y.1 sᶜ - 1 / infDist z.1 sᶜ|) :=         add_le_add (dist_triangle _ _ _) (dist_triangle (1 / infDist _ _) _ _)       _ = dist x y + dist y z := add_add_add_comm ..   · refine ⟨fun h x hx ↦ ?_, fun h ↦ isOpen_iff_mem_nhds.2 fun x hx ↦ ?_⟩     · rcases (Metric.isOpen_iff (α := s)).1 h x hx with ⟨ε, ε0, hε⟩       exact ⟨ε, ε0, fun y hy ↦ hε <| (dist_comm _ _).trans_lt <| (dist_val_le_dist _ _).trans_lt hy⟩     · rcases h x hx with ⟨ε, ε0, hε⟩       simp only [dist_eq, one_div] at hε       have : Tendsto (fun y : s ↦ dist x.1 y.1 + |(infDist x.1 sᶜ)⁻¹ - (infDist y.1 sᶜ)⁻¹|)           (𝓝 x) (𝓝 (dist x.1 x.1 + |(infDist x.1 sᶜ)⁻¹ - (infDist x.1 sᶜ)⁻¹|)) := by         refine (tendsto_const_nhds.dist continuous_subtype_val.continuousAt).add           (tendsto_const_nhds.sub <| ?_).abs         refine (continuousAt_inv_infDist_pt ?_).comp continuous_subtype_val.continuousAt         rw [s.isOpen.isClosed_compl.closure_eq, mem_compl_iff, not_not]         exact x.2       simp only [dist_self, sub_self, abs_zero, zero_add] at this       exact mem_of_superset (this <| gt_mem_nhds ε0) hε
polish_space.complete_copy_metric_space.description: This defines a metric space structure on an open subset of a metric space that ensures completeness by modifying the distance function to control behavior near the boundary.

TopologicalSpace.Opens.CompleteCopy.inst.code:
TopologicalSpace.Opens.CompleteCopy.instMetricSpace.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MetricSpace α] {s : Opens α} :
  MetricSpace s.CompleteCopy
TopologicalSpace.Opens.CompleteCopy.inst.comment:
A metric space structure on a subset `s` of a metric space, designed to make it complete
if `s` is open. It is given by `dist' x y = dist x y + |1 / dist x sᶜ - 1 / dist y sᶜ|`, where the
second term blows up close to the boundary to ensure that Cauchy sequences for `dist'` remain well
inside `s`.

Porting note: the definition changed to ensure that the `TopologicalSpace` structure on
`TopologicalSpace.Opens.CompleteCopy s` is definitionally equal to the original one.

polish_space.complete_space_complete_cop.fullDefinition: instance instCompleteSpace [CompleteSpace α] : CompleteSpace (CompleteCopy s) := by   refine Metric.complete_of_convergent_controlled_sequences ((1 / 2) ^ ·) (by simp) fun u hu ↦ ?_   have A : CauchySeq fun n => (u n).1 := by     refine cauchySeq_of_le_tendsto_0 (fun n : ℕ => (1 / 2) ^ n) (fun n m N hNn hNm => ?_) ?_     · exact (dist_val_le_dist (u n) (u m)).trans (hu N n m hNn hNm).le     · exact tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one (by norm_num) (by norm_num)   obtain ⟨x, xlim⟩ : ∃ x, Tendsto (fun n => (u n).1) atTop (𝓝 x) := cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete A   by_cases xs : x ∈ s   · exact ⟨⟨x, xs⟩, tendsto_subtype_rng.2 xlim⟩   obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ : ∃ C, ∀ n, 1 / infDist (u n).1 sᶜ < C := by     refine ⟨(1 / 2) ^ 0 + 1 / infDist (u 0).1 sᶜ, fun n ↦ ?_⟩     rw [← sub_lt_iff_lt_add]     calc       _ ≤ |1 / infDist (u n).1 sᶜ - 1 / infDist (u 0).1 sᶜ| := le_abs_self _       _ = |1 / infDist (u 0).1 sᶜ - 1 / infDist (u n).1 sᶜ| := abs_sub_comm _ _       _ ≤ dist (u 0) (u n) := le_add_of_nonneg_left dist_nonneg       _ < (1 / 2) ^ 0 := hu 0 0 n le_rfl n.zero_le   have Cpos : 0 < C := lt_of_le_of_lt (div_nonneg zero_le_one infDist_nonneg) (hC 0)   have Hmem : ∀ {y}, y ∈ s ↔ 0 < infDist y sᶜ := fun {y} ↦ by     rw [← s.isOpen.isClosed_compl.not_mem_iff_infDist_pos ⟨x, xs⟩]; exact not_not.symm   have I : ∀ n, 1 / C ≤ infDist (u n).1 sᶜ := fun n ↦ by     have : 0 < infDist (u n).1 sᶜ := Hmem.1 (u n).2     rw [div_le_iff' Cpos]     exact (div_le_iff this).1 (hC n).le   have I' : 1 / C ≤ infDist x sᶜ :=     have : Tendsto (fun n => infDist (u n).1 sᶜ) atTop (𝓝 (infDist x sᶜ)) :=       ((continuous_infDist_pt (sᶜ : Set α)).tendsto x).comp xlim     ge_of_tendsto' this I   exact absurd (Hmem.2 <| lt_of_lt_of_le (div_pos one_pos Cpos) I') xs

PolishSpace.IsClopenable.code: PolishSpace.IsClopenable.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [t : TopologicalSpace α] (s : Set α) : Prop
PolishSpace.IsClopenable.comment:
A set in a topological space is clopenable if there exists a finer Polish topology for which
this set is open and closed. It turns out that this notion is equivalent to being Borel-measurable,
but this is nontrivial (see `isClopenable_iff_measurableSet`).

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

PolishSpace.IsClopenable.fullDefinition: def IsClopenable [t : TopologicalSpace α] (s : Set α) : Prop :=   ∃ t' : TopologicalSpace α, t' ≤ t ∧ @PolishSpace α t' ∧ IsClosed[t'] s ∧ IsOpen[t'] s
PolishSpace.IsClopenable.description: A set in a topological space is considered clopenable if there exists a Polish topology that makes it both open and closed, which is equivalent to being Borel-measurable.

CantorScheme.inducedMap.comment:
From a `β`-scheme on `α` `A`, we define a partial function from `(ℕ → β)` to `α`
which sends each infinite sequence `x` to an element of the intersection along the
branch corresponding to `x`, if it exists.

  {K U : ι → Set X} (hK : ∀ (i : ι), IsClosed (K i)) (hU : ∀ (i : ι), IsOpen (U i)) (hKU : ∀ (i : ι), K i ⊆ U i)
  (hfin : LocallyFinite K) (x : X) : ∀ᶠ (p : ℝ≥0∞ × X) in 𝓝 0 ×ˢ 𝓝 x, ∀ (i : ι), p.2 ∈ K i → closedBall p.2 p.1 ⊆ U i
EMetric.eventually_nhds_zero_forall_clos.comment:
Let `K : ι → Set X` be a locally finite family of closed sets in an emetric space. Let
`U : ι → Set X` be a family of open sets such that `K i ⊆ U i` for all `i`. Then for any point
`x : X`, for sufficiently small `r : ℝ≥0∞` and for `y` sufficiently close to `x`, for all `i`, if
`y ∈ K i`, then `EMetric.closedBall y r ⊆ U i`.

EMetric.exists_continuous_real_forall_closedBall_subset.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {X : Type u_2} [EMetricSpace X]
  {K U : ι → Set X} (hK : ∀ (i : ι), IsClosed (K i)) (hU : ∀ (i : ι), IsOpen (U i)) (hKU : ∀ (i : ι), K i ⊆ U i)
  (hfin : LocallyFinite K) : ∃ δ, (∀ (x : X), 0 < δ x) ∧ ∀ (i : ι), ∀ x ∈ K i, closedBall x (ENNReal.ofReal (δ x)) ⊆ U i
EMetric.exists_continuous_real_forall_cl.comment:
Let `X` be an extended metric space. Let `K : ι → Set X` be a locally finite family of closed
sets, let `U : ι → Set X` be a family of open sets such that `K i ⊆ U i` for all `i`. Then there
exists a positive continuous function `δ : C(X, ℝ)` such that for any `i` and `x ∈ K i`,
we have `EMetric.closedBall x (ENNReal.ofReal (δ x)) ⊆ U i`.

thickenedIndicatorAux.code: thickenedIndicatorAux.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [PseudoEMetricSpace α] (δ : ℝ) (E : Set α) : α → ℝ≥0∞
thickenedIndicatorAux.comment:
The `δ`-thickened indicator of a set `E` is the function that equals `1` on `E`
and `0` outside a `δ`-thickening of `E` and interpolates (continuously) between
these values using `infEdist _ E`.

`thickenedIndicatorAux` is the unbundled `ℝ≥0∞`-valued function. See `thickenedIndicator`
for the (bundled) bounded continuous function with `ℝ≥0`-values.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.EMetric.infEdist: The minimum extended distance from a point to a set in a pseudo-metric space is defined.
explanatories.ENNReal.ofReal: This definition describes a function that converts a real number into the extended nonnegative real numbers, returning the number itself if it is nonnegative and zero if it is negative.

thickenedIndicatorAux.fullDefinition: def thickenedIndicatorAux (δ : ℝ) (E : Set α) : α → ℝ≥0∞ :=   fun x : α => (1 : ℝ≥0∞) - infEdist x E / ENNReal.ofReal δ
thickenedIndicatorAux.description: The δ-thickened indicator of a set assigns a value of one to points within that set, zero to points outside a δ-thickened region around the set, and interpolates smoothly between these values based on the distance to the set.

thickenedIndicatorAux_tendsto_indicator_.comment:
As the thickening radius δ tends to 0, the δ-thickened indicator of a set E (in α) tends
pointwise (i.e., w.r.t. the product topology on `α → ℝ≥0∞`) to the indicator function of the
closure of E.

This statement is for the unbundled `ℝ≥0∞`-valued functions `thickenedIndicatorAux δ E`, see
`thickenedIndicator_tendsto_indicator_closure` for the version for bundled `ℝ≥0`-valued
bounded continuous functions.

explanatories.Filter.atTop: This definition introduces a filter that captures the behavior of elements approaching infinity in an ordered set, generated by all sets containing elements greater than or equal to any given element.

thickenedIndicator.code: thickenedIndicator.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [PseudoEMetricSpace α] {δ : ℝ} (δ_pos : 0 < δ) (E : Set α) : α →ᵇ ℝ≥0
thickenedIndicator.comment:
The `δ`-thickened indicator of a set `E` is the function that equals `1` on `E`
and `0` outside a `δ`-thickening of `E` and interpolates (continuously) between
these values using `infEdist _ E`.

`thickenedIndicator` is the (bundled) bounded continuous function with `ℝ≥0`-values.
See `thickenedIndicatorAux` for the unbundled `ℝ≥0∞`-valued function.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.continuous_thickenedIndicatorAux: The thickened indicator function associated with a set is continuous when the thickness parameter is positive.
explanatories.thickenedIndicatorAux_le_one: The thickened indicator function of a set does not exceed the value one for any point in the space.
explanatories.lt_of_le_of_lt: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is also strictly less than the third.
explanatories.ENNReal.one_lt_top: This theorem asserts that one is less than the maximum element in the extended nonnegative real numbers.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.ENNReal.toNNReal: This definition describes a function that converts an extended nonnegative real number to a nonnegative real number, returning the original number if it is finite and zero if it is the designated top element.
explanatories.ContinuousOn.comp_continuous: The composition of two functions is continuous if the second function is continuous on a specific set, the first function is continuous, and every point in the domain maps into that set.
explanatories.ENNReal.continuousOn_toNNReal: This theorem states that the function converting extended non-negative real numbers to non-negative real numbers is continuous on the set of all extended non-negative real numbers excluding infinity.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne: A theorem indicating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then they must be distinct.
explanatories.NNReal.dist_eq: The distance between two non-negative real numbers is equal to the absolute difference of their corresponding real equivalents.
explanatories.abs_sub: This theorem states that the absolute value of the difference between two elements in a linear ordered additive commutative group is less than or equal to the sum of their absolute values.
explanatories.NNReal.abs_eq: This theorem asserts that the absolute value of a nonnegative real number is equal to the number itself when considered in the context of real numbers.
explanatories.one_add_one_eq_two: The theorem asserts that in any additive monoid with a unity element, the sum of one and one equals two.
explanatories.add_le_add: This theorem states that if two pairs of elements each satisfy an order relation, then the sum of the first pair is less than or equal to the sum of the second pair, preserving the order.
explanatories.ENNReal.toNNReal_le_toNNReal: This theorem asserts that the comparison of two positive extended nonnegative real numbers in their corresponding natural number form is equivalent to their comparison in the extended nonnegative real number system, provided neither number is infinity.
explanatories.ENNReal.one_ne_top: This theorem states that the number one is not equal to infinity in the context of extended nonnegative real numbers.

thickenedIndicator.fullDefinition: def thickenedIndicator {δ : ℝ} (δ_pos : 0 < δ) (E : Set α) : α →ᵇ ℝ≥0 where   toFun := fun x : α => (thickenedIndicatorAux δ E x).toNNReal   continuous_toFun := by     apply ContinuousOn.comp_continuous continuousOn_toNNReal       (continuous_thickenedIndicatorAux δ_pos E)     intro x     exact (lt_of_le_of_lt (@thickenedIndicatorAux_le_one _ _ δ E x) one_lt_top).ne   map_bounded' := by     use 2     intro x y     rw [NNReal.dist_eq]     apply (abs_sub _ _).trans     rw [NNReal.abs_eq, NNReal.abs_eq, ← one_add_one_eq_two]     have key := @thickenedIndicatorAux_le_one _ _ δ E     apply add_le_add <;>       · norm_cast         exact (toNNReal_le_toNNReal (lt_of_le_of_lt (key _) one_lt_top).ne one_ne_top).mpr (key _)
thickenedIndicator.description: The δ-thickened indicator of a set is a bounded continuous function that equals one for points in the set, zero for points outside a δ-thickened region, and smoothly interpolates between these values based on the distance from the set.

GromovHausdorff.ghDist_le_of_approx_subs.code:
GromovHausdorff.ghDist_le_of_approx_subsets.{u, v} {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] [Nonempty X]
  {Y : Type v} [MetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] [Nonempty Y] {s : Set X} (Φ : ↑s → Y) {ε₁ ε₂ ε₃ : ℝ}
  (hs : ∀ (x : X), ∃ y ∈ s, dist x y ≤ ε₁) (hs' : ∀ (x : Y), ∃ y, dist x (Φ y) ≤ ε₃)
  (H : ∀ (x y : ↑s), |dist x y - dist (Φ x) (Φ y)| ≤ ε₂) : ghDist X Y ≤ ε₁ + ε₂ / 2 + ε₃
GromovHausdorff.ghDist_le_of_approx_subs.comment:
If there are subsets which are `ε₁`-dense and `ε₃`-dense in two spaces, and
isometric up to `ε₂`, then the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between the spaces is bounded by
`ε₁ + ε₂/2 + ε₃`.

GromovHausdorff.ghDist_le_of_approx_subs.description: This theorem demonstrates that if two compact metric spaces have subsets that are dense within certain ε-bounds and are isometric up to a specified ε, then the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between the two spaces is constrained by the sum of those ε-bounds.

Gromov_Hausdorff.GH_dist_le_of_approx_su.code:
GromovHausdorff.ghDist_le_of_approx_subsets.{u, v} {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] [Nonempty X]
  {Y : Type v} [MetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] [Nonempty Y] {s : Set X} (Φ : ↑s → Y) {ε₁ ε₂ ε₃ : ℝ}
  (hs : ∀ (x : X), ∃ y ∈ s, dist x y ≤ ε₁) (hs' : ∀ (x : Y), ∃ y, dist x (Φ y) ≤ ε₃)
  (H : ∀ (x y : ↑s), |dist x y - dist (Φ x) (Φ y)| ≤ ε₂) : ghDist X Y ≤ ε₁ + ε₂ / 2 + ε₃
Gromov_Hausdorff.GH_dist_le_of_approx_su.comment:
If there are subsets which are `ε₁`-dense and `ε₃`-dense in two spaces, and
isometric up to `ε₂`, then the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between the spaces is bounded by
`ε₁ + ε₂/2 + ε₃`.

GromovHausdorff.totallyBounded.code:
GromovHausdorff.totallyBounded {t : Set GHSpace} {C : ℝ} {u : ℕ → ℝ} {K : ℕ → ℕ} (ulim : Tendsto u atTop (𝓝 0))
  (hdiam : ∀ p ∈ t, diam univ ≤ C) (hcov : ∀ p ∈ t, ∀ (n : ℕ), ∃ s, #↑s ≤ ↑(K n) ∧ univ ⊆ ⋃ x ∈ s, ball x (u n)) :
  TotallyBounded t
GromovHausdorff.totallyBounded.comment:
Compactness criterion: a closed set of compact metric spaces is compact if the spaces have
a uniformly bounded diameter, and for all `ε` the number of balls of radius `ε` required
to cover the spaces is uniformly bounded. This is an equivalence, but we only prove the
interesting direction that these conditions imply compactness.

vector spaces. Suppose that `f` is `C¹` smooth on a convex set `s` of Hausdorff dimension strictly

TopCat.GlueData.MkCore.t'.fullDefinition: def MkCore.t' (h : MkCore.{u}) (i j k : h.J) :     pullback (h.V i j).inclusion (h.V i k).inclusion ⟶       pullback (h.V j k).inclusion (h.V j i).inclusion := by   refine (pullbackIsoProdSubtype _ _).hom ≫ ⟨?_, ?_⟩ ≫ (pullbackIsoProdSubtype _ _).inv   · intro x     refine ⟨⟨⟨(h.t i j x.1.1).1, ?_⟩, h.t i j x.1.1⟩, rfl⟩     rcases x with ⟨⟨⟨x, hx⟩, ⟨x', hx'⟩⟩, rfl : x = x'⟩     exact h.t_inter _ ⟨x, hx⟩ hx'   -- Porting note: was `continuity`, see https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/issues/5030   have : Continuous (h.t i j) := map_continuous (self := ContinuousMap.toContinuousMapClass) _   set_option tactic.skipAssignedInstances false in   exact ((Continuous.subtype_mk (by fun_prop) _).prod_mk (by fun_prop)).subtype_mk _

TopCat.GlueData.mk'.fullDefinition: def mk' (h : MkCore.{u}) : TopCat.GlueData where   J := h.J   U := h.U   V i := (Opens.toTopCat _).obj (h.V i.1 i.2)   f i j := (h.V i j).inclusion   f_id i := by     -- Porting note (#12129): additional beta reduction needed     beta_reduce     exact (h.V_id i).symm ▸ (Opens.inclusionTopIso (h.U i)).isIso_hom   f_open := fun i j : h.J => (h.V i j).openEmbedding   t := h.t   t_id i := by ext; erw [h.t_id]; rfl  -- now `erw` after #13170   t' := h.t'   t_fac i j k := by     delta MkCore.t'     rw [Category.assoc, Category.assoc, pullbackIsoProdSubtype_inv_snd, ← Iso.eq_inv_comp,       pullbackIsoProdSubtype_inv_fst_assoc]     ext ⟨⟨⟨x, hx⟩, ⟨x', hx'⟩⟩, rfl : x = x'⟩     rfl   cocycle i j k := by     delta MkCore.t'     simp_rw [← Category.assoc]     rw [Iso.comp_inv_eq]     simp only [Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc, Category.assoc, Category.id_comp]     rw [← Iso.eq_inv_comp, Iso.inv_hom_id]     ext1 ⟨⟨⟨x, hx⟩, ⟨x', hx'⟩⟩, rfl : x = x'⟩     -- The next 9 tactics (up to `convert ...` were a single `rw` before leanprover/lean4#2644     -- rw [comp_app, ContinuousMap.coe_mk, comp_app, id_app, ContinuousMap.coe_mk, Subtype.mk_eq_mk,     --   Prod.mk.inj_iff, Subtype.mk_eq_mk, Subtype.ext_iff, and_self_iff]     erw [comp_app] --, comp_app, id_app] -- now `erw` after #13170     -- erw [ContinuousMap.coe_mk]     conv_lhs => erw [ContinuousMap.coe_mk]     erw [id_app]     rw [ContinuousMap.coe_mk]     erw [Subtype.mk_eq_mk]     rw [Prod.mk.inj_iff]     erw [Subtype.mk_eq_mk]     rw [Subtype.ext_iff]     rw [and_self_iff]     convert congr_arg Subtype.val (h.t_inv k i ⟨x, hx'⟩) using 3     refine Subtype.ext ?_     exact h.cocycle i j k ⟨x, hx⟩ hx'   -- Porting note: was not necessary in mathlib3   f_mono i j := (TopCat.mono_iff_injective _).mpr fun x y h => Subtype.ext h set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

TopCat.GlueData.ofOpenSubsets.fullDefinition: def ofOpenSubsets : TopCat.GlueData.{u} :=   mk'.{u}     { J       U := fun i => (Opens.toTopCat <| TopCat.of α).obj (U i)       V := fun i j => (Opens.map <| Opens.inclusion _).obj (U j)       t := fun i j => ⟨fun x => ⟨⟨x.1.1, x.2⟩, x.1.2⟩, by         -- Porting note: was `continuity`, see https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/issues/5030         refine Continuous.subtype_mk ?_ ?_         refine Continuous.subtype_mk ?_ ?_         continuity⟩       V_id := fun i => by         ext         -- Porting note: no longer needed `cases U i`!         simp       t_id := fun i => by ext; rfl       t_inter := fun i j k x hx => hx       cocycle := fun i j k x h => rfl } set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

Top.glue_data.of_open_subsets.fullDefinition: def ofOpenSubsets : TopCat.GlueData.{u} :=   mk'.{u}     { J       U := fun i => (Opens.toTopCat <| TopCat.of α).obj (U i)       V := fun i j => (Opens.map <| Opens.inclusion _).obj (U j)       t := fun i j => ⟨fun x => ⟨⟨x.1.1, x.2⟩, x.1.2⟩, by         -- Porting note: was `continuity`, see https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/issues/5030         refine Continuous.subtype_mk ?_ ?_         refine Continuous.subtype_mk ?_ ?_         continuity⟩       V_id := fun i => by         ext         -- Porting note: no longer needed `cases U i`!         simp       t_id := fun i => by ext; rfl       t_inter := fun i j k x hx => hx       cocycle := fun i j k x h => rfl } set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

PseudoMetricSpace.ofPreNNDist.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ofPreNNDist (d : X → X → ℝ≥0) (dist_self : ∀ x, d x x = 0)     (dist_comm : ∀ x y, d x y = d y x) : PseudoMetricSpace X where   dist x y := ↑(⨅ l : List X, ((x::l).zipWith d (l ++ [y])).sum : ℝ≥0)   dist_self x := NNReal.coe_eq_zero.2 <|       nonpos_iff_eq_zero.1 <| (ciInf_le (OrderBot.bddBelow _) []).trans_eq <| by simp [dist_self]   dist_comm x y :=     NNReal.coe_inj.2 <| by       refine reverse_surjective.iInf_congr _ fun l ↦ ?_       rw [← sum_reverse, zipWith_distrib_reverse, reverse_append, reverse_reverse,         reverse_singleton, singleton_append, reverse_cons, reverse_reverse,         zipWith_comm_of_comm _ dist_comm]       simp only [length, length_append]   dist_triangle x y z := by     -- Porting note: added `unfold`     unfold dist     rw [← NNReal.coe_add, NNReal.coe_le_coe]     refine NNReal.le_iInf_add_iInf fun lxy lyz ↦ ?_     calc       ⨅ l, (zipWith d (x::l) (l ++ [z])).sum ≤           (zipWith d (x::lxy ++ y::lyz) ((lxy ++ y::lyz) ++ [z])).sum :=         ciInf_le (OrderBot.bddBelow _) (lxy ++ y::lyz)       _ = (zipWith d (x::lxy) (lxy ++ [y])).sum + (zipWith d (y::lyz) (lyz ++ [z])).sum := by         rw [← sum_append, ← zipWith_append, cons_append, ← @singleton_append _ y, append_assoc,           append_assoc, append_assoc]         rw [length_cons, length_append, length_singleton]   -- Porting note: `edist_dist` is no longer inferred   edist_dist x y := rfl
PseudoMetricSpace.ofPreNNDist.description: This definition provides the maximal pseudo-metric space structure on a type such that the distance function satisfies specific properties, including being zero for identical points and symmetric for distinct points.

PseudoMetricSpace.le_two_mul_dist_ofPreN.code:
PseudoMetricSpace.le_two_mul_dist_ofPreNNDist.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} (d : X → X → ℝ≥0) (dist_self : ∀ (x : X), d x x = 0)
  (dist_comm : ∀ (x y : X), d x y = d y x)
  (hd : ∀ (x₁ x₂ x₃ x₄ : X), d x₁ x₄ ≤ 2 * max (d x₁ x₂) (max (d x₂ x₃) (d x₃ x₄))) (x y : X) : ↑(d x y) ≤ 2 * dist x y
PseudoMetricSpace.le_two_mul_dist_ofPreN.comment:
Consider a function `d : X → X → ℝ≥0` such that `d x x = 0` and `d x y = d y x` for all `x`,
`y`. Let `dist` be the largest pseudometric distance such that `dist x y ≤ d x y`, see
`PseudoMetricSpace.ofPreNNDist`. Suppose that `d` satisfies the following triangle-like
inequality: `d x₁ x₄ ≤ 2 * max (d x₁ x₂, d x₂ x₃, d x₃ x₄)`. Then `d x y ≤ 2 * dist x y` for all
`x`, `y`.

PseudoMetricSpace.le_two_mul_dist_ofPreN.description: If a distance function satisfies a specific triangle-like inequality, then the distance between any two points in the induced pseudo-metric space is at most twice the value given by that function.

ContinuousMap.HomotopyWith.trans.fullDefinition: def trans {f₀ f₁ f₂ : C(X, Y)} (F : HomotopyWith f₀ f₁ P) (G : HomotopyWith f₁ f₂ P) :     HomotopyWith f₀ f₂ P :=   { F.toHomotopy.trans G.toHomotopy with     prop' := fun t => by       simp only [Homotopy.trans]       change P ⟨fun _ => ite ((t : ℝ) ≤ _) _ _, _⟩       split_ifs       · exact F.extendProp _       · exact G.extendProp _ }

ContinuousMap.HomotopyRel.trans.fullDefinition: def trans (F : HomotopyRel f₀ f₁ S) (G : HomotopyRel f₁ f₂ S) : HomotopyRel f₀ f₂ S where   toHomotopy := F.toHomotopy.trans G.toHomotopy   prop' t x hx := by     simp only [Homotopy.trans]     split_ifs     · simp [HomotopyWith.extendProp F (2 * t) x hx, F.fst_eq_snd hx, G.fst_eq_snd hx]     · simp [HomotopyWith.extendProp G (2 * t - 1) x hx, F.fst_eq_snd hx, G.fst_eq_snd hx]
ContinuousMap.HomotopyRel.trans.description: This defines a relation showing that if two continuous functions are homotopic with respect to a set, and the second function is also homotopic to a third function with the same respect to that set, then the first and third functions are homotopic in relation to the same set.

continuous_map.homotopy_rel.cast.description: A homotopy that relates two continuous functions can be transformed to relate two different continuous functions preserving the homotopy relationship and a fixed subset of the domain, provided the initial and final functions are equal to the new functions.

TopologicalGroup.toHSpace.comment:
The definition `toHSpace` is not an instance because its additive version would
lead to a diamond since a topological field would inherit two `HSpace` structures, one from the
`MulOneClass` and one from the `AddZeroClass`. In the case of a group, we make
`TopologicalGroup.hSpace` an instance."

Suppose `p₀` and `q₀` are paths from `x₀` to `x₁`, `p₁` and `q₁` are paths from `x₁` to `x₂`.

from `p₀.trans p₁` to `q₀.trans q₁`.

Path.Homotopy.hcomp.fullDefinition: def hcomp (F : Homotopy p₀ q₀) (G : Homotopy p₁ q₁) : Homotopy (p₀.trans p₁) (q₀.trans q₁) where   toFun x :=     if (x.2 : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2 then (F.eval x.1).extend (2 * x.2) else (G.eval x.1).extend (2 * x.2 - 1)   continuous_toFun := continuous_if_le (continuous_induced_dom.comp continuous_snd) continuous_const     (F.toHomotopy.continuous.comp (by continuity)).continuousOn     (G.toHomotopy.continuous.comp (by continuity)).continuousOn fun x hx => by norm_num [hx]   map_zero_left x := by simp [Path.trans]   map_one_left x := by simp [Path.trans]   prop' x t ht := by     cases' ht with ht ht     · norm_num [ht]     · rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at ht       norm_num [ht]

explanatories.ContinuousMap.pi: This definition introduces a continuous map that is formed from a family of continuous maps, taking an input from a topological space and producing outputs in a product space defined by varying types indexed by a given set.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.Homotopy.pi: A collection of homotopies between continuous functions indexed by a set can be combined to produce a homotopy between the corresponding product of those functions.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.HomotopyWith.toHomotopy: This defines a standard homotopy between two continuous functions by transforming a homotopy with an associated property into a simpler form without the property.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.coe_mk: This theorem asserts that a function defined with a specific continuous structure is equivalent to its representation as a continuous map.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.pi_eval: This theorem states that evaluating a pointwise-defined function derived from a family of continuous maps at a specific point is equivalent to applying each continuous map to that point.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.toFun_eq_coe: This theorem demonstrates that the function associated with a continuous map is equal to the corresponding coercion of that map into a function type.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.HomotopyWith.coe_toContinu: The function associated with a homotopy that has an additional property is equal to its corresponding continuous map.
explanatories.forall_and: The universal quantification of a conjunction of two properties is equivalent to the conjunction of the universal quantifications of each property individually.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.HomotopyWith.prop': The intermediate maps of a specified homotopy between two continuous functions satisfy a given property throughout the homotopy.
explanatories.Path.pi: This definition constructs a path in a product space by taking a family of paths from each component space and combining them in a pointwise manner.

ContinuousMap.HomotopyRel.pi.fullDefinition: def HomotopyRel.pi (homotopies : ∀ i : I, HomotopyRel (f i) (g i) S) :     HomotopyRel (pi f) (pi g) S :=   { Homotopy.pi fun i => (homotopies i).toHomotopy with     prop' := by       intro t x hx       dsimp only [coe_mk, pi_eval, toFun_eq_coe, HomotopyWith.coe_toContinuousMap]       simp only [Function.funext_iff, ← forall_and]       intro i       exact (homotopies i).prop' t x hx }
ContinuousMap.HomotopyRel.pi.description: This defines a relative product homotopy for a family of functions, showing that the product of two homotopies between them also forms a homotopy relative to a specified set.

explanatories.ContinuousMap.prod_eval: This theorem shows that the evaluation of the product of two continuous maps at a given point yields a pair consisting of the outputs of each map evaluated at that point.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.Homotopy.apply_zero: The value of a homotopy between two continuous functions at a point with the initial parameter corresponds to the first function evaluated at that point.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.Homotopy.apply_one: The value of a homotopy between two continuous functions at a specified point corresponds to the second function at that point when evaluated at the final time of the homotopy.
explanatories.Path.Homotopy: The concept describes the type of homotopies that exist between two paths connecting the same endpoints in a topological space.
explanatories.Path.prod: This definition describes a method for creating a new path in the product space formed by two topological spaces, by combining paths from each space through a pointwise product.

ContinuousMap.Homotopy.prod.fullDefinition: def Homotopy.prod (F : Homotopy f₀ f₁) (G : Homotopy g₀ g₁) :     Homotopy (ContinuousMap.prodMk f₀ g₀) (ContinuousMap.prodMk f₁ g₁) where   toFun t := (F t, G t)   map_zero_left x := by simp only [prod_eval, Homotopy.apply_zero]   map_one_left x := by simp only [prod_eval, Homotopy.apply_one]
ContinuousMap.Homotopy.prod.description: This establishes that the product of two homotopies between continuous functions results in a homotopy between their corresponding product functions.

homotopyGroupEquivFundamentalGroupOfUniq.fullDefinition: def homotopyGroupEquivFundamentalGroupOfUnique (N) [Unique N] :     HomotopyGroup N X x ≃ FundamentalGroup X x := by   refine Equiv.trans ?_ (CategoryTheory.Groupoid.isoEquivHom _ _).symm   refine Quotient.congr (genLoopEquivOfUnique N) ?_   intros a₁ a₂; constructor <;> rintro ⟨H⟩   · exact       ⟨{  toFun := fun tx => H (tx.fst, fun _ => tx.snd)           map_zero_left := fun _ => H.apply_zero _           map_one_left := fun _ => H.apply_one _           prop' := fun t y iH => H.prop' _ _ ⟨default, iH⟩ }⟩   refine     ⟨⟨⟨⟨fun tx => H (tx.fst, tx.snd default), H.continuous.comp ?_⟩, fun y => ?_, fun y => ?_⟩, ?_⟩⟩   · exact continuous_fst.prod_mk ((continuous_apply _).comp continuous_snd)   · exact (H.apply_zero _).trans (congr_arg a₁ (eq_const_of_unique y).symm)   · exact (H.apply_one _).trans (congr_arg a₂ (eq_const_of_unique y).symm)   · rintro t y ⟨i, iH⟩     cases Unique.eq_default i     exact (H.eq_fst _ iH).trans (congr_arg a₁ (eq_const_of_unique y).symm)

homotopy_group_equiv_fundamental_group_o.fullDefinition: def homotopyGroupEquivFundamentalGroupOfUnique (N) [Unique N] :     HomotopyGroup N X x ≃ FundamentalGroup X x := by   refine Equiv.trans ?_ (CategoryTheory.Groupoid.isoEquivHom _ _).symm   refine Quotient.congr (genLoopEquivOfUnique N) ?_   intros a₁ a₂; constructor <;> rintro ⟨H⟩   · exact       ⟨{  toFun := fun tx => H (tx.fst, fun _ => tx.snd)           map_zero_left := fun _ => H.apply_zero _           map_one_left := fun _ => H.apply_one _           prop' := fun t y iH => H.prop' _ _ ⟨default, iH⟩ }⟩   refine     ⟨⟨⟨⟨fun tx => H (tx.fst, tx.snd default), H.continuous.comp ?_⟩, fun y => ?_, fun y => ?_⟩, ?_⟩⟩   · exact continuous_fst.prod_mk ((continuous_apply _).comp continuous_snd)   · exact (H.apply_zero _).trans (congr_arg a₁ (eq_const_of_unique y).symm)   · exact (H.apply_one _).trans (congr_arg a₂ (eq_const_of_unique y).symm)   · rintro t y ⟨i, iH⟩     cases Unique.eq_default i     exact (H.eq_fst _ iH).trans (congr_arg a₁ (eq_const_of_unique y).symm)

LowerSemicontinuousWithinAt.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace α] {β : Type u_2} [Preorder β] (f : α → β)
  (s : Set α) (x : α) : Prop
LowerSemicontinuousWithinAt.comment:
A real function `f` is lower semicontinuous at `x` within a set `s` if, for any `ε > 0`, for all
`x'` close enough to `x` in `s`, then `f x'` is at least `f x - ε`. We formulate this in a general
preordered space, using an arbitrary `y < f x` instead of `f x - ε`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

LowerSemicontinuousWithinAt.fullDefinition: def LowerSemicontinuousWithinAt (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (x : α) :=   ∀ y < f x, ∀ᶠ x' in 𝓝[s] x, y < f x'
LowerSemicontinuousWithinAt.description: A function is lower semicontinuous at a point within a set if, near that point, the function's values do not drop below the value at the point minus any small positive amount.

  (A : Set X) (x : X) : (𝓝 x).Germ Y → Prop
RestrictGermPredicate.comment:
Given a predicate on germs `P : Π x : X, germ (𝓝 x) Y → Prop` and `A : set X`,
build a new predicate on germs `RestrictGermPredicate P A` such that
`(∀ x, RestrictGermPredicate P A x f) ↔ ∀ᶠ x near A, P x f`, see
`forall_restrictGermPredicate_iff` for this equivalence.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Filter.Germ: A definition for the space of germs of functions from one type to another with respect to a given filter.
explanatories.Filter.Germ.liftOn: A definition for retrieving the value assigned by a function to a germ of an equivalence class of functions, under the condition that the function treats eventually equal functions as equal.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.and: A theorem stating that if two properties hold eventually with respect to a filter, then their conjunction also holds eventually with respect to that filter.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.eventually_nhds: If a property is true in a neighborhood around a point, then it remains true in neighborhoods around nearby points.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.mono: A theorem that states if a property holds for a filter and implies another property, then the latter property also holds for that filter.
explanatories.Filter.Germ.coe_eq: The theorem establishes the equivalence between the equality of the germs of two functions and the condition that those functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a given filter.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Filter.EventuallyEq.symm: A theorem asserting that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a filter, then they are also equal almost everywhere in the reverse order with respect to that filter.
explanatories.forall_congr': The universal quantification of two propositions is equivalent if there is a correspondence between the propositions for every element in the set.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.True.intro: The statement establishes that the proposition of truth is inherently valid, with a specific proof confirming its truth.

RestrictGermPredicate.fullDefinition: def RestrictGermPredicate (P : ∀ x : X, Germ (𝓝 x) Y → Prop)     (A : Set X) : ∀ x : X, Germ (𝓝 x) Y → Prop := fun x φ ↦   Germ.liftOn φ (fun f ↦ x ∈ A → ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝 x, P y f)     haveI : ∀ f f' : X → Y, f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] f' → (∀ᶠ y in 𝓝 x, P y f) → ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝 x, P y f' := by       intro f f' hff' hf       apply (hf.and <| Eventually.eventually_nhds hff').mono       rintro y ⟨hy, hy'⟩       rwa [Germ.coe_eq.mpr (EventuallyEq.symm hy')]     fun f f' hff' ↦ propext <| forall_congr' fun _ ↦ ⟨this f f' hff', this f' f hff'.symm⟩
RestrictGermPredicate.description: A new predicate on germs is created by restricting an existing predicate to a specified set of points, such that it holds if and only if it is satisfied for points near that set.

  {P : (x : X) → (𝓝 x).Germ Y → Prop} : (∀ (x : X), RestrictGermPredicate P A x ↑f) ↔ ∀ᶠ (x : X) in 𝓝ˢ A, P x ↑f

CompletelyRegularSpace.instRegularSpace.fullDefinition: instance CompletelyRegularSpace.instRegularSpace [CompletelyRegularSpace X] : RegularSpace X := by   rw [regularSpace_iff]   intro s a hs ha   obtain ⟨f, cf, hf, hhf⟩ := CompletelyRegularSpace.completely_regular a s hs ha   apply disjoint_of_map (f := f)   apply Disjoint.mono (cf.tendsto_nhdsSet_nhds hhf) cf.continuousAt   exact disjoint_nhds_nhds.mpr (hf.symm ▸ zero_ne_one).symm
CompletelyRegularSpace.instRegularSpace.description: A completely regular topological space is also a regular space.

explanatories.exists_continuous_zero_one_of_isClosed: In a normal topological space, the theorem establishes the existence of a continuous function that takes the value zero on one closed set, one on another disjoint closed set, and lies within the interval between zero and one for all elements in the space.

NormalSpace.instCompletelyRegularSpace.fullDefinition: instance NormalSpace.instCompletelyRegularSpace [NormalSpace X] : CompletelyRegularSpace X := by   rw [completelyRegularSpace_iff]   intro x K hK hx   have cx : IsClosed {x} := T1Space.t1 x   have d : Disjoint {x} K := by rwa [Set.disjoint_iff, subset_empty_iff, singleton_inter_eq_empty]   let ⟨⟨f, cf⟩, hfx, hfK, hficc⟩ := exists_continuous_zero_one_of_isClosed cx hK d   let g : X → I := fun x => ⟨f x, hficc x⟩   have cg : Continuous g := cf.subtype_mk hficc   have hgx : g x = 0 := Subtype.ext (hfx (mem_singleton_iff.mpr (Eq.refl x)))   have hgK : EqOn g 1 K := fun k hk => Subtype.ext (hfK hk)   exact ⟨g, cg, hgx, hgK⟩
NormalSpace.instCompletelyRegularSpace.description: A normal topological space, which satisfies the T1 separation axiom, is also a completely regular space.

PartitionOfUnity.IsSubordinate.comment:
A partition of unity `f i` is subordinate to a family of sets `U i` indexed by the same type if
for each `i` the closure of the support of `f i` is a subset of `U i`.
