BumpCovering.exists_isSubordinate_of_loc.code:
BumpCovering.exists_isSubordinate_of_locallyFinite_of_prop.{u, v} {ι : Type u} {X : Type v} [TopologicalSpace X]
  {s : Set X} [NormalSpace X] (p : (X → ℝ) → Prop)
  (h01 :
    ∀ (s t : Set X),
      IsClosed s → IsClosed t → Disjoint s t → ∃ f, p ⇑f ∧ EqOn (⇑f) 0 s ∧ EqOn (⇑f) 1 t ∧ ∀ (x : X), f x ∈ Icc 0 1)
  (hs : IsClosed s) (U : ι → Set X) (ho : ∀ (i : ι), IsOpen (U i)) (hf : LocallyFinite U) (hU : s ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) :
  ∃ f, (∀ (i : ι), p ⇑(f i)) ∧ f.IsSubordinate U
BumpCovering.exists_isSubordinate_of_loc.comment:
If `X` is a normal topological space and `U i`, `i : ι`, is a locally finite open covering of a
closed set `s`, then there exists a `BumpCovering ι X s` that is subordinate to `U`. If `X` is a
paracompact space, then the assumption `hf : LocallyFinite U` can be omitted, see
`BumpCovering.exists_isSubordinate`. This version assumes that `p : (X → ℝ) → Prop` is a predicate
that satisfies Urysohn's lemma, and provides a `BumpCovering` such that each function of the
covering satisfies `p`.

BumpCovering.toPOUFun.code:
BumpCovering.toPOUFun.{u, v} {ι : Type u} {X : Type v} [TopologicalSpace X] {s : Set X} (f : BumpCovering ι X s) (i : ι)
  (x : X) : ℝ
BumpCovering.toPOUFun.comment:
Partition of unity defined by a `BumpCovering`. We use this auxiliary definition to prove some
properties of the new family of functions before bundling it into a `PartitionOfUnity`. Do not use
this definition, use `BumpCovering.toPartitionOfUnity` instead.

The partition of unity is given by the formula `g i x = f i x * ∏ᶠ j < i, (1 - f j x)`. In other
words, `g i x = ∏ᶠ j < i, (1 - f j x) - ∏ᶠ j ≤ i, (1 - f j x)`, so
`∑ᶠ i, g i x = 1 - ∏ᶠ j, (1 - f j x)`. If `x ∈ s`, then one of `f j x` equals one, hence the product
of `1 - f j x` vanishes, and `∑ᶠ i, g i x = 1`.

In order to avoid an assumption `LinearOrder ι`, we use `WellOrderingRel` instead of `(<)`.

explanatories.WellOrderingRel: This definition describes a relation that allows any type to be equipped with a well-order derived from the well-order of cardinals through an embedding.

BumpCovering.toPOUFun.fullDefinition: def toPOUFun (i : ι) (x : X) : ℝ :=   f i x * ∏ᶠ (j) (_ : WellOrderingRel j i), (1 - f j x)
BumpCovering.toPOUFun.description: This definition describes a function that creates a partition of unity from a bump covering, expressed in terms of a product involving the functions from the bump covering.

BumpCovering.toPartitionOfUnity.comment:
The partition of unity defined by a `BumpCovering`.

The partition of unity is given by the formula `g i x = f i x * ∏ᶠ j < i, (1 - f j x)`. In other
words, `g i x = ∏ᶠ j < i, (1 - f j x) - ∏ᶠ j ≤ i, (1 - f j x)`, so
`∑ᶠ i, g i x = 1 - ∏ᶠ j, (1 - f j x)`. If `x ∈ s`, then one of `f j x` equals one, hence the product
of `1 - f j x` vanishes, and `∑ᶠ i, g i x = 1`.

In order to avoid an assumption `LinearOrder ι`, we use `WellOrderingRel` instead of `(<)`.

BumpCovering.toPartitionOfUnity.fullDefinition: def toPartitionOfUnity : PartitionOfUnity ι X s where   toFun i := ⟨f.toPOUFun i, f.continuous_toPOUFun i⟩   locallyFinite' := f.locallyFinite.subset f.support_toPOUFun_subset   nonneg' i x :=     mul_nonneg (f.nonneg i x) (finprod_cond_nonneg fun j hj => sub_nonneg.2 <| f.le_one j x)   sum_eq_one' x hx := by     simp only [ContinuousMap.coe_mk, sum_toPOUFun_eq, sub_eq_self]     apply finprod_eq_zero (fun i => 1 - f i x) (f.ind x hx)     · simp only [f.ind_apply x hx, sub_self]     · rw [mulSupport_one_sub]       exact f.point_finite x   sum_le_one' x := by     simp only [ContinuousMap.coe_mk, sum_toPOUFun_eq, sub_le_self_iff]     exact finprod_nonneg fun i => sub_nonneg.2 <| f.le_one i x

ContinuousMap.exists_restrict_eq.comment:

`s` be a closed set in a normal topological space `X`. Let `f` be a continuous function
on `s` with values in a `TietzeExtension` space `Y`. Then there exists a continuous function
`g : C(X, Y)` such that `g.restrict s = f`.

ContinuousMap.exists_extension.code:
ContinuousMap.exists_extension.{u, u₁, v} {X₁ : Type u₁} [TopologicalSpace X₁] {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X]

  (f : C(X₁, Y)) : ∃ g, g.comp { toFun := e, continuous_toFun := ⋯ } = f
ContinuousMap.exists_extension.comment:
**Tietze extension theorem** for `TietzeExtension` spaces. Let `e` be a closed embedding of a
nonempty topological space `X₁` into a normal topological space `X`. Let `f` be a continuous
function on `X₁` with values in a `TietzeExtension` space `Y`. Then there exists a
continuous function `g : C(X, Y)` such that `g ∘ e = f`.

explanatories.ContinuousMap.comp: This definition describes the composition of two continuous maps, resulting in a new continuous map from the first space to the third space.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.comp: A theorem stating that the composition of two functions that tend to maps between respective filters also results in a function that tends to map from the original filter to the final one.
explanatories.Continuous.comp: The composition of two continuous functions in topological spaces is itself continuous.

ContinuousMap.exists_extension.description: For every continuous function defined on a closed embedding of a nonempty topological space into a normal topological space, there exists an extension to a continuous function on the entire space that agrees with the original function when composed with the embedding.

BoundedContinuousFunction.tietze_extensi.code:
BoundedContinuousFunction.tietze_extension_step.{u_1, u_2} {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [TopologicalSpace Y] [NormalSpace Y] (f : X →ᵇ ℝ) (e : C(X, Y)) (he : ClosedEmbedding ⇑e) :
  ∃ g, ‖g‖ ≤ ‖f‖ / 3 ∧ dist (g.compContinuous e) f ≤ 2 / 3 * ‖f‖
BoundedContinuousFunction.tietze_extensi.comment:
One step in the proof of the Tietze extension theorem. If `e : C(X, Y)` is a closed embedding
of a topological space into a normal topological space and `f : X →ᵇ ℝ` is a bounded continuous
function, then there exists a bounded continuous function `g : Y →ᵇ ℝ` of the norm `‖g‖ ≤ ‖f‖ / 3`
such that the distance between `g ∘ e` and `f` is at most `(2 / 3) * ‖f‖`.

explanatories.Dist.dist: A distance function that defines how to measure the separation between elements of a type can be created when the type adheres to the properties of a distance metric.
explanatories.BoundedContinuousFunction.compContinuous: The composition of a bounded continuous function and a continuous function produces another bounded continuous function.

BoundedContinuousFunction.tietze_extensi.description: For a closed embedding of a topological space into a normal topological space and a bounded continuous function, there exists a bounded continuous function that approximates the original function closely while being suitably constrained in norm.

BoundedContinuousFunction.exists_extensi.comment:
**Tietze extension theorem** for real-valued bounded continuous maps, a version for a closed
embedding and a bounded continuous function that takes values in a non-trivial closed interval.
See also `exists_extension_forall_mem_of_closedEmbedding` for a more general statement that works
for any interval (finite or infinite, open or closed).

If `e : X → Y` is a closed embedding and `f : X →ᵇ ℝ` is a bounded continuous function such that
`f x ∈ [a, b]` for all `x`, where `a ≤ b`, then there exists a bounded continuous function
`g : Y →ᵇ ℝ` such that `g y ∈ [a, b]` for all `y` and `g ∘ e = f`.

BoundedContinuousFunction.exists_extensi.description: For a closed embedding of a topological space and a bounded continuous function that outputs values within a closed interval, there exists an extension to another bounded continuous function that remains within the same interval and matches the original function when composed with the embedding.

BoundedContinuousFunction.exists_extensi.comment:
**Tietze extension theorem** for real-valued bounded continuous maps, a version for a closed
embedding. Let `e` be a closed embedding of a nonempty topological space `X` into a normal
topological space `Y`. Let `f` be a bounded continuous real-valued function on `X`. Then there

IsClosed.mk_lt_continuum.comment:
Let `s` be a closed set in a separable normal space. If the induced topology on `s` is discrete,
then `s` has cardinality less than continuum.

The proof follows
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moore_plane#Proof_that_the_Moore_plane_is_not_normal

explanatories.IsLinearMap.mk': This definition provides a method to construct a linear map from a function that satisfies the properties of linearity with respect to a semiring and two modules.
explanatories.LinearMap.inverse: This definition states that if a function is both a left and right inverse of a linear map, then it is itself a linear map.
explanatories.Pretrivialization.symm_apply_apply_mk: Applying the inverse of a pretrivialization to an element of the fiber constructed from its projection returns the original fiber element itself.
explanatories.Pretrivialization.apply_mk_symm: The application of the symmetric pretrivialization at a given point in the base set results in a pair comprising that point and an element from the fiber corresponding to it.
explanatories.LinearMap.isLinear: This theorem asserts that a linear map between two modules over a semiring qualifies as a linear map when its function is considered.
explanatories.Pretrivialization.coe_symm_of_not_mem: When a point is not included in the base set of a pretrivialization, its value under the inverse mapping is defined to be zero.

explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.
explanatories.Trivialization.symm: This defines a fiberwise inverse to a trivialization, mapping elements from the base space and fibers to the total space while behaving like zero outside the base set.
explanatories.Continuous.snd: This theorem states that if a function from one topological space to a product of two other topological spaces is continuous, then the projection onto the second component of that product is also continuous.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm: The inverse of a continuous linear equivalence between two modules also forms a continuous linear equivalence between those modules.
explanatories.And.symm: The conjunction of two propositions can be reversed, meaning that if both are true in one order, they are also true in the opposite order.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.symm: This definition describes the inverse of a partial homeomorphism, which relates two topological spaces in the opposite direction.
explanatories.Bundle.TotalSpace.snd: This definition extracts the fiber element associated with a given total space structure.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.

Pretrivialization.symmₗ.fullDefinition: protected def symmₗ (e : Pretrivialization F (π F E)) [e.IsLinear R] (b : B) : F →ₗ[R] E b := by   refine IsLinearMap.mk' (e.symm b) ?_   by_cases hb : b ∈ e.baseSet   · exact (((e.linear R hb).mk' _).inverse (e.symm b) (e.symm_apply_apply_mk hb) fun v ↦       congr_arg Prod.snd <| e.apply_mk_symm hb v).isLinear   · rw [e.coe_symm_of_not_mem hb]     exact (0 : F →ₗ[R] E b).isLinear
Pretrivialization.symmₗ.description: This defines a fiberwise linear map that serves as an inverse to a given pretrivialization.

explanatories.LinearEquiv.right_inv: This theorem demonstrates that the inverse function of a linear equivalence serves as a right inverse of the linear equivalence's underlying function.

explanatories.Trivialization.symm: This defines a fiberwise inverse to a trivialization, mapping elements from the base space and fibers to the total space while behaving like zero outside the base set.

explanatories.And.symm: The conjunction of two propositions can be reversed, meaning that if both are true in one order, they are also true in the opposite order.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.symm: This definition describes the inverse of a partial homeomorphism, which relates two topological spaces in the opposite direction.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.invFun: This definition describes the inverse function associated with a linear equivalence between two modules, allowing for the mapping from one module back to the other.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul': This theorem asserts that a specific linear map interacts with scalar multiplication in such a way that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is equivalent to multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar's image under a specified semiring homomorphism.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.

Pretrivialization.linearEquivAt.fullDefinition: def linearEquivAt (e : Pretrivialization F (π F E)) [e.IsLinear R] (b : B) (hb : b ∈ e.baseSet) :     E b ≃ₗ[R] F where   toFun y := (e ⟨b, y⟩).2   invFun := e.symm b   left_inv := e.symm_apply_apply_mk hb   right_inv v := by simp_rw [e.apply_mk_symm hb v]   map_add' v w := (e.linear R hb).map_add v w   map_smul' c v := (e.linear R hb).map_smul c v
Pretrivialization.linearEquivAt.description: This defines a linear isomorphism between the fiber at a point in the base set of a vector bundle and the model space, given that the pretrivialization is linear at that point.

explanatories.Pretrivialization.symm: The fiberwise inverse of a pretrivialization maps elements from the fiber to a zero structure outside the base set while providing a local inverse within the base set.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.
explanatories.Trivialization.symm: This defines a fiberwise inverse to a trivialization, mapping elements from the base space and fibers to the total space while behaving like zero outside the base set.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm: The inverse of a continuous linear equivalence between two modules also forms a continuous linear equivalence between those modules.
explanatories.And.symm: The conjunction of two propositions can be reversed, meaning that if both are true in one order, they are also true in the opposite order.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.symm: This definition describes the inverse of a partial homeomorphism, which relates two topological spaces in the opposite direction.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.

Trivialization.linearEquivAt_symm_apply.description: The theorem states that the inverse of the linear equivalence at a specific point matches the application of the corresponding trivialization's inverse on that point and a vector from the model space.

Trivialization.coordChangeL.fullDefinition: def coordChangeL (e e' : Trivialization F (π F E)) [e.IsLinear R] [e'.IsLinear R] (b : B) :     F ≃L[R] F :=   { toLinearEquiv := if hb : b ∈ e.baseSet ∩ e'.baseSet       then (e.linearEquivAt R b (hb.1 : _)).symm.trans (e'.linearEquivAt R b hb.2)       else LinearEquiv.refl R F     continuous_toFun := by       by_cases hb : b ∈ e.baseSet ∩ e'.baseSet       · rw [dif_pos hb]         refine (e'.continuousOn.comp_continuous ?_ ?_).snd         · exact e.continuousOn_symm.comp_continuous (Continuous.Prod.mk b) fun y =>             mk_mem_prod hb.1 (mem_univ y)         · exact fun y => e'.mem_source.mpr hb.2       · rw [dif_neg hb]         exact continuous_id     continuous_invFun := by       by_cases hb : b ∈ e.baseSet ∩ e'.baseSet       · rw [dif_pos hb]         refine (e.continuousOn.comp_continuous ?_ ?_).snd         · exact e'.continuousOn_symm.comp_continuous (Continuous.Prod.mk b) fun y =>             mk_mem_prod hb.2 (mem_univ y)         exact fun y => e.mem_source.mpr hb.1       · rw [dif_neg hb]         exact continuous_id } set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
Trivialization.coordChangeL.description: This defines a continuous linear equivalence that represents the change of coordinates between two trivializations, which coincides with the identity when the given point is not in the base set of both trivializations.

  [Semiring R] [TopologicalSpace F] [TopologicalSpace B] [TopologicalSpace (TotalSpace F E)] [AddCommMonoid F]
  [Module R F] [(x : B) → AddCommMonoid (E x)] [(x : B) → Module R (E x)] (e e' : Trivialization F TotalSpace.proj)
  [Trivialization.IsLinear R e] [Trivialization.IsLinear R e'] (b : B) : F ≃L[R] F
trivialization.coord_changeL.comment:
A coordinate change function between two trivializations, as a continuous linear equivalence.
Defined to be the identity when `b` does not lie in the base set of both trivializations.

Trivialization.coe_coordChangeL.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_1} {B : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3} {E : B → Type u_4}
  [Semiring R] [TopologicalSpace F] [TopologicalSpace B] [TopologicalSpace (TotalSpace F E)] [AddCommMonoid F]

Trivialization.continuousLinearMapAt.fullDefinition: def continuousLinearMapAt (e : Trivialization F (π F E)) [e.IsLinear R] (b : B) : E b →L[R] F :=   { e.linearMapAt R b with     toFun := e.linearMapAt R b -- given explicitly to help `simps`     cont := by       dsimp       rw [e.coe_linearMapAt b]       refine continuous_if_const _ (fun hb => ?_) fun _ => continuous_zero       exact (e.continuousOn.comp_continuous (FiberBundle.totalSpaceMk_inducing F E b).continuous         fun x => e.mem_source.mpr hb).snd }

vector_prebundle.pretrivializationAtlas.fullDefinition: pretrivializationAtlas : Set (Pretrivialization F (π F E))   pretrivialization_linear' : ∀ e, e ∈ pretrivializationAtlas → e.IsLinear R   pretrivializationAt : B → Pretrivialization F (π F E)   mem_base_pretrivializationAt : ∀ x : B, x ∈ (pretrivializationAt x).baseSet   pretrivialization_mem_atlas : ∀ x : B, pretrivializationAt x ∈ pretrivializationAtlas   exists_coordChange : ∀ᵉ (e ∈ pretrivializationAtlas) (e' ∈ pretrivializationAtlas),     ∃ f : B → F →L[R] F, ContinuousOn f (e.baseSet ∩ e'.baseSet) ∧       ∀ᵉ (b ∈ e.baseSet ∩ e'.baseSet) (v : F), f b v = (e' ⟨b, e.symm b v⟩).2   totalSpaceMk_inducing : ∀ b : B, Inducing (pretrivializationAt b ∘ .mk b)

VectorPrebundle.exists_coordChange.code:
VectorPrebundle.exists_coordChange.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_1} {B : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3} {E : B → Type u_4}
  [NontriviallyNormedField R] [(x : B) → AddCommMonoid (E x)] [(x : B) → Module R (E x)] [NormedAddCommGroup F]
  [NormedSpace R F] [TopologicalSpace B] [(x : B) → TopologicalSpace (E x)] (self : VectorPrebundle R F E)
  (e : Pretrivialization F TotalSpace.proj) :
  e ∈ self.pretrivializationAtlas →
    ∀ e' ∈ self.pretrivializationAtlas,
      ∃ f,
        ContinuousOn f (e.baseSet ∩ e'.baseSet) ∧
          ∀ b ∈ e.baseSet ∩ e'.baseSet, ∀ (v : F), (f b) v = (↑e' { proj := b, snd := e.symm b v }).2

explanatories.ContinuousOn.prod_map: The product of two continuous functions remains continuous on the Cartesian product of their respective domains.
explanatories.continuousOn_id: The identity function is continuous on any given set within a topological space.

explanatories.VectorPrebundle.coordChange: The coordinate change in a vector prebundle provides a linear map that allows for the transition between different local trivializations over the base space.

VectorPrebundle.toFiberPrebundle.fullDefinition: def toFiberPrebundle (a : VectorPrebundle R F E) : FiberPrebundle F E :=   { a with     continuous_trivChange := fun e he e' he' ↦ by       have : ContinuousOn (fun x : B × F ↦ a.coordChange he' he x.1 x.2)           ((e'.baseSet ∩ e.baseSet) ×ˢ univ) :=         isBoundedBilinearMap_apply.continuous.comp_continuousOn           ((a.continuousOn_coordChange he' he).prod_map continuousOn_id)       rw [e.target_inter_preimage_symm_source_eq e', inter_comm]       refine (continuousOn_fst.prod this).congr ?_       rintro ⟨b, f⟩ ⟨hb, -⟩       dsimp only [Function.comp_def, Prod.map]       rw [a.mk_coordChange _ _ hb, e'.mk_symm hb.1] }

VectorPrebundle.toVectorBundle.comment:
Make a `VectorBundle` from a `VectorPrebundle`.  Concretely this means
that, given a `VectorPrebundle` structure for a sigma-type `E` -- which consists of a
number of "pretrivializations" identifying parts of `E` with product spaces `U × F` -- one
establishes that for the topology constructed on the sigma-type using
`VectorPrebundle.totalSpaceTopology`, these "pretrivializations" are actually
"trivializations" (i.e., homeomorphisms with respect to the constructed topology).
VectorPrebundle.toVectorBundle.description: This theorem establishes a structure of a vector bundle from a vector prebundle by demonstrating that the pretrivializations align as trivializations under the topology defined on the total space of the prebundle.

ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates.code:
ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates.{u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7, u_8, u_9} {B : Type u_2} (F : Type u_3)
  (E : B → Type u_4) [(x : B) → AddCommMonoid (E x)] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [TopologicalSpace B]
  [(x : B) → TopologicalSpace (E x)] {𝕜₁ : Type u_5} {𝕜₂ : Type u_6} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜₁]
  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜₂] {σ : 𝕜₁ →+* 𝕜₂} {B' : Type u_7} [TopologicalSpace B'] [NormedSpace 𝕜₁ F]
  [(x : B) → Module 𝕜₁ (E x)] [TopologicalSpace (TotalSpace F E)] (F' : Type u_8) [NormedAddCommGroup F']
  [NormedSpace 𝕜₂ F'] (E' : B' → Type u_9) [(x : B') → AddCommMonoid (E' x)] [(x : B') → Module 𝕜₂ (E' x)]
  [TopologicalSpace (TotalSpace F' E')] [FiberBundle F E] [VectorBundle 𝕜₁ F E] [(x : B') → TopologicalSpace (E' x)]
  [FiberBundle F' E'] [VectorBundle 𝕜₂ F' E'] (x₀ x : B) (y₀ y : B') (ϕ : E x →SL[σ] E' y) : F →SL[σ] F'
ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates.comment:
When `ϕ` is a continuous (semi)linear map between the fibers `E x` and `E' y` of two vector
bundles `E` and `E'`, `ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates F E F' E' x₀ x y₀ y ϕ` is a coordinate
change of this continuous linear map w.r.t. the chart around `x₀` and the chart around `y₀`.

It is defined by composing `ϕ` with appropriate coordinate changes given by the vector bundles
`E` and `E'`.
We use the operations `Trivialization.continuousLinearMapAt` and `Trivialization.symmL` in the
definition, instead of `Trivialization.continuousLinearEquivAt`, so that
`ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates` is defined everywhere (but see
`ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates_eq`).

This is the (second component of the) underlying function of a trivialization of the hom-bundle
(see `hom_trivializationAt_apply`). However, note that `ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates` is
defined even when `x` and `y` live in different base sets.
Therefore, it is also convenient when working with the hom-bundle between pulled back bundles.

explanatories.Trivialization.continuousLinearMapAt: This definition describes a linear map that is continuous at a given point in the base space of a vector bundle, relating elements of the fiber to a model space.
explanatories.Trivialization.symmL: This definition describes a linear map that serves as the inverse of a trivialization at a given point in the base space, mapping from the model space to the fiber at that point.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.comp: The composition of bounded linear maps results in another bounded linear map.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.

ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates.fullDefinition: def inCoordinates (x₀ x : B) (y₀ y : B') (ϕ : E x →SL[σ] E' y) : F →SL[σ] F' :=   ((trivializationAt F' E' y₀).continuousLinearMapAt 𝕜₂ y).comp <|     ϕ.comp <| (trivializationAt F E x₀).symmL 𝕜₁ x
ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates.description: This defines a way to describe how a continuous linear map between the fibers of two vector bundles changes when moving from one coordinate chart to another, ensuring it is well-defined even if the points are in different base sets.

  [(x : B) → TopologicalSpace (E x)] {𝕜₁ : Type u_5} {𝕜₂ : Type u_6} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜₁]
  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜₂] {σ : 𝕜₁ →+* 𝕜₂} {B' : Type u_7} [TopologicalSpace B'] [NormedSpace 𝕜₁ F]
  [(x : B) → Module 𝕜₁ (E x)] [TopologicalSpace (TotalSpace F E)] (F' : Type u_8) [NormedAddCommGroup F']
  [NormedSpace 𝕜₂ F'] (E' : B' → Type u_9) [(x : B') → AddCommMonoid (E' x)] [(x : B') → Module 𝕜₂ (E' x)]
  [TopologicalSpace (TotalSpace F' E')] [FiberBundle F E] [VectorBundle 𝕜₁ F E] [(x : B') → TopologicalSpace (E' x)]
  [FiberBundle F' E'] [VectorBundle 𝕜₂ F' E'] (x₀ x : B) (y₀ y : B') (ϕ : E x →SL[σ] E' y) : F →SL[σ] F'
continuous_linear_map.in_coordinates.comment:
When `ϕ` is a continuous (semi)linear map between the fibers `E x` and `E' y` of two vector
bundles `E` and `E'`, `ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates F E F' E' x₀ x y₀ y ϕ` is a coordinate
change of this continuous linear map w.r.t. the chart around `x₀` and the chart around `y₀`.

It is defined by composing `ϕ` with appropriate coordinate changes given by the vector bundles
`E` and `E'`.
We use the operations `Trivialization.continuousLinearMapAt` and `Trivialization.symmL` in the
definition, instead of `Trivialization.continuousLinearEquivAt`, so that
`ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates` is defined everywhere (but see
`ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates_eq`).

This is the (second component of the) underlying function of a trivialization of the hom-bundle
(see `hom_trivializationAt_apply`). However, note that `ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates` is
defined even when `x` and `y` live in different base sets.
Therefore, it is also convenient when working with the hom-bundle between pulled back bundles.

explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.

continuous_linear_map.in_coordinates.fullDefinition: def inCoordinates (x₀ x : B) (y₀ y : B') (ϕ : E x →SL[σ] E' y) : F →SL[σ] F' :=   ((trivializationAt F' E' y₀).continuousLinearMapAt 𝕜₂ y).comp <|     ϕ.comp <| (trivializationAt F E x₀).symmL 𝕜₁ x

  [(x : B) → Module 𝕜₁ (E x)] [TopologicalSpace (TotalSpace F E)] {F' : Type u_8} [NormedAddCommGroup F']
  [NormedSpace 𝕜₂ F'] (E' : B' → Type u_9) [(x : B') → AddCommMonoid (E' x)] [(x : B') → Module 𝕜₂ (E' x)]
  [TopologicalSpace (TotalSpace F' E')] [FiberBundle F E] [VectorBundle 𝕜₁ F E] [(x : B') → TopologicalSpace (E' x)]

VectorBundle.prod.fullDefinition: instance VectorBundle.prod [VectorBundle 𝕜 F₁ E₁] [VectorBundle 𝕜 F₂ E₂] :     VectorBundle 𝕜 (F₁ × F₂) (E₁ ×ᵇ E₂) where   trivialization_linear' := by     rintro _ ⟨e₁, e₂, he₁, he₂, rfl⟩     infer_instance   continuousOn_coordChange' := by     rintro _ _ ⟨e₁, e₂, he₁, he₂, rfl⟩ ⟨e₁', e₂', he₁', he₂', rfl⟩     refine (((continuousOn_coordChange 𝕜 e₁ e₁').mono ?_).prod_mapL 𝕜       ((continuousOn_coordChange 𝕜 e₂ e₂').mono ?_)).congr ?_ <;>       dsimp only [baseSet_prod, mfld_simps]     · mfld_set_tac     · mfld_set_tac     · rintro b hb       rw [ContinuousLinearMap.ext_iff]       rintro ⟨v₁, v₂⟩       show (e₁.prod e₂).coordChangeL 𝕜 (e₁'.prod e₂') b (v₁, v₂) =         (e₁.coordChangeL 𝕜 e₁' b v₁, e₂.coordChangeL 𝕜 e₂' b v₂)       rw [e₁.coordChangeL_apply e₁', e₂.coordChangeL_apply e₂', (e₁.prod e₂).coordChangeL_apply']       exacts [rfl, hb, ⟨hb.1.2, hb.2.2⟩, ⟨hb.1.1, hb.2.1⟩]

explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.Trivialization.coordChangeL: This defines a continuous linear equivalence that represents the change of coordinates between two trivializations, which coincides with the identity when the given point is not in the base set of both trivializations.
explanatories.Trivialization.coordChangeL_apply': This theorem provides an explicit formula for the application of a coordinate change between two linear trivializations, expressing it in terms of the components of the fibers mapped through the trivializations.
explanatories.Bundle.Trivial.trivialization.coordChang: This theorem states that the change of coordinates induced by a trivialization at any point of the base space is identical to the identity linear equivalence on the fiber space, highlighting its linear structure.
explanatories.Continuous.continuousOn: If a function is continuous on its entire domain, it is also continuous on any subset of that domain.
explanatories.Trivialization.baseSet: The base set of a trivialization is defined as a subset of the base space associated with a given projection.
explanatories.Trivialization.coordChangeL_apply: The theorem states that the change of coordinates between two linear trivializations at a point in their intersection of base sets maps a vector in the model space to the corresponding coordinate transformation defined by the second trivialization.
explanatories.continuousOn_coordChange: This theorem states that the coordinate change function between two trivializations of a vector bundle is continuous when restricted to the intersection of their base sets.
explanatories.ContinuousOn.congr: If two functions are equal on a set and one is continuous on that set, then the other function is also continuous on the same set.
explanatories.Trivialization.pullback: A fiber bundle trivialization can be adapted to correspond to a trivialization on the pullback bundle via a continuous map from a base space.
explanatories.ContinuousOn.comp: The composition of two continuous functions, where the output of the first function maps into the domain of the second, is itself continuous on the specified set of the first function.
explanatories.ContinuousMapClass.map_continuous: This theorem asserts that a mapping defined by a continuous map preserves the property of continuity when applied to a topological space.

VectorBundle.pullback.fullDefinition: instance VectorBundle.pullback [∀ x, TopologicalSpace (E x)] [FiberBundle F E] [VectorBundle 𝕜 F E]     (f : K) : VectorBundle 𝕜 F ((f : B' → B) *ᵖ E) where   trivialization_linear' := by     rintro _ ⟨e, he, rfl⟩     infer_instance   continuousOn_coordChange' := by     rintro _ _ ⟨e, he, rfl⟩ ⟨e', he', rfl⟩     refine ((continuousOn_coordChange 𝕜 e e').comp       (map_continuous f).continuousOn fun b hb => hb).congr ?_     rintro b (hb : f b ∈ e.baseSet ∩ e'.baseSet); ext v     show ((e.pullback f).coordChangeL 𝕜 (e'.pullback f) b) v = (e.coordChangeL 𝕜 e' (f b)) v     rw [e.coordChangeL_apply e' hb, (e.pullback f).coordChangeL_apply' _]     exacts [rfl, hb]
VectorBundle.pullback.description: This definition introduces the pullback of a vector bundle along a continuous map, resulting in a new vector bundle where the fibers are effectively the pullback of the fibers of the original bundle.

explanatories.Trivialization.open_baseSet: The base set of a trivialization is an open subset of the topological space.

Pretrivialization.continuousLinearMap.fullDefinition: def continuousLinearMap :     Pretrivialization (F₁ →SL[σ] F₂) (π (F₁ →SL[σ] F₂) (Bundle.ContinuousLinearMap σ E₁ E₂)) where   toFun p := ⟨p.1, .comp (e₂.continuousLinearMapAt 𝕜₂ p.1) (p.2.comp (e₁.symmL 𝕜₁ p.1))⟩   invFun p := ⟨p.1, .comp (e₂.symmL 𝕜₂ p.1) (p.2.comp (e₁.continuousLinearMapAt 𝕜₁ p.1))⟩   source := Bundle.TotalSpace.proj ⁻¹' (e₁.baseSet ∩ e₂.baseSet)   target := (e₁.baseSet ∩ e₂.baseSet) ×ˢ Set.univ   map_source' := fun ⟨x, L⟩ h => ⟨h, Set.mem_univ _⟩   map_target' := fun ⟨x, f⟩ h => h.1   left_inv' := fun ⟨x, L⟩ ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ => by     simp only [TotalSpace.mk_inj]     ext (v : E₁ x)     dsimp only [comp_apply]     rw [Trivialization.symmL_continuousLinearMapAt, Trivialization.symmL_continuousLinearMapAt]     exacts [h₁, h₂]   right_inv' := fun ⟨x, f⟩ ⟨⟨h₁, h₂⟩, _⟩ => by     simp only [Prod.mk_inj_left]     ext v     dsimp only [comp_apply]     rw [Trivialization.continuousLinearMapAt_symmL, Trivialization.continuousLinearMapAt_symmL]     exacts [h₁, h₂]   open_target := (e₁.open_baseSet.inter e₂.open_baseSet).prod isOpen_univ   baseSet := e₁.baseSet ∩ e₂.baseSet   open_baseSet := e₁.open_baseSet.inter e₂.open_baseSet   source_eq := rfl   target_eq := rfl   proj_toFun _ _ := rfl
Pretrivialization.continuousLinearMap.description: This definition describes the pretrivialization of a vector bundle of continuous semilinear maps between two bundles given their respective trivializations, providing a structured way to relate the fibers over a common base space.

pretrivialization.continuous_linear_map.comment:
Given trivializations `e₁`, `e₂` for vector bundles `E₁`, `E₂` over a base `B`,
`Pretrivialization.continuousLinearMap σ e₁ e₂` is the induced pretrivialization for the
continuous `σ`-semilinear maps from `E₁` to `E₂`. That is, the map which will later become a
trivialization, after the bundle of continuous semilinear maps is equipped with the right
topological vector bundle structure.

explanatories.Trivialization.symmL: This definition describes a linear map that serves as the inverse of a trivialization at a given point in the base space, mapping from the model space to the fiber at that point.
explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.Set.mem_univ: Any element of a type belongs to the universal set of that type.
explanatories.Bundle.TotalSpace.mk_inj: This theorem establishes that the total space structures constructed with the same base element are equal if and only if their corresponding fiber elements are equal.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply: The composition of two continuous linear maps yields a continuous linear map whose application to an element corresponds to the application of the second map followed by the first.
explanatories.Trivialization.symmL_continuousLinearMap: The theorem shows that applying the inverse linear map of a trivialization to the image of a point in the fiber under the continuous linear map at that point yields the original point in the fiber.
explanatories.Prod.mk_inj_left: If two pairs are equal and share the same first element, then their second elements must also be equal.
explanatories.Trivialization.continuousLinearMapAt_sym: The theorem states that applying the symmetric linear map at a point in the base set of a trivialization returns the original element in the model space.
explanatories.Trivialization.open_baseSet: The base set of a trivialization is an open subset of the topological space.
explanatories.IsOpen.prod: This theorem establishes that the Cartesian product of two open sets in topological spaces is also an open set in the product topology.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.

explanatories.Trivialization.symmL: This definition describes a linear map that serves as the inverse of a trivialization at a given point in the base space, mapping from the model space to the fiber at that point.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.add_comp: The composition of the sum of two continuous linear maps is equal to the sum of each map's composition with a third continuous linear map.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.comp_add: The composition of a continuous linear map with the sum of two other continuous linear maps is equal to the sum of the compositions of the continuous linear map with each of those two maps individually.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.smul_comp: The composition of a continuous linear map with another continuous linear map is compatible with scalar multiplication from a commutative monoid.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.comp_smulₛₗ: The theorem states that the composition of a continuous linear map with a scalar multiplication applied to another continuous linear map can be expressed as the scalar multiplication applied to the result of the composition of the two maps.
explanatories.RingHom.id_apply: This theorem states that the identity ring homomorphism returns any element from the semiring unchanged.

Pretrivialization.continuousLinearMap.is.fullDefinition: instance continuousLinearMap.isLinear [∀ x, ContinuousAdd (E₂ x)] [∀ x, ContinuousSMul 𝕜₂ (E₂ x)] :     (Pretrivialization.continuousLinearMap σ e₁ e₂).IsLinear 𝕜₂ where   linear x _ :=     { map_add := fun L L' =>         show (e₂.continuousLinearMapAt 𝕜₂ x).comp ((L + L').comp (e₁.symmL 𝕜₁ x)) = _ by           simp_rw [add_comp, comp_add]           rfl       map_smul := fun c L =>         show (e₂.continuousLinearMapAt 𝕜₂ x).comp ((c • L).comp (e₁.symmL 𝕜₁ x)) = _ by           simp_rw [smul_comp, comp_smulₛₗ, RingHom.id_apply]           rfl }
